### direct_sum — `direct_sum.py`

| v1 | what it did | v2 | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| `direct_sum.HilbertSpaceDirectSum` | A HilbertSpace formed as the direct sum of a list of component Hilbert spaces; a vector is a Python list whose i-th entry is a vector of the i-th subspace, and the inner product is the sum of component inner products. | `pygeoinf2.algebra.direct_sum.DirectSum (and the auto-dispatched subclass _CoordinateDirectSum)` | Renamed DirectSum. Vectors are tuples, not lists (copy/zero/axpy all return tuples). Constructor now validates (non-empty; optional labels= keyword, distinct, right count) and dispatches via __new__ to _CoordinateDirectSum only when every summand is a CoordinateSpace; a sum with a coordinate-free summand has no to_components/from_components/is_orthonormal. Inner product is now overridden directly as the sum of summand inner products (v1 went via dual components). New: labels, index(), component(), __len__, random(), white_noise(), shares_vectors_with, __repr__, structural _key identity (hashable). Does call the base through the ABC protocol (no HilbertSpace.__init__ exists in v2). |
| `direct_sum.HilbertSpaceDirectSum.__init__` | Stores the component spaces and precomputes the total dimension. | `DirectSum.__init__(self, spaces, /, *, labels=None)` | spaces is positional-only and copied to a tuple (v1 stored the caller's list). Raises ValueError('A direct sum needs at least one summand.') on empty input (v1 accepted). New labels keyword validated for count and distinctness. Paired with __new__ that returns a _CoordinateDirectSum when all summands are CoordinateSpaces; _CoordinateDirectSum.__init__ additionally precomputes component slices. Still does not call a base __init__ (none exists). |
| `direct_sum.HilbertSpaceDirectSum.is_orthonormal` | True iff every component subspace reports is_orthonormal. | `_CoordinateDirectSum.is_orthonormal` | Same all(...) logic, but only defined on the coordinate subclass (is_orthonormal lives on CoordinateSpace in v2), so a DirectSum with a coordinate-free summand has no is_orthonormal attribute. Companion has_diagonal_metric added. |
| `direct_sum.HilbertSpaceDirectSum.to_components` | Maps a list of subspace vectors to a single flat component array by concatenating each subspace's components in order. | `_CoordinateDirectSum.to_components` | Same concatenation, but only available when every summand is a CoordinateSpace (coordinate-free sums have no to_components). Input is a tuple. |
| `direct_sum.HilbertSpaceDirectSum.from_components` | Slices a flat component array by successive subspace dimensions and maps each slice back through the corresponding subspace's from_components. | `_CoordinateDirectSum.from_components` | Returns a tuple, not a list; uses slices precomputed in __init__ (:272-275) rather than a running index; only available on the coordinate subclass. |
| `direct_sum.HilbertSpaceDirectSum.zero` | The zero element: a list of each subspace's zero. | `DirectSum.zero()` | Method instead of property (library-wide change, DESIGN.md table line 1270 'space.zero (property) -> space.zero()'); returns a tuple of summand zeros. |
| `direct_sum.HilbertSpaceDirectSum.add` | Componentwise addition delegated to each subspace's add. | `HilbertSpace.add (inherited by DirectSum)` | Not overridden on DirectSum; the base derives it as axpy(1.0, x, copy(y)), which delegates componentwise through DirectSum.copy/axpy. Result is a tuple. v1 delegated to each subspace's own add (x + y by default), i.e. one fewer explicit copy per component. |
| `direct_sum.HilbertSpaceDirectSum.subtract` | Componentwise subtraction delegated to each subspace's subtract. | `HilbertSpace.subtract (inherited)` | Not overridden; base derives axpy(-1.0, y, copy(x)) through DirectSum.copy/axpy. Tuple result. |
| `direct_sum.HilbertSpaceDirectSum.multiply` | Scalar multiplication delegated componentwise to each subspace's multiply. | `HilbertSpace.scale(a, x) (inherited)` | Renamed multiply -> scale library-wide (DESIGN.md:1271 'space.multiply(a, x) \| space.scale(a, x)'); 'multiply' in v2 means the pointwise product on HilbertModule (spaces.py:758). Derived as scale_inplace(a, copy(x)) through DirectSum's componentwise copy/scale_inplace. Tuple result. |
| `direct_sum.HilbertSpaceDirectSum.ax` | In-place scaling x <- a*x, delegated componentwise to each subspace's ax. | `DirectSum.scale_inplace(a, x)` | Renamed ax -> scale_inplace (DESIGN.md:1270). Returns the resulting tuple (v1 returned None); per the v2 in-place contract callers must use the return value since immutable summands (Reals) return new objects. |
| `direct_sum.HilbertSpaceDirectSum.axpy` | In-place y <- a*x + y, delegated componentwise to each subspace's axpy. | `DirectSum.axpy(a, x, y)` | Same componentwise delegation, but returns a tuple of the summand results (v1 returned None and mutated ys); summand vectors are still updated in place where mutable. |
| `direct_sum.HilbertSpaceDirectSum.copy` | Deep-ish copy: new list whose entries are each subspace's copy of the corresponding component. | `DirectSum.copy(x)` | Same componentwise copy; returns a tuple instead of a list. |
| `direct_sum.HilbertSpaceDirectSum.__eq__` | Two direct sums are equal iff other is a HilbertSpaceDirectSum and their subspace lists compare equal (same count, each corresponding subspace equal). | `HilbertSpace.__eq__ via DirectSum._key() (the tuple of summands)` | Equality is now structural through the base: same exact type (DirectSum vs _CoordinateDirectSum are distinct types, though the public constructor always yields the same one for the same summands) and equal _key() = tuple of subspaces; labels deliberately excluded. Instances are now hashable (base __hash__); v1 defined __eq__ without __hash__. Added shares_vectors_with (summand-wise). |
| `direct_sum.HilbertSpaceDirectSum.subspaces` | The list of component subspaces (the same list object passed to the constructor). | `DirectSum.subspaces` | Returns the stored tuple (immutable) rather than the caller's list object; mutating it is no longer possible. |
| `direct_sum.HilbertSpaceDirectSum.subspace` | Returns the i-th component subspace. | `DirectSum.subspace(key: int \| str)` | Accepts a label as well as an index. Index validated by DirectSum.index(): negative indices now raise IndexError (v1 plain list indexing accepted them); unknown labels raise KeyError. |
| `direct_sum.HilbertSpaceDirectSum.subspace_projection` | Returns the projection operator from the direct sum onto the i-th subspace (xs -> xs[i]). | `DirectSum.projection(key)` | Renamed projection; accepts a label or index; memoised per index (same object on every call, so P.adjoint is S.inclusion(key) and the palindrome recognition in nodes.py fires). Still matrix-free via LinearOperator.from_callables with an explicit adjoint. |
| `direct_sum.HilbertSpaceDirectSum.subspace_inclusion` | Returns the inclusion operator from the i-th subspace into the direct sum (x -> [0,...,x,...,0]). | `DirectSum.inclusion(key)` | Renamed inclusion; accepts a label; defined as projection(key).adjoint (the memoised _Adjoint node of the projection) rather than an independently built operator, so inclusion(key).adjoint is projection(key). Still matrix-free. |
| `direct_sum.HilbertSpaceDirectSum._subspace_inclusion_mapping` | The mapping behind subspace_inclusion / the adjoint of subspace_projection: returns a list with x in slot i and each other subspace's zero elsewhere. | `closure `adjoint` inside DirectSum.projection` | Same behaviour (y placed uncopied in slot i, fresh zeros elsewhere via other.zero()), but returns a tuple instead of a list — the same list->tuple return change classified as ported_changed on copy/from_components/zero. |
| `direct_sum.HilbertSpaceDirectSum.vectors_are_lists` | Elements of a direct-sum space are plain Python lists of subspace vectors, in subspace order; all vector operations zip over subspaces. | `vectors are tuples (DirectSum[V](HilbertSpace[tuple]))` | Container changed from list to tuple: all operations return tuples; existing v1 code that builds a list and mutates slots (e.g. xs[i] = v) must build a tuple instead. Components remain mutable so axpy still updates in place. Named access via S.component(x, label). Length checks remain absent except in index validation (zip truncates silently, as in v1). |
| `direct_sum.HilbertSpaceDirectSum.inner_product_via_dual` | inner_product, norm, dual, gram_schmidt etc. are not overridden; the base HilbertSpace supplies them through this class's to_dual/from_dual, which go via concatenated dual components. | `DirectSum.inner_product (direct override); squared_norm/norm on _CoordinateDirectSum resolve to CoordinateSpace.squared_norm (component route)` | Inner product is overridden directly as the float sum of summand inner products, coordinate-free (works for sums with coordinate-free summands); on _CoordinateDirectSum the MRO (DirectSum before CoordinateSpace) keeps this override ahead of CoordinateSpace's component route. However DirectSum does NOT override squared_norm/norm, and _CoordinateDirectSum's MRO is (DirectSum, CoordinateSpace, HilbertSpace), so on any all-coordinate sum squared_norm resolves to CoordinateSpace.squared_norm (spaces.py:420-430): to_components on every summand, concatenated, then the block apply_gram — because uses_component_fast_paths is inherited True (spaces.py:449-456) without consulting the summands. So S.norm(x) is coordinate-free only on a sum with a coordinate-free summand; on the common all-coordinate case it goes through components, as v1 did (v1 went through concatenated dual components for everything). Not worse than v1, but the two routes (inner_product vs norm) differ within the same object. |
| `direct_sum.BlockStructure.row_dim` | Number of block rows. | `BlockOperator.row_dim (BlockLinearOperator inherits); len(op.operators) on Column/Row/BlockDiagonal` | Present with the same name only on BlockOperator/BlockLinearOperator (computed as len(self._blocks)). ColumnLinearOperator, RowLinearOperator and BlockDiagonalLinearOperator have no row_dim; use len(op.operators) (or 1 for Row). |
| `direct_sum.BlockStructure.col_dim` | Number of block columns. | `BlockOperator.col_dim; len(op.operators) on Column/Row/BlockDiagonal` | Present only on BlockOperator/BlockLinearOperator (len(self._blocks[0])). Not on Column/Row/BlockDiagonal. |
| `direct_sum.BlockStructure.block` | Abstract: returns the LinearOperator in the (i, j)-th sub-block. | `BlockOperator.block(i, j) (concrete, not abstract); op.operators[i] elsewhere` | Concrete method on BlockOperator only (returns self._blocks[i][j], no validation). Not abstract, not present on Column/Row/BlockDiagonal, which expose `.operators` instead. |
| `direct_sum.BlockLinearOperator` | A LinearOperator between two direct-sum spaces defined by a row-major 2D grid of sub-operators; maps a list of inputs [x_1, ...] to a list of outputs [y_1, ...] with y_i = sum_j A_ij x_j. | `BlockLinearOperator (subclass of new nonlinear BlockOperator and LinearOperator); BlockOperator([...]) dispatches to it when every block is linear` | Now sits under a nonlinear BlockOperator base whose derivative is the block of derivatives; BlockOperator(blocks) returns a BlockLinearOperator when all blocks are LinearOperators. Adds: traits (SELF_ADJOINT when the grid is its own adjoint transpose), a structured adjoint (transposed grid of adjoints, linked both ways) instead of the base's generic adjoint node, _known_matrix/_known_diagonals hooks, `blocks` property, zero-block skipping and allocation-light accumulation in the action. Loses: BlockStructure mixin and block-index validation; dense-matrix assembly now only when every block already knows its matrix (see _compute_dense_matrix row). Vectors are tuples. |
| `direct_sum.BlockLinearOperator.__init__` | Validates the grid for dimensional consistency and builds the direct-sum domain/codomain. | `BlockLinearOperator.__init__(blocks) with shared _check_grid` | Same four consistency checks but different messages ('A block operator needs at least one block.', 'Row {i} has {n} blocks, but row 0 has {w}.', 'Block (i, j) has domain ..., but column j is ...', 'Block (i, j) has codomain ..., but row i is ...'); blocks copied into tuples of tuples (v1 stored the caller's list); traits computed via _block_traits; no BlockStructure.__init__. LinearOperator.__init__ now takes only (domain, codomain, traits=) — the actions are methods _value/_adjoint_value rather than injected mappings. |
| `direct_sum.BlockLinearOperator.block` | Returns the (i, j)-th sub-operator. | `BlockOperator.block(i, j) (inherited)` | No _check_block_indices: out-of-range raises IndexError (not ValueError), negative indices accepted. Also available as the `blocks` property (tuple of tuples). |
| `direct_sum.BlockLinearOperator._mapping` | Matrix-free forward action: for each block row i, starts from codomains[i].zero and accumulates block(i,j)(xs[j]) with codomain.axpy(1.0, ...). | `BlockOperator._value(x) with _accumulate` | Same y_i = sum_j A_ij x_j, matrix-free, but: blocks that are the _Zero node are skipped (never applied); the row sum starts from a copy of the first image rather than codomain.zero(), then axpy; rows with only zero blocks still give codomain.zero(). Returns a tuple. Uses the axpy return value (v2 in-place contract). |
| `direct_sum.BlockLinearOperator._adjoint_mapping` | Matrix-free adjoint action: for each block column j, starts from domains[j].zero and accumulates block(i,j).adjoint(ys[i]) with domain.axpy(1.0, ...). | `BlockLinearOperator._adjoint_value(y) plus _make_adjoint` | Same x_j = sum_i A_ij^* y_i with the same zero-block skipping/copy-first accumulation. In addition, op.adjoint is now a real BlockLinearOperator of the transposed grid of adjoints (linked so adjoint.adjoint is op), rather than a generic adjoint wrapper over this action — so op.adjoint.block(i, j) works. The docstring claim 'the adjoint of a Column is a Row' is now true in code for Column/Row. |
| `direct_sum.BlockLinearOperator._compute_dense_matrix` | Override of the LinearOperator dense-matrix hook: asks each sub-block for block.matrix(dense=True, galerkin=galerkin, parallel=parallel, n_jobs=n_jobs) and assembles with np.block. | `BlockLinearOperator._known_matrix(form) -> _known_block_matrix; fallback LinearOperator.matrix() probing` | Hook renamed and semantics changed: the blockwise np.block assembly fires only when BOTH sides are CoordinateSpaces AND every block returns a non-None _known_matrix('components') (i.e. is matrix-backed/diagonal/zero/identity etc.). If any single block would need probing, the whole block operator returns None and LinearOperator.matrix() probes the entire operator column-by-column (or row-by-row via the adjoint) through the direct sum — re-deriving even the blocks whose matrices were known, and applying every non-zero block in every row for each basis vector. v1 always assembled blockwise, letting each block use its own route and forwarding parallel/n_jobs. Galerkin form now obtained by codomain.apply_gram_to_columns on the components assembly (blockwise Gram): blocks are always asked for the 'components' form, so a Galerkin-stored MatrixLinearOperator block is first converted components-wards (solve_gram_to_columns, operators.py:1766-1774) and then Gram-applied back — two metric passes where v1 read the stored Galerkin matrix directly (v1 linear_operators.py:1105-1113). The (galerkin, parallel, n_jobs) signature is gone; n_jobs only affects the fallback probe. |
| `direct_sum.ColumnLinearOperator` | A block operator from a single space to a direct sum: a column [A_1, ..., A_n]^T mapping x to [A_1(x), ..., A_n(x)]; typically the joint forward operator of several experiments. | `ColumnLinearOperator (subclass of new nonlinear ColumnOperator and LinearOperator); ColumnOperator([...]) dispatches to it` | Now under a nonlinear ColumnOperator base (derivative = column of derivatives). Adjoint is a genuine RowLinearOperator instance (linked both ways). Loses row_dim/col_dim/block(i, j) (use `.operators`), and loses the blockwise dense-matrix hook entirely (no _known_matrix override: matrix() always probes). Codomain is DirectSum of codomains; vectors are tuples. |
| `direct_sum.ColumnLinearOperator.__init__` | Validates a non-empty list of operators sharing a common domain and builds the direct-sum codomain. | `ColumnLinearOperator.__init__(operators); ColumnOperator.__init__ for the dispatch path` | Common-domain check kept with a new message ('Block {i} has domain ..., expected ...'). The empty-list check exists only in ColumnOperator.__init__ ('A column operator needs at least one block.'); constructing ColumnLinearOperator([]) directly (or ColumnOperator([]), which dispatches to the linear class since all() of nothing is True) hits self._operators[0] and raises IndexError instead of v1's ValueError('Operator list cannot be empty.'). Operators copied to a tuple. No BlockStructure.__init__. |
| `direct_sum.ColumnLinearOperator._mapping` | Matrix-free forward action: [op(x) for op in operators]. | `ColumnOperator._value(x)` | tuple(op(x) for op in operators) — identical apart from returning a tuple rather than a list (the same user-visible return-type change classified as ported_changed on copy/from_components/zero). |
| `direct_sum.ColumnLinearOperator._adjoint_mapping` | Matrix-free adjoint action: starts from domain.zero and accumulates op.adjoint(y_i) via domain.axpy(1.0, ...). | `ColumnLinearOperator._adjoint_value(y) via _accumulate; _make_adjoint returns RowLinearOperator` | Same sum of op.adjoint(y_i), but _Zero blocks skipped and accumulation starts from a copy of the first image instead of domain.zero(). op.adjoint is now a RowLinearOperator([op.adjoint for op in operators]) linked back. |
| `direct_sum.RowLinearOperator` | A block operator from a direct sum to a single space: a row [A_1, ..., A_n] mapping [x_1, ..., x_n] to A_1(x_1) + ... + A_n(x_n). | `RowLinearOperator (subclass of new nonlinear RowOperator and LinearOperator); RowOperator([...]) dispatches to it` | Now under a nonlinear RowOperator base (derivative = row of derivatives at each component). Adjoint is a genuine ColumnLinearOperator instance (linked). Loses row_dim/col_dim/block(i, j) (use `.operators`) and the hstack dense-matrix hook (matrix() always probes). Domain is DirectSum of domains; input is a tuple. |
| `direct_sum.RowLinearOperator.__init__` | Validates a non-empty list of operators sharing a common codomain and builds the direct-sum domain. | `RowLinearOperator.__init__(operators); RowOperator.__init__ for the dispatch path` | Common-codomain check kept ('Block {i} has codomain ..., expected ...'). Empty check only in RowOperator.__init__ ('A row operator needs at least one block.'); RowLinearOperator([]) directly, or RowOperator([]) (dispatches to the linear class), raises IndexError at self._operators[0] instead of v1's ValueError. Operators stored as a tuple. |
| `direct_sum.RowLinearOperator._mapping` | Matrix-free forward action: starts from codomain.zero and accumulates op(x_i) via codomain.axpy(1.0, ...). | `RowOperator._value(x) via _accumulate` | Same sum of op(x_i), but _Zero blocks are skipped and accumulation starts from a copy of the first image rather than codomain.zero(). |
| `direct_sum.RowLinearOperator._adjoint_mapping` | Matrix-free adjoint action: [op.adjoint(y) for op in operators]. | `RowLinearOperator._adjoint_value(y); _make_adjoint returns ColumnLinearOperator` | Same tuple(op.adjoint(y)) action (tuple not list); op.adjoint is now a ColumnLinearOperator of the adjoints, linked back. |
| `direct_sum.BlockDiagonalLinearOperator` | A square block operator between direct sums whose off-diagonal blocks are zero: maps [x_1, ..., x_n] to [A_1(x_1), ..., A_n(x_n)]. | `BlockDiagonalLinearOperator (subclass of new nonlinear BlockDiagonalOperator and LinearOperator); BlockDiagonalOperator([...]) dispatches to it` | Now under a nonlinear BlockDiagonalOperator base. Adds: traits = intersection of the blocks' traits (self-adjoint/PSD/PD iff every block is), structured adjoint (block diagonal of adjoints, linked), _known_matrix/_known_diagonals hooks, apply_block/_adjoint_apply_block passing blocks of vectors to each sub-operator's own fast path, `operators` property. Loses: row_dim/col_dim/block(i, j) (off-diagonal zero blocks are no longer synthesised for the user), and unconditional blockwise dense assembly (only when every diagonal block knows its matrix). BlockDiagonalOperator path now rejects an empty list. |
| `direct_sum.BlockDiagonalLinearOperator.__init__` | Stores the diagonal operators and builds direct-sum domain and codomain. | `BlockDiagonalLinearOperator.__init__(operators); BlockDiagonalOperator.__init__ for the dispatch path` | v1 did no validation and accepted an empty list. v2: BlockDiagonalOperator.__init__ raises ValueError('A block diagonal operator needs at least one block.') on empty; BlockDiagonalLinearOperator.__init__ (reached directly, or via BlockDiagonalOperator([]) dispatch) raises IndexError at self._operators[0].traits on empty. Computes closed intersection of traits. Operators stored as a tuple; still no domain/codomain consistency needed. |
| `direct_sum.BlockDiagonalLinearOperator._mapping` | Matrix-free forward action: [op(x) for op, x in zip(operators, xs)] — only n applications, never touching off-diagonal zero blocks. | `BlockDiagonalOperator._value(x)` | tuple(op(x_i)) — n applications, off-diagonals untouched, identical apart from returning a tuple rather than a list (the same return-type change classified as ported_changed elsewhere in this unit). |
| `direct_sum.BlockDiagonalLinearOperator._adjoint_mapping` | Matrix-free adjoint action: [op.adjoint(y) for op, y in zip(operators, ys)]. | `BlockDiagonalLinearOperator._adjoint_value(y); _make_adjoint returns a BlockDiagonalLinearOperator of adjoints` | Same tuple(op.adjoint(y_i)) action; additionally op.adjoint is a structured BlockDiagonalLinearOperator linked back (or op itself when the intersected traits include SELF_ADJOINT). |
| `direct_sum.BlockDiagonalLinearOperator._compute_dense_matrix` | Override of the dense-matrix hook: assembles the diagonal operators' dense matrices with scipy.linalg.block_diag. | `BlockDiagonalLinearOperator._known_matrix(form) -> _known_block_matrix over a synthesised grid with _Zero off-diagonals` | scipy.linalg.block_diag replaced by np.block over a full grid whose off-diagonal entries are _Zero nodes (each contributing np.zeros). Assembly fires only when both sides are CoordinateSpaces and every diagonal block knows its matrix; otherwise the whole operator is probed by LinearOperator.matrix() (each basis vector of the sum applies every diagonal block, including to the zero components of the other summands). v1 always assembled blockwise and forwarded galerkin/parallel/n_jobs to each block. As for BlockLinearOperator, Galerkin-stored blocks are asked for 'components' and converted back (two metric passes). Also adds _known_diagonals for the main diagonal (Jacobi) without forming the matrix. |

### linear_solvers — `linear_solvers.py`

| v1 | what it did | v2 | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| `linear_solvers.LinearSolver` | Empty abstract marker base class for every solver in the module; used as the type of the `preconditioning_method` argument accepted by the iterative solvers. | `pygeoinf2.numerics.solvers.LinearSolver` | No longer an empty marker. It now carries ClassVars `requires: Traits` and `requires_coordinates: bool`, a concrete `__call__` that runs `_validate` (dim equality, domain == codomain identity, trait superset, coordinates) and then the abstract `_invert`, and returns an `InverseOperator` rather than a plain LinearOperator. Consequence for the v1 role 'type of preconditioning_method': `LeastSquaresSolver`/`LSQRSolver` are siblings, not subclasses (solvers.py:1372), so LSQR can no longer be handed in as a preconditioner or to `resolve_solver`. |
| `linear_solvers.DirectLinearSolver` | Abstract base for factorisation-based solvers. Stores the galerkin / parallel / n_jobs options and provides the shared helper that turns array-level solve callables into a LinearOperator representing the inverse. | `pygeoinf2.numerics.solvers.DirectSolver` | Renamed DirectSolver. Constructor is `__init__(*, n_jobs: int \| None = None)`: the `galerkin` flag is gone (replaced by a per-class ClassVar `form`, fixed to 'components' for LU and 'galerkin' for Cholesky/Eigen) and the `parallel` flag is gone (folded into n_jobs; None/1 = serial, v1 default was parallel=False, n_jobs=-1). `requires_coordinates = True`. Inherits `_validate`, so it now also refuses operators whose domain and codomain are different spaces of equal dimension. |
| `linear_solvers.DirectLinearSolver.dense_matrix_formation` | Every direct solver (LU, Cholesky, Eigen) always forms the full dense matrix of the operator before factorising; this is the module's deliberate dense path. | `DirectSolver._invert -> operator.matrix(form=self.form, n_jobs=self._n_jobs)` | Still forms the full dense ndarray once and factorises once. Differences: `form` is fixed per class rather than chosen by `galerkin=`; `parallel` flag gone (n_jobs alone, serial by default where v1 with parallel=True used joblib with n_jobs=-1); `matrix()` now takes `by='auto'` choosing rows (adjoint probes) when codomain is smaller. IMPROVED, but narrower than first stated: v1's `MatrixLinearOperator._compute_dense_matrix` already returned the stored `_matrix` when `galerkin == self.is_galerkin and self.is_dense` (linear_operators.py:1106-1115), so a matrix-backed operator in the matching form was read in v1 too. v2's `_known_matrix` (operators.py:733-737) additionally converts between forms (from_matrix :1773 via `_in_form`; from_columns :1588-1593) and propagates through sum/composition/adjoint/diagonal/direct-sum nodes (nodes.py:71, :180, :270, :365, :494; diagonal.py:298; direct_sum.py:598, :839), where v1 fell back to column probing. |
| `linear_solvers.LUSolver` | Direct solver based on scipy.linalg.lu_factor / lu_solve of the operator's dense matrix representation; works for general (non-symmetric) square operators. | `pygeoinf2.numerics.solvers.LUSolver` | Constructor now `LUSolver(*, n_jobs=None)` — `galerkin` and `parallel` kwargs removed; form fixed to 'components'. Generality narrowed: v1 `assert operator.is_square` accepted any operator between two spaces of equal dimension; v2 `_validate` raises ValueError when `operator.domain != operator.codomain` even if dims match (solvers.py:117-129), so LU between distinct same-dimension spaces is refused (pinned by tests/test_solvers.py:801-818). |
| `linear_solvers.LUSolver.__call__` | Forms the dense (Galerkin or standard) matrix, LU-factorises it with `lu_factor(matrix, overwrite_a=True)`, and returns the inverse operator whose forward action is `lu_solve(factor, c, 0)` and whose adjoint action is `lu_solve(factor, c, 1)` (transposed solve). | `LUSolver._factorise via LinearSolver.__call__` | `lu_factor(matrix)` without `overwrite_a=True` (one extra dense copy); forward `lu_solve(factor, c)`, adjoint `lu_solve(factor, c, trans=1)` retained so no second factorisation (verified by tests/test_solvers.py:417-450). Adjoint now applies the metric corrections G_X / G_Y^-1 around the transposed solve (solvers.py:492-507). Returns InverseOperator; `solve()` returns SolveResult(iterations=0, residual 0.0, converged True). |
| `linear_solvers.CholeskySolver` | Direct solver for symmetric positive-definite operators using scipy.linalg.cho_factor / cho_solve on the dense matrix. | `pygeoinf2.numerics.solvers.CholeskySolver` | Constructor lost `galerkin`, `parallel` and `check_finite` (grep 'check_finite' in pygeoinf2: no hits). Form fixed to 'galerkin'. New precondition: `requires = Traits.POSITIVE_DEFINITE` — an operator that does not *claim* the trait is refused with ValueError (v1 factorised anything square and let LAPACK complain). The matrix is symmetrised `0.5*(M+M.T)` before `cho_factor`. |
| `linear_solvers.CholeskySolver.__call__` | Forms the dense matrix, computes `cho_factor(matrix, overwrite_a=False, check_finite=self._check_finite)`, and returns an inverse operator applying `cho_solve(factor, c, check_finite=...)`. | `CholeskySolver._factorise via LinearSolver.__call__` | Same `cho_factor`/`cho_solve` on the dense Galerkin matrix; `check_finite` no longer passed (SciPy default True, so per-solve validation cannot be disabled). Adjoint: `apply_transposed=None`, `components_adjoint_action = components_action` because SELF_ADJOINT (solvers.py:509-511); since the inverse inherits SELF_ADJOINT, `inverse.adjoint is inverse` (operators.py:592-593), so no refactorisation. |
| `linear_solvers.EigenSolver` | Direct solver based on the symmetric eigendecomposition (scipy.linalg.eigh) of the dense matrix; yields a pseudo-inverse that zeroes eigenvalues below a relative threshold. | `pygeoinf2.numerics.solvers.EigenSolver` | Constructor `EigenSolver(*, rtol=1e-12, n_jobs=None)`: `galerkin` and `parallel` gone, form fixed to 'galerkin'. New precondition `requires = Traits.SELF_ADJOINT` (trait claim mandatory). Matrix symmetrised before `eigh`. |
| `linear_solvers.EigenSolver.__call__` | Forms the dense matrix, computes eigenvalues/eigenvectors with `eigh`, inverts eigenvalues whose magnitude exceeds `rtol * max\|lambda\|` (others set to 0), and returns an inverse operator applying V diag(1/lambda) V^T. | `EigenSolver._factorise` | Same eigh + thresholded reciprocal + V diag V^T apply; `apply` also accepts a matrix of columns (for `known_matrix`). Operates on the Galerkin matrix with RHS premultiplied by G_Y (solvers.py:466-468) — equivalent to v1 galerkin=True branch; v1's default galerkin=False path (eigh of the components matrix, only symmetric on an orthonormal space) is not available. |
| `linear_solvers.IterativeLinearSolver` | Abstract base for iterative solvers. Holds an optional `preconditioning_method` (a LinearSolver used to manufacture a preconditioner from the operator at call time) and an iteration counter, and implements the generic __call__ that turns a solver into an inverse LinearOperator. | `pygeoinf2.numerics.solvers.IterativeSolver` | Renamed IterativeSolver. Constructor `(*, rtol=1e-8, atol=0.0, maxiter=None, preconditioner: LinearSolver\|LinearOperator\|None=None, strict=True, callback=None)`: `preconditioning_method` -> `preconditioner`, which now also accepts a ready LinearOperator; rtol/atol/maxiter/callback moved from the subclasses into the base; new `strict` (raise ConvergenceError on non-convergence). Stateless: no `_iterations` counter. New methods `with_preconditioner` (refuses to replace an existing one), `preconditioner` property, `resolved_for`. Subclasses implement `_solve(operator, preconditioner, b, x0) -> SolveResult`. On a CoordinateSpace with `uses_component_fast_paths` the loop runs on component arrays through `ComponentView` (solvers.py:865-888). |
| `linear_solvers.IterativeLinearSolver.solve_linear_system` | Abstract: solve A x = y for x given an optional preconditioner and optional initial guess, returning the solution Vector. | `InverseOperator.solve(y, /, *, x0=None) -> SolveResult (backed by IterativeSolver._solve)` | The user entry point is now `solver(A).solve(y, x0=x0)`; the preconditioner is no longer a per-call positional argument (it lives on the solver); returns a `SolveResult(solution, iterations, residual_norm, converged, history)` instead of the bare Vector; raises ConvergenceError (strict) or warns on non-convergence via `_finish`. Initial guess x0 is supported on this path (tests/test_solvers.py:258-263). |
| `linear_solvers.IterativeLinearSolver.iterations` | Number of iterations performed by the most recent solve; zero if the solver has not been called yet. | `SolveResult.iterations (and ProgressCallback.iterations)` | Moved off the solver onto the per-solve result: `solver(A).solve(y).iterations`. Semantics made uniform: 0 when converged at the initial residual, k when converged at step k, maxiter on exhaustion (v1's per-solver off-by-one quirks and FCG's 'always 1' bug are gone). DESIGN.md:1274 names it `inverse.last_solve.iterations`, which does not exist — `solve()` is the actual API. |
| `linear_solvers.IterativeLinearSolver.solve_adjoint_linear_system` | Solves the adjoint system A* y = x by delegating to `solve_linear_system(operator.adjoint, adjoint_preconditioner, x, y0)`. | `solver(A).adjoint.solve(x, x0=y0)  (InverseOperator._make_adjoint -> self._solver(A.adjoint))` | Write `inv = solver(A); inv.adjoint.solve(x, x0=y0)` (or `inv.adjoint_inverse(x)` for the bare vector). For an iterative inverse `_adjoint_solve_fn` is None, so `_make_adjoint` falls through to `self._solver(self._operator.adjoint)` (solvers.py:354) — the same delegation to the solver on A* as v1. Both preconditioner branches differ from v1, though. (1) Fixed LinearOperator P: `_resolve_preconditioner(A*)` returns P unchanged (:798-800), whereas v1 used `P.adjoint` (linear_solvers.py:311-313); for a non-self-adjoint fixed P the adjoint solve is wrongly preconditioned (Review B confirmed `inv.adjoint.solver._resolve_preconditioner(B.adjoint) is P`). (2) Deferred LinearSolver preconditioner (e.g. LUSolver): it is rebuilt from A* (:793-797, :835), which for a direct method is a second dense extraction and O(n^3) factorisation — Review B measured 2 `_factorise` calls for `BiCGStabSolver(preconditioner=LUSolver())(B).adjoint`. v1 took `_preconditioner.adjoint` of the already-built LU inverse, i.e. `lu_solve(trans=1)` with no refactorisation (linear_solvers.py:311-313, :122-128). The rebuild is mathematically correct, so this branch is a cost regression not a correctness one. Only for SELF_ADJOINT operators (where `adjoint` returns self, operators.py:592-593) is either issue avoided. |
| `linear_solvers.IterativeLinearSolver.__call__` | Returns a LinearOperator(codomain -> domain) whose mapping is `solve_linear_system(operator, P, y, None)` and whose adjoint_mapping is `solve_adjoint_linear_system(operator, P.adjoint, x, None)`; the solve is deferred until the returned operator is applied. | `LinearSolver.__call__ -> IterativeSolver._invert` | Signature `__call__(operator)` — the `preconditioner=` kwarg is gone (use constructor or `with_preconditioner`). `assert operator.is_automorphism` replaced by `_validate` raising ValueError for dim mismatch, distinct spaces, or missing required traits. Returns `InverseOperator` whose application runs `_solve` with x0=None and whose adjoint is built lazily by `_make_adjoint`. Preconditioner still resolved once at call time (solvers.py:835) and captured. The typo variable is gone. |
| `linear_solvers.IterativeLinearSolver.preconditioner_precedence` | A preconditioner can be supplied either as a ready LinearOperator (per call) or as a `preconditioning_method` solver (per solver instance) that is applied to the operator to build the preconditioner when __call__ is invoked; explicit always wins. | `IterativeSolver(preconditioner=...), with_preconditioner, resolved_for, resolve_solver` | Per-call override is gone: there is one slot, `preconditioner`, accepting either a LinearSolver (deferred, applied to the operator at __call__) or a LinearOperator (used as-is). `with_preconditioner` raises ValueError if one is already set rather than overriding (solvers.py:753-759; v1 explicit-wins rule has no equivalent). New: `resolved_for(operator)` freezes a deferred preconditioner; module-level `resolve_solver(solver_or_factory, operator, default=)` lets a callable build the solver from the operator. Nested solvers still work (any IterativeSolver is a LinearSolver; catalogue row 152 says pass `IterativeSolver(strict=False)`). |
| `linear_solvers.CGSolver` | Pure matrix-free preconditioned Conjugate Gradient on abstract Hilbert-space vectors for self-adjoint positive-definite automorphisms; never forms a matrix. | `pygeoinf2.numerics.solvers.CGSolver` | Defaults changed: rtol 1e-5 -> 1e-8; maxiter None -> max(2*dim, 20) instead of 10*dim; atol 0.0 unchanged. `preconditioning_method` -> `preconditioner` (LinearSolver or LinearOperator). `callback` signature changed from `callback(x)` to `callback(iteration, residual_norm)` — the iterate is no longer passed. New `strict=True` raises ConvergenceError on exhaustion (v1 returned silently). New precondition `requires = Traits.POSITIVE_DEFINITE` — operators without the trait claim are refused (tests/test_solvers.py:107-113). |
| `linear_solvers.CGSolver.solve_linear_system` | Standard PCG recurrence using only `domain.zero/copy/subtract/inner_product/squared_norm/axpy/ax` and operator/preconditioner applications; returns the solution vector and sets `iterations`. | `CGSolver._solve (via InverseOperator.solve)` | Same PCG recurrence (1 operator, 1 preconditioner application, 2 inner products + 1 norm per step; `axpy`/`scale_inplace`). Convergence test `norm(r) <= max(rtol*\|\|b\|\|, atol)` on the unpreconditioned residual — equivalent to v1's squared form. Skips the `A(0)` application when x0 is None (:903-909). The initial residual is recorded as iteration 0 and a zero/small RHS returns immediately with converged=True. Returns SolveResult. On coordinate spaces the loop runs on component arrays (ComponentView) with the same metric. |
| `linear_solvers.CGSolver.breakdown_detection` | CGSolver checks every recurrence scalar: non-finite or non-positive <r,z> (initially), non-finite or non-positive <p,Ap>, non-finite alpha, non-finite or negative <r,z> (after an iteration), non-finite beta — each raises FloatingPointError with a diagnostic message naming the likely cause (operator or preconditioner not positive definite / rescale). | `CGSolver._solve curvature check` | Only `<p, Ap> <= 0` is checked, raising ConvergenceError (not FloatingPointError) with a message pointing at `testing.check_traits()`. v1's additional checks — non-finite <r,z>, non-positive initial <r,z>, negative in-loop <r,z>, non-finite alpha and beta — are gone; a NaN from an ill-posed preconditioner propagates until the residual test fails or maxiter is hit. |
| `linear_solvers.CGSolver.callback_protocol` | If a callback was given at construction, CGSolver duck-types `reset`/`finalize` hooks around the solve and calls the callback with the live solution vector `x` after each completed iteration (not on the iteration in which convergence is detected). | `IterativeSolver._record -> callback(iteration, residual_norm)` | Callback now receives `(iteration, residual_norm)` rather than the live solution vector; invoked at iteration 0 (initial residual) and after every step including the one on which convergence is detected. No duck-typed `reset()`/`finalize()` hooks (grep 'finalize' in pygeoinf2: none); `ProgressCallback` resets itself when it sees iteration 0. |
| `linear_solvers.MinResSolver` | Matrix-free MINRES (Lanczos-based residual minimisation) on Hilbert-space vectors for symmetric, possibly indefinite or singular systems, with optional symmetric positive-definite preconditioning. | `pygeoinf2.numerics.solvers.MinResSolver` | Defaults changed: rtol 1e-5 -> 1e-8, atol 1e-8 -> 0.0, maxiter 10*dim -> max(2*dim, 20). `preconditioning_method` -> `preconditioner`. New `requires = Traits.SELF_ADJOINT` (trait claim mandatory), `strict`, and callback/history support (v1 had none). SPD preconditioning retained (the earlier review's 'preconditioning lost' finding is no longer true: solvers.py:1174-1295, tests/test_solvers.py:531-630). |
| `linear_solvers.MinResSolver.solve_linear_system` | Runs the preconditioned Lanczos/MINRES recurrence (Givens rotations on the tridiagonal system) using domain.inner_product/norm/axpy/ax/multiply/copy; returns x and sets iterations. | `MinResSolver._solve` | Same Paige-Saunders Lanczos/Givens recurrence in the M-inner product with one operator and one preconditioner application per step. Stopping: `\|phi_bar\| <= max(rtol * \|\|b\|\|_M, atol)` — relative to the M-norm of b rather than v1's beta1 (the initial residual's M-norm; identical for x0=None, differs for a warm start). The `gamma` floor of 1e-15 is replaced by `gamma == 0 -> return converged`; `beta_next == 0` also returns converged. Non-PD preconditioner still raises ValueError (:1205-1210). Residual history recorded each step; returns SolveResult. |
| `linear_solvers.BICGStabSolver` | Matrix-free BiCGStab on Hilbert-space vectors for non-symmetric automorphisms, with right preconditioning. | `pygeoinf2.numerics.solvers.BiCGStabSolver` | Renamed BiCGStabSolver (capitalisation). Defaults changed: rtol 1e-5 -> 1e-8, atol 1e-8 -> 0.0, maxiter 10*dim -> max(2*dim, 20). `preconditioning_method` -> `preconditioner`. New `strict` and callback/history. `requires = Traits.NONE` (no trait claim needed). |
| `linear_solvers.BICGStabSolver.solve_linear_system` | Standard BiCGStab recurrence with shadow residual r_hat = r0, right-preconditioned (phat = P(p), shat = P(r)); two operator applications and two preconditioner applications per iteration. | `BiCGStabSolver._solve` | Same right-preconditioned BiCGStab recurrence (y = P(p), z = P(s); 2 operator + 2 preconditioner applications per step). Tolerance `max(rtol*\|\|b\|\|, atol)`, tested on the half-step `s` and on `r`, as v1. Differences: zero-RHS shortcut is via the residual test at iteration 0; `omega = 0` when `<t,t> == 0` rather than dividing; returns SolveResult with history; runs on components when coordinates exist. |
| `linear_solvers.BICGStabSolver.breakdown_handling` | On any of the three classic BiCGStab breakdown conditions the solver breaks out of the loop, records iterations=k, and returns the current iterate without raising. | `BiCGStabSolver._solve early returns with converged=False` | Breakdown (`rho == 0`, `omega == 0`, `<r0, v> == 0`) now returns `SolveResult(..., converged=False)`, which `_finish` turns into a ConvergenceError under `strict=True` (default) or a RuntimeWarning under strict=False — instead of v1's silent return of the current iterate. Tests are exact equality with zero rather than v1's `abs(.) < 1e-16`. The error message says 'did not converge', not 'breakdown'. |
| `linear_solvers.LSQRSolver` | Matrix-free LSQR (Golub-Kahan bidiagonalisation) for least-squares problems min \|\|A x - y\|\|^2 + damping^2 \|\|x\|\|^2 on possibly rectangular operators, using operator.adjoint. | `pygeoinf2.numerics.solvers.LSQRSolver (a LeastSquaresSolver)` | Now a subclass of the sibling ABC `LeastSquaresSolver`, not of LinearSolver/IterativeSolver — so it cannot be passed as a `preconditioner=` or to `resolve_solver`. Constructor `(*, damping=0.0, rtol=1e-10, maxiter=None, strict=True, callback=None)`: `damping` moved from the per-solve call to the constructor (validated non-negative); `atol` removed; rtol default 1e-5 -> 1e-10; maxiter default 2*max(dim_X, dim_Y) -> 4*dim_X. Callback/history added, but with two differences from the IterativeSolver family: `strict=False` neither raises nor warns (LSQRSolver._invert only raises under strict, solvers.py:1439-1445; no `warnings.warn`, unlike `IterativeSolver._finish` :820-832), so a non-strict LSQR non-convergence is as silent as v1's; and the callback/history never receive an iteration-0 record (:1519-1560), which breaks the ProgressCallback auto-reset convention the rest of the module relies on. |
| `linear_solvers.LSQRSolver.solve_linear_system` | Runs the LSQR recurrence with optional Tikhonov damping, using codomain.norm/ax/axpy/subtract and domain.norm/ax/axpy/copy plus one operator and one adjoint application per iteration; returns the least-squares solution. | `LSQRSolver._solve via InverseOperator.solve(b, x0=)` | Same Golub-Kahan recurrence with one operator and one adjoint application per step, damping as an extra rotation. Stopping changed: `normal_residual <= rtol*alpha0*beta0` or `\|phi_bar\| <= rtol*\|\|b\|\|` (both relative; no `atol`); v1 tested `sqrt(phibar^2 + sum psi^2) <= atol + rtol*\|\|y\|\|` or `arnorm <= atol`. The damped-residual accumulation (`res2 += psi**2`) is dropped, so the residual test uses \|phi_bar\| alone. Warm start: supported and tolerances are taken relative to the data (`\|\|b\|\|`, `\|\|A* b\|\|`) rather than the shifted residual (:1507-1512); a warm start *with* damping raises ValueError (:1473-1479) where v1 silently penalised the correction. `residual_norm` in the result is the normal residual \|\|A* r\|\|, and history records it. |
| `linear_solvers.LSQRSolver.rectangular_and_damping` | LSQRSolver genuinely supports domain != codomain and damped least squares, but only when `solve_linear_system` is invoked directly; the inherited `__call__` asserts `operator.is_automorphism` and never passes `damping`, so the operator-inverse form is limited to square automorphisms with damping=0. | `LeastSquaresSolver.__call__ -> InverseOperator with traits=NONE` | IMPROVED: `LSQRSolver(damping=d)(A)` works on rectangular A through `__call__` (no squareness check, solvers.py:1384-1388) and returns a pseudo-inverse InverseOperator whose adjoint is LSQR on A* (:354). Damping is per-solver, not per-solve. Restriction added: damping > 0 with x0 is refused. |
| `linear_solvers.FCGSolver` | Matrix-free Flexible Conjugate Gradient, designed for variable (e.g. inner-iterative) preconditioners: the beta coefficient is computed as -<z_new, Ap>/<p, Ap> instead of the standard Fletcher-Reeves ratio. | `pygeoinf2.numerics.solvers.FlexibleCGSolver` | Renamed FlexibleCGSolver, exported from numerics and the package root. Defaults changed: rtol 1e-5 -> 1e-8, atol 1e-8 -> 0.0, maxiter 2*dim -> max(2*dim, 20). `preconditioning_method` -> `preconditioner`. New `requires = Traits.POSITIVE_DEFINITE`, `strict`, callback/history, curvature breakdown check (v1 had none). The `iterations`-reports-1 bug is gone. |
| `linear_solvers.FCGSolver.solve_linear_system` | Runs FCG: z = P(r), p = z, then per iteration alpha = <r,z>/<p,Ap>, x += alpha p, r -= alpha Ap, convergence check, z_new = P(r), beta = -<z_new,Ap>/<p,Ap>, p = z_new + beta p. | `FlexibleCGSolver._solve` | The flexible beta is a different formula: v1 uses `beta = -<z_new, Ap>/<p, Ap>` (Notay's FCG, orthogonalising the new direction against Ap); v2 uses Polak-Ribiere `beta = <r_new - r_old, z_new>/<r_old, z_old>` (solvers.py:1039-1041). Both handle a variable preconditioner but are not the same iteration. v2 costs one extra copy (`previous = copy(r)`) and one `subtract` per step. Identity-operator substitution for a missing preconditioner replaced by using r directly. Convergence `norm(r) <= max(rtol*\|\|b\|\|, atol)` vs v1 `< atol + rtol*\|\|y\|\|`. |
| `linear_solvers.ProgressCallback` | Simple solver callback that prints a running iteration count to the console (carriage-return overwrite) and implements the reset/finalize protocol recognised by CGSolver and ScipyIterativeSolver. | `pygeoinf2.numerics.solvers.ProgressCallback` | Constructor `ProgressCallback(*, report: Callable[[str], None] \| None = None)` — nothing is printed unless `report` (e.g. `print`) is given; the `message` prefix is gone and the line format is fixed 'iteration {i}: residual {r:.6g}'. `__call__(iteration, residual)` instead of `__call__(xk)`. Records `residuals: list[float]`; exposes `iterations` and `residual` properties. Resets itself when it sees iteration 0 (no `reset()`/`finalize()` methods). Works with every iterative solver, not only CG and the SciPy wrapper. |
| `linear_solvers.ProgressCallback.iteration` | Count of callback invocations since the last reset. | `ProgressCallback.iterations (property)` | Renamed `iterations`; now a read-only property computed as `max(len(residuals) - 1, 0)` (excludes the iteration-0 record) rather than a mutable counter attribute. The formula assumes an iteration-0 entry, which LSQRSolver never supplies (solvers.py:1519-1560), so for LSQR `progress.iterations` under-reports by one relative to `SolveResult.iterations` (Review B measured 6 vs 5) and, because no reset fires, over-reports on reuse. v1's `iteration` attribute counted callback invocations exactly for every solver that called it. |
| `linear_solvers.ProgressCallback.reset` | Resets `iteration` to 0 for a new solve. | `ProgressCallback.__call__ when iteration == 0 (does not fire for LSQRSolver)` | No `reset()` method; the callback clears `residuals` itself when a solver reports iteration 0, which the IterativeSolver subclasses all do (`_record(0, ...)` at solvers.py:939, :1009, :1092, :1222, :1314), so reuse across CG/FCG/GMRES/MINRES/BiCGStab solves is automatic (tests/test_solvers.py:480-494). LSQRSolver never reports iteration 0: its `_note` is called only inside the loop that starts at iteration 1 (:1519, :1554), so a ProgressCallback reused across LSQR solves accumulates (Review B measured len(residuals) 6 then 12 on two solves of a 6x6 system) and there is no explicit `reset()` for the user to call instead. v1's `reset()` was callable for every solver. |
| `linear_solvers.ProgressCallback.__call__` | Increments `iteration` and prints `f'{message}{iteration}'` with end='\r'. | `ProgressCallback.__call__(iteration, residual)` | Signature `(iteration: int, residual: float)` instead of `(xk)`; appends the residual to `residuals`, resets on iteration 0, and calls `report(line)` only if one was given (no unconditional print). |
| `linear_solvers.ResidualTrackingCallback` | Callback that computes the exact residual norm \|\|y - A(x)\|\| in the codomain norm at every iteration and records it in `residuals`; costs one extra forward-operator application per iteration. | `ProgressCallback.residuals / SolveResult.history` | Residual tracking is built in: every iterative solver records a residual per step, available as `ProgressCallback.residuals` live or `SolveResult.history` afterwards, at no extra operator application. What changed: it is the solver's *recurrence* residual in the space norm (CG/BiCGStab: \|\|r\|\|; MINRES: \|phi_bar\| in the M-norm; GMRES: preconditioned residual when preconditioned; LSQR: the normal residual \|\|A* r\|\|), not v1's exactly recomputed \|\|y - A x\|\| — and an exact recompute cannot be written by the user because the callback never receives x. No `custom_message` format; no `operator`/`y` needed. |
| `linear_solvers.ResidualTrackingCallback.residuals` | List of exact residual norms, one per callback invocation. | `ProgressCallback.residuals (list[float]); SolveResult.history (tuple[float, ...])` | Same shape for the IterativeSolver subclasses (one float per step plus an iteration-0 entry), but the value is the solver's recurrence residual (see previous row), and the list is cleared automatically at the start of each solve rather than accumulating across solves. LSQRSolver is the exception: its history has no iteration-0 entry (`_note` called only from iteration 1, solvers.py:1554) and, since the auto-reset keys on iteration 0, the ProgressCallback list is not cleared between LSQR solves. |
| `linear_solvers.ResidualTrackingCallback.__call__` | Increments `iteration`; converts xk to a domain Vector if it is a numpy array (via `operator.domain.from_components`), otherwise uses it directly; computes r = y - A(x), appends \|\|r\|\| to `residuals`, and prints the formatted message if `print_progress`. | `ProgressCallback.__call__(iteration, residual)` | Receives the residual from the solver rather than computing it from xk; no ndarray-vs-Vector branch, no extra forward application, no formatted print unless `report` given. |
| `linear_solvers.callback_hook_protocol` | Solvers that support callbacks (CGSolver via constructor `callback`, ScipyIterativeSolver via kwargs `callback`) invoke optional `reset()` before and `finalize()` after each solve, so stateful callback objects can be reused across solves; plain functions work too. | `IterativeSolver(callback=...), LSQRSolver(callback=...)` | IMPROVED coverage: CG, FlexibleCG, GMRES, MINRES, BiCGStab and LSQR all honour `callback` (verified by tests/test_solvers.py:265-298). LOST: the duck-typed `reset()`/`finalize()` hooks — a stateful callback must reset itself on iteration 0 as `ProgressCallback` does; plain functions still work. That convention does not hold for LSQRSolver, which never reports iteration 0 (solvers.py:1519-1560), so for LSQR there is no per-solve boundary signal at all. Signature `(iteration, residual)` rather than `(x)`. Inconsistency between the two callback-bearing families: `LSQRSolver(strict=False)` returns an unconverged SolveResult silently (its `_invert` only raises under strict, no `warnings.warn`, :1437-1447), whereas `IterativeSolver._finish` warns with RuntimeWarning (:820-832). |
| `linear_solvers.matrix_free_vs_matrix_backed` | Three tiers of representation: the pure Hilbert-space solvers touch only operator/preconditioner applications and HilbertSpace vector primitives (zero, copy, add, subtract, multiply, axpy, ax, inner_product, norm, squared_norm, identity_operator); ScipyIterativeSolver works on component arrays through the operator's (non-dense) matrix representation; the direct solvers always build a dense ndarray. | `IterativeSolver (coordinate-free, ComponentView fast path) / DirectSolver (dense)` | Two tiers instead of three: the SciPy matrix-representation tier is gone. Iterative solvers are written against `inner_product`/`norm`/`axpy`/`scale_inplace`/`scale`/`copy`/`subtract`/`zero` and run unchanged on a space without a component map (tests/test_solvers.py:148-189). On a CoordinateSpace with `uses_component_fast_paths` they run on component arrays through `ComponentView` (same metric) and an operator offering `_components_action` stays in components; otherwise from_components/to_components per application (solvers.py:607-651, :865-888). Direct solvers still form the dense matrix via `matrix(form, n_jobs)`, with the `_known_matrix` read short-circuit. |
| `linear_solvers.maxiter_defaults` | Each matrix-free solver derives a dimension-based iteration cap when none is given; the caps are inconsistent across solvers. | `IterativeSolver._limit; LSQRSolver._solve` | Unified for every IterativeSolver (CG, FlexibleCG, GMRES, MINRES, BiCGStab): `max(2*domain.dim, 20)` replaces 10*dim (CG/MinRes/BiCGStab) and 2*dim (FCG). LSQR: `4*max(domain.dim, 1)` replaces `2*max(domain.dim, codomain.dim)`. On exhaustion every solver now raises ConvergenceError (strict=True default) or warns (strict=False) instead of silently returning the iterate. `IterativeSolver.__init__` docstring at :707-709 now matches `_limit`. |
| `linear_solvers.tolerance_defaults` | All matrix-free solvers default to rtol=1e-5; atol defaults to 0.0 for CGSolver and 1e-8 elsewhere; the way atol and rtol combine (max versus sum) and the quantity tested (true residual, recurrence estimate, or preconditioned estimate) differ per solver. | `IterativeSolver.__init__ / _tolerance; LSQRSolver.__init__` | Unified for IterativeSolvers: rtol=1e-8 (was 1e-5 everywhere), atol=0.0 (was 1e-8 except CG), combined as `max(rtol*\|\|b\|\|, atol)` in the space norm (v1 FCG/LSQR used the sum). MINRES measures relative to the M-norm of b. GMRES with a preconditioner measures the preconditioned residual relative to \|\|P b\|\|. LSQR: rtol=1e-10, no atol, tested on both the normal residual and \|phi_bar\|. Docstring :696-705 documents why 1e-8 was chosen over v1's 1e-5. |

### preconditioners — `preconditioners.py`

| v1 | what it did | v2 | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| `preconditioners.JacobiPreconditioningMethod` | LinearSolver wrapper producing a Jacobi (inverse-diagonal) preconditioner from either a stochastic (Hutchinson-type) or an exact extraction of the operator's Galerkin diagonal. | `pygeoinf2.numerics.preconditioners.JacobiPreconditioner` | Signature now keyword-only: JacobiPreconditioner(*, floor=1e-14, samples=None, rng=None, n_jobs=None). Changes: (1) num_samples -> samples, DEFAULT FLIPPED from 20 (stochastic) to None (exact: one operator application per component unless the operator can report its diagonal); (2) v1's method='variable'/'fixed', rtol=1e-2, block_size=10 are GONE — the estimate is a fixed sample count, the adaptive stopping is unreachable from this class even though numerics.randomised.random_diagonal supports rtol/max_samples/block_size; (3) parallel= gone, n_jobs kept (None = serial; v1 n_jobs=-1 with parallel=False); (4) new floor= and rng= kwargs; (5) validates samples >= 1 (ValueError); (6) GENERALITY LOSS, not merely stricter validation: requires the operator to CLAIM Traits.SELF_ADJOINT (requires = SELF_ADJOINT, enforced by LinearSolver._validate) and to have coordinates — v1 accepted any square operator with no trait system. Nothing in the computation needs the claim (operator.diagonals(form='galerkin') and random_diagonal(form='galerkin') accept any coordinate operator), yet v2 ships GMRESSolver (requires NONE) and BiCGStabSolver (inherits requires NONE) for non-symmetric systems and v1's Jacobi was the natural preconditioner for those; v2 therefore has NO Jacobi preconditioner for a non-symmetric Krylov solve unless the user lies with with_traits(SELF_ADJOINT). (7) Minor cost change: v1's random_diagonal capped the sample count at the dimension (num_samples = min(size_estimate, n)); v2's random_diagonal has no cap, so samples=n with n > dim costs n applications where the exact branch would cost dim. |
| `preconditioners.JacobiPreconditioningMethod.__call__` | Estimates or extracts the Galerkin diagonal of `operator`, inverts it elementwise, and returns a DiagonalSparseMatrixLinearOperator on domain -> domain built with galerkin=True. | `JacobiPreconditioner._invert` | Exact branch: operator.diagonals(offsets=(0,), form='galerkin', n_jobs) instead of operator.extract_diagonal(galerkin=True, parallel, n_jobs) — IMPROVED: diagonals() reads a known diagonal with zero applications for matrix-backed, diagonal, scaled, summed, adjoint and block-diagonal operators (_known_diagonals hooks), probing only when it must (v1 had a narrower fast path: only a dense MatrixLinearOperator whose stored form matched the requested galerkin flag, linear_operators.py:1129). Stochastic branch: random_diagonal(operator, samples=, form='galerkin', rng=, n_jobs=) with Rademacher probes, fixed count (v1: Gaussian probes by default, adaptive). Inversion floor now self._floor. Result: InverseOperator with solve_fn y -> from_components(inv_diag * apply_gram(to_components(y))), traits=SELF_ADJOINT. METRIC SEMANTICS CHANGED (an improvement): the component action is now D^-1 G, whereas v1's DiagonalSparseMatrixLinearOperator(..., galerkin=True) applied _mapping_galerkin, i.e. c -> D^-1 c -> codomain.dual.from_components -> codomain.from_dual = G^-1 D^-1 c. Since A_c = G^-1 M_A and so A_c^-1 = M_A^-1 G ~ D^-1 G, v2 is the correct approximation to the inverse and v1 was right only for an identity Gram; the two are NOT mathematically the same on a non-identity metric. No squareness check of its own (v1 used operator.domain twice); now inherited from _validate. Adjoint: because the result claims SELF_ADJOINT, .adjoint is the operator itself (operators.py:592). |
| `preconditioners.JacobiPreconditioningMethod.stochastic_vs_exact_diagonal` | num_samples not None (default 20) selects a randomized diagonal estimate via low_rank.random_diagonal on the matrix-free Galerkin SciPy operator; num_samples=None selects exact extraction via operator.extract_diagonal(galerkin=True). | `JacobiPreconditioner(samples=None \| int)` | Both branches survive but: default is now EXACT (samples=None) where v1 defaulted to 20 stochastic samples; the stochastic branch is a FIXED number of Rademacher probes — v1's default 'variable' method (progressive blocks of block_size=10 until relative change < rtol=1e-2, capped at dim) is not reachable from the class (no rtol/method/block_size kwargs are forwarded, though random_diagonal(rtol=, max_samples=, block_size=) exists). v1 also capped the sample count at dim; v2 does not. Both still use the Galerkin form. The exact branch can now be free (known diagonals) where v1's fast path covered only dense matrix operators in the matching form. |
| `preconditioners.JacobiPreconditioningMethod.diagonal_floor` | Diagonal entries with absolute value <= 1e-14 are replaced by an inverse of 1.0 rather than dividing by (near) zero. | `JacobiPreconditioner(floor=1e-14)` | Same semantics (entries with \|d\| <= floor are replaced so their inverse is 1.0 — safe = where(\|d\| > floor, d, 1.0); inverse = 1/safe) and same default 1e-14, but the threshold is now a public constructor kwarg `floor` instead of a hard-coded literal. |
| `preconditioners.SpectralPreconditioningMethod` | LinearSolver wrapper producing a spectral (low-rank) preconditioner: a randomized eigendecomposition inverts the dominant modes exactly and the unresolved tail is treated as a damped identity. | `pygeoinf2.numerics.preconditioners.SpectralPreconditioner` | Signature reduced to SpectralPreconditioner(*, rank=20, damping=None, rng=None). LOST kwargs: method ('variable'/'fixed' — v2 always calls random_eig with a fixed rank; the adaptive rank=None path of random_eig is unreachable because rank < 1 raises), max_rank, power (v2 inherits random_eig/random_range's default power=1 vs v1's 2), rtol, block_size, parallel, n_jobs (random_eig accepts n_jobs via **kwargs but the class does not forward it). ADDED: rng. Validates rank >= 1. Requires the operator to claim SELF_ADJOINT (random_eig also raises otherwise). MEANING OF `damping` CHANGED: v1 squared it (d_sq = damping**2, user passes the un-squared damping); v2 uses it directly as the tail eigenvalue, and raises if it is <= 0. |
| `preconditioners.SpectralPreconditioningMethod.__call__` | Computes LowRankEig.from_randomized(operator, rank, ...) and returns a matrix-free self-adjoint LinearOperator on space=operator.domain implementing r -> (1/d^2) * (r - U diag(s/(s+d^2)) U* r). | `SpectralPreconditioner._invert` | Different preconditioner. v1 returned the Woodbury inverse of (U S U* + d^2 I): r -> (1/d^2)(r - U diag(s/(s+d^2)) U* r), so resolved modes are inverted as 1/(s_i + d^2) — it ADDS the damping itself and its docstring says it expects the undamped misfit operator A*WA. v2 returns (1/d) I + U diag(1/lambda_i - 1/d) U*: resolved modes inverted EXACTLY as 1/lambda_i, unresolved tail as 1/d, with eigenvalues <= 0 treated as tail; it expects the full (already damped) operator, consistent with the rest of the module's convention (v1's own Jacobi comment 'the operator passed is already damped'). Passing the same (damped) operator to both gives different results; v1's form double-damps. Still matrix-free (two low-rank products per application: factor.adjoint then factor), still declared self-adjoint (traits=SELF_ADJOINT instead of adjoint_mapping=mapping). Eigen-decomposition via random_eig(operator, rank=, rng=) (LowRankEig.factor / .eigenvalues, sorted by \|lambda\| descending) instead of LowRankEig.from_randomized(...).u_factor/.eigenvalues. Returns InverseOperator rather than a bare LinearOperator. |

NEW: after assembly the pattern is symmetrised — mirrored = T^T; entries of the mirror absent from T are added (CSR boolean mask + eliminate_zeros) — so the factorised matrix is symmetric. Mechanism changed from operator.matrix(galerkin) @ e_j (SciPy LinearOperator wrapper) to codomain.to_components(operator(domain.from_components(e_j))) with codomain.apply_gram(...) when galerkin. CONFIRMED CORRECTNESS DEFECT (new in v2): _probe_columns reuses a single `basis` array, applies the operator, then sets basis[index] = 0.0 BEFORE yielding the column. On a zero-copy space (EuclideanSpace.to_components/from_components return the array itself by design, spaces.py:1165-1191; apply_gram returns its input on an orthonormal space) any operator whose _value returns its input unchanged therefore yields an all-zero column, because `image` IS `basis`. Reproduced in the project venv on EuclideanSpace(4): LinearOperator.identity(E) probes as four zero columns; identity.with_traits(SELF_ADJOINT), I @ I, I.adjoint and from_callables(E, E, lambda x: x, ...) likewise; BlockPreconditioner([[0,1],[2,3]])(I) and ColumnThresholdedPreconditioner(0.0)(I) both raise RuntimeError('Factor is exactly singular'). (1.0*I and I + 0*I are unaffected because those nodes allocate.) v1 built a fresh e_j per column (preconditioners.py:349-355, :467-472) and returns the correct inverse on E.identity_operator(). JacobiPreconditioner and BandedPreconditioner are unaffected: diagonals() uses basis_vector(column) afresh, and the identity's _known_diagonals short-circuits. Fix is trivial (copy the image, or allocate a fresh basis per column). Galerkin selection: Block via form= ('auto' = Galerkin iff SELF_ADJOINT claimed), ColumnThresholded hard-coded Galerkin (v1: galerkin kwarg, default True, on both). Serial generator — no parallel branch (v1 joblib Parallel over columns). Block probes np.unique(columns) which is all dim columns after the diagonal fill; ColumnThresholded probes range(dim) — same dim applications as v1. Cannot use a known matrix: unlike diagonals(), _probe_columns has no _known_matrix short-circuit, so a matrix-backed operator is still probed dim times (v1 likewise). |
| `preconditioners.joblib_parallelism` | Every method except Identity and Iterative accepts parallel/n_jobs; ExactBlock and ColumnThresholded run their column probes with joblib Parallel(n_jobs=n_jobs)(delayed(_process_column)(j) ...) when parallel=True, while Jacobi, Spectral and Banded forward the flags to random_diagonal / LowRankEig.from_randomized / extract_diagonal / extract_diagonals. | `JacobiPreconditioner(n_jobs=) only; pygeoinf2/parallel.py parallel_map behind LinearOperator.diagonals(n_jobs=) and random_diagonal(n_jobs=)` | The `parallel: bool` flag is gone everywhere (v2 convention: n_jobs=None serial, int or -1 parallel, per D-6). Only JacobiPreconditioner exposes n_jobs, forwarding it to operator.diagonals (exact branch) and random_diagonal (stochastic branch). SpectralPreconditioner does not forward n_jobs to random_eig although random_eig accepts it; BandedPreconditioner does not pass n_jobs to operator.diagonals although diagonals accepts it; BlockPreconditioner and ColumnThresholdedPreconditioner probe columns with a serial generator and have no n_jobs. So 4 of the 5 v1 parallel options are lost. joblib remains a required dependency (parallel.py:21) but is imported lazily inside parallel_map only when n_jobs requests workers (parallel.py:168), so importing the preconditioners module no longer imports joblib — IMPROVED. review/parallel.md R7 (:316-318) named BandedPreconditioner among the classes that should build on diagonals' n_jobs; not delivered (REVIEW2.md:139-140: D-6's n_jobs 'reached about half its list'). |
| `preconditioners.square_operator_requirement` | Banded, ExactBlock and ColumnThresholded raise ValueError when operator.domain.dim != operator.codomain.dim; Identity, Jacobi, Spectral and Iterative perform no such check and use operator.domain for the result. | `LinearSolver._validate, numerics/solvers.py:109-125 — applied to every preconditioner via LinearSolver.__call__` | Now enforced for ALL seven replacements (Identity, Jacobi, Spectral included — v1 checked only Banded, ExactBlock and ColumnThresholded), with a generic message naming the solver class and dimensions. STRICTER: besides operator.domain.dim == operator.codomain.dim it also requires operator.domain == operator.codomain (structural equality via _key(), spaces.py:130-135 — same space, not merely same dimension) — v1 compared dimensions only. _validate additionally checks `requires` traits (SELF_ADJOINT for Jacobi/Spectral/ColumnThresholded — for Jacobi and ColumnThresholded this removes v1's applicability to non-symmetric systems, see those rows) and coordinates (Jacobi/Banded/Block/ColumnThresholded). WoodburyPreconditioner overrides _validate to also check the dimension matches its model or data space. |
| `preconditioners.linear_solver_protocol` | All seven preconditioning methods subclass linear_solvers.LinearSolver and implement the same callable protocol (operator -> approximate inverse LinearOperator), so a preconditioning method can be passed anywhere a LinearSolver is accepted and vice versa (IterativePreconditioningMethod exploits this by wrapping an IterativeLinearSolver). | `class XPreconditioner(numerics.solvers.LinearSolver) with `_invert(operator) -> InverseOperator`; LinearSolver.__call__ = _validate + _invert` | Protocol preserved in spirit (every preconditioner IS a LinearSolver and every LinearSolver can be a preconditioner — the module docstring says so explicitly) but the shape changed: subclasses implement `_invert` rather than `__call__` (the base __call__ validates first); they declare `requires: ClassVar[Traits]` and `requires_coordinates: ClassVar[bool]`; the return type is InverseOperator (a LinearOperator subclass carrying .solve(y, x0) -> SolveResult, .operator, .solver) instead of a bare LinearOperator. Hand-over to a Krylov solver is IterativeSolver(preconditioner=LinearSolver \| LinearOperator) or .with_preconditioner(...), replacing v1's preconditioning_method= kwarg; with_preconditioner raises if one is already attached. Settings remain private (underscore attributes, no public properties) except WoodburyPreconditioner.model_space/data_space. One extra class, WoodburyPreconditioner (:483-740), lives in this module with no v1 counterpart in preconditioners.py (it ports the inversion-class woodbury_* methods). |

### functional_calculus — `functional_calculus.py`

| v1 | what it did | v2 | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| `functional_calculus.LanczosOperatorFunction` | A matrix-free LinearOperator subclass representing f(A) for a self-adjoint (positive) operator A and a vectorised real function f; every application f(A)x is computed on the fly by the Lanczos process rather than by forming a dense matrix. | `pygeoinf2.numerics.functional_calculus.OperatorFunction (also reachable via operator_function / operator_sqrt / operator_log / operator_exp / operator_power / operator_inverse_sqrt)` | Renamed LanczosOperatorFunction -> OperatorFunction. Constructor signature changed from (operator, func, size_estimate, *, method='variable', max_k=None, reorth='full', rtol=1e-3, atol=1e-8, check_interval=5) to (operator, function, /, *, traits=Traits.NONE, max_iterations=50, rtol=1e-10, reorthogonalise=True). Lost keywords: size_estimate, method ('fixed'/'variable'), max_k (and its None -> space.dim default; the cap is now a hard 50), atol, check_interval; reorth str -> reorthogonalise bool. Defaults changed: rtol 1e-3 -> 1e-10; iteration cap dim -> 50. New: traits keyword (result claims close(traits \| SELF_ADJOINT)). Gating changed: v1 accepted any automorphism; v2 raises ValueError unless operator.traits carries SELF_ADJOINT (user must call with_traits first) -- the trait requirement itself is designed in pygeoinf2/DESIGN.md section 5.7 (:1036-1038, 'Requires SELF_ADJOINT'), though that design proposed a method='auto' keyword that did not ship (dispatch is by isinstance in operator_function :527-586). Export changed: v1 exported at package level (pygeoinf.LanczosOperatorFunction); v2 exports from pygeoinf2.numerics only, not from pygeoinf2 top level. Still lazy/matrix-free, still recomputes Lanczos per application, still self-adjoint by construction. Inherits the coordinate-free aliasing bug recorded on the iter row: OperatorFunction(LinearOperator.identity(space), f) applied on a non-CoordinateSpace (or one with uses_component_fast_paths=False) returns the zero vector silently. |
| `functional_calculus.LanczosOperatorFunction._mapping_impl` | The action f(A)x is delegated wholesale to apply_operator_function(base_operator, x, func, size_estimate, method=..., max_k=..., reorth=..., rtol=..., atol=..., check_interval=...) and the same function serves as the adjoint mapping. | `OperatorFunction._value / OperatorFunction._adjoint_value (delegating to apply_operator_function)` | Same design: each application runs apply_operator_function from scratch, no caching, adjoint is the same computation (_adjoint_value calls _value), no matrix of f(A) formed. Changes: forwards only max_iterations, rtol, reorthogonalise (the dropped v1 options are not forwarded because they no longer exist); uses v2's _value/_adjoint_value override protocol instead of passing mapping callables to LinearOperator.__init__. On a CoordinateSpace with uses_component_fast_paths the underlying Lanczos now runs on a preallocated (dim, max_iterations) component array and additionally keeps the basis as vectors (see iter row); on a coordinate-free space behaviour is as v1 except for the aliasing regression on the iter row. |
| `functional_calculus.LanczosOperatorFunction.__init__.automorphism_check` | The constructor refuses any operator whose domain and codomain differ, with the message 'Functional calculus via Lanczos requires an automorphism (domain == codomain).' | `_require_self_adjoint(operator, 'An operator function') in OperatorFunction.__init__, backed by LinearOperator.__init__/with_traits refusing SELF_ADJOINT on domain != codomain` | The check moved from 'domain == codomain' to 'operator claims Traits.SELF_ADJOINT'. Because LinearOperator refuses the SELF_ADJOINT claim on a non-endomorphism (operators.py:517-519, 567-569), a non-automorphism is still rejected, but now indirectly and with a different message ('... needs a self-adjoint operator; this one claims ...'). Stricter than v1: a genuinely self-adjoint automorphism that has not been tagged with the trait is now refused too; v1 accepted it. Still no verification of actual self-adjointness or positivity (traits are claims). The SELF_ADJOINT requirement is an owner-recorded design decision (pygeoinf2/DESIGN.md:1036-1038, section 5.7), so the gating is documented even though the option drops on other rows are not. Traits is defined at pygeoinf2/traits.py:30, not under pygeoinf2.algebra. |
| `functional_calculus.apply_operator_function` | Computes f(A)v by the Lanczos approximation: builds the Krylov basis Q and tridiagonal T from v, diagonalises T with scipy.linalg.eigh_tridiagonal, evaluates f on the Ritz values, forms g = S @ (f(lambda) * S[0,:]) and returns \|\|v\|\| * sum_i g_i q_i. | `pygeoinf2.numerics.functional_calculus.apply_operator_function` | Signature changed from (operator, v, func, size_estimate, *, method, max_k, reorth, rtol=1e-3, atol=1e-8, check_interval) to (operator, function, x, /, *, max_iterations=50, rtol=1e-10, reorthogonalise=True): argument order swapped (function now before the vector) and positional-only. Lost: size_estimate (minimum steps before first check), method='fixed' (substitute: rtol=0.0 runs to max_iterations -- verified 3 applications for max_iterations=3), max_k=None -> space.dim default (now hard 50), atol (criterion is change <= rtol*max(\|\|g\|\|,1e-300)), check_interval (check now every step from step 2), reorth string. Defaults: rtol 1e-3 -> 1e-10. Measured cost at defaults: on a WELL-conditioned 200-dim operator (cond 1e2) all 50 applications are used where v1's rtol=1e-3 stopped at 12; at cond 1e4 the 50 cap is hit unconverged (rel err 1e-3 to 2e-3) where rtol=1e-3 stopped at 22-24 -- so every default f(A)x costs ~50 applications, 2-4x v1's default. New: requires SELF_ADJOINT trait (ValueError otherwise); eigensolve per step uses np.linalg.eigh on the dense k x k T for k <= 32, eigh_tridiagonal above; function output no longer .ravel()'d; reconstruction uses axpy and no longer skips exactly-zero weights; component fast path on CoordinateSpace. Kept: zero-vector fast path, coefficient-space convergence test with zero-padding, single recombination at the end, silent fallback to last state on non-convergence. Inherits the coordinate-free aliasing regression (iter row): with an operator that returns its argument (e.g. LinearOperator.identity) on a non-CoordinateSpace, returns the zero vector with no error (verified: rel err 1.0). |
| `functional_calculus.operator_function_quadratic_form` | Computes the quadratic form <v, f(A)v> by Lanczos/Gauss quadrature: eigen-decomposes T, uses weights S[0,:]^2 and nodes = Ritz values, returns \|\|v\|\|^2 * sum_i f(lambda_i) * S[0,i]^2 as a Python float. | `pygeoinf2.numerics.functional_calculus.operator_quadratic_form` | Renamed operator_function_quadratic_form -> operator_quadratic_form. Signature now (operator, function, x, /, *, max_iterations=30, rtol=1e-10, reorthogonalise=True): same losses as apply_operator_function (size_estimate, method, max_k->dim default, atol, check_interval, reorth string), argument order swapped, rtol default 1e-3 -> 1e-10, cap default dim -> 30 (note: 30, not 50). Convergence test retained (scalar \|val - prev\| <= rtol*max(\|val\|,1e-300), every step) -- the round-1 review's 'no convergence test' finding has since been fixed. Requires SELF_ADJOINT trait. Uses space.squared_norm instead of norm**2. Returns a Python float on every CoordinateSpace (squared_norm wraps in float()). On the coordinate-free aliasing case it happens to return the right value only because it uses the norm computed before the basis is corrupted. |
| `functional_calculus.lanczos_tridiagonalize` | Convenience wrapper that drives iter_lanczos_tridiagonalize to completion and returns only the final (Q, T): the list of orthonormal Krylov basis vectors and the k x k symmetric tridiagonal matrix. | `pygeoinf2.numerics.functional_calculus.lanczos_tridiagonalise` | Renamed (British spelling). Signature (operator, start, max_iterations, /, *, reorthogonalise=True, breakdown_tol=1e-12): v -> start, max_k -> max_iterations (positional-only), reorth str -> reorthogonalise bool; new breakdown_tol keyword. Requires SELF_ADJOINT trait. Validation lost: v1 raised ValueError for max_k < 1; v2 with max_iterations=0 returns ([], zeros((0,0))) on the coordinate-free path and raises IndexError on the component path (verified by running it). Same wrapper semantics otherwise (returns final basis, T; fewer vectors on breakdown). Inherits the coordinate-free aliasing regression (iter row): lanczos_tridiagonalise(LinearOperator.identity(strict_space), x, 3) returns a single basis vector of norm 3.4e-16 and T=[[1.]]. |
| `functional_calculus.iter_lanczos_tridiagonalize` | Generator implementing the Lanczos recurrence on an abstract self-adjoint LinearOperator; at each step k = 1..max_k yields (Q, T) where Q is the current list of k orthonormal Krylov vectors and T the current k x k symmetric tridiagonal numpy array. | `pygeoinf2.numerics.functional_calculus.iter_lanczos_tridiagonalise (+ private _iter_lanczos_on_components)` | Renamed; signature (operator, start, max_iterations, /, *, reorthogonalise=True, breakdown_tol=1e-12). Requires SELF_ADJOINT trait (ValueError). Lost validation for max_iterations < 1 and for bad reorth strings (now a bool). Two code paths now: (a) coordinate-free (any HilbertSpace) using operator(), inner_product, axpy, scale, norm -- single-pass modified Gram-Schmidt with NO Kahan second pass (v1 had full pass + 'twice is enough' re-pass); (b) new component path taken automatically when the domain is a CoordinateSpace with uses_component_fast_paths: basis kept as columns of a preallocated (dim, max_iterations) float array, one to_components/from_components per step, metric through apply_gram, classical GS with a second pass whose trigger is in practice unconditional (see reorthogonalisation row). CORRECTNESS REGRESSION on the coordinate-free path (not 'as v1'): w = operator(basis[-1]) at :135 is then updated in place by space.axpy(-alpha, basis[-1], w) at :139 (v2's in-place contract, spaces.py:59-64; ArrayVectorMixin.axpy does y += a*x at :323-326).
