If the operator returns its argument aliased -- v2's own LinearOperator.identity does (nodes.py:65-66), as does any LinearOperator.self_adjoint(space, lambda x: x) or with_traits copy thereof -- then w IS basis[-1] and the first Krylov vector is zeroed in place. Verified: on StrictSpace(make_weighted_space()), lanczos_tridiagonalise(I, x, 3) gives a basis vector of norm 3.4e-16 and T=[[1.]]; apply_operator_function(LinearOperator.identity(strict), np.sqrt, x, max_iterations=4) returns the zero vector (rel err 1.0) with no exception. v1 was immune because it used out-of-place space.subtract (v1 :461-463). The component path is immune only because np.array(space.to_components(...)) at :201 copies, so the bug is confined to non-CoordinateSpace HilbertSpaces (e.g. MassWeightedSpace, spaces.py:802) and spaces with uses_component_fast_paths=False -- the coordinate-free case the module docstring advertises. No v2 test exercises an aliasing operator on that path (tests:407-422 uses a fresh from_components result). Fix: copy w when it is basis[-1], or use space.copy/subtract on the operator output as v1 did. Breakdown: scale is max(\|alpha_j\|, 1.0) of the current alpha only (v1: running max over \|\|v\|\|, 1, all alphas, all betas), tolerance 1e-12 configurable (v1 1e-13 fixed); beta also computed on the final step (v1 skipped it). Yields list(basis) copy each step (v1 yielded the same mutable list -- aliasing quirk fixed). T rebuilt each step via _tridiagonal, O(k^2) per step as v1. Memory: component path allocates dim*max_iterations doubles up front and additionally keeps every basis vector as a space vector (about 2x v1's storage for the basis). |
| `functional_calculus._BREAKDOWN_TOL` | Module-level (underscore-named) relative tolerance used to detect Lanczos breakdown: iteration stops when beta_j < _BREAKDOWN_TOL * max_scale. | `breakdown_tol keyword of iter_lanczos_tridiagonalise / lanczos_tridiagonalise` | No module constant; the tolerance is now a keyword argument breakdown_tol with default 1e-12 (v1 fixed 1e-13). User-configurable on the two low-level functions, but NOT exposed through apply_operator_function, operator_quadratic_form or OperatorFunction, which always use the default. The value it is compared against also changed (see breakdown row). |
| `functional_calculus.behaviour.breakdown_detection` | iter_lanczos_tridiagonalize tracks max_scale = max(\|\|v\|\|, 1, all \|alpha_j\|, all beta_j) and terminates cleanly (no exception) when the new off-diagonal beta_j falls below 1e-13 times that scale, meaning v lies in an invariant subspace of dimension < max_k. | `iter_lanczos_tridiagonalise lines 159-161 and _iter_lanczos_on_components lines 229-230` | Still clean early termination (no exception) on an invariant subspace, still treated as the fallback/exact path by the high-level routines. Criterion changed: v2 stops when beta <= breakdown_tol * max(\|alpha_j\|, 1.0) using only the CURRENT alpha, whereas v1 used max(\|\|v\|\|, 1, all \|alpha_i\| so far, all beta_i so far); tolerance 1e-12 (configurable) vs 1e-13 (fixed); comparison <= vs <. v2 also computes beta on the last step (v1 skipped it when j == max_k-1); harmless extra norm. Consequence: on an operator whose early Ritz values are large and a later alpha is small, v2's threshold is relatively tighter than v1's; on a start vector with \|\|v\|\| >> 1 v2 no longer scales by \|\|v\|\| (but the start is normalised first, so alphas carry the scale anyway). Note the aliasing regression on the iter row manifests as a spurious breakdown after step 1 (beta ~ 1e-16), so it is invisible to callers as an error. |
| `functional_calculus.behaviour.reorthogonalisation` | With reorth='full' the residual r is orthogonalised against every stored basis vector q_i (skipping exactly-zero projections), then, following Kahan's 'twice is enough' rule, a second full pass is run only if \|\|r\|\| dropped below 0.707 times its pre-pass norm. With reorth='none' only the standard three-term recurrence (orthogonalise against q_j and q_{j-1}) is used. | `reorthogonalise: bool = True on iter_lanczos_tridiagonalise, lanczos_tridiagonalise, apply_operator_function, operator_quadratic_form, OperatorFunction; coordinate-free path :142-155, component path :204-217` | reorth='full'\|'none' (str, ValueError on other values) -> reorthogonalise=True\|False (bool, no validation). Default still 'full'. The 'full' algorithm changed on BOTH paths, and neither reproduces v1's conditional 'twice is enough'. Coordinate-free path: one pass of modified Gram-Schmidt against the whole basis with NO Kahan second pass (v1: full pass then a second full pass if the norm dropped below 0.707x; v1 also skipped exactly-zero projections). The implementer's in-code justification (measured max\|Q Q^T - I\| unchanged by the second pass on three adversarial cases) is at :146-153; review/r2_numerics.md:20 accepts it as 'sound for modified GS with a full basis'. Component path: classical GS with a second pass gated on beta < (1/sqrt(2)) * before -- but 'before' (:208) is the norm of A q itself, taken BEFORE alpha q and beta q_prev are removed, whereas v1 (:467) took the baseline after the three-term recurrence. Since removing alpha q removes most of \|\|A q\|\|, the condition is met essentially every step: measured on a 200-dim SPD operator, 30 steps, 91 apply_gram calls = 3.03 per step (2 = no second pass, 3 = second pass every step; re-run and confirmed). So the component path does an effectively UNCONDITIONAL second pass: one extra apply_gram plus two (dim x k) GEMVs per step, O(dim^2) per step on a dense-Gram space, which v1's conditional re-pass rarely incurred. Orthogonality is fine (7.8e-16); the point is cost and the misdescription in the docstring at :182-185. 'none' path unchanged (three-term recurrence only). Cost class on the coordinate-free path unchanged (O(k) inner products per step); on the component path each pass is one apply_gram plus two GEMVs instead of k inner products (measured 3.1-3.7x on the sphere overall). |
| `functional_calculus.behaviour.convergence_schedule` | 'fixed' runs exactly size_estimate Lanczos steps (max_k is overridden to size_estimate); 'variable' runs at least size_estimate steps, then every check_interval steps compares the projected solution with the previous check and stops when the change is <= atol + rtol * (current magnitude), up to max_k (defaulting to space.dim). | `max_iterations / rtol on apply_operator_function (50, 1e-10), operator_quadratic_form (30, 1e-10), OperatorFunction (50, 1e-10)` | The method='fixed'\|'variable' switch, size_estimate, max_k, atol and check_interval are all gone. v2 always behaves like 'variable' with: first check at step 2 (v1: step size_estimate + check_interval), a check EVERY step (v1: every check_interval steps), criterion change <= rtol * max(magnitude, 1e-300) (v1: change <= atol + rtol*magnitude; so there is no absolute tolerance, and a result that is exactly zero can only converge through the 1e-300 floor), cap = max_iterations hard default 50 (apply/OperatorFunction) or 30 (quadratic form) (v1: space.dim). rtol default tightened 1e-3 -> 1e-10; combined with the hard cap of 50 this means the default run typically uses all 50 applications: measured on a well-conditioned 200-dim operator (cond 1e2) v2 used all 50 (v1 rtol=1e-3: 12), and at cond 1e4 it hit the cap unconverged (rel err 1e-3 to 2e-3; v1 rtol=1e-3 stopped at 22-24) -- so the cost regression is not confined to ill-conditioned operators and REVIEW.md 3.7's 'effectively always 50 applications' is confirmed. 'fixed' mode is reachable only as a workaround: rtol=0.0 with max_iterations=k (verified: 3 applications for max_iterations=3). The 'unrecognised method silently disables checks' quirk is gone with the option. Non-convergence is still silent (no flag/warning). The every-step check is a recorded implementer decision (REVIEW2.md:283-286: checking every k steps 'is a regression, measured'), not an owner-agreed catalogue/DESIGN decision. |
| `functional_calculus.behaviour.tridiagonal_eigensolve` | The only dense linear algebra in the module is the eigen-decomposition of the small k x k tridiagonal T, done on its extracted diagonals with scipy.linalg.eigh_tridiagonal (O(k^2)); f is applied elementwise to the Ritz values via np.asarray(func(eigvals)).ravel(). | `_eigh_tridiagonal(matrix) in numerics/functional_calculus.py` | Dense work is still confined to the k x k T. Changes: (1) a dispatch: k == 1 returns (T[0], [[1]]) directly; k <= _DENSE_EIGH_LIMIT (32) uses np.linalg.eigh on the dense k x k array (measured faster at these sizes, comment :358-369); k > 32 uses scipy.linalg.eigh_tridiagonal(np.diag(T), np.diag(T, 1)) as v1. (2) It is now invoked at EVERY Lanczos step (v1: only at check steps, i.e. roughly every check_interval steps), so the total eigensolve work per run is sum_k O(k^2..k^3) rather than that divided by check_interval -- accepted by the implementer on measurement (comment :371-384, 27% of a cheap-operator SLQ). (3) function(values) is wrapped in np.asarray but no longer .ravel()'d, so a function returning a column-shaped array would now mis-broadcast. Still numpy + scipy only; no joblib/parallel branches; no n_jobs anywhere in the module. |

### low_rank — `low_rank.py`

| v1 | what it did | v2 | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| `low_rank.LowRankSVD` | A LinearOperator subclass representing a low-rank SVD, A ~= U @ Sigma @ V*, usable directly as an operator while exposing the U, Sigma and V factors. | `pygeoinf2.numerics.randomised.LowRankSVD(left, singular_values, right)` | Constructor signature changed from (u_op, sigma_op: DiagonalSparseMatrixLinearOperator, v_op) to positional-only (left: LinearOperator, singular_values: np.ndarray, right: LinearOperator). Sigma is no longer an operator: it is a stored 1-D array and the action is `left(sigma * right.adjoint(x))` written directly in _value/_adjoint_value rather than composing full_op = U @ Sigma @ V*. Still fully matrix-free, still a LinearOperator subclass. Properties renamed: u_factor -> left_factor, v_factor -> right_factor; sigma_factor has no counterpart. No traits claimed on the result. |
| `low_rank.LowRankSVD.u_factor` | Returns the left singular vectors operator U (an isometry from EuclideanSpace(k) into the codomain). | `LowRankSVD.left_factor` | Renamed u_factor -> left_factor. Same meaning (isometry R^k -> codomain). In random_svd it is a _ColumnOperator built via from_component_columns(codomain, columns @ vectors, orthonormal=True) on coordinate spaces (holds an (n,k) dense column array) or from_vectors(..., orthonormal=True) otherwise, rather than v1's composition Q_op @ U_tilde_op; it now claims Traits.ISOMETRY. |
| `low_rank.LowRankSVD.v_factor` | Returns the right singular vectors operator V (an isometry from EuclideanSpace(k) into the domain). | `LowRankSVD.right_factor` | Renamed v_factor -> right_factor. Same meaning (isometry R^k -> domain). Built as from_component_columns(domain, (pulled_columns @ vectors) / singular_values, orthonormal=True) or from_vectors of explicitly scaled vectors, instead of v1's B.adjoint @ U_tilde_op @ sigma_inv_op composition; singular values below max*1e-14 are dropped before the division rather than v1's absolute 1e-12 cutoff to zero. |
| `low_rank.LowRankSVD.from_randomized` | Computes a randomized low-rank SVD of an arbitrary (possibly rectangular) LinearOperator via the unified range finder, returning a LowRankSVD. | `pygeoinf2.numerics.randomised.random_svd(operator, /, *, rank=None, rng=None, **kwargs)` | Classmethod became a module function random_svd. Signature: size_estimate -> rank (None = adaptive, int = fixed); `measure` kwarg removed (probes always domain.white_noise -- a prior-weighted probe distribution is no longer possible); `galerkin` removed; `method` removed (replaced by rank None/int); `parallel` removed; n_jobs default -1 -> None (serial); power default 2 -> 1; new `oversampling=10` (so a fixed-rank call applies the operator to rank+10 probes and truncates to rank); explicit `rng`. Same mathematics (eigh of the k x k Gram C = (A*q_i, A*q_j) = B B*) but the core is assembled from inner products / columns.T @ G(columns) rather than by `.matrix(dense=True)` on a composed operator; np.linalg.eigh instead of scipy. Singular values below max*1e-14 are dropped (rank can come back smaller); v1 kept them and zeroed the inverses below 1e-12. Raises ValueError if the range is trivial (v1 did not). Docstring claims ValueError for rank > min dimension but the code silently clips (count = min(rank+oversampling, ceiling)). In adaptive mode (rank=None) no truncation is applied (randomised.py:656-658), so the add-before-check rank inflation of random_range (see _abstract_variable_rank_random_range) carries through as extra noise-level singular triplets. Factors are _ColumnOperator (dense (n,k) component arrays) on coordinate spaces, from_vectors elsewhere, and claim ISOMETRY. |
| `low_rank.LowRankEig` | A LinearOperator subclass representing a low-rank eigendecomposition of a self-adjoint operator, A ~= U @ D @ U*, exposing eigenvectors and eigenvalues. | `pygeoinf2.numerics.randomised.LowRankEig(factor, eigenvalues)` | Constructor changed from (u_op, d_op: DiagonalSparseMatrixLinearOperator) to positional-only (factor: LinearOperator, eigenvalues: np.ndarray). D is a stored array; action is factor(eigenvalues * factor.adjoint(x)) directly (matrix-free, as before). u_factor -> factor; d_factor has no counterpart. New: claims Traits.SELF_ADJOINT, and POSITIVE_SEMIDEFINITE when all eigenvalues >= 0 (IMPROVED). rank, eigenvalues, trace, apply_function retained (apply_function changed; see its row). |
| `low_rank.LowRankEig.u_factor` | Returns the eigenvector operator U (isometry from EuclideanSpace(k) into the space). | `LowRankEig.factor` | Renamed u_factor -> factor. Same meaning (isometry R^k -> space). Built by from_component_columns(space, columns @ vectors, orthonormal=True) (a _ColumnOperator holding an (n,k) component array) on coordinate spaces, or from_vectors(..., orthonormal=True) elsewhere, rather than the composition Q_op @ U_tilde_op; claims ISOMETRY. |
| `low_rank.LowRankEig.from_randomized` | Computes a randomized low-rank eigendecomposition of a self-adjoint operator via the unified range finder, returning a LowRankEig. | `pygeoinf2.numerics.randomised.random_eig(operator, /, *, rank=None, rng=None, **kwargs)` | Classmethod became module function random_eig. Signature changes as for random_svd: size_estimate -> rank (None adaptive / int fixed), measure/galerkin/method/parallel removed, n_jobs default -1 -> None, power 2 -> 1, oversampling=10 added, explicit rng. New precondition: raises ValueError unless the operator CLAIMS Traits.SELF_ADJOINT (v1 only checked domain == codomain; a self-adjoint operator without the trait is now refused). Truncates to exactly `rank` eigenpairs after drawing rank+oversampling probes; ordering by \|lambda\| rather than signed value. In adaptive mode (rank=None) there is no truncation (randomised.py:588-589), so the basis inflation of adaptive random_range (final below-tolerance block appended before the convergence test) is carried through as extra noise-floor eigenpairs. Core T = Q* A Q assembled as columns.T @ G(A Q) on coordinate spaces or an inner-product double loop elsewhere, symmetrised, np.linalg.eigh -- no `.matrix(dense=True)` on a composed operator. Raises if range is trivial. Same operator count (k probes + power*2k + k for T) plus oversampling. Eigenvalues not clipped (as v1). |
| `low_rank.LowRankEig.apply_function` | Applies a scalar function to the spectrum, returning a new LowRankEig representing f(A + regularization*I) restricted to the retained eigenspace (same U, new D = f(eigenvalues + regularization)). | `LowRankEig.apply_function(function, /)` | The `regularization: float = 0.0` keyword is gone (user must write `eig.apply_function(lambda l: f(l + reg))`). The TypeError/AttributeError fallback to np.vectorize is gone: the callable must accept an ndarray. The Galerkin flag propagation is moot (no D operator). Returns LowRankEig(self.factor, function(eigenvalues)) -- same semantics on the retained spectrum; traits recomputed by the constructor (PSD if all new values >= 0). |
| `low_rank.LowRankCholesky` | A LinearOperator subclass representing a low-rank Cholesky-like factorization A ~= L @ L* of a positive semi-definite operator, useful for drawing samples from Gaussian measures. | `pygeoinf2.numerics.randomised.LowRankCholesky(factor, /)` | Constructor argument renamed l_op -> factor and made positional-only; property l_factor -> factor. Action written directly as factor(factor.adjoint(x)) (matrix-free as before). New: claims SELF_ADJOINT \| POSITIVE_SEMIDEFINITE traits. rank = factor.domain.dim unchanged. |
| `low_rank.LowRankCholesky.l_factor` | Returns the Cholesky-like factor L such that A ~= L @ L*. | `LowRankCholesky.factor` | Renamed l_factor -> factor. Representation differs: v1's L = A @ Q @ (Q*AQ)^{-1/2} was a composition whose application cost one operator application; v2's L = U sqrt(D) from random_eig is a _ColumnOperator over an (n,k) array (or from_vectors of scaled vectors) -- cheaper to apply, no operator application, but it is a different (projection, not Nystrom) approximation. Directly usable as GaussianMeasure(covariance_factor=...) in v2. |
| `low_rank.LowRankCholesky.from_randomized` | Computes a robust randomized approximate Cholesky factorization of a positive semi-definite operator via the range finder (Nystrom-style: L = A Q (Q* A Q)^{-1/2}), with a safe eigendecomposition fallback if the dense Cholesky fails. | `pygeoinf2.numerics.randomised.random_cholesky(operator, /, *, rank=None, rng=None, **kwargs)` | Classmethod became module function random_cholesky. Signature changes as for random_eig (size_estimate -> rank, measure/galerkin/method/parallel removed, power 2 -> 1, oversampling=10, rng, n_jobs None). ALGORITHM CHANGED: v1 computed the Nystrom factor L = A Q (Q* A Q)^{-1/2} (dense k x k Cholesky of Q*AQ with solve_triangular, and an eigh-based pseudo-inverse-sqrt fallback with relative 1e-12 threshold on LinAlgError), giving the Nystrom approximation A Q (Q*AQ)^{-1} Q* A, which for PSD operators is more accurate than the projection Q(Q*AQ)Q* at the same rank. v2 calls random_eig and returns L = U sqrt(clip(D, 0)), i.e. the projection approximation; the Cholesky attempt and fallback are gone, and the factor no longer applies the operator. New precondition: raises ValueError unless the operator CLAIMS POSITIVE_SEMIDEFINITE (callers such as GaussianMeasure.low_rank_approximation wrap with .with_traits(PSD)). Eigenvalues clipped at 0 rather than thresholded at 1e-12*max; negative-eigenvalue directions become zero columns rather than being dropped. Inherits random_eig's adaptive-mode rank inflation when rank=None. |
| `low_rank.random_range` | Unified randomized range finder: computes an orthonormal basis Q for the range of an operator and returns it as an isometric LinearOperator from EuclideanSpace(k) into the codomain (Q* Q = I), selecting a geometry-respecting abstract path or a component-based SciPy path. | `pygeoinf2.numerics.randomised.random_range(operator, /, *, rank=None, oversampling=10, power=1, block_size=10, rtol=1e-4, max_rank=None, rng=None, n_jobs=None) -> list[vector]` | RETURN TYPE: a Python list of orthonormal codomain vectors, not an isometric LinearOperator from EuclideanSpace(k) (to get v1's Q write `LinearOperator.from_vectors(operator.codomain, basis, orthonormal=True)`). RETURN LENGTH: v1 method='fixed' returned exactly size_estimate (clipped) columns; v2 rank=k returns min(k + oversampling, ceiling) vectors -- the truncation to k happens only inside random_eig/random_svd (order[:rank]), so a direct caller asking for rank=5 gets 15 vectors unless oversampling=0 is passed. SIGNATURE: size_estimate (positional) -> rank keyword (None = adaptive, int = fixed); `method` removed; `measure` removed -- probes are always `operator.domain.white_noise(rng)`, so v1's ability to draw probes from a supplied prior GaussianMeasure (Path A with explicit measure; used live in v1 gaussian_measure.py:1895 to probe a covariance from the prior itself) is LOST (nearest substitute: random_range(operator @ measure.covariance_factor, ...), which spans A L xi); `galerkin` removed (irrelevant, orthonormalisation is always in the codomain's inner product); `parallel` removed; n_jobs -1 -> None; power 2 -> 1; new oversampling. GENERALITY: because probes come from domain.white_noise, the routine (and random_eig/svd/cholesky/trace) runs only on spaces implementing white_noise: CoordinateSpace (default dense Gram Cholesky), DiagonalMetricSpace, OrthonormalSpace, ComponentView, DirectSum and the MFEM backends do; the generic MassWeightedSpace (spaces.py:802-950, the analogue of v1's MassWeightedHilbertSpace) implements `random` but NOT `white_noise` -- its own docstring at spaces.py:946 points to a white_noise it never defines -- so every randomised routine raises NotImplementedError on an operator over it, where v1's guard (low_rank.py:547-548) made random_range run on every v1 space. Nothing in pygeoinf2 outside spaces.py and tests constructs a MassWeightedSpace, so current exposure is low, but DESIGN.md §9 does not record the omission as a decision. DISPATCH: on the codomain being a CoordinateSpace with uses_component_fast_paths (component Gram-Schmidt on (dim,k) arrays through apply_gram) vs coordinate-free orthonormal_basis, not on `measure is None` / is_orthonormal; both paths are metric-aware. The scipy.linalg.qr Householder path is gone (CGS with 'twice is enough' reorthogonalisation replaces it). ADAPTIVE MODE: no initial size_estimate block -- grows from empty in block_size steps; tolerance is rtol * max first-block norm (v1: rtol * RMS); residual discard threshold relative 1e-12*scale (v1: absolute 1e-12); the final block's residuals are appended BEFORE the convergence test (v1 broke first), inflating the realised rank by up to block_size below-tolerance directions on any operator with a small non-zero tail; power iterations applied to the whole final basis after growth (v1: to the initial block only). Only the new block is orthogonalised against the existing basis, with reorthogonalisation. UserWarning for ignored rtol/block_size/max_rank in fixed mode is gone; ValueError on unknown method gone; ValueError on rank <= 0 added. max_rank no longer clipped to min(dim). Operator applications to a block go through apply_block(n_jobs=) (fused GEMM for matrix-backed operators; optional parallel per-probe) -- IMPROVED. Returns [] (not an error) for ceiling <= 0 or zero first block. |
| `low_rank._abstract_fixed_rank_random_range` | Internal Path A fixed-rank range finder: draws exactly `rank` samples from the measure, applies the operator, and orthonormalises the images with the codomain's abstract gram_schmidt; power iterations alternate adjoint/operator applications with Gram-Schmidt in domain and codomain. | `random_range(rank=k) fixed path: _probe_range + codomain.orthonormal_basis + _power_iterate (randomised.py:75-117, 269-274; component variant 195-201, 206-217)` | Probes from operator.domain.white_noise(rng) instead of measure.samples (measure argument gone; no check that measure.domain == operator.domain because there is no measure). rank+oversampling probes instead of exactly rank, and the result is not truncated to rank here. Orthonormalisation by orthonormal_basis (drops dependent vectors, reorthogonalises) instead of gram_schmidt (raised ValueError on dependence). Power iteration identical in structure (adjoint, orthonormalise in domain, apply, orthonormalise in codomain) but breaks early on an empty basis. Operator applications via apply_block(n_jobs=) -- parallel and fused where the operator supports it (v1: sequential list comprehension; its parallel/n_jobs only reached measure.samples). On coordinate spaces the basis is carried as component columns (one analysis per vector) -- IMPROVED. Returns list of vectors (then random_range returns it directly rather than wrapping in from_vectors(...).adjoint). |
| `low_rank._abstract_variable_rank_random_range` | Internal Path A variable-rank range finder: starts from the fixed-rank basis, then repeatedly draws blocks of `block_size` test samples, projects them off the current basis using the codomain inner product, and appends the Gram-Schmidt-orthonormalised residuals until the max residual norm falls below rtol times a norm estimate, or max_rank is reached. | `random_range(rank=None) adaptive loop (randomised.py:276-312) and _adaptive_range_on_components (315-373)` | No initial_rank block: the basis starts empty and grows by min(block_size, ceiling-len) probes per round (v1 started from a fixed-rank block of size_estimate with power iterations). Probes are white noise on the domain, not measure samples. Scale/tolerance: rtol * max(norm of first block) (v1: rtol * sqrt(sum \|\|Aw\|\|^2)/sqrt(block_size)); stop when largest residual <= rtol*scale (v1: max_err < tol). Residuals below 1e-12*scale discarded (v1: absolute 1e-12). ORDER OF OPERATIONS REGRESSION: v1 tested `if max_err < tol: break` BEFORE `q_basis.extend(...)` (low_rank.py:725-733), so a converged test block added nothing; v2 runs `basis.extend(codomain.orthonormal_basis(residuals)[:room])` at randomised.py:309 and only then tests `largest <= rtol * scale` at :310-311, so the whole final below-tolerance block (every residual above the 1e-12*scale floor) is added. On any operator with a small non-zero tail -- every covariance with a decaying spectrum -- the returned rank is inflated by up to block_size directions the caller's rtol said to ignore, and adaptive random_eig/random_svd/random_cholesky carry them as extra noise-level pairs because they do not truncate when rank is None (randomised.py:588-589, 656-658). Review B reproduced this by execution (dim 40, rank-5 dominant part + 1e-3 tail, block_size 10: 20 vectors for rtol 1e-1, 1e-2 and 1e-3 alike; random_eig(rtol=1e-2) rank 20 with 15 eigenvalues ~1.5e-3 against a leading 54). The v2 test fixture (tests/test_randomised.py:30-39, 63-66) has an exactly zero tail so cannot observe it. Residual projection uses codomain._orthogonalise_against (with a second pass when the norm drops sharply) and the kept residuals are orthonormalised with orthonormal_basis (v1: plain projection loop then gram_schmidt, stopping on ValueError). Power iterations run once on the final basis after growth (v1: only on the initial block). Component path does the same arithmetic on (dim,k) arrays with apply_gram_to_columns, two projection passes, and _orthonormalise_columns(against=existing) -- one analysis per probe. Test at tests/test_randomised.py:321-378 records 33749 vs 82788 inner products at dim 600/rank 120 against an intermediate v2 version, not against v1. |
| `low_rank._component_fixed_rank_random_range` | Internal Path B fixed-rank range finder: draws an (n, rank) standard-normal Gaussian matrix, multiplies by the matrix-like operator, and takes an economic SciPy QR; power iterations alternate matrix.T and matrix products with QR re-orthonormalisation. | `_range_with_columns fixed branch (randomised.py:195-201, 206-217) with _orthonormal_columns -> CoordinateSpace._orthonormalise_columns` | scipy.linalg.qr(mode='economic') Householder QR replaced by classical Gram-Schmidt on component columns with a 'twice is enough' second pass, weighted by apply_gram (metric-aware; v1's path was Euclidean-only and hence restricted to orthonormal codomains -- generality IMPROVED). Probes are white-noise components (N(0, G^-1)) not np.random.randn; drawn from an explicit rng. parallel_mat_mat removed; products go through operator.apply_block (a matrix-backed operator does one GEMM; n_jobs parallelises per probe otherwise). Uses operator.adjoint rather than matrix.T. rank+oversampling probes. Still forms (dim,k) dense probe/basis arrays as v1 did. |
| `low_rank._component_variable_rank_random_range` | Internal Path B variable-rank range finder: forms an initial basis from `initial_rank` Gaussian probes (with power iterations), then repeatedly adds blocks of `block_size` probes, computes the residual after projection off the basis, and appends the QR of the residual until the spectral norm of the residual falls below rtol times a Frobenius norm estimate or max_rank is reached. | `_adaptive_range_on_components (randomised.py:315-373)` | Same shape (block probes, project off basis, append orthonormalised residual) but: no initial_rank block and no power iterations inside (power applied afterwards to the whole basis by _range_with_columns/_power_iterate); tolerance rtol * max first-block metric norm (v1: rtol * Frobenius/sqrt(block_size)); error criterion is the largest single residual G-norm (v1: spectral norm of the residual block); projection done twice (reorthogonalisation) and residuals orthonormalised against the existing basis via _orthonormalise_columns(against=...) (v1: single projection then QR, not re-orthogonalised against the basis); scipy QR replaced by CGS2 on columns; metric-aware through apply_gram_to_columns (v1 Euclidean only); parallel_mat_mat removed in favour of apply_block(n_jobs=). ORDER OF OPERATIONS REGRESSION (same as the abstract row): v1 Path B tested `if error < tol: break` (low_rank.py:841-842) before the np.hstack (:850); v2 writes `columns[:, count:count+added] = fresh[:, :added]` (randomised.py:369-370) and only then tests `largest <= rtol * scale` (:371), so the final below-tolerance block is kept and the realised rank overshoots by up to block_size. This is the path every CoordinateSpace with uses_component_fast_paths takes -- the default on EuclideanSpace and the symmetric-space Sobolev spaces -- reproduced by Review B on EuclideanSpace(40) (20 vectors for rtol 1e-1..1e-3 on a rank-5-dominant operator, block_size 10). Preallocates a (dim, ceiling) array (ceiling = max_rank if given, even if > dim). |
| `low_rank.random_diagonal` | Estimates the diagonal of a square matrix-like object (ndarray or scipy LinearOperator) with Hutchinson's method, diag(A) ~= mean_i (z_i * A z_i), either with a fixed number of probes or progressively adding blocks until the running estimate converges. | `pygeoinf2.numerics.randomised.random_diagonal(operator, /, *, samples=100, rtol=None, max_samples=None, block_size=20, form='galerkin', rng=None, n_jobs=None) -> np.ndarray` | INPUT: a pygeoinf2 LinearOperator on CoordinateSpaces (require_coordinates), not an ndarray / scipy LinearOperator; an ndarray must be wrapped with LinearOperator.from_matrix(..., form='components'). New `form` keyword chooses the component or Galerkin diagonal (v1 left that to the caller's matrix). PROBES: Rademacher only (generator.integers(0,2)*2-1); `use_rademacher=False` Gaussian probes LOST. Estimator is Bekas-Kokiopoulou-Saad numerator/denominator (identical to v1's mean for Rademacher probes). DEFAULTS: fixed 100 samples (v1: method='variable' from size_estimate up to n); adaptive only when rtol is given; max_samples default samples+20*block_size (v1: n); block_size 20 (v1: 10). CONVERGENCE TEST: \|\|standard error\|\| / \|\|estimate\|\| <= rtol (v1: relative change between successive estimates < rtol, default 1e-2); rtol must lie in (0,1). `method` and `parallel` removed; n_jobs -1 -> None, applied through operator.apply_block over a block of probes (fused GEMM for matrix operators). Explicit rng (v1: global np.random). Probes are lifted with domain.from_components and read back with codomain.to_components, each probe an operator application (v1 likewise via the scipy wrapper). No guard on samples <= 0: samples=0 runs probe_block(0) and returns numerator/denominator = 0/0 = NaN (v1's random_diagonal also returned NaN at size_estimate=0, so this is not itself a regression -- but see deflated_diagonal, which relied on a guard). |
| `low_rank.deflated_diagonal` | Estimates the diagonal of a square operator's component (or Galerkin) matrix by combining a deterministic diagonal of a rank-`rank` randomized SVD with a Hutchinson estimate of the diagonal of the residual operator (operator - svd_op). | `pygeoinf2.numerics.randomised.deflated_diagonal(operator, /, *, rank=10, samples=100, form='galerkin', rng=None, n_jobs=None) -> np.ndarray` | rank and size_estimate became keywords with defaults (rank=10, samples=100). Deflation is by random_eig, not LowRankSVD: the operator must CLAIM Traits.SELF_ADJOINT (random_eig raises otherwise), so v1's support for general non-self-adjoint square operators is LOST. NO ADAPTIVE STOPPING: method/rtol/max_samples/block_size are gone -- the remainder is sampled with exactly `samples` Rademacher probes (v1 default method='variable' with rtol 1e-2); use_rademacher gone (Rademacher only). DETERMINISTIC RANK-ONLY MODE LOST: v1 guarded the stochastic stage with `if size_estimate > 0:` (low_rank.py:1033), so deflated_diagonal(op, rank, 0) returned exactly the low-rank diagonal; v2 calls random_diagonal unconditionally (randomised.py:907-910) and random_diagonal has no samples guard, so `rank > 0, samples == 0` runs probe_block(0) and returns 0/0 = NaN, and `exact + nan` wipes out the exact part too (Review B reproduced: deflated_diagonal(A, rank=5, samples=0) -> all NaN, no exception). The docstring (randomised.py:871-872) promises ValueError 'for a non-positive rank or sample count' but only `rank < 0` is checked (:876). galerkin: bool=False -> form: 'galerkin'\|'components' with default 'galerkin' (DEFAULT FLIPPED). Requires CoordinateSpaces (require_coordinates) and checks domain/codomain rather than dims. Exact part: reads the eigenvector component columns (dense (n,rank), as v1's U_mat/V_mat were) and forms sum lambda_i (G c_i)(G c_i) or lambda_i c_i (G c_i) -- correct for a non-diagonal Gram matrix in both forms (v1's galerkin=False path used c_v where the component matrix needs G c_v, low_rank.py:1020-1025, so the exact part is IMPROVED). parallel removed; n_jobs None default, forwarded to random_eig and random_diagonal. Random deflation uses power default 1 (v1 power 2 via from_randomized). rank == 0 falls through to random_diagonal; rank < 0 raises (v1 also raised for size_estimate < 0; v2's samples is unchecked here). |
| `low_rank.random_trace` | Estimates the trace of an endomorphism using Hutchinson's method with Euclidean Rademacher probes on the component representation: draws z_c in {-1,1}^dim, lifts to the space via from_components, applies the operator, takes to_components, and averages z_c . (A z)_c. | `pygeoinf2.numerics.randomised.random_trace(operator, /, *, samples=100, rtol=None, max_samples=None, block_size=20, rng=None, n_jobs=None) -> Estimate` | RETURN TYPE: Estimate(value, standard_error, samples) frozen dataclass, not float (use `.value`). size_estimate -> samples keyword (default 100; must be >= 2 or ValueError). DEFAULT MODE: fixed (rtol=None); adaptive only when rtol given, stopping when standard_error <= rtol*\|mean\| (v1: relative change of the running mean < rtol=1e-2, default 'variable'); max_samples default samples+20*block_size (v1: dim); block_size 20 (v1: 10); `method` removed. PROBES: white noise on the space with the space's inner product, (A x, x), instead of component Rademacher probes with a Euclidean dot; both estimate tr(A) = tr(A_c) unbiasedly (v1's component form was already correct, contrary to the v2 docstring's claim at randomised.py:765-767 and DESIGN.md:1206-1208), but v2's Gaussian white-noise probes have higher variance than Rademacher for the same sample count, and on a non-orthonormal CoordinateSpace each probe costs a G^-1 factor draw (dense Cholesky of the Gram matrix cached on first use unless the space overrides white_noise_components). Like the range finders, it raises NotImplementedError on a space without white_noise (MassWeightedSpace). `parallel` removed; n_jobs None default through parallel_map with one spawned rng stream per probe (result independent of n_jobs -- IMPROVED reproducibility; v1 used global np.random inside joblib workers, non-reproducible). Requires operator.is_endomorphism (same as v1's domain == codomain check). Also used by log_determinant(method='stochastic') (functional_calculus.py:780). |
| `low_rank.behaviour.path_a_vs_path_b` | Path A works on lists of abstract Vectors using measure.samples, operator application, adjoint application and HilbertSpace.gram_schmidt/inner_product/axpy/subtract/norm; Path B extracts operator.matrix(dense=False, galerkin=..., parallel=..., n_jobs=...) (a scipy LinearOperator wrapper) and works on numpy arrays with scipy.linalg.qr and parallel_mat_mat. | `dispatch in random_range / _range_with_columns on `_fast(space)` = isinstance(space, CoordinateSpace) and space.uses_component_fast_paths` | Still two paths, but the dispatch key changed from `measure is None` (and codomain.is_orthonormal) to the space type: a coordinate-free loop over vectors (orthonormal_basis, _orthogonalise_against, axpy, inner_product) versus a component path on (dim,k) arrays with apply_gram(_to_columns) and _orthonormalise_columns. Both are metric-aware and both draw white-noise probes; the component path is a performance route (one analysis per vector) not a Euclidean fallback. v1's Path B scipy.linalg.qr is replaced by CGS2 in the metric; v1's Path A measure.samples is replaced by domain.white_noise. The `galerkin` flag (which in v1 affected only Path B's matrix representation) is gone. Factorisations (random_eig/svd) likewise branch on `columns is not None` to assemble the k x k core as columns.T @ G(images) (k analyses) versus k^2 inner products. Coordinate-free path verified on OpaqueSpace (tests/test_randomised.py:260-318). |
| `low_rank.behaviour.fixed_vs_variable_method` | All range-finding entry points accept method='fixed' (exactly size_estimate probes; rank = size_estimate clipped to min dim) or method='variable' (start at size_estimate, grow in block_size steps until residual < rtol * norm estimate or max_rank). With 'fixed', passing non-default rtol/block_size/max_rank triggers a UserWarning that they are ignored. | `rank: int \| None on random_range/random_eig/random_svd/random_cholesky; rtol: float \| None on random_trace/random_diagonal` | The `method='fixed'\|'variable'` string keyword is gone everywhere. Range finding: rank=int is fixed (rank+oversampling probes; random_range returns all of them, the factorisations truncate to rank), rank=None is adaptive (grow by block_size until largest residual <= rtol*scale or max_rank, with the final block appended before the test so the realised rank overshoots by up to block_size). Default mode unchanged (adaptive) for range finding, but FLIPPED to fixed for the estimators: random_trace and random_diagonal sample a fixed `samples` unless rtol is given; deflated_diagonal has no adaptive mode at all. The UserWarning when rtol/block_size/max_rank are passed with method='fixed' is gone (they are silently ignored when rank is given: randomised.py:269-274 never reads block_size/rtol). The ValueError on an unknown method is gone (no method); _range_options raises TypeError on unknown **kwargs instead. Estimators' convergence test changed from successive-estimate change to standard error (randomised.py:818-825, 1006-1015); rtol must be in (0,1). |
| `low_rank.behaviour.power_iterations` | Each power iteration applies A* then A to the current basis with re-orthonormalisation (Gram-Schmidt in Path A, economic QR in Path B) to sharpen singular-value decay before the core factorization; default is 2 iterations at the public API, 0 at the internal helpers. | `power: int = 1 keyword on random_range (and forwarded via **kwargs by _range_options from random_eig/svd/cholesky); _power_iterate / the loop in _range_with_columns` | Default lowered from 2 to 1 at every public entry point (REVIEW.md:114 flags this as an undocumented default change). Mechanics unchanged: each iteration applies A* then A with re-orthonormalisation at both half steps (orthonormal_basis / _orthonormalise_columns instead of gram_schmidt / economic QR). In the adaptive mode power iterations are now applied to the WHOLE final basis after growth (v1: only to the initial block, never to added residual blocks) -- more work but more uniform accuracy. Early exit if a half-step empties the basis. Applications go through apply_block(n_jobs=). |
| `low_rank.behaviour.dense_core_factorization` | After the range finder, every from_randomized method deliberately forms a dense k x k matrix (M = B B* for SVD, B = Q* A Q for Eig and Cholesky) via LinearOperator.matrix(dense=True) and factorises it with scipy.linalg.eigh or scipy.linalg.cholesky; the resulting small factors are re-wrapped as LinearOperators on EuclideanSpace(k) and composed with Q so the final factors remain matrix-free compositions. | `k x k `projected` (random_eig:576-585) and `gram` (random_svd:644-654) arrays, np.linalg.eigh` | A small dense k x k core is still formed and eigendecomposed, but assembled from inner products (or columns.T @ apply_gram_to_columns(...) on coordinate spaces) rather than by `.matrix(dense=True)` on a composed LinearOperator; it is explicitly symmetrised (0.5*(T+T.T)) before np.linalg.eigh (v1: scipy.linalg.eigh, no symmetrisation). Still costs k operator applications (A Q for eig; A* Q for svd). The dense k x k Cholesky / solve_triangular step of LowRankCholesky is gone entirely (random_cholesky reuses random_eig's eigh). Small factors are no longer re-wrapped as LinearOperator.from_matrix on EuclideanSpace(k) and composed with Q; instead the rotated basis columns @ vectors is materialised as an (n,k) array (_ColumnOperator) on coordinate spaces or built vector-by-vector with axpy elsewhere. Cutoffs: svd clips eigenvalues at 0 and drops sigma <= max*1e-14 (v1: kept, inverse zeroed below 1e-12 absolute); cholesky clips at 0 (v1: relative 1e-12*max threshold in fallback only); eig unclipped (same as v1). |
| `low_rank.behaviour.parallel_and_n_jobs` | Every public entry point exposes parallel and n_jobs. In Path A they are forwarded to measure.samples(...) (sample generation) only; in Path B and random_diagonal they select parallel_mat_mat(matrix, X, n_jobs) from pygeoinf.parallel for matrix-block products and are forwarded to operator.matrix(...); in random_trace they drive joblib Parallel/delayed over independent probe evaluations. | `n_jobs: int \| None = None on random_range/random_eig/random_svd/random_cholesky/random_trace/random_diagonal/deflated_diagonal; pygeoinf2.parallel.parallel_map / LinearOperator.apply_block` | The `parallel: bool` flag is removed everywhere; `n_jobs` alone controls it, with default None (serial; v1 default -1 meant 'all cores' but was only active when parallel=True, so effective default was also serial). -1 still means all cores (parallel.py:92-118). Where it acts changed: v1 Path A parallelised only measure.samples, Path B used parallel_mat_mat on the scipy wrapper, random_trace used joblib Parallel directly; v2 parallelises the operator applications to a block of probes via apply_block -> parallel_map (one probe per worker), and random_trace via parallel_map over spawned rng streams. Probes are drawn before application so results do not depend on n_jobs (IMPROVED; v1's random_trace drew inside the workers). joblib remains a hard dependency (parallel.py:21) but is only imported when n_jobs is set. parallel_mat_mat has no v2 counterpart (grep: no hits). Nested loops inside a worker run serially. review/r2_numerics.md:35 recorded n_jobs as missing from random_range/eig/svd/diagonal at the time; the current code has it on all of them. |
| `low_rank.behaviour.global_random_state` | All component-based probes use the global numpy random state (np.random.randn, np.random.choice) and abstract probes come from GaussianMeasure.samples; no function accepts a seed, rng or random_state argument, so reproducibility requires the caller to seed np.random globally (and whatever the measure uses). | `rng: numpy.random.Generator \| None = None on every public function; _resolve_rng / np.random.default_rng() fallback` | Every entry point takes an explicit `rng` Generator (IMPROVED: reproducible, and random_trace spawns one stream per probe so results are independent of n_jobs). Behavioural consequence: the fallback when rng is None is a fresh np.random.default_rng() (randomised.py:806, 881, 976; spaces._resolve_rng), NOT the global legacy np.random state -- so `np.random.seed(...)` no longer makes these functions reproducible; callers must pass rng=np.random.default_rng(seed). No use of np.random.randn / np.random.choice remains (grep 'np.random.randn\|np.random.choice' in pygeoinf2: no hits). |
| `low_rank.behaviour.rank_clipping` | random_range silently clips size_estimate (and max_rank if given) to min(operator.domain.dim, operator.codomain.dim), so requesting a rank larger than the operator's dimensions yields a full-dimension basis rather than an error. | `random_range / _range_with_columns: ceiling = max_rank if given else min(domain.dim, codomain.dim); count = min(rank + oversampling, ceiling)` | The probe count rank+oversampling is clipped to the ceiling, so a rank above the dimensions still yields a full-dimension basis silently (as v1), but the factorisations then truncate `order[:rank]` so the returned rank is min(rank, k). random_range itself does not truncate: a caller asking for rank=k receives min(k+oversampling, ceiling) vectors (v1 fixed mode returned exactly the clipped size_estimate). max_rank is NO LONGER clipped to min(dim): ceiling = max_rank as given, so _adaptive_range_on_components preallocates np.empty((dim, max_rank)) even when max_rank > dim (harmless, growth stops when residuals vanish). New: rank <= 0 raises ValueError (v1 accepted 0). ceiling <= 0 returns [] (v1 would error downstream). random_svd's docstring promises ValueError for rank exceeding the smaller dimension but the code does not raise. Realised rank may be smaller than requested when the range is genuinely smaller (orthonormal_basis drops dependent probes) or, in random_svd, when singular values fall below max*1e-14; in adaptive mode it may be LARGER than v1's by up to block_size (final block appended before the convergence test). |

### nonlinear_optimisation — `nonlinear_optimisation.py`

| v1 | what it did | v2 | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| `nonlinear_optimisation.line_search` | Wraps scipy.optimize.line_search (strong Wolfe conditions) for a NonLinearForm on a HilbertSpace: converts xk, pk and the optional gradient gfk to components, wraps the form and its derivative, and returns SciPy's tuple (alpha, fc, gc, new_fval, old_fval, new_slope). | `StrongWolfeLineSearch(decrease=1e-4, curvature=0.9, max_iterations=30, max_step=1e8)(functional, point, direction, /, *, value, slope, initial_step=1.0) -> LineSearchResult; also ArmijoLineSearch (backtracking, no v1 counterpart)` | Free function wrapping scipy.optimize.line_search -> a LineSearch class hierarchy with a native bracket-and-zoom implementation (no SciPy). Signature: form/xk/pk -> functional/point/direction (positional-only); gfk/old_fval optional -> value and slope REQUIRED keyword-only (caller must precompute f(x) and (grad f, p)); old_old_fval dropped; c1 -> decrease, c2 -> curvature (now validated 0 < decrease < curvature < 1, line_search.py:170-171); maxiter=10 -> max_iterations=30; amax=None -> max_step=1e8 (a bracketing cap that is always finite, and whose semantics differ: the bracketing loop breaks as soon as step reaches max_step without evaluating there, line_search.py:239-241, where SciPy clipped alpha to amax and evaluated at it); extra_condition dropped entirely; initial_step=1.0 added. The v1 up-front ValueError for a form without a gradient (v1:164-165) has no counterpart on the line search itself: a derivative-less Functional fails at the first trial inside functional.at with NotImplementedError (operators.py:2072); the guard lives only on Optimiser.minimise (optimisation.py:153-157). Return: SciPy tuple (alpha, fc, gc, new_fval, old_fval, new_slope) -> frozen dataclass LineSearchResult(step, point, value, evaluations, converged, model): no separate gradient-evaluation count, no new_slope, no old_fval; on failure converged=False with a concrete step/point instead of None. Zoom phase is pure bisection (line_search.py:269) where SciPy's uses cubic/quadratic interpolation (REVIEW.md:156 notes this). Coordinate-free: works on spaces without components. Returns the QuadraticModel at the accepted point so the optimiser need not re-evaluate (IMPROVED). |
| `nonlinear_optimisation.line_search.gradient_recomputation` | If the caller passes the current gradient and function values they are forwarded to SciPy and not recomputed; otherwise SciPy recomputes them via the wrapped f and myfprime. | `LineSearch.__call__(..., *, value: float, slope: float, initial_step=1.0) and LineSearchResult.model` | Reuse of the starting value is mandatory at the interface rather than optional: value and slope are required keyword-only arguments (line_search.py:69-70, :184-185), and the caller supplies the slope (a scalar) rather than the gradient vector gfk. old_old_fval is not accepted (the optimiser handles initial_step via _slope_ratio_step, optimisation.py:342-347). However, the search does NOT fully honour the reuse: StrongWolfeLineSearch._zoom re-evaluates the functional at the bracket's low end on entry (line_search.py:263-266). When zoom is entered from the first trial (the common case when the unit step fails Armijo), low == previous_step == 0.0 and this is f(point), i.e. the `value` the caller was required to pass; otherwise it is previous_value, already computed in the bracketing loop. SciPy's _zoom, which v1 wrapped, receives phi_lo as an argument and never re-evaluates it. So each zoom-entered search costs one value evaluation v1 did not spend. IMPROVED on the output side, with that offset: StrongWolfeLineSearch returns the QuadraticModel at the accepted point (LineSearchResult.model, line_search.py:40-49, :225, :283), and _DescentMethod reuses it instead of re-evaluating (optimisation.py:271-277), saving one value+gradient evaluation per outer iteration; net per-iteration saving is that evaluation minus the zoom re-evaluation when a zoom occurs. Counting: v1 returned fc and gc separately; v2 returns a single evaluations count (each Wolfe trial is one functional.at yielding value and gradient together; the zoom entry evaluation is counted, :266). Two further differences: (a) on both failure paths functional(trial) is called without incrementing evaluations (line_search.py:243-244, :289-291), so the reported count understates by one when converged is False; (b) Functional.at (_linearise, operators.py:1878-1880) constructs the Hessian at every Wolfe trial when the functional has one, whereas v1's line search called only form() and form.derivative(). |

### small_modules — `parallel.py, utils.py, auxiliary.py, config.py, datasets.py, dynamical_system.py`

| v1 | what it did | v2 | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| `parallel.joblib_dependency` | parallel.py imports joblib.Parallel and joblib.delayed unconditionally at module import; joblib is therefore a required (not optional) dependency of any v1 module importing parallel (low_rank.py, linear_operators.py). | `pygeoinf2/parallel.py:21-23,115,123,131,168; pyproject.toml:16` | joblib remains a required dependency (pyproject.toml:16 `joblib>=1.5.3`; parallel.py:21 'It is a required dependency, as it was in v1') but is imported lazily, only when a loop actually runs in parallel (parallel.py:168); the serial path never touches joblib (parallel.py:165-166; `workers == 1` short-circuits before _inside_a_worker()). Default n_jobs is None (serial) everywhere instead of -1 (all cores). resolve_jobs (parallel.py:92-118) validates n_jobs (0 or < -1 raises ValueError) and maps -1 to joblib.cpu_count(). New behaviours: one BLAS/OpenMP thread per worker via parallel_config(inner_max_num_threads=1) unless a joblib.parallel_config context is set (parallel.py:175-182); nested loops inside a worker run serially (parallel.py:121-126,165). Review B confirmed the private joblib internals it reads (_backend/default_parallel_config/get_active_backend) exist in joblib 1.5.3. |
| `datasets.load_gsn_stations` | Loads the GSN station list (cached copy preferred, else bundled copy, else downloads it) and returns a list of (lat, lon) tuples in degrees, or (name, lat, lon) if include_names=True, optionally randomly subsampled to n_stations. | `Sphere.stations(*, count=None, rng=None) in pygeoinf2/symmetric_space/sphere.py:1688-1708, with _read_table/_as_points/_subsample at sphere.py:1954-2000` | Now an instance method on Sphere (Lebesgue/Sobolev on the sphere) rather than a module function plus a Sphere @staticmethod; requires a space instance. Loss of generality: v1 load_gsn_stations was stdlib-only (datasets.py:8-16), exported at package top level (v1 __init__.py:150,286), and Sphere.iris_stations was a @staticmethod (v1 sphere.py:350), so the station table was reachable with no optional dependency and no space. In v2 the only public route is a method on a constructed Sphere, and Sphere.__init__ calls _require_pyshtools() (sphere.py:125-133,195), so the station list now needs the optional 'sphere' extra (pyshtools, pyproject.toml:22) and an lmax to be chosen. The module-level _read_table/_subsample work without pyshtools but are private. REPRODUCED: with sys.modules['pyshtools'] = None, `sphere.Lebesgue(8)` raises ImportError ('Spherical harmonic spaces need pyshtools...') while `sphere._read_table('gsn_stations.csv')` returns a 3-column dict of 177 rows. `n_stations` -> `count`; `include_names` dropped (the Station column is parsed into the table at sphere.py:1960-1970 but never returned). Returns a list of np.ndarray([lat, lon]) not tuples. Subsampling uses numpy Generator.choice(replace=False) with an explicit `rng` (sphere.py:1995-1997) instead of unseeded stdlib random.sample. `count` greater than the table size raises ValueError (sphere.py:1993-1994) where v1 silently returned all stations. No cache lookup and no download fallback: always the bundled CSV via importlib.resources. |
| `datasets.sample_earthquakes` | Returns n_events randomly chosen real earthquake locations as (latitude, longitude, depth_km) tuples, drawn from a local cache file usgs_event_cache.csv, refetching a larger catalogue from USGS if the cache is too small. | `Sphere.earthquakes(*, count=None, minimum_magnitude=0.0, rng=None) in pygeoinf2/symmetric_space/sphere.py:1710-1735` | Instance method on Sphere. Same loss of generality as load_gsn_stations: v1 sample_earthquakes was stdlib-only, top-level exported (v1 __init__.py:153,289), and Sphere.random_earthquakes was a @staticmethod (v1 sphere.py:369); v2 reaches the catalogue only via a constructed Sphere, whose __init__ requires pyshtools (sphere.py:195, optional extra). `n_events` -> `count` and now optional (None returns the whole catalogue; v1 required it). `min_magnitude` -> `minimum_magnitude`, default 5.0 -> 0.0, and it now actually filters the cached table (sphere.py:1733) where v1 applied it only on the download path; however the shipped usgs_event_cache.csv holds 188 events with magnitudes 5.0-7.5 (checked with csv.DictReader), so the default change is inert on the bundled data and the filter only bites above 5.0. Returns (lat, lon) arrays only; the depth_km third element is dropped (v1 Sphere.random_earthquakes already stripped it, but datasets.sample_earthquakes exposed it). The 'smart fetch' is gone: count greater than the (filtered) catalogue raises ValueError (sphere.py:1993-1994) instead of downloading max(2000, 1.2*n) events and returning what it could; so v2 can never return fewer than asked nor more than the 188-event seed file holds. Sampling by numpy Generator with explicit rng, not unseeded stdlib random. |
| `small_modules.package_export_status` | Of this unit, pygeoinf/__init__.py re-exports (and lists in __all__) only configure_threading, load_gsn_stations, download_gsn_stations, download_usgs_earthquakes, sample_earthquakes, DATADIR and CACHEDIR; parallel.*, auxiliary.empirical_data_error_measure and the four dynamical_system classes are public in their modules but reachable only via their submodule paths. | `pygeoinf2/__init__.py:14-238` | None of the seven v1 top-level names from this unit (configure_threading, load_gsn_stations, download_gsn_stations, download_usgs_earthquakes, sample_earthquakes, DATADIR, CACHEDIR) is exported or exists in pygeoinf2/__init__.py or its __all__ (grep over pygeoinf2/__init__.py: no hits). The two surviving capabilities are reached only as methods on the sphere spaces `pygeoinf2.symmetric_space.sphere.Lebesgue/Sobolev(...).stations()/.earthquakes()` (sphere.py:2003 `class Lebesgue(Sphere)`, :2028 `class Sobolev(Sphere)`). The `Lebesgue`/`Sobolev` re-exported at pygeoinf2/__init__.py:64 are the Fourier-geometry classes (symmetric_space/__init__.py:35 `from .fourier import Lebesgue, PeriodicBox, Sobolev`), so `pygeoinf2.Lebesgue(...)` has no .stations()/.earthquakes(); a user must import from the sphere submodule. pygeoinf2.parallel (parallel_map, resolve_jobs) is, like v1's parallel module, submodule-only. No dynamical_system or auxiliary submodule exists to import from. |

### gaussian_measure — `gaussian_measure.py`

| v1 | what it did | v2 | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gaussian_measure.GaussianMeasure` | Gaussian measure on an abstract Hilbert space, defined by an expectation vector (None means exactly zero) and a self-adjoint PSD covariance LinearOperator; optionally carries a covariance factor L (C = L L*), an inverse covariance (precision), an inverse covariance factor Li (C^-1 = Li* Li) and a zero-argument sampler callable. | `pygeoinf2.probability.gaussian.GaussianMeasure (subclass of probability.base.ProbabilityMeasure)` | Constructor now takes the domain positionally as a required first argument; keywords renamed inverse_covariance->precision, inverse_covariance_factor->precision_factor; a precision-only measure (no covariance) is now legal (covariance property returns None); covariance and precision operators MUST carry Traits.SELF_ADJOINT\|POSITIVE_SEMIDEFINITE or the constructor raises ValueError (an operator built with from_callables without traits is refused; verified empirically); the explicit `sample` callable now has signature sample(rng) and must return a CENTRED draw (the mean is added by GaussianMeasure.sample); factor-based sampling is metric-correct white noise on the factor's domain. Exported from pygeoinf2/__init__ via probability/__init__.py. |
| `gaussian_measure.GaussianMeasure.__init__` | Derives missing pieces at construction: covariance = covariance_factor @ covariance_factor.adjoint when only the factor is given; inverse_covariance = inverse_covariance_factor.adjoint @ inverse_covariance_factor when the inverse factor is given (takes precedence over an explicit inverse_covariance); a sampler is auto-installed from the factor. | `GaussianMeasure.__init__` | Derivations kept (covariance = L L* when only factor given, :186-190; precision = Li* Li when only precision_factor given, :192-193) but precision derivation no longer takes precedence over an explicit precision (v1 let the inverse factor override). ValueError now only when NONE of covariance/factor/precision/precision_factor is given (:195-199), so precision-only measures exist. Precedence of samplers REVERSED: an explicit `sample` callable wins over the factor (:637-641), whereas v1 always replaced a user sampler with _sample_from_factor. Explicit sampler must be centred and take rng. BUG FOUND: the internally-built sampler closures in _combine_affine (:2178-2184), _combine_add (:2252-2255) and from_product (:427-431) call the public self.sample() (which already includes the mean) and the result is then added to the new expectation again, so translate(v) with v != -m, affine_map, + and from_product of a measure that has an explicit sampler but no factor (e.g. every result of condition()) doubles the mean. Verified: translate(zero) of such a measure with mean [10,20,30] samples with mean [20,40,60]; affine_map(2I) gives [40,80,120]; from_product gives [20,40,60]. The bug is harmless only when the NEW mean is the zero vector (translate(-m) is centred, verified). SECOND DEFECT: _combine_scale (:2275-2318) passes no `sample=` to _rebuild, so scaling, negation (-1.0*mu), subtraction and rescale_directional_variance silently make explicit-sampler, factor-less measures unsamplable (verified (2*mu).can_sample False, (2*cond).can_sample False); v1 wrapped the sampler through __neg__/__mul__/__sub__/zero_expectation. |
| `gaussian_measure.GaussianMeasure.from_standard_deviation` | Creates an isotropic measure whose covariance is standard_deviation**2 times the identity operator of the domain. | `GaussianMeasure.from_standard_deviation(domain, standard_deviation, /, *, expectation=None) (classmethod)` | Same construction: factor = sd*identity, precision_factor = (1/sd)*identity. Two user-visible behaviour changes: (1) the sampling law changed — v1 drew standard-normal COMPONENTS (domain.random() = from_components(randn), hilbert_space.py:244-253), so on any space whose Gram matrix is not the identity the samples had component covariance sd^2 I, inconsistent with the operator sd^2 I; v2 draws white noise in the space's metric (component covariance sd^2 G^-1). This is the fix DESIGN §9 records, but the sample distribution on every weighted/Sobolev space differs from v1. (2) New validation: refuses an array (ValueError pointing to from_standard_deviations, gaussian.py:266-271) and non-positive sd (:272-273); v1 accepted a negative or zero sd (zero divided by zero in the inverse factor). |
| `gaussian_measure.GaussianMeasure.from_standard_deviations` | Creates a measure with a diagonal covariance factor whose diagonal entries are the given per-component standard deviations. | `GaussianMeasure.from_standard_deviations(domain, standard_deviations, /, *, expectation=None)` | Semantics changed: the factor is now DiagonalLinearOperator(domain, sds) — diag(sigma) as an OPERATOR on the space in its own basis (so Var((x,e_i)) = sigma_i^2 \|\|e_i\|\|^2) — where v1 built a map from EuclideanSpace(dim) into the domain (covariance component matrix diag(sigma^2) with metric entering through the adjoint). The two agree only on an orthonormal basis; the v2 docstring says so explicitly. Also now rejects non-positive entries (v1 allowed 0 and would produce inf in the inverse factor) and requires exact shape (dim,). Precision factor now a DiagonalLinearOperator on the domain rather than a sparse map into Euclidean space. Diagonal representation enables the O(dim) spectral fast paths in kl_divergence, norms and ambient_ball. |
| `gaussian_measure.GaussianMeasure.from_covariance_matrix` | Creates a measure from a dense symmetric PSD covariance matrix by a full eigendecomposition, producing a covariance factor L = U sqrt(D) and a pseudo-inverse factor Li = D^{-1/2} U^T. | `GaussianMeasure.from_covariance_matrix(domain: CoordinateSpace, matrix, /, *, form='galerkin', expectation=None, rtol=1e-10)` | New `form` keyword ('galerkin' default \| 'components') saying which representation the array is in (v1 always took Galerkin, galerkin=True); domain must be a CoordinateSpace (require_coordinates). Factorisation: tries np.linalg.cholesky first, falls back to eigh with the same clip/warn/ValueError rules as v1 (_semidefinite_factors). Singular covariance now gets NO precision factor (v1 attached a pseudo-inverse Li with reciprocal 0 on zero eigenvalues); a nonsingular one gets precision_factor = R^-1 G (metric-correct, v1 dropped G) and a precision claiming POSITIVE_DEFINITE. Result still has covariance = L L* as composition. |
| `gaussian_measure.GaussianMeasure.from_samples` | Estimates a measure empirically: mean via domain.sample_expectation and an unbiased (1/(n-1)) sample covariance built as a self-adjoint tensor-product operator over the centred samples. | `GaussianMeasure.from_samples(domain, samples: Sequence, /)` | n == 1 now raises ValueError (v1 returned a zero-covariance measure whose sampler returns the mean); the `assert x in domain` check is gone. Covariance now carried as a covariance FACTOR L: EuclideanSpace(n) -> domain (from_callables, adjoint = inner products with deviations) so covariance = L L* (rank <= n-1) and the sampler comes from the factor (v1 used self_adjoint_from_tensor_product plus a hand-rolled global-RNG sampler). Mean via domain.mean. Still matrix-free. |
| `gaussian_measure.GaussianMeasure.from_direct_sum` | Builds the product measure on the direct sum of the input domains: block-diagonal covariance, concatenated (list) expectation, block-diagonal inverse covariance and a per-block sampler when available. | `GaussianMeasure.from_product(measures, /, *, labels=None); also probability.product(measures, labels=) and ProductMeasure for non-Gaussians` | Renamed. New `labels` keyword for the DirectSum summands. Propagation extended: block-diagonal covariance FACTOR when every input has one (v1 never propagated factors), block-diagonal precision_factor as fallback when precisions are absent. Expectation is always a tuple of per-block expectations (v1 used the None sentinel when all were zero, so has_zero_expectation is now False for a product of centred measures, losing the zero-mean fast paths). Raises ValueError if any input is precision-only. Explicit sampler only when no block factor and all can_sample — and that sampler double-counts the means (see __init__ row; verified from_product mean doubled). |
| `gaussian_measure.GaussianMeasure.covariance` | The covariance operator (always available; either supplied or formed as factor @ factor.adjoint). | `GaussianMeasure.covariance (property) -> LinearOperator \| None` | No longer always available: returns None for a precision-only measure. Methods that need it go through _require_covariance and raise ValueError. |
| `gaussian_measure.GaussianMeasure.inverse_covariance` | The precision operator; raises AttributeError if not set. | `GaussianMeasure.precision (property)` | Renamed; returns None instead of raising AttributeError when absent. Now propagated through translate, scalar scaling and invertible diagonal maps (_mapped_precision, _combine_scale), which v1 did not do. Used by credible_set, mahalanobis_squared, log_density, grad_log_density, kl stochastic route. |
| `gaussian_measure.GaussianMeasure.covariance_factor` | The covariance factor L; raises AttributeError if not set. | `GaussianMeasure.covariance_factor (property)` | Returns None instead of raising AttributeError when absent. Factor domain is now the measure's domain for from_standard_deviation(s) (DiagonalLinearOperator) and EuclideanSpace(n) for from_samples / from_covariance_matrix / low_rank_approximation. |
| `gaussian_measure.GaussianMeasure.inverse_covariance_factor` | The inverse covariance factor Li; raises AttributeError if not set. | `GaussianMeasure.precision_factor (property)` | Renamed; returns None when absent instead of raising. |
| `gaussian_measure.GaussianMeasure.has_zero_expectation` | True when the expectation is stored as the None sentinel meaning exactly zero. | `GaussianMeasure.has_zero_expectation (property)` | Same None-sentinel test on the stored expectation, but the sentinel is now lost through EVERY algebraic operation, not only from_product: _combine_affine always stores the mapped mean as a vector (even the identity with no translation, :2164-2168, :2200), _combine_scale stores domain.scale(alpha, expectation) (:2313), _combine_add stores domain.add(...) (:2268), from_product stores a tuple (:435). v1 preserved None in __neg__, __mul__, affine_mapping (no translation) and __add__/__sub__ (both zero). Verified on a centred factor-backed z: (2*z), z.affine_map(I), z+z, -1*z and z.translate(0) all report has_zero_expectation False. Consequence: the zero-mean fast paths (sample() skipping the add, _deviation, condition()'s centring, KL shift) are only taken on freshly constructed measures. |
| `gaussian_measure.GaussianMeasure.sample_set` | True if a sampler callable is available (either user-supplied or derived from a covariance factor). | `GaussianMeasure.can_sample (property, overriding ProbabilityMeasure.can_sample)` | Renamed to can_sample; same meaning (explicit sampler or factor present). |
| `gaussian_measure.GaussianMeasure.sample` | Draws one random sample from the measure by calling the stored sampler. | `GaussianMeasure.sample(*, rng: Generator \| None = None)` | Takes an explicit numpy Generator. Factor path draws covariance_factor.domain.white_noise(rng) (metric-correct; v1 used domain.random()). Explicit sampler is called as sample_fn(rng) and must be centred; mean added afterwards. Still NotImplementedError when neither factor nor sampler. |
| `gaussian_measure.GaussianMeasure.samples` | Draws n independent samples, serially or via joblib. | `ProbabilityMeasure.samples(n, *, rng=None, n_jobs=None)` | `parallel: bool, n_jobs: int=-1` pair replaced by a single `n_jobs: int\|None=None` (None = serial) through pygeoinf2.parallel.parallel_map (joblib underneath, still a required dependency). Each draw gets its own generator spawned from rng, so results are seed-determined and independent of n_jobs. n=0 now allowed (v1 raised for n<1); negative n raises. |
| `gaussian_measure.GaussianMeasure.sample_expectation` | Monte Carlo estimate of the mean from n samples via domain.sample_expectation. | `ProbabilityMeasure.sample_expectation(n, *, rng=None, n_jobs=None)` | Same estimator via domain.mean; `parallel` flag folded into n_jobs, rng added. |
| `gaussian_measure.GaussianMeasure.deflated_pointwise_variance` | Estimates the pointwise variance field by a deflated Hutchinson scheme: a deterministic part from a rank-`rank` randomized low-rank factor F (sum_i (F e_i)^2 pointwise) plus a stochastic Rademacher estimate of diag(C - F F*). | `SymmetricSpace.pointwise_variance_at(measure, points, /, *, rank=0, samples=None, rng=None, n_jobs=None) built on numerics.randomised.deflated_diagonal(operator, rank=, samples=, form=, rng=, n_jobs=)` | Moved off the measure onto SymmetricSpace and restricted to it; returns an ndarray of variances at given POINTS rather than a field in the domain; the estimator is the Bekas-Kokiopoulou-Saad diagonal of E C E* (E = point evaluation) with `rank` eigenpairs deflated via random_eig — not v1's factor-based sum of (F e_i)^2 plus Rademacher on the residual in the module's pointwise algebra. Lost: method='variable' adaptive stopping, rtol, block_size, max_samples (random_diagonal has rtol/max_samples/block_size but pointwise_variance_at does not forward them); rank==1 no longer refused. Gained: exact route (samples=None) at one covariance application per point, closed form for invariant measures, rng. deflated_diagonal requires CoordinateSpace. |
| `gaussian_measure.GaussianMeasure.credible_set` | Returns a probability-calibrated credible subset (subsets.Ellipsoid or subsets.Ball) in one of four geometries: Mahalanobis ellipsoid, Cameron-Martin unit ball, ambient-norm ball, or weakened-covariance (fractional) ellipsoid. | `GaussianMeasure.credible_set(/, *, level=0.95) -> geometry.convex.Ellipsoid; GaussianMeasure.ambient_ball(...) -> Ball` | Only the Mahalanobis ellipsoid geometry remains under this name; `probability` positional -> keyword `level`; `geometry`, `rank` (df is always domain.dim), `open_set`, `theta`, `spectrum*`, `radius_method`, `quantile_*`, `fractional_apply`, `n_samples`, `lanczos_*`, `rng` all gone. Cameron-Martin ball ('cameron_martin'/'cm'/'ball'/'norm_ball') and weakened ellipsoid ('weakened_ellipsoid'/'fractional') geometries are LOST (grep 'cameron\\|weakened\\|fractional_apply' in pygeoinf2/*.py -> nothing). Ambient ball moved to ambient_ball(). When the measure has no precision v2 now forms the dense Galerkin inverse G C_gal^-1 G (O(N^3); requires coordinates) instead of raising AttributeError. Returns Ellipsoid(domain, precision/threshold, centre=, covariance=C*threshold) (scaled operators) rather than Ellipsoid with an explicit radius — the same region, since Ellipsoid is {x : (x-c, P(x-c)) <= 1}. |
| `gaussian_measure.GaussianMeasure.ambient_ball` | Shortcut for credible_set(probability, geometry='ambient_ball', **kwargs). | `GaussianMeasure.ambient_ball(/, *, level=0.95, method='auto', quantile_method='auto', rank=None, samples=10_000, dense_limit=1024, rng=None, n_jobs=None) -> Ball` | Now a first-class method rather than a credible_set shortcut. `probability` -> `level`; `radius_method` -> `method` with values 'auto'\|'diagonal'\|'dense'\|'spectral'\|'sampling' (v1: 'auto'\|'spectral'\|'sampling'); 'auto' preference order changed to diagonal -> dense (if CoordinateSpace and dim<=dense_limit) -> sampling -> spectral(if rank given) (v1: spectral if spectrum passed else sampling). Lost: passing a precomputed `spectrum` (array / LowRankEig / callable), `spectrum_size`, `spectrum_low_rank_kwargs`, `quantile_tol`, `open_set`. New dense route (generalised eigh of (C_gal, G), O(N^3)) is the default for dim<=1024. Gained: O(dim) diagonal route, rng, n_jobs on the sampling route (v1 always serial), automatic imhof/matched quantile selection. Used by inference.backus.harden_error. |
| `gaussian_measure.GaussianMeasure.with_dense_covariance` | Returns an equivalent measure whose covariance is stored as an explicit dense Galerkin matrix, with eigendecomposition-derived factor and inverse factor. | `GaussianMeasure.with_dense_covariance(/, *, n_jobs=None)` | `parallel` flag folded into n_jobs. Same algorithm (dim applications to form the Galerkin matrix, then from_covariance_matrix for factor/precision_factor, covariance replaced by the matrix-backed operator with PSD traits). New: result is cached on the instance so a second call is free (and a later n_jobs ignored); singular covariances get no precision (v1 attached a pseudo-inverse factor). Requires CoordinateSpace. |
| `gaussian_measure.GaussianMeasure.with_regularized_inverse` | Returns a measure equipped with an inverse covariance obtained by applying a LinearSolver to (C + damping*I). | `GaussianMeasure.with_regularized_inverse(solver, /, *, damping=0.0)` | `preconditioner` keyword removed (v2 solvers carry their preconditioner themselves, e.g. IterativeSolver.with_preconditioner). Semantics changed: the returned measure keeps the ORIGINAL covariance C while the precision is (C + damping I)^-1 — deliberately inconsistent (docstring: 'The covariance itself is left alone'); v1 returned covariance C + damping I with a matching sampler (adding sqrt(damping) isotropic noise). v2 keeps factor and the old sampler unchanged (so sampler and precision disagree when damping>0). Lost fast path: damping==0 with a precision already present no longer returns self. Solver is called as solver(operator.with_traits(POSITIVE_DEFINITE)) — the operator is re-traited as definite without verification — and called directly (gaussian.py:1380) rather than through resolve_solver, so unlike condition() it does not accept solver=None or a factory. |
| `gaussian_measure.GaussianMeasure.with_sparse_approximation` | Builds an approximately equivalent measure with a thresholded sparse covariance matrix (SparseMatrixLinearOperator) and an exact sparse-LU precision operator, using only operator applications. | `GaussianMeasure.with_sparse_approximation(/, *, threshold=1e-3, form='galerkin')` | Algorithm replaced by a much cruder one: forms the FULL DENSE matrix via covariance.matrix(form) (v1 swept columns through the operator and assembled COO->CSC directly, never holding a dense matrix), thresholds \|entry\| < threshold * max\|entry\| GLOBALLY (v1 thresholded by CORRELATION \|c_ij\|/sqrt(d_i d_j) >= threshold, always kept the diagonal), runs np.linalg.eigvalsh on the dense matrix (O(N^3)) to refuse a non-PSD result (v1 regularised instead), then wraps csr_matrix. Lost: max_nnz per-column cap, diag_rank/diag_samples deflated-diagonal option, regularization_fraction, parallel/n_jobs, and — most important — the sparse-LU PRECISION operator (v1 returned a measure with inverse_covariance via splu; v2 returns covariance only, no precision, no sampler, no factor). Uses self._covariance directly without _require_covariance (TypeError on precision-only measure). New `form` keyword. |
| `gaussian_measure.GaussianMeasure.affine_mapping` | Push-forward of the measure under y = A(x) + b: mean A(m)+b, covariance A C A* (or factor A L), sampler A(sample)+b; optionally constructs the push-forward precision by solving a KKT saddle-point system. | `ProbabilityMeasure.affine_map(operator, /, *, translation=None); push_forward(operator) accepting AffineOperator/LinearOperator/nonlinear Operator; translate(vector); `A @ mu` via __rmatmul__; Gaussian specialisation in GaussianMeasure._combine_affine` | Split into three methods; `operator` is now positional and required for affine_map (translation-only is translate(v); affine_operator is push_forward(aff)). Mean, factor (A @ L) / covariance (A C A* with congruence traits) and sampler handled as in v1. LOST: `inverse_solver` / `inverse_preconditioner` — the KKT saddle-point construction of the push-forward precision is gone; grep 'BlockLinearOperator\\|inverse_solver\\|saddle' in probability/ -> none. Instead _mapped_precision propagates the precision only for the identity (translation) and for invertible DiagonalLinearOperators, and gives None otherwise. Translation-only path no longer special: goes through _combine_affine with identity (precision kept via _mapped_precision). Sampler closure double-counts the mean for explicit-sampler measures whenever the new mean is non-zero (see __init__ row; verified). The result always stores a vector mean, so has_zero_expectation is False even for the identity map of a centred measure. A precision-only measure under a general operator falls back to a PushForwardMeasure (sample-only). |
| `gaussian_measure.GaussianMeasure.as_multivariate_normal` | Converts the measure to a frozen scipy.stats.multivariate_normal using the dense Galerkin covariance matrix. | `GaussianMeasure.as_multivariate_normal() -> scipy.stats.multivariate_normal` | Generalised from EuclideanSpace-only to any CoordinateSpace: returns the covariance OF THE COMPONENTS G^-1 C_gal G^-1 (column-by-column solve_gram) with mean to_components(expectation). Lost: parallel/n_jobs for the matrix assembly, and the eigh-clipping retry when scipy rejects a non-PSD matrix (v2 relies on allow_singular=True only; a negative eigenvalue would propagate scipy's ValueError). Still dense O(N^2) storage, O(N) applications plus 2N Gram solves. |
| `gaussian_measure.GaussianMeasure.low_rank_approximation` | Returns a low-rank measure whose covariance factor is the L factor of a randomized LowRankCholesky of the covariance. | `GaussianMeasure.low_rank_approximation(/, *, rank=None, rng=None, **kwargs) over numerics.randomised.random_cholesky -> random_eig -> random_range` | Signature changed: v1's positional `size_estimate` + method='variable'\|'fixed' become `rank=None` (None = adaptive growth until rtol; an int = fixed rank+oversampling in one block); `max_rank`, `power` (default 1, v1 2), `rtol` (1e-4), `block_size` (10), `n_jobs` pass through **kwargs to random_range; new `oversampling` (10); `parallel` flag gone; `rng` added. Refuses a precision-only measure. Result still factor-backed (samplable), expectation kept, precision dropped, matrix-free.
