Note: random_cholesky requires the covariance to claim POSITIVE_SEMIDEFINITE and this method force-adds the trait with with_traits rather than checking it. |
| `gaussian_measure.GaussianMeasure.two_point_covariance` | Covariance function radiating from a spatial point: applies the covariance operator to the domain's Dirac representation of that point. | `ProbabilityMeasure.two_point_covariance(point, /) (on the base class); plus SymmetricSpace.covariance_function(measure, distances) closed form for invariant measures` | Moved to the base class; uses `space.dirac(point).representer` (attribute renamed from dirac_representation) and raises TypeError (docstring says NotImplementedError) rather than NotImplementedError when the space has no point evaluation. One covariance application, as before. On a precision-only GaussianMeasure it calls self.covariance(...) with covariance None and raises TypeError ("'NoneType' object is not callable") instead of the _require_covariance ValueError used elsewhere (base.py:208); no such path existed in v1. |
| `gaussian_measure.GaussianMeasure.rescale_directional_variance` | Returns a measure scaled so that Var[<x, direction>] equals std**2, keeping the original expectation. | `GaussianMeasure.rescale_directional_variance(direction, standard_deviation, /)` | Same algorithm: (std/sqrt(var)) * centred then translate back; ValueError if var <= 0. Precision now survives (scale and translate propagate it) where v1 dropped it. REGRESSION: for any measure with an explicit sampler and no covariance factor (every condition() result, every +/from_product result built from samplers) the rescaled measure is NOT samplable — the chain translate(-m) -> alpha * centred -> translate(m) passes through _combine_scale, which never carries an explicit sampler, so the final translate finds can_sample False. v1 kept a sampler at every step (zero_expectation, __mul__ and translation each wrapped it). Verified: mu.rescale_directional_variance(e1, 3.0).can_sample is False and .sample() raises NotImplementedError for both a hand-built sampler measure and a condition() result; mean and variance of the result are correct. It does NOT inherit the double-mean defect (the centring translate stores a zero-vector mean, so the re-add is harmless). Factor-backed measures are unaffected. |

Default changed from 'dense' to 'auto', which picks spectral (both covariances DiagonalLinearOperator, O(dim)), else dense when CoordinateSpace and dim<=dense_limit, else RAISES rather than going stochastic. Stochastic route reformulated as one Hutchinson trace of g(M)=M-1-log M with M similar to C_o^-1 C_s; it now requires either self.covariance_factor or other.precision_factor (ValueError otherwise) and either other.precision/precision_factor or a POSITIVE_DEFINITE-traited other.covariance plus a solver (round-trip checked); v1 required only other.inverse_covariance. Lost knobs: hutchinson_size_estimate/hutchinson_method/block_size (samples + sample_rtol + max_samples now), rtol renamed sample_rtol, lanczos_* replaced by **kwargs to functional_calculus.operator_function; parallel flag -> n_jobs. Gained: rng, error bar, spectral route, refusal of estimates whose error exceeds the value. |
| `gaussian_measure.GaussianMeasure.nuclear_norm` | Trace (nuclear) norm of the covariance operator, exactly from the diagonal or by Hutchinson trace estimation. | `GaussianMeasure.nuclear_norm(/, *, method='auto', samples=100, rtol=None, rng=None, n_jobs=None)` | `exact: bool` -> `method` in {'auto','diagonal','dense','stochastic'}. DEFAULT CHANGED from stochastic (exact=False) to exact ('auto' = diagonal spectrum if DiagonalLinearOperator, else DENSE). Exact route now forms the full component matrix covariance.matrix(form='components') and takes np.trace — O(N) applications but O(N^2) storage — where v1 used extract_diagonal (O(N) storage; fast for diagonal/dense operators). Stochastic route via numerics.randomised.random_trace with Gaussian white-noise probes and standard-error-based rtol; `size_estimate`/`method='variable'\|'fixed'`/`max_samples`/`block_size`/`parallel` not exposed (samples, rtol, n_jobs, rng instead). | `gaussian_measure.GaussianMeasure.__mul__` | Scales the measure by a scalar: expectation alpha*m, covariance alpha**2*C (or factor alpha*L), sampler alpha*sample. | `ProbabilityMeasure.__mul__(alpha) -> GaussianMeasure._combine_scale(alpha)` | Same law (mean alpha m, factor alpha L or covariance alpha^2 C). Accepts only int/float (returns NotImplemented for other types; numpy float64 passes as a float subclass). Works for covariance-only and precision-only measures (v1 required covariance or factor). REGRESSION: the explicit sampler is NOT carried — _combine_scale passes no `sample=` to _rebuild and returns a GaussianMeasure whenever any of covariance/factor/precision exists, so there is no fallback to the affine_map pushforward sampler; a measure with an explicit sampler and no factor simply becomes unsamplable under scaling. v1 __mul__ wrapped it as alpha*sample(). | `gaussian_measure.GaussianMeasure.__add__` | Sum of two independent measures on the same domain: expectations add, covariances add (operator sum), sampler = sum of samplers when both exist. | `ProbabilityMeasure.__add__ -> GaussianMeasure._combine_add; falls back to base._IndependentSum` | Same law for two Gaussians with covariances. New: when the summed covariance is a DiagonalLinearOperator the result regains a factor and precision (_diagonal_inverse). If either has covariance None the result is an _IndependentSum (sample-only generic measure), not a Gaussian. REGRESSIONS FOUND: (1) the summed sampler closure calls self.sample()/other.sample() (with means) and the mean is added again, so the sum of two explicit-sampler, factor-less Gaussians has DOUBLE the mean (verified: (mu+mu) mean [40,80,120] for m=[10,20,30]); (2) the operator sum C1 + C2 does not retain POSITIVE_SEMIDEFINITE for composite covariances, so adding two condition() results raises ValueError ('The covariance must claim SELF_ADJOINT\|POSITIVE_SEMIDEFINITE; it claims SELF_ADJOINT') — verified with cond + cond. ADDITIONAL REGRESSION: because -1.0 * other goes through _combine_scale, which drops an explicit sampler, `mu - nu` is unsamplable whenever `nu` is an explicit-sampler measure without a factor (condition() results, sums built from samplers); the sum's sampler closure requires other.can_sample (gaussian.py:2249-2255). v1 __sub__ built sample() - other.sample() directly. Priority reversed: an explicit `sample` callable overrides the factor (v1: factor overrode the callable). |

| `gaussian_measure.GaussianMeasure.behaviour.stochastic_estimator_protocol` | All randomized estimators share one control scheme: draw `size_estimate` probes, and if method == 'variable' keep adding `block_size` probes until the relative change of the running estimate falls below `rtol` or `max_samples` is reached; 'fixed' stops after the initial batch. | `samples / rtol (or sample_rtol) / max_samples / block_size on numerics.randomised.random_trace and random_diagonal; rank=None adaptive growth with rtol/block_size/max_rank on random_range` | 'size_estimate' -> 'samples'; method='variable'\|'fixed' replaced by rtol=None (fixed) vs rtol=float (adaptive); stopping criterion changed from relative change of the running estimate to standard error <= rtol*\|mean\| (random_trace) or \|\|stderr\|\|/\|\|estimate\|\| <= rtol (random_diagonal); max_samples default is samples + 20*block_size rather than domain.dim; block_size default 20 for diagonals, 10 for traces. | `gaussian_measure.GaussianMeasure.behaviour.attribute_propagation` | Derived measures propagate stored attributes unevenly: translation-only affine_mapping keeps everything; operator affine_mapping, __neg__, __mul__, zero_expectation, low_rank_approximation keep the covariance factor (sampler via factor) but drop inverse covariance/inverse factor (unless affine_mapping's inverse_solver rebuilds one); __add__/__sub__ keep only covariance sum and combined sampler; from_direct_sum keeps covariance, inverse covariance (if all) and samplers but not factors; with_regularized_inverse and with_sparse_approximation drop the factor; with_dense_covariance rebuilds factor and inverse factor from eigh. | `GaussianMeasure._rebuild / _combine_affine / _mapped_precision / _combine_add / _combine_scale / _diagonal_inverse` | Mostly improved: translate and scalar scaling keep factor, precision and precision_factor (v1 dropped precisions); invertible DiagonalLinearOperator maps keep the precision; from_product keeps factors and precision_factors; with_regularized_inverse keeps factor and sampler; sums of diagonal covariances regain factor and precision. Regressions: general-operator affine_map drops the precision and there is no KKT option to rebuild it; with_sparse_approximation now drops the precision (v1 provided one) and the sampler; the None expectation sentinel is lost through EVERY operation (affine/translate/scale/add/product all store a vector or tuple), not only from_product; explicit samplers are not carried by _combine_scale, so scaling, negation, subtraction and rescale_directional_variance make explicit-sampler measures (condition() results in particular) unsamplable where v1 wrapped the sampler at every step; the samplers that ARE carried (_combine_affine, _combine_add, from_product) double-count a non-zero mean; low_rank_approximation still drops the precision (by design). | `gaussian_measure.GaussianMeasure.behaviour.dense_formation_points` | Dense Galerkin matrices are formed only in from_covariance_matrix (input), with_dense_covariance, as_multivariate_normal, and _kl_divergence_dense; a SciPy sparse CSC matrix plus splu factorisation is formed only in with_sparse_approximation; from_standard_deviations uses a sparse diagonal operator. Every other method stays matrix-free (operator compositions and applications). | `dense/sparse matrices formed in: from_covariance_matrix (input), with_dense_covariance, as_multivariate_normal, kl_divergence 'dense' (default for dim<=4000 when not spectral), nuclear_norm/hilbert_schmidt_norm 'dense' (the DEFAULT 'auto' route for non-diagonal covariances), credible_set when no precision (dense Gram-weighted inverse), ambient_ball 'dense' (default 'auto' for dim<=1024), with_sparse_approximation (now forms the full dense matrix first, then eigvalsh, then csr), _weighted_squared fallback (dense solve when other has no precision, used by the dense KL route), log_normalising_constant via functional_calculus.log_determinant (dense below its own dense_limit=4000)` | The set of deliberate dense points GREW: nuclear/HS norms default to a dense matrix where v1 defaulted to Hutchinson and its exact mode used only the diagonal; credible_set densifies when no precision where v1 raised; ambient_ball defaults to a dense generalised eigenproblem for dim<=1024 where v1 used a randomised spectrum or sampling; with_sparse_approximation is dense-first where v1 never held a dense matrix and no longer produces a sparse-LU precision. Matrix-free paths remain for affine maps, algebra, low_rank_approximation, stochastic KL/norms, sampling. |

### convex_analysis — `convex_analysis.py`

| v1 | what it did | v2 | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| `convex_analysis.SupportFunction` | Abstract base class (ABC, subclass of NonLinearForm) for the support function h_S(q) = sup_{x in S} <q, x> of a closed convex set S in a Hilbert space H, with H identified with H* via Riesz so h is defined on the primal space. | `pygeoinf2.numerics.convex.SupportFunction(domain, /) — subclass of algebra.operators.Functional; the set-side view is geometry.convex.ConvexSet.support_function()` | Base class now Functional (v1 NonLinearForm); constructor argument renamed primal_domain -> domain and made positional-only; subclass contract is _value(y) + _maximiser(y) (both declared @abstractmethod, but Operator is not an ABC so _maximiser is unenforced and a subclass that omits it silently returns None from subgradient); the algebra methods image/translate/scale are gone (compose_with replaces image; translate is h + SupportFunction.of_point(...); scale is alpha * h); classmethods callable/point replaced by staticmethods of_ball/of_point, with no general callable constructor; value_and_support_point gone; class no longer exported from the package top level (only from pygeoinf2.numerics). |
| `convex_analysis.SupportFunction.primal_domain` | The Hilbert space H in which the underlying convex set lives. | `SupportFunction.domain (inherited Operator.domain property)` | Property renamed: primal_domain -> domain. v1 exposed both (primal_domain and the inherited domain); v2 has only domain. Any v1 code reading h.primal_domain breaks. |
| `convex_analysis.SupportFunction._mapping` | Abstract method that subclasses implement to evaluate h(q); it is the function registered as the NonLinearForm mapping, so h(q) via __call__ dispatches here. | `SupportFunction._value(self, y) -> float` | Hook renamed _mapping -> _value; dispatch is Operator.__call__ -> self._value(x) rather than a registered callback. Subclasses must now also implement _maximiser (v1 made the maximiser optional via support_point returning None). Because Operator is not an ABC the 'abstract' decorators are not enforced at instantiation. |
| `convex_analysis.SupportFunction.support_point` | Optionally return a maximiser x*(q) in argmax_{x in S} <q, x>; the base default returns None (not available). The maximiser is a subgradient of h_S at q. | `SupportFunction._maximiser(self, y) (protected, on the functional); ConvexSet.support_maximiser(direction) (public, on the set)` | Public support_point(q) -> Optional[Vector] replaced by a protected abstract _maximiser(y) on the functional and a public support_maximiser(direction) on the convex set. The 'None means unavailable' protocol is gone: unavailability is signalled by raising (ConvexSet base raises NotImplementedError; Ellipsoid.support_maximiser raises AttributeError) or, for _OracleSupport/_ShiftedSupport which never define _maximiser, by silently returning None from subgradient while has_subgradient reports True. Set-level support_maximiser is overridden only on Ball and Ellipsoid; _MinkowskiSum, _Translated and _OracleSet inherit the raising base even when their support_function().subgradient() works. |
| `convex_analysis.SupportFunction.subgradient` | Override of NonLinearForm.subgradient returning a subgradient of the support function at q, computed as self._subgradient_impl(q) (i.e. the support point). | `SupportFunction.subgradient(self, y) -> Any` | Same role (returns the maximiser), but the failure mode when no maximiser exists changed from raising NotImplementedError to returning None (_OracleSupport, _ShiftedSupport) — downstream callers such as _MinkowskiSupport._maximiser then fail with TypeError ('float' * NoneType) instead of a clear error. |
| `convex_analysis.SupportFunction.callable` | Convenience constructor wrapping a user-supplied callable q -> float (and optional q -> Vector support-point callable) as a CallableSupportFunction. | `ConvexSet.from_support_function(domain, oracle, /, *, maximiser=None).support_function() -> _OracleSupport (value only); the maximiser is reachable only as the set's .maximiser(direction)` | No SupportFunction.callable. The oracle route builds a ConvexSet, whose support_function() wraps only the value callable: _OracleSet.support_function() constructs _OracleSupport(domain, oracle) and drops self._maximiser, and _OracleSupport defines no _maximiser, so h.subgradient(q) returns None even when a maximiser was supplied. _OracleSet.maximiser(direction) returns it, but _OracleSet.support_maximiser (the ConvexSet API used by inference/backus.py:1088 and numerics/convex.py:1910) still raises NotImplementedError. Functional.from_callables(domain, value, subgradient=...) gives a plain Functional with a working subgradient but not a SupportFunction (no closed algebra). The value half is genuinely ported; the support-point half is recorded as lost under CallableSupportFunction.support_point. |
| `convex_analysis.SupportFunction.point` | Convenience constructor for the support function of the singleton set {p}, h(q) = <q, p>. | `SupportFunction.of_point(domain, point, /) (staticmethod) -> _PointSupport` | Renamed point -> of_point; classmethod -> staticmethod; arguments positional-only. Any v1 call SupportFunction.point(H, p) fails with AttributeError in v2 (grep 'def point' in numerics/convex.py: none). Semantics of the result unchanged: h(q) = <p, q>, maximiser p. |
| `convex_analysis.SupportFunction.image` | Return the support function of the linear image A(C), living on operator.codomain, with value h_{A(C)}(q) = h_C(A* q). | `SupportFunction.compose_with(operator, /) -> _ImageSupport` | Non-trivial rename image -> compose_with. Domain compatibility now tested by equality (operator.domain != self.domain) instead of identity ('is'); ValueError message names the mistake of passing the adjoint. Result _ImageSupport lives on operator.codomain with value h(A* y), exactly as v1. The catalogue's claim that v1 had domain/codomain 'the wrong way round' is not supported by the code — v1 LinearImageSupportFunction also checked operator.domain against base.primal_domain and lived on operator.codomain. DESIGN.md §9 (lines 1188ff) contains no such defect entry; the entry that exists is DESIGN.md §11.8 (line 1730), 'compose_with had its domains backwards', which describes a bug in v2's own early implementation found by v2's tests, not a v1 defect. |
| `convex_analysis.SupportFunction.__add__` | Operator overload: h_C + h_D gives the Minkowski-sum support function. | `SupportFunction.__add__(other) -> _MinkowskiSupport when other is a SupportFunction on an equal domain, else Functional/Operator sum` | v1 raised TypeError for any non-SupportFunction operand; v2 falls back to Operator.__add__ and returns a generic _FunctionalSum (probe: h + Functional -> _FunctionalSum). Domain mismatch now raises ValueError('Domain mismatch...') from Operator._check_same_spaces, by equality not identity (distinct equal spaces are accepted). Result is n-ary _MinkowskiSupport((self, other)). |
| `convex_analysis.SupportFunction.__mul__` | Operator overload: h_C * alpha gives the scaled support function alpha*h_C. | `SupportFunction.__mul__(alpha) -> _ScaledSupport iff isinstance(alpha, (int, float)) and alpha > 0.0, else Operator.__mul__ -> _FunctionalScaled` | v1: accepted int/float/np.floating/np.integer, cast to float, alpha == 0 allowed (ScaledSupportFunction with zero fast path), alpha < 0 ValueError. v2: h * np.integer / h * np.float32 and alpha == 0 silently give a generic _FunctionalScaled (not a SupportFunction; has_subgradient reports True but subgradient(y) raises NotImplementedError '_BallSupport carries no derivative' because Functional.subgradient defers to gradient when has_derivative is True); alpha < 0 no longer an error, also a generic _FunctionalScaled. The type test is narrower than Operator.__mul__'s (int, float, np.floating, np.integer), which is what makes the numpy-scalar result order-dependent (see __rmul__). |
| `convex_analysis.SupportFunction.__rmul__` | Reflected scalar multiplication alpha * h_C; delegates to __mul__. | `Operator.__rmul__(alpha) -> self.__mul__(alpha) (inherited; SupportFunction does not override)` | Same delegation to __mul__ as v1, so it inherits the v2 __mul__ changes: only int/float alpha > 0 stays a SupportFunction; zero and negative scalars give a generic _FunctionalScaled without a working subgradient. For numpy scalars the outcome is order-dependent: np.int64(2) * h yields _ScaledSupport (numpy unboxes the scalar to a Python int before calling h.__rmul__), whereas h * np.int64(2) yields _FunctionalScaled. |
| `convex_analysis.SupportFunction.__call__` | Not overridden: calling a support function evaluates the registered mapping, i.e. the subclass _mapping(q); the inherited domain property equals primal_domain. | `Operator.__call__(x) -> self._value(x); Operator.domain property` | h(q) and h.domain work identically. Flags changed: v1 has_gradient False / has_subgradient True / has_hessian False; v2 has no has_gradient — has_derivative is True for every SupportFunction (Functional overrides _linearise, which Operator.has_derivative takes as 'derivative available'), gradient(q) raises NotImplementedError('_BallSupport carries no derivative'), has_hessian False, has_subgradient True. So v2 advertises a derivative it cannot produce. |
| `convex_analysis.SupportFunction.__neg__` | Negation and subtraction are inherited from NonLinearForm and therefore return a generic NonLinearForm (with a wrapped subgradient), not a SupportFunction; the support-function algebra (image/translate/scale/support_point) is lost on the result. | `Operator.__neg__ -> self * -1.0 -> _FunctionalScaled; Operator.__sub__ -> self + (-other) -> _FunctionalSum` | As in v1 the result leaves the SupportFunction type. But v1's NonLinearForm result still carried a wrapped subgradient; v2's _FunctionalScaled/_FunctionalSum do not override subgradient, so (-h).subgradient(y) and (h - g).subgradient(y) raise NotImplementedError although has_subgradient reports True. |
| `convex_analysis.BallSupportFunction` | Support function of the closed ball B(c, r) = {x : \|\|x - c\|\| <= r}: h(q) = <q, c> + r \|\|q\|\|. | `SupportFunction.of_ball(domain, /, *, radius=1.0, centre=None) -> numerics.convex._BallSupport; geometry.convex.Ball(domain, /, *, radius, centre).support_function()` | Class is now private (_BallSupport); construction via staticmethod of_ball or Ball.support_function(). Arguments keyword-only, center -> centre, centre defaults to domain.zero(), radius defaults to 1.0, radius < 0 now raises ValueError (v1 accepted any float). Same formula r\|\|y\|\| + <centre, y>, matrix-free. |
| `convex_analysis.BallSupportFunction.support_point` | Return x* = c + r q/\|\|q\|\|, the point of the ball achieving the supremum in direction q. | `_BallSupport._maximiser(y) (numerics/convex.py:349-354); duplicated as Ball.support_maximiser(direction) (geometry/convex.py:592-599)` | Same formula c + r y/\|\|y\|\| via axpy/scale. Near-zero rule changed from \|\|q\|\| < 1e-14 to an exact norm == 0.0 test. Never None (as v1). The formula is implemented twice (REVIEW.md:238 notes 'Ball.support_maximiser ≡ _BallSupport._maximiser') and the two copies have diverged in aliasing: _BallSupport._maximiser returns space.copy(centre) at a zero direction, while Ball.support_maximiser returns the stored centre object itself (probe: B.support_maximiser(0) is B.centre -> True; B.support_function()._maximiser(0) is B.centre -> False), so an axpy-based accumulator over Ball.support_maximiser results could mutate the ball's centre — the same hazard v1 had. |
| `convex_analysis.BallSupportFunction.near_zero_threshold` | Hard-coded absolute tolerance 1e-14 on \|\|q\|\| decides when q is treated as zero for support-point purposes (same constant used in EllipsoidSupportFunction on \|\|A^{-1/2} q\|\|). | `if norm == 0.0: return centre  (exact zero test)` | Hard-coded absolute 1e-14 replaced by an exact == 0.0 test in all four maximiser implementations (ball functional, Ball set, ellipsoid functional, Ellipsoid set). Still not user-configurable. Directions with 1e-14 > \|\|q\|\| > 0 are now divided through rather than mapped to the centre. |
| `convex_analysis.EllipsoidSupportFunction` | Support function of the ellipsoid E = {x : <A(x-c), x-c> <= r^2} with A SPD: h(q) = <q, c> + r \|\|A^{-1/2} q\|\|. | `geometry.convex.Ellipsoid(domain, precision, /, *, centre=None, covariance=None).support_function() -> geometry.convex._EllipsoidSupport(domain, covariance, centre)` | Class private and constructed only through Ellipsoid. Parametrisation changed: no radius (set is {(x-c, P(x-c)) <= 1}; a radius must be folded into precision/covariance by the user); shape_operator -> precision, now required and validated for SELF_ADJOINT\|POSITIVE_DEFINITE traits and for domain == codomain == domain (ValueError otherwise); inverse_operator -> covariance keyword; inverse_sqrt_operator (the A^{-1/2} evaluation route) is gone. Missing covariance now raises NotImplementedError at support_function() (v1: ValueError at evaluation; v1 also allowed value-only evaluation through A^{-1/2}). Formula <c,y> + sqrt(<Cy,y>) otherwise unchanged; matrix-free. Note the precision operator is required even though the support function never uses it; inference/backus.py:391-396, 488-492 satisfies this by wrapping the covariance in a solver-backed inverse — matrix-free, but an extra construction v1 did not demand. |
| `convex_analysis.EllipsoidSupportFunction._mapping` | Evaluates <q,c> + r*\|\|A^{-1/2} q\|\|, preferring the direct route \|\|A^{-1/2} q\|\| = H.norm(A_inv_sqrt(q)) when inverse_sqrt_operator is supplied, else sqrt(<q, A^{-1} q>) via inverse_operator. | `_EllipsoidSupport._value(y): inner(centre, y) + sqrt(max(inner(C y, y), 0.0))` | Only the A^{-1} (covariance) route survives: sqrt(<q, C q>) with the negative clamp. The preferred direct route \|\|A^{-1/2} q\|\| via inverse_sqrt_operator is lost, as is the radius factor. The 'neither inverse given' ValueError moved to construction time of the support function (NotImplementedError). |
| `convex_analysis.EllipsoidSupportFunction.support_point` | Return x* = c + r (A^{-1} q) / \|\|A^{-1/2} q\|\| where \|\|A^{-1/2} q\|\| = sqrt(<q, A^{-1} q>). | `_EllipsoidSupport._maximiser(y) (geometry/convex.py:1045-1051); Ellipsoid.support_maximiser(direction) (geometry/convex.py:863-886)` | Same formula c + (C q)/sqrt(<q, C q>) (no radius). Never returns None: Ellipsoid.support_maximiser without covariance raises AttributeError (docstring promises ValueError) and _EllipsoidSupport is only built when covariance exists. Near-zero test is exact == 0.0. The two implementations differ: _EllipsoidSupport._maximiser clamps the quadratic form at 0, Ellipsoid.support_maximiser (line 883) does np.sqrt on the raw inner product and would return NaN on a slightly negative value — and that is the route inference/backus.py:1088-1089 uses. |
| `convex_analysis.EllipsoidSupportFunction.negative_clamp` | In every A^{-1}-based path the quadratic form <q, A^{-1} q> is clamped at zero to absorb numerical noise before taking the square root. | `max(quadratic, 0.0) in _EllipsoidSupport._value and _maximiser` | Clamp present (silent, as v1) in the functional's _value (line 1042) and _maximiser (line 1048), but absent from Ellipsoid.support_maximiser (line 883: np.sqrt(inner_product(image, direction)) unclamped), which is the maximiser the Backus dual route calls. |
| `convex_analysis.CallableSupportFunction` | Support function defined by a user-provided callable fn(q) -> float, with an optional support_point_fn(q) -> Vector supplying the maximiser/subgradient. | `geometry.convex._OracleSupport(domain, oracle, /) via ConvexSet.from_support_function(domain, oracle, /, *, maximiser=None).support_function()` | Value half ported: _OracleSupport._value = float(oracle(y)). Support-point half not ported into the functional: _OracleSet.support_function() builds _OracleSupport without the maximiser, and _OracleSupport has no _maximiser, so subgradient(q) returns None (with has_subgradient True). The maximiser lives only on the set as _OracleSet.maximiser(direction) / has_maximiser — accessors nothing in the tree calls; the standard ConvexSet.support_maximiser raises NotImplementedError for oracle sets. Class is private and not directly exported; argument support_point_fn -> maximiser (keyword-only). |
| `convex_analysis.PointSupportFunction` | Support function of the singleton set {p}: h(q) = <q, p>, with support point always p. | `numerics.convex._PointSupport(domain, point, /) via SupportFunction.of_point(domain, point)` | Class renamed and made private (_PointSupport), absent from every __all__ and from the pygeoinf2 top level, constructor positional-only; 'from pygeoinf import PointSupportFunction' has no v2 counterpart and users must go through of_point. Formula h(q) = <p, q> and maximiser p unchanged (the maximiser now returns a copy, recorded in its own row). A rename/visibility change rather than a loss, but not a plain port. |
| `convex_analysis.PointSupportFunction.support_point` | Returns p, the unique maximiser for every direction q. | `_PointSupport._maximiser(y): domain.copy(self._point)` | Returns a fresh copy of p on every call instead of the stored object (v1 returned the object itself, no copy). Safer against in-place mutation by axpy-based callers; one allocation per call. |
| `convex_analysis.LinearImageSupportFunction` | Support function of the linear image A(C) of a convex set C: h_{A(C)}(q) = h_C(A* q) for q in operator.codomain. | `numerics.convex._ImageSupport(base, operator, /) via SupportFunction.compose_with(operator)` | Private class; the domain-compatibility check moved out of the constructor into compose_with (equality, not identity) so direct _ImageSupport(base, A) construction is unchecked and fails only at evaluation with an opaque backend error (probe: ValueError 'shapes (3,) and (2,) not aligned') where v1 raised a clear ValueError in the constructor. The adjoint is not cached at construction (operator.adjoint is called per evaluation; v2 LinearOperator memoises adjoint — probe: A.adjoint is A.adjoint True; REVIEW.md:130 — so cost is equivalent). Lives on operator.codomain with h(A* y), as v1. |
| `convex_analysis.LinearImageSupportFunction.support_point` | Returns A(x_C*(A* q)): the base support point at the pulled-back direction, pushed forward by the operator; None if the base has no support point. | `_ImageSupport._maximiser(y): self._operator(self._base.subgradient(self._operator.adjoint(y)))` | Same push-forward A x_C*(A* q). The try/except NotImplementedError -> None guard is gone: a base without a maximiser either raises through or (oracle/shifted bases) returns None, which is then passed to operator(None) — undefined behaviour instead of a clean 'unavailable'. |
| `convex_analysis.MinkowskiSumSupportFunction` | Support function of the Minkowski sum C + D: h(q) = h_C(q) + h_D(q). | `numerics.convex._MinkowskiSupport(parts: tuple[SupportFunction, ...], /) via SupportFunction.__add__; geometry.convex._MinkowskiSum (set level, lines 337-383)` | Private; n-ary (tuple of parts with a .parts property) instead of binary left/right; constructor performs no domain check (the check happens in SupportFunction.__add__ by equality; direct construction with mismatched parts is unchecked, takes parts[0].domain, and fails only at evaluation with an opaque backend error). Set-level counterpart _MinkowskiSum exposes summands, refuses project/contains, and inherits the raising ConvexSet.support_maximiser even though its support_function().subgradient() works. |
| `convex_analysis.MinkowskiSumSupportFunction.support_point` | Returns x_L*(q) + x_R*(q) via H.add when both operands provide support points; otherwise None (conservative). | `_MinkowskiSupport._maximiser(y): axpy-accumulated sum of part.subgradient(y)` | Same sum of maximisers, but the conservative 'None if either operand lacks one' rule is gone: a part whose subgradient returns None (oracle or shifted support) makes _maximiser fail with TypeError ("unsupported operand type(s) for *: 'float' and 'NoneType'"), and a part that raises propagates the raise. The propagated maximiser is also unreachable through the set-level API for composite sets (ConvexSet.support_maximiser raises on _MinkowskiSum), which is the API the Backus dual route calls. |
| `convex_analysis.ScaledSupportFunction` | Support function of the nonnegatively scaled set alpha*C: h(q) = alpha*h_C(q); for alpha = 0 the set is {0} and h = 0. | `numerics.convex._ScaledSupport(base, alpha, /) via alpha * h for int/float alpha > 0` | Private; constructor no longer casts alpha to float or validates alpha >= 0 (direct construction with negative alpha is accepted silently). Through the operator only strictly positive int/float reaches it; alpha == 0 goes to the generic _FunctionalScaled, losing SupportFunction type and subgradient. |
| `convex_analysis.ScaledSupportFunction.support_point` | For alpha == 0 returns primal_domain.zero; for alpha > 0 returns alpha * x_C*(q) via H.multiply, or None if the base has no support point. | `_ScaledSupport._maximiser(y): domain.scale(self._alpha, self._base.subgradient(y))` | Same alpha * x_C*(q) for alpha > 0. The alpha == 0 -> domain.zero branch is gone (zero never reaches _ScaledSupport via *, and a direct _ScaledSupport(base, 0.0) would scale the base maximiser to zero — correct but still evaluates it). The NotImplementedError -> None guard is gone: a None from the base produces TypeError in scale. |
| `convex_analysis.package_export` | All nine classes are re-exported from pygeoinf/__init__.py and listed in its __all__ under a '# convex_analysis' comment. | `pygeoinf2.numerics.SupportFunction (numerics/__init__.py:17, 141); pygeoinf2.Ball / Ellipsoid / HalfSpace / ConvexSet (top-level __init__.py:48-60, 210-216)` | Only the abstract SupportFunction is public, and only from pygeoinf2.numerics — it is NOT in the top-level pygeoinf2 namespace (probe: hasattr(pygeoinf2, 'SupportFunction') False). All eight concrete v1 classes have no public counterpart: _BallSupport, _PointSupport, _MinkowskiSupport, _ScaledSupport, _ImageSupport, _EllipsoidSupport, _OracleSupport, _ShiftedSupport are private and absent from every __all__; HalfSpaceSupportFunction has none. Users reach them through SupportFunction.of_ball/of_point, +, *, /, compose_with, or <set>.support_function(). |
| `convex_analysis.support_point_propagation` | LinearImage, MinkowskiSum and Scaled combinators propagate support points from their operands (push-forward, sum, scale) and uniformly convert a NotImplementedError raised by an operand's support_point into 'unavailable' (None), so composite support functions expose subgradients exactly when every leaf does. | `_ImageSupport._maximiser, _MinkowskiSupport._maximiser, _ScaledSupport._maximiser (numerics/convex.py:386-422)` | Push-forward, sum and scale propagation are implemented at the functional level, but the uniform NotImplementedError -> None conversion is gone, so composites no longer 'expose subgradients exactly when every leaf does': a leaf lacking a maximiser either raises through the composite or (oracle/shifted leaves) yields None that the composite then mishandles (TypeError in the Minkowski sum; operator(None) in the image). No v2 leaf returns None by design, but _OracleSupport and _ShiftedSupport do so by omission. At the set level the propagation is not exposed at all: _MinkowskiSum, _Translated and _OracleSet inherit the raising ConvexSet.support_maximiser, and the v2 consumers (inference/backus.py:1088-1089; numerics/convex.py:1910) call support_maximiser rather than support_function().subgradient, so v1's propagation of support points through sums/translations does not reach the Backus dual route for composite priors such as the sum of two ellipsoids that ConvexSet.__add__'s docstring (geometry/convex.py:171-177) says route (b) returns. |
| `convex_analysis.domain_identity_checks` | Compatibility of spaces in image() and + is decided with the 'is' operator, so two structurally equal but distinct HilbertSpace objects are rejected with ValueError. | `operator.domain != self.domain (compose_with, numerics/convex.py:316); other.domain == self.domain (SupportFunction.__add__ :294); Operator._check_same_spaces (algebra/operators.py:336-345); other.domain != self.domain (ConvexSet.__add__, geometry/convex.py:180)` | IMPROVED: compatibility is now decided by HilbertSpace equality rather than object identity, so structurally equal but distinct spaces are accepted (probe: EuclideanSpace(3) == EuclideanSpace(3) True and their supports add to a _MinkowskiSupport). Conversely the checks moved out of the combinator constructors: _ImageSupport and _MinkowskiSupport built directly are unchecked and fail only at evaluation with an opaque backend error (probe: ValueError 'shapes (3,) and (2,) not aligned' for both) instead of v1's constructor ValueError; on an Opaque/non-numpy space the error would be whatever that backend raises. |

### convex_optimisation — `convex_optimisation.py`

| v1 | what it did | v2 | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| `convex_optimisation.SubgradientResult` | Dataclass returned by SubgradientDescent.solve: best point/value, final iterate/value, iteration count, convergence flag, history of function values and optional list of iterates. | `pygeoinf2.numerics.optimisation.OptimisationResult (returned by numerics.convex.SubgradientDescent.minimise)` | Replaced by the shared OptimisationResult: x_best->minimiser, f_best->value, num_iterations->iterations, function_values->history, converged kept; x_final, f_final and iterates (store_iterates) have no counterpart; gradient_norm, evaluations and message are new. |
| `convex_optimisation.SubgradientDescent` | Constant-step subgradient descent x_{k+1} = x_k - alpha*g_k for a NonLinearForm with a subgradient oracle; documented as for learning/testing only (no convergence guarantee). | `pygeoinf2.numerics.convex.SubgradientDescent(Optimiser)` | Now an Optimiser subclass: the oracle is no longer a constructor argument but passed to minimise(functional, x0); oracle must be a Functional with has_subgradient (a smooth Functional's gradient counts), not a NonLinearForm. step_size is optional (default 1.0) and scales a step rule rule in {'sqrt','inverse','constant','polyak'} (default 'sqrt', so v1's constant step is rule='constant'); new target_value for Polyak. max_iterations comes via Optimiser kwargs (default 500, same); store_iterates and stagnation_window are gone; a gtol stop on the subgradient norm is new. |
| `convex_optimisation.SubgradientDescent.solve` | Runs at most max_iterations constant-step subgradient steps from x0, tracking the best (lowest) function value seen, and returns a SubgradientResult. | `SubgradientDescent.minimise(functional, x0) -> OptimisationResult` | Renamed solve->minimise and takes the functional per call. Loop order differs: evaluates f(x0) first, then per iteration subgradient -> stop if \|\|g\|\| <= gtol (new criterion, converged=True) -> step -> evaluate; tracks best point/value and history like v1. No is_element(x0) check; no stagnation-window stop; no iterates list. Step is x - step_k*g via space.axpy with step_k from the rule (v1 constant). Result has minimiser=best point (v1 also returned x_final/f_final separately; lost). |
| `convex_optimisation.Bundle.linearization_matrix` | Builds the DENSE inequality system A_ineq @ [lambda; t] <= b_ineq for the epigraph QP: row i is [g_i_components, -1] and b_i = g_i_components . x_i_components - f_i. | `LevelBundleMethod._cut_rows(space, cuts) (staticmethod, private)` | Same dense (n_cuts, dim+1) rows [g_c, -1] and b = g_c.x_c - f via to_components and Euclidean dot, rebuilt from scratch per master/LP call; now private to LevelBundleMethod (unused stability_center arg dropped; no empty-bundle ValueError). ProximalBundleMethod no longer uses any such matrix: it keeps an incrementally extended Gram matrix of inner products (_gram). |
| `convex_optimisation.QPResult` | Dataclass returned by every QPSolver.solve: solution component array x, objective value obj, and status string ('solved' on success, otherwise a backend-specific failure message). | `pygeoinf2.numerics.quadratic_programming.QPResult` | Field obj renamed objective; dataclass now frozen; new `solved` property (status == 'solved') and a __repr__. Status semantics unchanged. |
| `convex_optimisation.QPSolver` | Protocol (structural type) for quadratic-programme solvers in OSQP standard form: min 1/2 x'Px + q'x subject to l <= Ax <= u; used by the bundle methods for their master problems. | `pygeoinf2.numerics.quadratic_programming.QPSolver (runtime_checkable Protocol); consumed by LevelBundleMethod._master` | Same structural protocol, same OSQP standard form, still @runtime_checkable. The contract tightened, not just the spelling: solve's five arrays are positional-only and x0 keyword-only (l,u -> lower,upper), and the only in-library consumer (LevelBundleMethod._master) now tests `result.solved`, a property that exists only on v2's QPResult. A third-party backend written to v1's documented contract (return an object with `.status == 'solved'`) still passes isinstance(obj, QPSolver) but raises AttributeError inside LevelBundleMethod. |
| `convex_optimisation.QPSolver.solve` | Protocol method: solve the dense QP with symmetric PSD P (n,n), linear cost q (n,), constraint matrix A (m,n), bounds l,u (m,) using -inf/+inf for one-sided constraints, optional warm start x0. | `QPSolver.solve(P, q, A, lower, upper, /, *, x0=None) -> QPResult` | l,u renamed lower,upper; the five arrays are now positional-only and x0 keyword-only. Semantics identical. |
| `convex_optimisation.SciPyQPSolver` | QPSolver backed by scipy.optimize.minimize(method='SLSQP'); the default solver for both bundle methods when qp_solver=None. | `pygeoinf2.numerics.quadratic_programming.SciPyQPSolver(*, tolerance=1e-9, iterations=1000)` | Gained constructor options tolerance (SLSQP ftol) and iterations (maxiter), which v1 hard-coded at the same values. No longer the default backend of the bundle methods (LevelBundleMethod defaults to best_available_qp_solver(); ProximalBundleMethod uses no QPSolver at all). |
| `convex_optimisation.SciPyQPSolver.solve` | Converts each row of l <= Ax <= u into SLSQP constraint dicts (equality when l_i == u_i finite; otherwise up to two 'ineq' constraints for finite u_i and finite l_i) and minimises 0.5 x'Px + q'x with analytic gradient P x + q. | `SciPyQPSolver.solve(P, q, A, lower, upper, /, *, x0=None)` | Same row-wise eq/ineq closures, analytic gradient, zeros warm start, 'solved'/message status. New: inputs go through _validate, which raises ValueError on shape mismatch or lower > upper (v1 passed them through). |
| `convex_optimisation.OSQPQPSolver` | QPSolver backed by the OSQP ADMM solver (optional dependency 'osqp'); supports warm-starting; a fresh OSQP instance is created on every solve. | `pygeoinf2.numerics.quadratic_programming.OSQPQPSolver(*, absolute_tolerance=1e-6, relative_tolerance=1e-6, iterations=10000, polish=True, verbose=False)` | Keyword renames eps_abs->absolute_tolerance, eps_rel->relative_tolerance, max_iter->iterations (same defaults). ImportError text changed: no longer says 'pip install pygeoinf[osqp]' (the extra still exists in pyproject.toml:25), now points at best_available_qp_solver(). |
| `convex_optimisation.OSQPQPSolver.solve` | Solves the QP with OSQP: converts P and A to scipy.sparse csc, replaces -inf/+inf bounds by -1e30/+1e30, sets up a new osqp.OSQP() with the stored tolerances, polishing and warm_starting=True, warm-starts from x0 if given, and returns the solution. | `OSQPQPSolver.solve(P, q, A, lower, upper, /, *, x0=None)` | Same csc conversion, +-1e30 infinity substitution, fresh osqp.OSQP per call, warm_starting=True, x0 warm start, 'solved' substring normalisation, obj_val. New: inputs pass through _validate, which coerces dtype/shape (atleast_1d/2d) and raises ValueError on a shape mismatch or any lower > upper, where v1 handed the arrays straight to osqp.setup. Error behaviour therefore changed, the same change that marks SciPyQPSolver.solve ported_changed. |
| `convex_optimisation.ClarabelQPSolver` | QPSolver backed by the Clarabel interior-point solver (optional dependency 'clarabel'); converts l <= Ax <= u into Clarabel's cone form. | `pygeoinf2.numerics.quadratic_programming.ClarabelQPSolver(*, absolute_tolerance=1e-8, relative_tolerance=1e-8, iterations=200, verbose=False)` | Keyword renames eps_abs->absolute_tolerance, eps_rel->relative_tolerance, max_iter->iterations (same defaults). ImportError text no longer names 'pip install pygeoinf[clarabel]'. |
| `convex_optimisation.ClarabelQPSolver.solve` | Splits constraint rows into equalities (l_i==u_i, mapped to clarabel.ZeroConeT) and inequalities (finite u_i -> row A_i, b=u_i; finite l_i -> row -A_i, b=-l_i; mapped to clarabel.NonnegativeConeT), builds sparse csc matrices, runs clarabel.DefaultSolver, and returns the primal solution. | `ClarabelQPSolver.solve(P, q, A, lower, upper, /, *, x0=None)` | Same ZeroConeT/NonnegativeConeT split, x0 ignored, manual objective, 'solved' substring. New: raises ValueError when there are no constraint rows at all ('Clarabel needs at least one constraint'), plus _validate checks. |
| `convex_optimisation.BundleResult` | Dataclass returned by ProximalBundleMethod.solve, LevelBundleMethod.solve and SmoothedLBFGSSolver.solve: best iterate and value (upper bound), cutting-plane lower bound f_low, gap, convergence flag, iteration/serious-step counts, function-value history and optional iterates. | `pygeoinf2.numerics.convex.BundleResult (frozen dataclass)` | Fields renamed to OptimisationResult's: x_best->minimiser, f_best->value, num_iterations->iterations; converged and gap kept. LOST: f_low, num_serious_steps, function_values, iterates. NEW: evaluations, message. gap now means the proximal model's predicted decrease (ProximalBundleMethod) or upper-lower (LevelBundleMethod). For ProximalBundleMethod, `value`/`minimiser` are the stability centre's (updated on serious steps only), not the least value over all evaluations as v1's f_best/x_best were, despite the docstring 'The least value found'. No longer returned by the smoothed route (LBFGS returns OptimisationResult). |
| `convex_optimisation.ProximalBundleMethod` | Proximal bundle method for minimising a non-smooth convex NonLinearForm: each iteration solves the master QP min_{lambda,t} t + (rho/2)\|\|lambda - lambda_hat\|\|^2 s.t. cutting-plane constraints, then classifies the step as serious (f decreases at the stability centre) or null (rho increased). | `pygeoinf2.numerics.convex.ProximalBundleMethod(*, weight=1.0, tolerance=1e-8, iterations=200, capacity=40, descent=0.1)` | Substantially rewritten. Oracle moved from constructor to minimise(functional, start, *, subgradient=None). Options: rho0->weight; rho_factor REMOVED (fixed x2 / x0.5 with clamps [1e-8, 1e12]); max_iterations->iterations (default 500->200); bundle_size->capacity (default 100->40); store_iterates REMOVED; qp_solver REMOVED (master solved by an internal accelerated projected gradient on the k-cut simplex, not a QPSolver); tolerance default 1e-6->1e-8 and now RELATIVE (gap <= tol*max(\|best\|,1)); new descent fraction (Armijo-style serious-step test) and new subgradient= override. Master problem is now the k x k dual with true Hilbert inner products (metric-correct, no dense d x d) instead of the dense (d+1)^2 component QP. No constructor validation of weight/tolerance/iterations/capacity (only descent). |
| `convex_optimisation.ProximalBundleMethod.solve` | Runs the proximal bundle loop from x0: evaluates the oracle at x0 (cut 0), then for k in range(max_iterations) solves the master QP, evaluates the oracle at the candidate, updates best point, does serious/null classification, appends and compresses the bundle, and checks gap = f_hat - f_low <= tolerance. | `ProximalBundleMethod.minimise(functional, start, *, subgradient=None) -> BundleResult` | Renamed and re-ordered: per iteration solve model -> check gap (model's predicted decrease, relative tolerance; can trigger at iteration 1 with no null step) -> evaluate candidate -> add cut at candidate -> serious/null test. Cuts are now taken at the candidate, not the centre (convex.py:961-971 explains this as a deliberate fix for duplicate cuts / singular Gram matrices). f_low is not tracked and not returned; num_serious_steps, function_values and iterates not returned; no QP warm start (no QP). converged only via the model gap; iteration count excludes the initial evaluation as in v1. New warning when the inner simplex solve does not converge (_minimise_on_simplex). REGRESSION: the returned value/minimiser are the stability centre's, updated only on a serious step (best - value >= descent*gap); a candidate with value < best that fails the sufficient-decrease test is a null step and discarded, so BundleResult.value can exceed the least value actually evaluated. v1 tracked f_up/best_lam over every evaluation and returned those. |
| `convex_optimisation.ProximalBundleMethod._solve_master` | Builds the master QP in DENSE form over z=[lambda_components (d), t]: P = blockdiag(rho*I_d, 0), q = [-rho*lam_hat_components, 1], A/b from Bundle.linearization_matrix, l=-inf, u=b; solves via the configured QPSolver and returns (domain.from_components(z[:d]), t). | `ProximalBundleMethod._solve_model(space, centre, value, cuts, weight) + _gram + _minimise_on_simplex + _project_on_simplex` | Master QP replaced by its dual: minimise w'(G/rho)w/2 - e'w over the unit simplex in k = n_cuts variables, where G_ij = <g_i, g_j> (space inner product, incrementally cached) and e_i = max(f(c) - f_i - <g_i, c - x_i>, 0) are linearisation errors; candidate = centre - (1/rho) sum w_i g_i; gap = (1/2rho)\|\|sum w_i g_i\|\|^2 + w'e. Solved by FISTA with closed-form simplex projection, KKT-residual stopping, warns (RuntimeWarning) if 1000 iterations exhausted with residual > 1e-4. No dense (d+1)^2 Hessian, no QPSolver, no Euclidean-component assumption. Accuracy is limited by the ill-conditioned Gram (REVIEW2 item 3.1/ O3), whereas v1 used an exact QP backend. |
| `convex_optimisation.ProximalBundleMethod.step_classification` | Serious step iff f_next < f_hat (strict decrease at the stability centre, no Armijo-style fraction): lam_hat <- lam_next, n_serious += 1, rho <- rho / rho_factor, f_low <- -inf. Null step otherwise: rho <- rho * rho_factor, f_low <- max(f_low, t_opt). | `ProximalBundleMethod.minimise lines 989-993` | Serious step iff best - value >= descent*gap (sufficient-decrease fraction, default 0.1) rather than strict f_next < f_hat; on serious: weight = max(weight*0.5, 1e-8); on null: weight = min(weight*2, 1e12) (v1: rho/rho_factor and rho*rho_factor, unclamped, factor configurable). f_low reset/update logic removed entirely (no f_low). Because `best` is only updated on a serious step, the result reports the centre's value rather than the least value seen (see ProximalBundleMethod.solve). |

Only alpha is validated (v1 also validated tolerance, max_iterations, bundle_size). Explicitly requires a coordinate space (TypeError via require_coordinates). A user-supplied qp_solver must return an object with a `.solved` attribute (v2 QPResult), not merely `.status`. |
| `convex_optimisation.LevelBundleMethod.solve` | Runs the level bundle loop from x0: per iteration (1) LP lower bound f_low = max(f_low, f_LP); (2) convergence check gap = f_up - f_low <= tolerance (before any master solve); (3) level QP with up to three alpha-widening attempts, else emergency proximal step; (5) oracle evaluation; (6) serious step iff f_next < f_hat; always add cut and compress. | `LevelBundleMethod.minimise(functional, start, *, subgradient=None) -> BundleResult` | Same outer shape (LP bound -> gap check -> level QP with widening -> proximal fallback -> oracle -> add cut/compress) but: (1) NO serious/null classification — the stability centre is moved to the candidate every iteration (`centre = point`), whereas v1 moved it only if f_next < f_hat; (2) when lower = -inf the level QP is skipped entirely and the proximal fallback is used (v1 set level = f_up and still ran the level QP); (3) the level/fallback QPs are solved with no warm start x0 (v1 warm-started [lam_hat_c, t]); (4) if the fallback QP also fails the loop breaks with message 'the master problem could not be solved' (v1 used the fallback's x regardless of status); (5) result lacks f_low, num_serious_steps, function_values, iterates; (6) the iteration count on convergence is off by one relative to v1: v2 loops `for iteration in range(1, ...)` and returns `iteration` at the gap check, before any master solve in that iteration, so converging at the first check reports iterations=1 where v1 (`for k in range(max_iterations)`, `num_iterations=k`) reported 0. | `convex_optimisation.LevelBundleMethod._solve_level_master` | Builds min 0.5\|\|lambda - lam_hat\|\|^2 over z=[lambda_c, t] with P=blockdiag(I_d,0), q=[-lam_hat_c,0], constraints = bundle cuts stacked with the level row [0..0,1] @ z <= f_lev; returns the raw QPResult so the caller can inspect status. | `LevelBundleMethod._master(space, cuts, centre, level) with level not None` | Same dense P = blockdiag(I_d, 0), q = [-centre_c, 0], cut rows plus level row [0..0,1] <= level, l = -inf. | `convex_optimisation.LevelBundleMethod.infeasibility_recovery` | If the level QP status != 'solved', alpha_try <- min(alpha_try*1.5, 0.9) and the QP is retried; up to 3 attempts total, then the emergency proximal step is used. | `LevelBundleMethod.minimise lines 1417-1436` | Same rule: up to 3 attempts, alpha <- min(alpha*1.5, 0.9), reset each iteration; any non-solved status triggers retry. ImportError message no longer names 'pip install pygeoinf[clarabel]' (extra still at pyproject.toml:26). Same cone types used. |
| `convex_optimisation.optional_dependency.joblib` | joblib.Parallel/delayed is imported only inside solve_support_values when n_jobs > 1; absence produces a RuntimeWarning and a sequential fallback rather than an error. | `pygeoinf2.parallel.parallel_map / resolve_jobs, used by DualFeasibleProperty.support_values(n_jobs=...)` | joblib is a required dependency (pyproject.toml:16; parallel.py:21) and the 'not installed -> RuntimeWarning -> sequential' branch of v1's solve_support_values is gone. Nothing was actually lost: v1 already imported joblib at module level in preconditioners.py:4, linear_forms.py:13, parallel.py:12, low_rank.py:23, linear_operators.py:30, gaussian_measure.py:33 and linear_bayesian.py:34 (all imported by pygeoinf/__init__), and pyproject.toml:16 already required joblib>=1.5.3, so the v1 fallback was unreachable in any working install. Parallelism remains the dual route only; primal/kkt/smoothed routes stay sequential and silently ignore n_jobs. |
| `convex_optimisation.bundle_component_coordinates` | Bundle.linearization_matrix, ProximalBundleMethod._solve_master, LevelBundleMethod._solve_level_master/_compute_lp_lower_bound/_solve_emergency_proximal and SmoothedLBFGSSolver.solve all convert Hilbert-space vectors to component arrays and use np.dot / identity-Hessian proximal terms; no Gram matrix is applied. | `ProximalBundleMethod: space inner products (metric-correct); LevelBundleMethod._cut_rows/_lower_bound/_master: dense Euclidean component arrays (as v1); smoothed route: LBFGS in the space (metric-correct)` | Split outcome. ProximalBundleMethod no longer uses components at all: cuts, proximal term and Gram matrix use space.inner_product/squared_norm, so it is metric-correct on a non-orthonormal basis and never allocates a d x d array (IMPROVED — by inspection only: every ProximalBundleMethod/LevelBundleMethod test runs on EuclideanSpace; the weighted OpaqueSpace in tests/test_convex.py:370 exercises prox/projection/support functions only). The smoothed route uses the space-aware LBFGS instead of component L-BFGS-B (IMPROVED). LevelBundleMethod retains v1's arrangement exactly: dense (d+1)x(d+1) P, component dot products, Euclidean proximal term, rebuilt every LP/QP call — so it is still only metric-correct for orthonormal components and still O(d^2) memory (401 MB at 5000 data per CURRENT_STATE.md:111-114). |
| `convex_optimisation.solver_interface_convention` | Every solver is a configured object with a `solve` method (never __call__) returning a result dataclass; ProximalBundleMethod, LevelBundleMethod and SmoothedLBFGSSolver are interchangeable in solve_support_values because they all return BundleResult and store the oracle in self._oracle. | `SubgradientDescent/ProximalBundleMethod/LevelBundleMethod/LBFGS: .minimise(functional, start) -> result; ChambollePockSolver.solve(objective, *, start=None); PrimalKKTSolver.solve(objective)` | The minimisers no longer hold the oracle: they expose minimise(functional, start) and the objective is passed per call (so no `_oracle` attribute and nothing for a parallel branch to patch). Chambolle-Pock and KKT keep the configured-object + solve(c) shape. Interchangeability in support_values is via `method=` at DualFeasibleProperty construction and requires only .minimise(cost, start) returning an object with .value, .minimiser, .converged — BundleResult and OptimisationResult both qualify, so LBFGS or SubgradientDescent can be dropped in where only bundle methods could in v1. Results are frozen dataclasses. Package surface moved: v1 exported SubgradientDescent, ProximalBundleMethod, PrimalKKTSolver, KKTResult from the pygeoinf top level; v2 exports the whole family from pygeoinf2.numerics, not from pygeoinf2's top level. |

### subsets — `subsets.py`

| v1 | what it did | v2 | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| `subsets.Subset` | Abstract base class for a subset of a HilbertSpace: knows its domain, decides membership via is_element, exposes its boundary, and supports CSG (complement / intersect / union) plus plotting. | `pygeoinf2.geometry.sets.Subset` | domain is now a required positional-only argument (no detached sets, no ValueError path); is_element renamed contains with rtol default 1e-6 -> 1e-9; complement is a method not a property; is_empty, boundary (abstract) and plot are gone from the base; operator overloads __and__/__or__/__invert__/__contains__ and __repr__ added; _check_domain helper added. |
| `subsets.Subset.domain` | The underlying Hilbert space the subset lives in. | `Subset.domain` | Same property, but the domain can no longer be None, so the ValueError('... does not have an associated domain.') path no longer exists. |
| `subsets.Subset.is_element` | Abstract membership oracle: True if x lies in the set, within relative tolerance rtol. | `Subset.contains(x, /, *, rtol=1e-9) and Subset.__contains__` | Renamed is_element -> contains; default rtol 1e-6 -> 1e-9; `x in subset` added at the default tolerance. Per-class tolerance scaling also changed (see tolerance_convention row). |
| `subsets.Subset.boundary` | Abstract property returning a new Subset representing the topological boundary dS. | `Ball.boundary, HalfSpace.boundary, Ellipsoid.boundary (concrete properties only)` | No longer an abstract member of Subset. Only Ball (-> BallSurface), HalfSpace (-> Hyperplane) and Ellipsoid (-> EllipsoidSurface) define it; EmptySet, UniversalSet, Complement, Intersection, Union, Hyperplane, BallSurface, EllipsoidSurface, Polytope, ConvexIntersection have no boundary at all (AttributeError rather than a set or NotImplementedError). Generic code cannot rely on s.boundary. |
| `subsets.Subset.complement` | Returns the complement S^c as a generic Complement wrapper around this set. | `Subset.complement() and ~subset` | Property -> method (call sites must add parentheses); `~s` added. EmptySet/UniversalSet/Complement overrides kept; the Intersection/Union De Morgan overrides are gone (base wrapper returned instead). |
| `subsets.Subset.intersect` | Returns S ∩ O. If every constituent is a ConvexSubset returns a ConvexIntersection (single max-functional); otherwise a generic Intersection. | `Subset.intersect(other, /) / ConvexSet.intersect / `&`` | Base returns Intersection([self, other]); flattening moved into Intersection.__init__ (now flattens either side and nested ConvexIntersections flatten in ConvexIntersection.__init__). Convex upgrade moved to ConvexSet.intersect and fires only when self is a ConvexSet and other is a ConvexSet: an existing plain Intersection whose parts are all convex, intersected with a further convex set, stays a plain Intersection (v1 re-examined all merged parts). Hyperplane, HalfSpace and Polytope are now ConvexSets so they do upgrade (v1 fell back to generic). `&` operator added — but `&` and intersect are NOT equivalent on every set: Polytope.__and__ (convex.py:511-522) shadows Subset.__and__, is typed for another Polytope and reads other.is_outer with no isinstance guard, so `polytope & ball` / `polytope & half_space` / `polytope & convex_intersection` raise AttributeError ('Ball' object has no attribute 'is_outer') where polytope.intersect(ball) returns a ConvexIntersection and v1 PolyhedralSet.intersect(ball) returned a working Intersection. Verified at runtime. |
| `subsets.Subset.union` | Returns S ∪ O as a generic Union. | `Subset.union(other, /) / `\|`` | Now flattens both operands (Union.__init__ flattens nested Unions; v1 flattened only the right operand); `\|` added; other is positional-only. |
| `subsets.EmptySet` | Represents the empty set ∅. | `pygeoinf2.geometry.sets.EmptySet` | Constructor now requires a domain (v1 allowed EmptySet()); no boundary property; complement is a method. |
| `subsets.EmptySet.is_element` | Always False. | `EmptySet.contains` | Renamed is_element -> contains; default rtol 1e-6 -> 1e-9 (unused either way); always False. Status aligned with the sibling is_element rows, which record the same rename and default change as ported_changed. |
| `subsets.EmptySet.complement` | Returns UniversalSet(self.domain). | `EmptySet.complement()` | Property -> method; returns UniversalSet(self._domain) as before. |
| `subsets.UniversalSet` | Represents the whole domain Ω. | `pygeoinf2.geometry.sets.UniversalSet` | Domain required; no boundary; complement is a method; no is_empty. |
| `subsets.UniversalSet.is_element` | Always True (no check that x actually belongs to the domain). | `UniversalSet.contains` | Renamed to contains; default rtol 1e-6 -> 1e-9 (unused); always True; still no check that x belongs to the domain. Status aligned with the sibling is_element rows. |
| `subsets.UniversalSet.complement` | Returns EmptySet(self.domain). | `UniversalSet.complement()` | Property -> method; returns EmptySet(domain). |
| `subsets.Complement.is_element` | Returns `not subset.is_element(x, rtol=rtol)`. | `Complement.contains` | Renamed; still `not subset.contains(x, rtol=rtol)` (tolerance favours the inner set); default rtol 1e-6 -> 1e-9. |
| `subsets.Complement.complement` | Returns the original wrapped set ((S^c)^c = S), avoiding double wrapping. | `Complement.complement()` | Property -> method; still returns the original wrapped set. |
| `subsets.Intersection` | Generic intersection S_1 ∩ S_2 ∩ ... of arbitrary subsets, used when they cannot be merged into a single convex functional. | `pygeoinf2.geometry.sets.Intersection` | Constructor now flattens nested Intersections itself; ValueError on empty kept; domain check kept (via _check_domain, `!=`); parts stored as a tuple; no boundary member and no De Morgan complement override; subsets argument positional-only. |
| `subsets.Intersection.subsets` | Direct (non-copied) access to the component list. | `Intersection.subsets -> tuple[Subset, ...]` | Returns an immutable tuple rather than the internal mutable list. |
| `subsets.Intersection.is_element` | True iff x is in ALL components (short-circuit all()). | `Intersection.contains` | Renamed; short-circuit all() kept; default rtol 1e-6 -> 1e-9. |
| `subsets.Intersection.complement` | De Morgan: returns Union(s.complement for s in subsets). | `Subset.complement() (inherited)` | De Morgan expansion into Union(s.complement ...) dropped; returns a generic Complement(Intersection) wrapper. Same set; different structure (no .subsets on the result), and the tolerance is applied inside the intersection rather than per complemented part. |
| `subsets.Union` | Generic union S_1 ∪ S_2 ∪ ... of subsets. | `pygeoinf2.geometry.sets.Union` | As Intersection: flattens nested Unions in the constructor, tuple storage, positional-only argument, no boundary, no De Morgan complement override. |
| `subsets.Union.subsets` | Direct (non-copied) access to the component list. | `Union.subsets -> tuple[Subset, ...]` | Tuple instead of the internal list. |
| `subsets.Union.is_element` | True iff x is in ANY component (short-circuit any()). | `Union.contains` | Renamed; any() kept; default rtol 1e-6 -> 1e-9. |
| `subsets.Union.complement` | De Morgan: returns Intersection(s.complement for s in subsets). | `Subset.complement() (inherited)` | De Morgan expansion into Intersection(s.complement ...) dropped; generic Complement wrapper returned. |
| `subsets.ConvexSubset` | Abstract closed convex set with dual representations: sublevel set of a convex functional and a support function h(q) = sup{<q,x> : x in S}. | `pygeoinf2.geometry.convex.ConvexSet` | Renamed ConvexSubset -> ConvexSet. No longer a SublevelSet: there is no defining form/level/gradient/Hessian, no open_set flag, no support_fn argument; the constructor is just Subset's (domain). The abstract contract is now project(x) (metric projection); contains defaults to \|\|x - project(x)\|\| <= rtol*max(\|\|x\|\|,1); support_function() is a non-abstract method that raises NotImplementedError by default; directional_bound is replaced by support_maximiser(direction). Gains indicator() (prox = projection), from_support_function (oracle sets), __add__ (Minkowski sum), translate(), and intersect override returning ConvexIntersection. |
| `subsets.ConvexSubset.support_function` | Abstract: returns the SupportFunction for this set or None if unavailable; must not raise on construction (errors deferred to evaluation). | `ConvexSet.support_function() -> SupportFunction` | Property -> method; 'unavailable' is now NotImplementedError raised at call time rather than returning None; not abstract (default raises); result is a pygeoinf2.numerics.convex.SupportFunction (a Functional with subgradient = maximiser) built anew on each call. |
| `subsets.ConvexSubset.directional_bound` | Abstract: returns (x_max, h(q)) — the extreme point argmax{<q,x> : x in S} and the support value in direction q. | `ConvexSet.support_maximiser(direction, /) plus support_function()(direction)` | Split into two calls: support_maximiser returns only the extreme point x_max (no (x_max, h(q)) tuple); the value is obtained separately via support_function()(direction) or SupportFunction.subgradient. Not abstract: default raises NotImplementedError. Note _OracleSet exposes its maximiser as .maximiser(direction)/.has_maximiser (convex.py:230-254) rather than overriding support_maximiser, so ConvexSet.support_maximiser on an oracle set built with maximiser= still raises NotImplementedError. |
| `subsets.ConvexIntersection` | Intersection of convex sets represented as a single ConvexSubset with max-functional F(x) = max_i (f_i(x) - c_i) and level 0, so optimisers see one convex constraint with gradient/Hessian of the active constraint. | `pygeoinf2.geometry.convex.ConvexIntersection` | No longer a single max-functional SublevelSet: there is no combined NonLinearForm F(x)=max_i(f_i(x)-c_i), no gradient/Hessian of the active constraint, no level, no open flag. It is a ConvexSet whose contains is all(parts) and whose project is Dykstra's algorithm over the parts (iterations=1000 default). Adds: flattening of nested ConvexIntersections, TypeError for non-convex parts, domain consistency check (v1 had none), support_bound. Still not a subclass of Intersection. |
| `subsets.ConvexIntersection.subsets` | Direct access to the individual convex constraints. | `ConvexIntersection.subsets -> tuple[ConvexSet, ...]` | Tuple instead of list. |
| `subsets.ConvexIntersection.support_function` | Always None: the support function of an intersection is not min_i σ_i (not sublinear), so none is provided. | `ConvexIntersection.support_function()` | Property returning None -> method raising NotImplementedError (with a message pointing at support_bound and inference.backus). |
| `subsets.ConvexIntersection.support_upper_bound` | Safe upper bound on the true support: min_i σ_{C_i}(direction). | `ConvexIntersection.support_bound(direction, /)` | Renamed support_upper_bound -> support_bound. Parts whose support_function() raises NotImplementedError (e.g. HalfSpace) are skipped instead of raising ValueError; raises NotImplementedError only when no part has one. Same min_i h_i value otherwise. Caveat: the NotImplementedError catch wraps the whole evaluation part.support_function()(direction), so a part whose support function exists but fails during evaluation is silently skipped as if unbounded. |
| `subsets.ConvexIntersection.directional_bound` | Not available: always raises NotImplementedError (true bound needs constrained maximisation over the intersection). | `ConvexSet.support_maximiser (inherited, raises NotImplementedError)` | Still unavailable, now under the name support_maximiser via the ConvexSet default; ConvexIntersection does not override it. |
| `subsets._EllipsoidalGeometry` | Private mixin shared by Ellipsoid and EllipsoidSurface: validates centre ∈ domain (domain.is_element) and radius >= 0, stores center/radius/operator and builds the quadratic NonLinearForm f(x) = <A(x-c), x-c> with gradient 2A(x-c) and Hessian 2A, level = radius**2. | `Ellipsoid.mahalanobis_squared / Ellipsoid.__init__ / EllipsoidSurface.__init__ (inline)` | The quadratic form <A(x-c),x-c> survives only as Ellipsoid.mahalanobis_squared (and inline in EllipsoidSurface.contains); radius is folded into the operator (level fixed at 1); there is no NonLinearForm, no gradient 2A(x-c), no Hessian 2A. Validation changed: centre membership check (domain.is_element(center)) dropped; instead the precision must carry Traits.SELF_ADJOINT\|POSITIVE_DEFINITE and (Ellipsoid only) map domain->domain (v1 checked neither). Shared via duplication, not a mixin. |
| `subsets.Ellipsoid` | Solid ellipsoid E = {x \| <A(x-c), x-c> <= r^2} (or < r^2 if open_set); a ConvexSubset built on _EllipsoidalGeometry. | `pygeoinf2.geometry.convex.Ellipsoid(domain, precision, /, *, centre=None, covariance=None)` | Signature rewritten: operator -> precision (positional), center -> centre (keyword, default zero), radius removed (fold into precision), inverse_operator -> covariance, inverse_sqrt_operator dropped entirely, open_set dropped. Precision must declare SELF_ADJOINT\|POSITIVE_DEFINITE traits or ValueError (an operator from LinearOperator.from_matrix carries Traits.NONE by default and is refused; v1 accepted any LinearOperator). Gains project (Newton on the secular equation; default CholeskySolver forms a dense matrix of I+lambda P twice per step), translate, mahalanobis_squared; support_maximiser raises AttributeError (docstring says ValueError) without covariance. |
| `subsets.Ellipsoid.center` | The centre vector c. | `Ellipsoid.centre` | Renamed center -> centre (British spelling), but more than a spelling change: a required, validated positional argument became an optional, unvalidated keyword. centre defaults to domain.zero() when omitted, and v1's check that the centre belongs to the domain (domain.is_element(center) -> ValueError 'Center vector must be in the domain.') is gone, so any object is accepted as a centre. |
| `subsets.Ellipsoid.operator` | The self-adjoint positive-definite metric operator A. | `Ellipsoid.precision` | Renamed operator -> precision; must carry SELF_ADJOINT\|POSITIVE_DEFINITE traits and have domain == codomain == the set's domain (validated). |
| `subsets.Ellipsoid.support_function` | Lazily constructs and caches an EllipsoidSupportFunction(domain, center, radius, operator, inverse_operator=..., inverse_sqrt_operator=...) from .convex_analysis. | `Ellipsoid.support_function() -> _EllipsoidSupport` | Method, not property; raises NotImplementedError immediately when covariance is None (docstring says ValueError; v1 always returned an object and deferred the error to evaluation); no caching (new object each call); the inverse_sqrt_operator route to h(q) is gone — only the covariance route exists. Value h(q) = <c,q> + sqrt(<Cq,q>) and maximiser c + Cq/sqrt(<Cq,q>) are computed in separate methods (two covariance applications where v1's fused value_and_support_point needed one). |
| `subsets.Ellipsoid.directional_bound` | Returns (x_max, h(q)) with x_max = c + r A^{-1}q / \|\|A^{-1/2} q\|\| obtained from support_function.support_point(direction), and h(q) = support_function(direction). | `Ellipsoid.support_maximiser(direction, /) + Ellipsoid.support_function()(direction)` | Split into two calls; returns only x_max = c + Cq/sqrt(<Cq,q>) (no tuple). Requires covariance= at construction; otherwise raises AttributeError (not NotImplementedError; docstring wrongly says ValueError). Zero direction returns the centre. No open-set warning. |
| `subsets.EllipsoidSurface` | Surface of an ellipsoid {x \| <A(x-c), x-c> = r^2}; a LevelSet built on _EllipsoidalGeometry. | `pygeoinf2.geometry.convex.EllipsoidSurface(domain, precision, /, *, centre=None)` | Signature rewritten as for Ellipsoid (radius folded, operator -> precision, centre keyword, trait check). No longer a LevelSet (no form/level). Has only precision, centre, contains; no boundary, no normalized, no project/sample (BallSurface has project and sample, EllipsoidSurface does not). Unlike Ellipsoid.__init__, does not check that precision.domain == precision.codomain == domain. |
| `subsets.EllipsoidSurface.center` | The centre vector c. | `EllipsoidSurface.centre` | Renamed center -> centre; now an optional keyword defaulting to domain.zero(), and the v1 centre-membership validation (domain.is_element(center)) is removed, so any object is accepted unchecked. Additionally EllipsoidSurface.__init__ (unlike Ellipsoid.__init__) does not check that precision.domain == precision.codomain == domain. |
| `subsets.EllipsoidSurface.operator` | The metric operator A. | `EllipsoidSurface.precision` | Renamed operator -> precision with trait requirement SELF_ADJOINT\|POSITIVE_DEFINITE. |
| `subsets.Ball` | Ball {x \| \|\|x-c\|\| <= r} (or < r): an Ellipsoid whose operator is domain.identity_operator(). | `pygeoinf2.geometry.convex.Ball(domain, /, *, radius=1.0, centre=None)` | Arguments are keyword-only with defaults (v1: positional center, radius); center -> centre; open_set removed (always closed; v1 default was open); no longer an Ellipsoid subclass (Ball(ConvexSet), so no operator/precision property and no mahalanobis form); radius 0 allowed and meaningful; radius property survives unchanged (convex.py:609-612). Gains project, translate, indicator() returning numerics.convex.BallIndicator, support_maximiser. |
| `subsets.Ball.is_element` | Fast-path override: computes dist = \|\|x - c\|\| directly and tests dist < r + margin (open) or dist <= r + margin, margin = rtol * max(1, r). | `Ball.contains` | Renamed; still one norm (fast path kept); closed only; tolerance is now offset <= r*(1+rtol), i.e. purely relative to r with no max(1, r) floor — for r<1 it is tighter than v1 and at r=0 it admits exactly the centre; default rtol 1e-9. Verified: Ball(X, radius=1e-3).contains(r*(1+1e-8)) is False in v2 but True under v1's rtol*max(1,r) margin. |
| `subsets.Ball.boundary` | Returns Sphere(domain, center, radius). | `Ball.boundary -> BallSurface(domain, radius=, centre=)` | Returns BallSurface (renamed from Sphere); raises ValueError for radius 0 because BallSurface requires radius > 0 (v1 Sphere accepted 0). |
| `subsets.Ball.support_function` | Lazily constructs and caches BallSupportFunction(domain, center, radius) from .convex_analysis; always available. | `Ball.support_function() -> SupportFunction.of_ball(domain, radius=, centre=)` | Method not property; builds numerics.convex._BallSupport anew on each call (no _support_fn cache); value r\|\|y\|\| + <c,y> and maximiser as before. |
| `subsets.Ball.directional_bound` | Returns (x_max, h(q)) with x_max = c + r q/\|\|q\|\| and h(q) = <q,c> + r\|\|q\|\|, via support_function.support_point / __call__. | `Ball.support_maximiser(direction, /) + Ball.support_function()(direction)` | Split into two calls, returns x_max only; zero direction returns centre (v1 returned (center, 0.0)); no open-set warning; exact ==0.0 test instead of <1e-14. Note the generic ConvexSet.translate(ball, v) path (_Translated) does not override support_maximiser and raises NotImplementedError, whereas Ball.translate's override works. |
| `subsets.Sphere` | Sphere {x \| \|\|x-c\|\| = r}: an EllipsoidSurface with the identity operator. | `pygeoinf2.geometry.convex.BallSurface(domain, /, *, radius=1.0, centre=None)` | Renamed Sphere -> BallSurface (Sphere now names the symmetric space). Keyword-only radius/centre with defaults; radius must be > 0 (v1 allowed >= 0); not an EllipsoidSurface subclass and not a ConvexSet; no operator property; radius property kept (convex.py:1079-1082). Gains project (nearest point, ValueError at the centre) and sample(rng=) (uniform on the surface via white noise). |
| `subsets.Sphere.is_element` | Fast-path override: True if \| \|\|x-c\|\| - r \| <= rtol * max(1, r). | `BallSurface.contains` | Renamed; still uses the norm directly; tolerance abs(d - r) <= rtol*r (no max(1, r) floor, so tighter for r<1); default rtol 1e-9. |
| `subsets.HyperPlane` | Hyperplane H = {x \| <a, x> = b}, a codimension-1 affine set given by normal a and offset b. | `pygeoinf2.geometry.convex.Hyperplane(domain, normal, /, *, offset=0.0)` | Renamed HyperPlane -> Hyperplane; normal_vector -> normal (positional-only); offset keyword-only with default 0. Now a ConvexSet (so it gains indicator(), translate, Minkowski __add__, and `&` with another ConvexSet upgrades to ConvexIntersection). Zero-normal test is exact squared_norm == 0 (v1: norm < 1e-14). Loses normal_norm, distance_to, boundary, dimension. support_function() inherits NotImplementedError (v1 had none either). |
| `subsets.HyperPlane.is_element` | True if \|<a,x> - b\| <= rtol * max(1, \|b\|). | `Hyperplane.contains` | Renamed; tolerance scale changed from max(1, \|b\|) to max(\|b\|, \|\|x\|\|*\|\|a\|\|, 1) so it also scales with the point; default rtol 1e-9. |
| `subsets.HalfSpace` | Closed half-space {x \| <a,x> <= b} (default) or {x \| <a,x> >= b}. | `pygeoinf2.geometry.convex.HalfSpace(domain, normal, /, *, offset=0.0)` | normal_vector -> normal (positional-only), offset keyword-only default 0; inequality_type removed ('<=' only; '>=' needs a negated normal and offset). Now a ConvexSet (indicator/prox, translate, Minkowski, `&` upgrade). project changed from projection-onto-boundary to the metric projection (identity inside). Loses distance_to, normal_norm, is_bounded, is_empty and support_function (inherits NotImplementedError). Keeps boundary -> Hyperplane. Zero-normal test exact. |
| `subsets.HalfSpace.is_element` | '<=': <a,x> <= b + tol; '>=': <a,x> >= b - tol; tol = rtol * max(1, \|b\|). | `HalfSpace.contains` | Renamed; '<=' only; tolerance scale max(\|b\|, \|\|x\|\|*\|\|a\|\|, 1) instead of max(1, \|b\|) (now recomputes \|\|a\|\| via domain.norm each call rather than using the cached squared norm); default rtol 1e-9. |
| `subsets.HalfSpace.project` | Orthogonal projection of x onto the boundary hyperplane {z \| <a,z> = b} (independent of inequality type; NOT the projection onto the half-space itself). | `HalfSpace.project(x, /)` | Semantics changed: v2 is the metric projection onto the half-space (returns x unchanged when <a,x> <= b; otherwise drops to the plane). v1 projected every point onto the boundary plane regardless of side. v1's map is available as half_space.boundary.project(x). The change is documented in the module docstring (convex.py:17-21) and demonstrated in examples/17_sets.py:42-51. |
