| `subsets.PolyhedralSet` | Polyhedral set P = ∩_i H_i, the intersection of finitely many HalfSpace objects. | `pygeoinf2.geometry.convex.Polytope(domain, half_spaces, /, *, outer: bool)` | Renamed PolyhedralSet -> Polytope; a new REQUIRED keyword outer (True = contains the set it approximates) must be passed; half_spaces positional-only and stored as a tuple. Domain check is `!=` (structural HilbertSpace.__eq__, spaces.py:130-136) instead of v1's identity check. Now a ConvexSet: gains project (Dykstra, iterations=1000), indicator(), is_outer, and an `__and__` override merging constraint lists (refuses mixing inner/outer). That override is a REGRESSION for mixed operands: it is typed only for Polytope and reads other.is_outer with no isinstance guard, so `polytope & ball`, `polytope & half_space`, `polytope & convex_intersection` raise AttributeError ('Ball' object has no attribute 'is_outer') instead of producing a ConvexIntersection; only the method form polytope.intersect(ball) works (via ConvexSet.intersect). v1 PolyhedralSet.intersect(ball) returned a working generic Intersection. Verified at runtime. Loses boundary/is_bounded/is_empty (all raised in v1) and support_function returns via base NotImplementedError. |
| `subsets.PolyhedralSet.is_element` | True iff x satisfies every half-space (short-circuits on the first failure). | `Polytope.contains` | Renamed; all() short-circuit kept; each HalfSpace.contains now uses the point-scaled tolerance; default rtol 1e-9; an odd hasattr(plane, 'contains') guard returns False for non-set entries. |
| `subsets.PolyhedralSet.support_function` | Always None (inf_i σ_{H_i} would require LP-based evaluation). | `Polytope.support_function() (inherited ConvexSet default)` | Property returning None -> inherited method raising NotImplementedError; still no LP-based evaluation. |
| `subsets.behaviour.tolerance_convention` | Every membership test uses an absolute margin rtol * max(1.0, \|reference\|), where reference is the level c (SublevelSet/LevelSet), the radius r (Ball/Sphere — applied to the distance, not r^2) or the offset b (HyperPlane/HalfSpace). | `contains(x, /, *, rtol=1e-9) on every set` | Keyword-only rtol kept, default 1e-6 -> 1e-9. The uniform rule 'margin = rtol*max(1, \|reference\|)' is gone; each class scales differently: Ball: d <= r*(1+rtol) (no floor of 1); BallSurface: \|d-r\| <= rtol*r (no floor); Ellipsoid: m^2 <= 1+rtol and EllipsoidSurface: \|m^2-1\| <= rtol (absolute on the normalised level); Hyperplane/HalfSpace: rtol*max(\|b\|, \|\|x\|\|*\|\|a\|\|, 1); ConvexSet default: \|\|x-P(x)\|\| <= rtol*max(\|\|x\|\|,1). No open sets, so the 'open still permissive' quirk is gone. |
| `subsets.behaviour.matrix_free` | No class in this module forms a dense or sparse matrix; all membership, distance, projection, gradient/Hessian and directional-bound computations use HilbertSpace vector algebra (inner_product, norm, add, subtract, multiply) and LinearOperator application. | `geometry/sets.py, geometry/convex.py` | All membership, support values, support maximisers, half-space/hyperplane/ball/surface projections and Dykstra remain matrix-free (inner_product/norm/axpy/scale/operator application). The one dense place is new: Ellipsoid.project defaults to CholeskySolver (numerics/solvers.py:550-562 factorises the dense Galerkin matrix; DirectSolver.requires_coordinates = True, solvers.py:445-452) applied to identity + lambda*precision TWICE per Newton step (convex.py:996 for the derivative, :1004 for the update; up to 2*iterations = 200 factorisations), so a projection onto an ellipsoid is dense by default on a coordinate space and fails on one with no component map unless solver= is passed. That escape hatch does NOT reach the intersection machinery: _dykstra (convex.py:386-416, line 410 `current = part.project(shifted)`) calls part.project bare and ConvexIntersection.project / Polytope.project pass only iterations, so ConvexIntersection.project, Polytope.project and the indicator prox of any intersection containing an Ellipsoid always use the dense CholeskySolver and raise TypeError on a coordinate-free space ('OpaqueSpace provides no coordinate map'; verified at runtime for (Ellipsoid & Ball).project(x) and .indicator().prox(x, 1.0)). So the v2 replacement for v1's max-functional ConvexIntersection is coordinate-bound whenever an ellipsoid is a part — the common credible-region case — whereas v1's max-functional needed only operator application. v1 had no ellipsoid projection, so this is a dense new capability rather than a regression of an existing one. The v1 Hessian `2.0 * operator` is simply gone (no form). |
| `subsets.behaviour.convex_intersection_max_functional` | Subset.intersect automatically upgrades to ConvexIntersection when all parts are ConvexSubset, producing one NonLinearForm F(x)=max_i(f_i(x)-c_i) whose gradient/Hessian come from the active (argmax) constraint — a subgradient at ties. | `ConvexSet.intersect -> ConvexIntersection (membership + Dykstra projection)` | The automatic upgrade to a convex intersection is kept (ConvexSet.intersect / `&`, and it now also covers HalfSpace, Hyperplane, Polytope, oracle sets — except that `&` with a Polytope on the left is Polytope-only, see PolyhedralSet row). What is lost is the representation: there is no combined functional F(x)=max_i(f_i(x)-c_i) with active-constraint gradient/Hessian for a smooth constrained optimiser. Instead the intersection is consumed through indicator() (prox = Dykstra projection, ConvexSet.indicator convex.py:133-139) or contains(). Flattening of nested ConvexIntersections is new (v1 nested them). |
| `subsets.behaviour.domain_validation_variants` | Intersection and Union reject components with s.domain != domain (ValueError); PolyhedralSet rejects hs.domain is not domain (identity); ConvexIntersection performs no domain check at all; _EllipsoidalGeometry checks domain.is_element(center). | `Subset._check_domain, Polytope.__init__, Ellipsoid.__init__` | Unified to one rule: Intersection, Union and ConvexIntersection all call Subset._check_domain (`!=`, i.e. HilbertSpace.__eq__ structural key comparison, spaces.py:130-136) and Polytope uses `!=` too (v1 used identity for PolyhedralSet). ConvexIntersection now validates domains (v1 did not; IMPROVED). Lost: the centre-membership check domain.is_element(center) of _EllipsoidalGeometry — v2 Ellipsoid/EllipsoidSurface/Ball/BallSurface accept any centre object unchecked. New: Ellipsoid/EllipsoidSurface require the precision to carry SELF_ADJOINT\|POSITIVE_DEFINITE traits, and Ellipsoid (but not EllipsoidSurface) requires precision.domain == precision.codomain == domain. |

### subspaces — `subspaces.py`

| v1 | what it did | v2 | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| `subspaces.OrthogonalProjector` | Subclass of LinearOperator representing an orthogonal projection P = P* = P^2 on a Hilbert space; described in its docstring as the 'internal engine for subspace projections'. | `pygeoinf2.geometry.subspaces.OrthogonalProjector` | Signature is now OrthogonalProjector(domain, mapping, /, *, complement: OrthogonalProjector \| None = None): the keyword `complement_projector` (any LinearOperator) became keyword-only `complement` typed as an OrthogonalProjector; domain/mapping are positional-only. The operator is declared with traits SELF_ADJOINT \| IDEMPOTENT (PSD by closure) instead of being built via LinearOperator(domain, domain, mapping, adjoint_mapping=mapping); self-adjointness is still enforced by routing _value and _adjoint_value through the same callable and idempotence is still unchecked. Matrix-free as before. Gains a `basis()` method and an `onto_kernel` classmethod (new). Note that basis() carries a rank over-reporting bug (see subspaces.AffineSubspace.get_tangent_basis). |
| `subspaces.OrthogonalProjector.complement` | Returns the projector onto the orthogonal complement, (I - P). | `OrthogonalProjector.complement()` | Property became a method `complement()`. Return type is OrthogonalProjector (lazily built as x -> x - P(x) with `complement=self`, so P.complement().complement() is the original object) instead of a generic LinearOperator `identity - P`. Caching on the instance is retained. |
| `subspaces.OrthogonalProjector.from_basis` | Constructs the projector onto the span of the given basis vectors as a sum of rank-one tensor products P = sum_i e_i (x) e_i. | `OrthogonalProjector.from_basis(domain, vectors, /, *, orthonormal=False)` | `basis_vectors` renamed `vectors` (positional-only); `orthonormalize: bool = True` replaced by the inverted-sense keyword-only `orthonormal: bool = False` (default behaviour unchanged: orthonormalise unless told the family already is). Orthonormalisation uses domain.orthonormal_basis (drops dependent vectors at relative rtol 1e-10, reorthogonalises once) instead of domain.gram_schmidt (which raised ValueError on dependence at absolute 1e-12), so the result rank is the true rank rather than an error. Action is the same tensor-product sum (k inner products + k axpy) written inline rather than via LinearOperator.self_adjoint_from_tensor_product. Empty (or entirely dependent) input returns an OrthogonalProjector wrapping the zero map rather than v1's plain domain.zero_operator, so `.complement()` works on it. |
| `subspaces.AffineSubspace` | Subclass of Subset representing an affine subspace A = x0 + V of a Hilbert space, given by an orthogonal projector P onto the tangent space V and a translation x0. Serves both as a geometric subset (projection, membership) and as a constraint definition {u \| B(u) = w} for Bayesian conditioning of Gaussian measures. | `pygeoinf2.geometry.subspaces.AffineSubspace` | Base class changed from Subset to ConvexSet (gains indicator(), support_function(), convex intersect, `x in S`). Constructor reduced to AffineSubspace(projector, /, *, translation=None): the constraint_operator, constraint_value, solver and preconditioner parameters are gone (an equation can only be attached by from_linear_equation / from_kernel / with_translation / with_constraint_value, which set private _equation/_solver/_inverse). The translation is no longer validated with domain.is_element (v1 raised ValueError 'Translation vector not in domain.'). No default CholeskySolver is installed. Gains dimension() (new, needs coordinates). |
| `subspaces.AffineSubspace.tangent_space` | Returns the LinearSubspace V parallel to this affine subspace, built as LinearSubspace(self.projector). | `AffineSubspace.tangent` | Renamed `tangent_space` -> `tangent`. Semantics identical: LinearSubspace(self._projector), dropping equation and solver. |
| `subspaces.AffineSubspace.get_tangent_basis` | Extracts an orthonormal basis of the tangent space by applying P to every standard basis vector e_i of the domain and running a tolerant Gram-Schmidt to discard dependent projections. | `OrthogonalProjector.basis() (call as subspace.projector.basis())` | Moved from the subspace to the projector and renamed `basis()`. Same algorithm shape (apply P to each domain.basis_vector(i), then orthonormalise) but with a CORRECTNESS REGRESSION, not merely a tolerance convention change: v1 first discarded every P e_i whose ABSOLUTE norm was <= 1e-10 and then ran Gram-Schmidt with the same absolute cut-off; v2 hands all dim projected vectors to domain.orthonormal_basis, whose only test is residual_norm > 1e-10 * norm(input), with norm(input) floored at 1e-300. When an ambient basis vector e_i lies in the orthogonal complement of the range, P e_i is rounding noise of size ~1e-16 whose direction is outside the range; it passes the relative test, is normalised to unit length and returned as a 'basis vector'. basis() therefore over-reports the rank and returns vectors not in the range, precisely for the common coordinate-aligned ('fix component k') constraints. Verified in this audit: AffineSubspace.from_linear_equation(<0.3 e_0, .>, 1) on EuclideanSpace(6) with the default CG gives len(basis()) == 6 while dimension() == 5 and norm(P e_0) == 1.1e-16 (v1 get_tangent_basis gives 5); over 200 random constraints fixing 1-3 coordinates of R^20 with random weights, v2 basis() returns the wrong rank in 131/200 cases (default CG) and 55/200 (CholeskySolver()), v1 in 0/200. dimension() (trace) and to_hyperplanes() (via complement().basis(), where the complement of a kernel projector annihilates kernel directions exactly rather than to rounding) were correct in all sampled cases, so the damage is confined to basis() and its callers. Explicitly calls require_coordinates(domain). Still costs dim projector applications; for a projector built by from_linear_equation/onto_kernel with the default CG solver each application is a CG solve. Not recorded as a decision in DESIGN.md or REVIEW*.md. |
| `subspaces.AffineSubspace.constraint_operator` | Returns the operator B defining the subspace as {u \| B(u) = w}. | `AffineSubspace.constraint_operator` | When the subspace has no explicit equation it now raises AttributeError (pointing at to_hyperplanes) instead of falling back to the singular projector.complement (I - P). Explicit case unchanged (returns the stored A). |
| `subspaces.AffineSubspace.constraint_value` | Returns the right-hand side w of the defining equation B(u) = w. | `AffineSubspace.constraint_value` | Raises AttributeError when there is no explicit equation instead of computing (I - P) x0 as the implicit right-hand side. |
| `subspaces.AffineSubspace.pseudo_inverse` | Returns the right pseudo-inverse B^dagger = B* (B B*)^{-1} of the explicit constraint operator. | `AffineSubspace.pseudo_inverse()` | Property became a method. Returns `operator.adjoint @ inverse` where `inverse` is the cached (A A*)^{-1} built once at construction (self._inverse), falling back to _normal_inverse(operator, self._solver); v1 rebuilt G = B B* and re-solved on every access. Default solver is CGSolver(rtol=1e-12) (matrix-free, a CG solve per application) instead of CholeskySolver(galerkin=True) (dense Galerkin matrix, one factorisation). No isinstance(IterativeLinearSolver) preconditioner branch. Missing equation raises AttributeError (via constraint_operator), not ValueError. |
| `subspaces.AffineSubspace.projection_operator` | Returns the affine orthogonal projection onto the subspace as an AffineOperator, P_A(x) = P x + (I - P) x0. | `AffineSubspace.projection_operator()` | Property became a method. Same construction AffineOperator(P, t - P t), offset computed at call time. |
| `subspaces.AffineSubspace.boundary` | Override of the Subset boundary: an affine subspace has no boundary, so returns EmptySet(self.domain). | `AffineSubspace.boundary()` | Property became a method, and the ANSWER changed: v1 returned EmptySet(self.domain) ('an affine subspace has no boundary'); v2 returns `self` (every point of a proper affine subspace is a boundary point in the ambient space). Both are defensible readings but they disagree, so any v1 code testing `isinstance(sub.boundary, EmptySet)` breaks. |
| `subspaces.AffineSubspace.from_linear_equation` | Constructs the subspace {u \| B(u) = w} from a linear operator and right-hand side, computing the minimum-norm point x0 = B* (B B*)^{-1} w and the projector P = I - B* (B B*)^{-1} B. | `AffineSubspace.from_linear_equation(operator, value, /, *, solver=None)` | `preconditioner` parameter removed (attach it to the solver instead). Default solver changed from CholeskySolver(galerkin=True) to CGSolver(rtol=1e-12); A A* is tagged POSITIVE_DEFINITE by assertion (full-row-rank precondition; CG stalls rather than errors on a rank-deficient A, though on a CONSISTENT singular system it was observed to converge). The docstring's suggestion to pass a least-squares solver for a rank-deficient constraint does work in practice: _normal_inverse calls solver(normal) with no isinstance check and LeastSquaresSolver.__call__ returns a pseudo-inverse LinearOperator, so LSQRSolver() duck-types through (verified: 3-row rank-2 A on R^10 with consistent b gives \|\|A x - b\|\| = 1.5e-14 and dimension() == 8), although the type hint `LinearSolver \| None` does not admit it. The inverse (A A*)^{-1} is built once and stored as _inverse, then shared by the projector, the translation, pseudo_inverse, with_constraint_value and with_translation (v1 only baked it into the projector). The projector is built by OrthogonalProjector._onto_kernel(operator, inverse) WITHOUT a pre-supplied complement, so P.complement() is the lazily built x - P(x) rather than v1's B* G^{-1} B. Stores (operator, value), solver. |
| `subspaces.AffineSubspace.from_tangent_basis` | Constructs an affine subspace geometrically from a point x0 and basis vectors spanning the tangent space V; the constraint is implicit, (I - P)u = (I - P)x0. | `AffineSubspace.from_tangent_basis(domain, vectors, /, *, translation=None)` | `orthonormalize`, `solver` and `preconditioner` parameters removed: the vectors are always orthonormalised (via orthonormal_basis, dependent ones dropped) and no solver can be attached. The UserWarning about the singular implicit constraint is gone (there is no implicit-constraint conditioning path to warn about). The result has no equation: constraint_operator/constraint_value raise AttributeError rather than returning I - P and (I-P) x0. |
| `subspaces.AffineSubspace.from_complement_basis` | Constructs the subspace {u \| <u - x0, v_i> = 0} orthogonal to a set of complement basis vectors, producing an EXPLICIT constraint operator B: domain -> EuclideanSpace(m) with B(u)_i = <e_i, u>. | `AffineSubspace.from_complement_basis(domain, vectors, /, *, translation=None)` | Now returns cls(OrthogonalProjector.from_basis(domain, vectors).complement(), translation=translation) and NOTHING ELSE: the explicit constraint operator B: domain -> EuclideanSpace(m), B(u)_i = <e_i, u>, its value w = B(x0), and the hard-coded CholeskySolver are no longer built. has_explicit_equation is therefore False, so constraint_operator/constraint_value/pseudo_inverse/with_constraint_value raise AttributeError and the constrained-inversion parameterisation refuses it (inference/point.py:918-924). `orthonormalize` parameter removed (always orthonormalised). To recover the v1 explicit form a user must instead write AffineSubspace.from_linear_equation(LinearOperator.from_vectors(X, vs).adjoint, values) or from_hyperplanes([...]). |
| `subspaces.AffineSubspace.from_hyperplanes` | Constructs an affine subspace as the intersection of m hyperplanes {x \| <a_i, x> = b_i}, by assembling B: domain -> EuclideanSpace(m), w = (b_i) and delegating to from_linear_equation. | `AffineSubspace.from_hyperplanes(hyperplanes, /)` | `solver` and `preconditioner` parameters removed entirely: the A A* solve always uses the CGSolver default and there is no way to pass a solver (unlike from_linear_equation). The constraint operator is built as LinearOperator.from_vectors(domain, normals).adjoint instead of Python loops of inner products; on a CoordinateSpace with fast paths that is a _ColumnOperator holding the normals' components as a (dim, m) array. Reads `plane.normal` / `plane.offset` (v1 `normal_vector`/`offset`); a missing attribute is no longer re-raised as ImportError. Empty list and mismatched domains still raise ValueError. Normals still not orthonormalised; delegates to from_linear_equation as before. |
| `subspaces.AffineSubspace.to_hyperplanes` | Decomposes an explicitly-defined subspace into a list of HyperPlane objects, one per component of the constraint codomain: a_i = B*(e_i), b_i = w[i]. | `AffineSubspace.to_hyperplanes()` | Algorithm changed: v1 used the stored equation (a_i = B*(e_i), b_i = w[i], m applications of B*, ValueError if implicit or codomain not Euclidean); v2 ignores the stored equation and computes an orthonormal basis of the complement via self._projector.complement().basis() (dim projector applications + Gram-Schmidt, requires coordinates), with offsets <n_i, translation>. Consequences: works for implicit subspaces too (no ValueError), returns codim hyperplanes (rank-reduced, so a rank-deficient equation gives fewer planes than v1), returns geometry.convex.Hyperplane(domain, normal, offset=) rather than subsets.HyperPlane, and is O(dim) rather than O(m) in projector/operator applications (each a CG solve for an equation-built subspace with the default solver). Despite relying on basis(), it was rank-correct in all 200 sampled coordinate-aligned cases, because the complement of a kernel projector (x -> A*(AA*)^{-1}A x) annihilates kernel directions exactly rather than to rounding; it is the only non-test caller of basis(). |
| `subspaces.AffineSubspace.is_element` | Override of Subset.is_element: returns True if the projection residual \|\|x - P_A(x)\|\| is at most rtol * max(1, \|\|x\|\|). | `AffineSubspace.contains(x, /, *, rtol=1e-9) (inherited from ConvexSet), also `x in subspace`` | Renamed `is_element` -> `contains` (base-class method, not overridden on AffineSubspace). Same test \|\|x - project(x)\|\| <= rtol * max(\|\|x\|\|, 1), but the default rtol tightened from 1e-6 to 1e-9. |
| `subspaces.AffineSubspace.with_translation` | Returns a new parallel AffineSubspace passing through new_translation, sharing the same projector, solver and preconditioner. | `AffineSubspace.with_translation(translation, /)` | Argument is positional-only and no longer validated against the domain (v1 raised ValueError). Explicit equation is kept with value recomputed as A t (same as v1), and now also carries the cached (A A*)^{-1} so a later pseudo_inverse() costs no new solve. Always returns AffineSubspace (same as v1). Preconditioner no longer a separate attribute to carry. |
| `subspaces.AffineSubspace.with_constraint_value` | Returns a new parallel AffineSubspace satisfying B(u) = new_value, with translation computed as pseudo_inverse(new_value) (the minimum-norm solution). | `AffineSubspace.with_constraint_value(value, /)` | Positional-only argument. Reuses the cached (A A*)^{-1} (self._inverse) so no new Gram solve/factorisation (v1 triggered a fresh one via pseudo_inverse). Raises AttributeError (via constraint_operator) instead of ValueError when there is no explicit equation. Shares projector, operator, solver as before. |
| `subspaces.LinearSubspace` | Subclass of AffineSubspace representing a linear subspace, i.e. an affine subspace through the origin (translation = domain.zero). | `pygeoinf2.geometry.subspaces.LinearSubspace` | Constructor unchanged (projector only, positional-only). Inherits ConvexSet via AffineSubspace. Overrides project() to apply P directly (skips the zero translation). Classmethods still poke private attributes (_equation, _solver, _inverse) after construction. No longer used by an isinstance check in geometric conditioning (that method is gone). LinearSubspace.from_complement_basis classmethod is absent (see its row). |
| `subspaces.LinearSubspace.complement` | Returns the orthogonal complement V^perp as a new LinearSubspace built from projector.complement. | `LinearSubspace.complement()` | Property became a method. Built as LinearSubspace(self._projector.complement()); since projector.complement() is now always an OrthogonalProjector there is no wrapping of a generic operator via its private _mapping, and complement().complement() returns the original projector object (v1 rebuilt I - P_perp). Deliberately shadows Subset.complement (set-theoretic complement) — `~subspace` therefore yields the orthogonal complement, unlike every other Subset. Still carries no equation or solver. |
| `subspaces.LinearSubspace.from_kernel` | Constructs the kernel (null space) K = {u \| A(u) = 0} of an operator as a LinearSubspace with an explicit constraint. | `LinearSubspace.from_kernel(operator, /, *, solver=None)` | `preconditioner` parameter removed; default solver CGSolver(rtol=1e-12) instead of CholeskySolver(galerkin=True); A A* asserted POSITIVE_DEFINITE (full-row-rank precondition). Records equation (A, codomain.zero()), solver and the shared (A A*)^{-1} directly rather than via AffineSubspace.from_linear_equation. One solve at construction as in v1; pseudo_inverse() reuses it. |
| `subspaces.LinearSubspace.from_basis` | Constructs the linear span of a set of basis vectors as a LinearSubspace with an implicit constraint. | `LinearSubspace.from_basis(domain, vectors, /, *, orthonormal=False)` | `basis_vectors` -> `vectors` (positional-only); `orthonormalize=True` -> inverted-sense `orthonormal=False` (default behaviour the same); `solver` and `preconditioner` parameters removed. Orthonormalisation drops dependent vectors instead of raising. Still no warning on a missing solver (there is nothing to warn about). |
| `subspaces.behaviour.default_cholesky_galerkin_solver` | Wherever an explicit constraint operator B exists and no solver is given (AffineSubspace.__init__, from_linear_equation, from_complement_basis, from_hyperplanes, from_kernel), the Gram operator G = B B* is inverted with CholeskySolver(galerkin=True). | `_normal_inverse(operator, solver) -> (solver or CGSolver(rtol=1e-12))(A A* with POSITIVE_DEFINITE trait)` | Default changed from the dense CholeskySolver(galerkin=True) to a matrix-free CGSolver(rtol=1e-12): no dense Galerkin matrix is formed by default, but each application of the kernel projector, pseudo-inverse or minimum-norm translation now runs a CG iteration on A A* rather than a back-substitution against a one-off factorisation. CholeskySolver() can still be passed (it picks the Galerkin form itself, no galerkin= flag). from_hyperplanes offers no solver at all. A A* is tagged POSITIVE_DEFINITE by claim, so a rank-deficient A stalls CG rather than raising as Cholesky would (on a consistent singular system CG was observed to converge anyway). Since _normal_inverse does a plain solver(normal) call with no type check, an LSQRSolver (a LeastSquaresSolver, not a LinearSolver) also works as the 'solver', giving a pseudo-inverse of A A*. |
| `subspaces.behaviour.explicit_vs_implicit_constraint` | A subspace is either 'explicit' (B, w stored; from_linear_equation, from_complement_basis, from_hyperplanes, from_kernel) or 'implicit' (only P stored; constraint_operator falls back to the singular I - P and constraint_value to (I-P)x0; from_tangent_basis, LinearSubspace.from_basis, tangent_space, LinearSubspace.complement, direct construction). | `AffineSubspace.has_explicit_equation and the AttributeError-raising constraint_operator/constraint_value` | The dichotomy survives (has_explicit_equation), but the implicit fallbacks are removed: constraint_operator/constraint_value raise AttributeError instead of returning the singular I - P and (I-P) x0, so implicit subspaces cannot be conditioned or parameterised at all (no MinRes path). Membership changed: from_complement_basis is now IMPLICIT (was explicit); from_kernel remains explicit; direct construction, from_tangent_basis, from_basis, tangent, complement remain implicit. Explicit-only operations (pseudo_inverse, with_constraint_value) raise AttributeError not ValueError; to_hyperplanes is no longer explicit-only. The from_tangent_basis UserWarning is gone. |
| `subspaces.behaviour.complement_caching` | OrthogonalProjector caches its complement (I - P); constructors that already know the complement (from_linear_equation: B* G^{-1} B; from_complement_basis: sum of tensor products of the complement basis) pass it in so it is never re-derived as identity - P. | `OrthogonalProjector._complement cache with complement=self back-reference; AffineSubspace._inverse cache` | Complement caching kept and improved (complement().complement() is the original object; from_complement_basis obtains the tensor-sum projector as the stored complement of its result). Changed: from_linear_equation/onto_kernel no longer pre-supply B* G^{-1} B as the complement — complement() is the lazily built x - P(x), i.e. one extra subtraction per application (negligible). New: (A A*)^{-1} is cached on the subspace (_inverse) and reused by pseudo_inverse, with_constraint_value and with_translation, whereas v1 pseudo_inverse re-solved on every access. |
| `subspaces.behaviour.matrix_free_projectors` | All projectors are LinearOperators defined by callables (tensor-product sums, x - P_perp(x), or B* G^{-1} B compositions); constraint operators from complement bases / hyperplanes are Python loops of inner products with hand-written adjoints. No dense or sparse matrix is formed outside the linear solver. | `callable-based OrthogonalProjector; LinearOperator.from_vectors for hyperplane constraints` | Projectors remain matrix-free callables (tensor sums, x - A*(AA*)^{-1}A x, x - P x). The default Gram solve is now iterative, so nothing dense is formed unless a DirectSolver is passed (v1 formed a dense Galerkin matrix by default). One representation change: from_hyperplanes' constraint operator is LinearOperator.from_vectors(...).adjoint, which on a CoordinateSpace with component fast paths is a _ColumnOperator that stores the m normals' components as a (dim, m) array and applies them by matvec (columns computed lazily); on coordinate-free spaces it is the same inner-product loop as v1. The from_complement_basis explicit constraint operator no longer exists at all. |
| `subspaces.behaviour.tolerances` | get_tangent_basis uses a hard-coded absolute tolerance 1e-10 for dropping near-zero / dependent vectors; is_element uses rtol=1e-6 scaled by max(1, \|\|x\|\|). | `orthonormal_basis rtol=1e-10 (relative, no absolute floor); ConvexSet.contains rtol=1e-9; CGSolver(rtol=1e-12)` | Tangent-basis extraction switched from v1's ABSOLUTE 1e-10 norm floor on P e_i (plus an absolute 1e-10 Gram-Schmidt cut-off) to orthonormal_basis's purely RELATIVE threshold residual > 1e-10 * norm(input) with the input norm floored at 1e-300. This is a loss of a guard, not a convention change: the absolute floor is what made get_tangent_basis rank-correct when an ambient basis vector is numerically annihilated by the projector; a purely relative threshold cannot distinguish a genuine 1e-16-norm direction from rounding noise, so v2 basis() admits noise vectors lying outside the range (131/200 and 55/200 wrong ranks for default CG and CholeskySolver() respectively on coordinate-aligned constraints in R^20; v1 0/200). Membership default rtol tightened from 1e-6 to 1e-9 (same max(1, \|\|x\|\|) scaling); the default Gram solve has its own rtol=1e-12 CG tolerance (v1's Cholesky was exact to rounding). |
| `subspaces.behaviour.local_imports_circularity` | condition_gaussian_measure imports LinearForwardProblem and LinearBayesianInversion inside the method; to_hyperplanes imports HyperPlane inside the method; GaussianMeasure is imported only under TYPE_CHECKING. | `local imports of Hyperplane (.convex), AffineOperator and require_coordinates/LinearOperator (..algebra.operators)` | The lazy imports of LinearForwardProblem/LinearBayesianInversion and the TYPE_CHECKING import of GaussianMeasure are gone with condition_gaussian_measure; the subspace module no longer depends on the inference or probability layers. Hyperplane is still imported locally (from .convex instead of .subsets, no ImportError re-raise). New local imports of AffineOperator, LinearOperator and require_coordinates inside methods, although LinearOperator and require_coordinates are already imported at module level (line 30) — redundant. Module-level imports: numpy, LinearOperator/require_coordinates, HilbertSpace, CGSolver/LinearSolver, Traits, ConvexSet. Adds __all__. |
| `subspaces.behaviour.empty_basis_zero_operator` | OrthogonalProjector.from_basis([]) returns domain.zero_operator(domain), a plain LinearOperator rather than an OrthogonalProjector; downstream AffineSubspace/LinearSubspace built from it will have a projector lacking the .complement property. | `OrthogonalProjector.from_basis returns cls(domain, lambda x: domain.zero()) for an empty or wholly dependent family` | An empty basis (or one whose orthonormalisation leaves nothing) now yields a genuine OrthogonalProjector wrapping the zero map, so `.complement()` works (giving the identity projector) and AffineSubspace/LinearSubspace built from it are fully functional; v1 returned a plain domain.zero_operator LinearOperator lacking .complement. |

### forward_problem_inversion — `forward_problem.py, inversion.py`

| v1 | what it did | v2 | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| `forward_problem.ForwardProblem` | General (possibly nonlinear) forward problem: a forward operator mapping model space to data space, with an optional GaussianMeasure describing the data error distribution. | `pygeoinf2.inference.problem.ForwardProblem` | Keyword renamed data_error_measure -> error, and it now accepts a ProbabilityMeasure OR a geometry Subset (set-valued data relation) or None. forward_operator is typed Operator (any v2 operator). The domain check is only applied when the error object exposes a .domain attribute (v1 always checked; Subset does expose .domain so set-valued errors are covered). The base class now also carries synthetic_data, chi_squared, chi_squared_from_residual, critical_chi_squared, chi_squared_test and the new consistency_set, so these work for nonlinear forward operators (v1 had them only on LinearForwardProblem). Adds __repr__. |
| `forward_problem.ForwardProblem.data_error_measure_set` | True if a data error measure was supplied at construction. | `ForwardProblem.has_error` | Renamed data_error_measure_set -> has_error. Semantics widened: True also when the uncertainty is a Subset rather than a measure, so it no longer guarantees that error_measure will succeed (that raises TypeError for a set). |
| `forward_problem.ForwardProblem.data_error_measure` | Returns the Gaussian measure from which data errors are drawn. | `ForwardProblem.error_measure (plus .error and .error_set)` | Renamed data_error_measure -> error_measure; return type is ProbabilityMeasure not necessarily GaussianMeasure. Still raises AttributeError when nothing was supplied (message changed to 'This problem has no data uncertainty.'), and now raises TypeError when the uncertainty is a set. Two siblings added: error (whatever was supplied) and error_set. |
| `forward_problem.LinearForwardProblem` | Linear forward problem d = A(u) + e with A a LinearOperator; adds Gaussian-measure push-forwards, synthetic-data generation, chi-squared misfit/testing, direct-sum joining, and parameterisation / data-reduction surrogates. | `pygeoinf2.inference.problem.LinearForwardProblem` | Non-LinearOperator now raises TypeError (v1: ValueError). Keyword error= replaces data_error_measure= and may be a Subset. Method set changed: parameterized_problem -> parameterised, data_reduced_problem -> data_reduced (both without dense/parallel/n_jobs), chi-squared family moved up to ForwardProblem. Everything remains matrix-free (push_forward, translate, ColumnLinearOperator/BlockLinearOperator). |
| `forward_problem.LinearForwardProblem.from_direct_sum` | Builds a joint forward problem for joint inversions from a list of problems sharing one model space; the joint data space is the direct sum of the individual data spaces. | `LinearForwardProblem.from_direct_sum(problems, /)` | Semantics changed: a mixture of problems with and without an error measure now raises ValueError ('Every problem needs an error measure, or none may') instead of silently returning a joint problem with no error (the v1 behaviour was flagged as a bug, REVIEW.md I Must-3). Joint error built with GaussianMeasure.from_product (renamed from from_direct_sum); calls problem.error_measure so a member with a set-valued error raises TypeError. Argument is positional-only and accepts any Sequence. Still a matrix-free ColumnLinearOperator; still always returns LinearForwardProblem. |
| `forward_problem.LinearForwardProblem.data_measure_from_model_measure` | Pushes a Gaussian measure on the model space forward through A and adds the data error measure (if set) to give the induced measure on data space. | `LinearForwardProblem.data_measure_from_model_measure(measure, /)` | Parameter renamed model_measure -> measure and made positional-only; generality widened to any ProbabilityMeasure (non-Gaussian input yields a samplable PushForwardMeasure via measure.push_forward(A), and '+' falls back to _IndependentSum). Same ValueError on wrong domain; same matrix-free push-forward-plus-error structure. A factor-only Gaussian prior still yields a GaussianMeasure (the v2 constructor derives covariance from a factor, gaussian.py:197-200). |
| `forward_problem.LinearForwardProblem.joint_measure` | Returns the joint Gaussian measure on model_space (+) data_space for (u, d) given a prior on u. | `LinearForwardProblem.joint_measure(measure, /)` | Parameter renamed and positional-only; annotated ProbabilityMeasure. The widening to non-Gaussian measures is real only on the error-free branch (measure.push_forward(ColumnLinearOperator [I, A])). With an error measure the method calls GaussianMeasure.from_product([measure, error_measure]), which reads covariance_factor, covariance, precision, precision_factor and can_sample off every factor and returns a GaussianMeasure; the ProbabilityMeasure base defines none of covariance_factor/precision/precision_factor, so a non-Gaussian model measure raises AttributeError and a non-Gaussian error would be treated as Gaussian. In practice Gaussian-only with an error, as in v1. Identical block structure (BlockLinearOperator [[I,0],[A,I]] on from_product([prior, error])) built from LinearOperator.identity/LinearOperator.zero(data_space, codomain=model_space) rather than space.identity_operator()/zero_operator(). Both v1 and v2 drop the precision under the block push-forward (parity). Still no domain check on the input measure. Matrix-free. |
| `forward_problem.LinearForwardProblem.synthetic_data` | Generates one synthetic data vector d = A(model) + e by sampling the data measure induced by the model. | `ForwardProblem.synthetic_data(model, /, *, rng=None)` | Moved to the base class so it works for nonlinear operators. New error-free fallback: returns A(model) when there is no error (v1 raised AttributeError). Implemented directly as A(model) + error_measure.sample(rng) rather than data_measure_from_model(model).sample(). Adds rng keyword (seedable). Raises TypeError for a set-valued error. |
| `forward_problem.LinearForwardProblem.synthetic_model_and_data` | Draws a random model from the prior and the corresponding synthetic data, returned as (u, d). | `LinearForwardProblem.synthetic_model_and_data(prior, /, *, rng=None)` | Adds rng keyword and positional-only prior; otherwise identical (one draw from joint_measure(prior), unpacked as a direct-sum pair). Works with or without an error measure as in v1. |
| `forward_problem.LinearForwardProblem.critical_chi_squared` | Critical value of the chi-squared statistic at the given significance level, with degrees of freedom equal to the data space dimension. | `ForwardProblem.critical_chi_squared(*, level=0.95)` | significance_level (positional, required) -> level (keyword-only, default 0.95); new ValueError for level outside (0,1); result cast to float; scipy.stats.chi2 imported lazily inside the method; lives on the base class. Same dof = data_space.dim. |
| `forward_problem.LinearForwardProblem.chi_squared_from_residual` | Computes the chi-squared statistic from a data residual vector, weighted by the inverse data covariance if a data error measure exists. | `ForwardProblem.chi_squared_from_residual(residual, /)` | On the base class; positional-only. With an error it delegates to GaussianMeasure.mahalanobis_squared (metric-aware inner product with the precision, same value as v1), which raises NotImplementedError when the measure has no precision (v1 raised via inverse_covariance). Raises TypeError for a set-valued or non-Gaussian error. The code subtracts the expectation then adds it back before calling mahalanobis_squared, which subtracts it again — correct but roundabout (two wasted vector operations per call). Error-free branch is the plain squared norm as in v1. |
| `forward_problem.LinearForwardProblem.chi_squared` | Chi-squared misfit between observed data and A(model): (d-Au)^T C_e^{-1} (d-Au) if an error measure is set, else \|\|d-Au\|\|^2. | `ForwardProblem.chi_squared(model, data, /)` | Moved to the base class (works for nonlinear operators); arguments positional-only. Same computation: one forward application, residual via data_space.subtract, then chi_squared_from_residual. |
| `forward_problem.LinearForwardProblem.chi_squared_test` | Goodness-of-fit test: True if chi_squared(model, data) is strictly below critical_chi_squared(significance_level). | `ForwardProblem.chi_squared_test(model, data, /, *, level=0.95)` | Argument order changed from (significance_level, model, data) to (model, data, *, level=0.95); same strict '<' test against critical_chi_squared. New companion consistency_set(model, level=) returns the Ellipsoid the test asks membership of. |
| `forward_problem.LinearForwardProblem.parameterized_problem` | Creates a new forward problem on a parameter space by composing A with a parameterization operator P (new operator A @ P), keeping the same data error measure. | `LinearForwardProblem.parameterised(parameterisation, /)` | Renamed parameterized_problem -> parameterised. The dense=, parallel=, n_jobs= options are gone: the composed operator A @ P is always left matrix-free and the error is passed through unchanged (see forward_problem.dense_surrogate_option for the v2 route). Same ValueError on codomain mismatch; still returns a plain LinearForwardProblem. A set-valued error is carried across. |
| `forward_problem.LinearForwardProblem.data_reduced_problem` | Creates a new forward problem on a reduced/sketched data space with operator R @ A; the data error measure is pushed forward through R unless an explicit reduced measure is supplied. | `LinearForwardProblem.data_reduced(reduction, /, *, error=None)` | Renamed data_reduced_problem -> data_reduced; reduced_data_error_measure -> error (may be a Subset). dense/parallel/n_jobs dropped. Returns LinearForwardProblem instead of type(self), so subclasses are no longer preserved. The explicit-error domain check now happens in the ForwardProblem constructor (same ValueError). A set-valued current error with no explicit error raises TypeError from error_measure (docstring says ValueError). Default push-forward through R remains matrix-free (push_forward). |
| `forward_problem.error_free_branches` | Several methods have a deterministic fallback when data_error_measure is None: data_measure_from_model_measure omits the noise term, joint_measure uses a ColumnLinearOperator [I, A], chi_squared_from_residual uses the plain squared norm, and from_direct_sum yields no measure. | `has_error branches in problem.py` | Two branches changed: synthetic_data now has an error-free fallback returning A(model) (v1 raised AttributeError); from_direct_sum now raises ValueError on a mixed list instead of yielding no measure. Unchanged: data_measure_from_model still raises without a measure; data_measure_from_model_measure omits the noise term; joint_measure uses ColumnLinearOperator [I, A]; chi_squared_from_residual uses the plain squared norm; critical_chi_squared/chi_squared_test work without a measure. New third state: a set-valued error, for which the measure-only methods raise TypeError. |
| `forward_problem.scipy_chi2_dependency` | The chi-squared critical value is computed with scipy.stats.chi2.ppf; SciPy is a hard (not optional) import of forward_problem.py. | `lazy 'from scipy.stats import chi2' inside critical_chi_squared` | SciPy is no longer a module-level import of problem.py; chi2 is imported inside critical_chi_squared on first call (documented as an import-time saving). Still the only SciPy use in the unit. |
| `inversion.Inversion.forward_problem` | The forward problem associated with this inversion. | `.problem property on LeastSquares, DiscrepancyPrinciple, LinearGaussianInversion, LinearGaussianMixtureInversion` | Renamed forward_problem -> problem, and not universal: it exists on LeastSquares (and MinimumNorm by inheritance), DiscrepancyPrinciple, LinearGaussianInversion and LinearGaussianMixtureInversion, but ConstrainedLeastSquares, ConstrainedMinimumNorm, BackusGilbert, BackusInference, FeasibleProperty and MaximumAPosteriori keep the problem private (_problem) with no public accessor. Not on the Estimator base. |
| `inversion.LinearInversion.formalism` | The algebraic space in which the normal equations are assembled and solved. | `.formalism property on LeastSquares, ConstrainedLeastSquares, LinearGaussianInversion (and NormalOperator/TikhonovNormalOperator)` | Present as a read-only str property on LeastSquares/MinimumNorm, ConstrainedLeastSquares and LinearGaussianInversion, resolving 'auto' to the concrete choice. Not exposed on DiscrepancyPrinciple or ConstrainedMinimumNorm although both take a formalism keyword (kept as private _formalism). DiscrepancyPrinciple's v1 counterpart LinearMinimumNormInversion inherited the public formalism property from LinearInversion. |
| `inversion.LinearInversion.with_formalism` | Abstract hook: return a new instance of the inversion using the specified formalism. | `with_formalism(formalism, /) on LeastSquares, ConstrainedLeastSquares, LinearGaussianInversion` | No longer an abstract hook on a base class; it is implemented concretely (rebuilding with the same damping/solver/prior/subspace) on LeastSquares (hence MinimumNorm), ConstrainedLeastSquares and LinearGaussianInversion. Argument is positional-only and accepts 'auto'. Missing on DiscrepancyPrinciple and ConstrainedMinimumNorm, which do take a formalism at construction; v1's LinearMinimumNormInversion (DiscrepancyPrinciple's counterpart) had a concrete with_formalism (linear_optimisation.py:816-830). |
| `inversion.LinearInversion.parameterized_inversion` | Builds a surrogate inversion on a parameter space by calling forward_problem.parameterized_problem and re-instantiating the concrete inversion class on it. | `parameterised(parameterisation, /) on LeastSquares, ConstrainedLeastSquares, ConstrainedMinimumNorm; LinearGaussianInversion.parameterised(P, *, prior)` | Renamed parameterized_inversion -> parameterised. Dropped: dense=, parallel=, n_jobs= and the formalism= override (the new estimator always inherits the parent's formalism). The constrained classes pull the constraint back as (B M) p == w exactly as v1's ConstrainedLinearLeastSquaresInversion/ConstrainedLinearMinimumNormInversion already did (v2's docstring: 'That is v1's construction'), raising NotImplementedError for basis-defined subspaces in both versions — so this is parity, not new; what is gone there is v1's optional dense materialisation of the pulled-back constraint (new_B.with_dense_matrix). LinearGaussianInversion.parameterised now requires prior= on the parameter space: v1's parameter_prior=None defaulted to model_prior_measure.affine_mapping(operator=parameterization.adjoint) (review/inference.md:44 calls the removal 'defensible' since that was not a true pull-back, but no D-decision records it). v1 also densified the (parameter) prior with with_dense_covariance whenever dense=True OR the target formalism was 'model_space', guaranteeing a precision for Q^-1 + A* R^-1 A; v2 passes the prior through untouched, so parameterised(...) on a model_space LinearGaussianInversion whose prior lacks a precision raises ValueError from NormalOperator — the user must call prior.with_dense_covariance() themselves. Each v2 class re-instantiates with its own full state (damping, solver, subspace, prior) via type(self)(...) or LinearGaussianInversion(...); the v1 base contract type(self)(fp, formalism=) applied only to the stateless LinearLeastSquaresInversion/LinearMinimumNormInversion, the stateful v1 subclasses overrode it. Not available on DiscrepancyPrinciple (whose v1 counterpart LinearMinimumNormInversion inherited a working parameterized_inversion because its constructor is (fp, formalism=)), BackusGilbert, BackusInference, FeasibleProperty or the mixture inversion. |
| `inversion.LinearInversion.data_reduced_inversion` | Builds a surrogate inversion on a reduced (sketched) data space by calling forward_problem.data_reduced_problem and re-instantiating the concrete inversion class on it. | `data_reduced(reduction, /, *, error=None) on LeastSquares, ConstrainedLeastSquares, ConstrainedMinimumNorm, LinearGaussianInversion` | Renamed data_reduced_inversion -> data_reduced; reduced_data_error_measure -> error. Dropped: dense=, parallel=, n_jobs=, formalism= override. Each class re-instantiates with its own state (damping/solver/prior/subspace), as the stateful v1 subclasses also did in their own overrides. The constrained classes forward *args/**kwargs to problem.data_reduced (which accepts only error=, so v1-style dense=/parallel=/n_jobs= keywords raise TypeError). LinearGaussianInversion.data_reduced no longer densifies the prior when the target formalism is 'model_space' (v1 did, linear_bayesian.py:1462-1466), so a precision-less prior in model_space now raises ValueError from NormalOperator. Not on DiscrepancyPrinciple (v1's LinearMinimumNormInversion inherited a working data_reduced_inversion), the Backus classes or the mixture inversion. |
| `inversion.LinearInversion.surrogate_reinstantiation_contract` | Both surrogate builders assume every concrete LinearInversion subclass can be constructed from (forward_problem, formalism=...) alone; this is the implicit contract v1 subclasses (least-squares, Bayesian, etc.) either satisfy or override. | `explicit per-class rebuilds in parameterised/data_reduced/with_formalism/with_solver` | The implicit base-class contract type(self)(fp, formalism=) is gone; there is no base implementation at all, and each class rebuilds itself with its own full constructor arguments. In v1 that contract served only the stateless LinearLeastSquaresInversion/LinearMinimumNormInversion (the constrained and Bayesian classes overrode the methods to carry their state), so v2 is at parity on state preservation for those classes and simply has no inherited default for new subclasses. LeastSquares and the constrained classes use type(self)(...) (subclass-preserving); LinearGaussianInversion names the class directly (LinearGaussianInversion(...)), so a subclass of it would not be preserved by parameterised/data_reduced/with_formalism (v1's LinearBayesianInversion used type(self)). |
| `inversion.LinearInversion.formalism_option` | A user-visible switch, validated at construction, that tells concrete linear inversions whether to assemble/solve normal equations in model space (n x n system) or data space (m x m system). | `Formalism = Literal['auto','model_space','data_space'] keyword on the linear estimators; choose_formalism` | Values extended with 'auto' (pick the smaller space; opt-in, default remains 'data_space' as in v1). Validation moved from the inversion constructor to choose_formalism (ValueError) invoked when NormalOperator/TikhonovNormalOperator is built. New restriction, confined to NormalOperator (i.e. LinearGaussianInversion): 'model_space' is refused (ValueError) when the problem has no error measure, because Q^-1 + A*A is the R=I problem, not the exact-data one (v1's LinearBayesianInversion silently solved it). TikhonovNormalOperator — used by LeastSquares, MinimumNorm, DiscrepancyPrinciple and the constrained classes — still accepts model_space with no error and assembles the unweighted A*A + tI exactly as v1 did. 'model_space' requires the error precision (and, for NormalOperator, the prior precision) to be present (ValueError); the error-precision requirement is unchanged from v1's assert_inverse_data_covariance in the constructors, only the exception type differs. |
| `inversion.Inference.property_space` | The property space (codomain of the property operator). | `Estimator.target_space` | Renamed property_space -> target_space and generalised: it is the model space for an inverse problem and the property space (T.codomain) after push_forward or for a Backus estimator built with target=T. |

### linear_bayesian — `linear_bayesian.py`

| v1 | what it did | v2 | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| `linear_bayesian.LinearBayesianInversion` | Subclass of LinearInversion that solves d = A(u) + e with a Gaussian prior on u and Gaussian noise e, yielding the exact posterior Gaussian measure p(u\|d) (expectation, covariance, exact sampling), evidence diagnostics, several preconditioner factories and surrogate/reduced problem builders. | `pygeoinf2.inference.gaussian.LinearGaussianInversion (GaussianEstimator)` | Renamed LinearBayesianInversion -> LinearGaussianInversion. It is now an Estimator (callable data -> GaussianMeasure) subclassing GaussianEstimator, not a LinearInversion subclass. The solver moves from every method's argument list to the constructor (solver=None -> CGSolver; a callable factory is accepted via resolve_solver); the normal operator, its inverse, the Kalman gain and the posterior covariance are built ONCE in __init__ and cached rather than rebuilt per call. All formalism-dependent algebra moved to inference.normal.NormalOperator; all preconditioner factories moved out of the class to free-standing LinearSolver classes (inference.preconditioners, numerics.preconditioners.WoodburyPreconditioner). The eight surrogate/preconditioner methods are replaced by surrogate()/low_rank_surrogate() returning a NormalOperator. No compat alias for the v1 name exists (grep LinearBayesianInversion in pygeoinf2/*.py finds only catalogue/review prose). New members with no v1 counterpart: with_solver, solver, inverse_normal_operator, evidence_terms. |
| `linear_bayesian.LinearBayesianInversion.__init__` | Calls LinearInversion.__init__(forward_problem, formalism=formalism), stores the prior, and validates that the 'model_space' formalism has the precision operators it needs. | `LinearGaussianInversion.__init__(problem, prior, /, *, solver=None, formalism='data_space')` | Adds keyword solver (default CGSolver, or a callable factory receiving the assembled normal operator). Validates that prior is a GaussianMeasure (TypeError), that prior.domain == problem.model_space (ValueError) and that any error is a GaussianMeasure (TypeError) -- v1 checked none of these. The precision checks for model_space moved into NormalOperator.__init__ (normal.py:281-294) and now also require prior.covariance for data_space (normal.py:266-270); model_space with NO error measure is refused outright (normal.py:250-258) where v1 accepted it. Construction is eager: solver(normal) runs in __init__ (gaussian.py:113-114), so a direct solver extracts and factorises the matrix at construction (solvers.py:459-461) and an iterative solver resolves any deferred preconditioner (solvers.py:793-800, inside _invert) even if the estimator is never applied. formalism accepts 'auto'. |
| `linear_bayesian.LinearBayesianInversion.with_formalism` | Returns a new instance of the same concrete type sharing the same forward problem and prior measure but using the requested formalism. | `LinearGaussianInversion.with_formalism(formalism, /)` | Rebuilds with the same problem and prior as v1, but three things differ. (1) The stored solver is carried over (gaussian.py:241-243) and, because construction is eager, solver(normal) re-runs immediately: with a direct solver the other normal operator is factorised at the switch; with an iterative solver a deferred preconditioner is resolved against the new operator (solvers.py:793-800). A solver carrying a data-space-only preconditioner (NormalDiagonalPreconditioner / LocalisedPreconditioner / InvariantDistancePreconditioner all pass through _require_normal, preconditioners.py:50-64, which raises ValueError for formalism != 'data_space') or a pre-resolved data-space LinearOperator therefore makes with_formalism('model_space') raise at construction -- v1's with_formalism took no solver (linear_bayesian.py:129-131) and could only fail on the precision check. (2) v1 returned type(self)(...) preserving subclasses; v2 hard-codes LinearGaussianInversion (gaussian.py:241). (3) Argument is positional-only and 'auto' is accepted. The remedy for (1) is with_formalism(...).with_solver(new_solver) with a fresh solver, or building the other inversion by hand. |
| `linear_bayesian.LinearBayesianInversion.normal_operator` | Builds the Bayesian normal operator for the current formalism: 'data_space' gives A @ Q @ A.adjoint (+ R.covariance if a data error measure is set); 'model_space' gives Q.inverse_covariance + A.adjoint @ R.inverse_covariance @ A (or Q^-1 + A* A without a data error measure). | `LinearGaussianInversion.normal_operator (property) -> inference.normal.NormalOperator` | Same matrix-free assembly (A Q A* + R or Q^-1 + A* R^-1 A, normal.py:271-295) but built ONCE at construction and cached, and returned as a NormalOperator that carries its factors (forward, prior, error, covariances, precisions, formalism) and claims SELF_ADJOINT\|POSITIVE_DEFINITE traits. The no-error model_space branch Q^-1 + A* A no longer exists (refused, normal.py:250-258). NormalOperator can also be built stand-alone without an inversion. |
| `linear_bayesian.LinearBayesianInversion._compute_data_residual` | Private helper that computes v = d - A(mu_u) - mu_e, the data residual shifted by the prior expectation pushed through A and by the noise expectation; it is the residual all posterior/evidence computations act on. | `LinearGaussianInversion._data_shift(problem, prior) (static) + _residual_solve(data)` | Same quantity v = d - A mu_u - mu_e (gaussian.py:433-435), but v1's has_zero_expectation short-circuits are gone: A is always applied to prior.expectation and the error expectation always subtracted, so a zero-mean prior costs one forward action per residual (and one at construction for the affine translation, gaussian.py:118-119). The residual, its rhs and the solve are memoised in a one-entry cache keyed on the data's component bytes (gaussian.py:384-440), so posterior mean and mahalanobis share one solve. The memo requires a CoordinateSpace data space and costs one to_components plus a buffer copy per call (gaussian.py:384-406); on a data space without coordinates the memo is off and est(data) followed by mahalanobis(data) costs two solves, as in v1. |
| `linear_bayesian.LinearBayesianInversion.kalman_operator` | Constructs the Kalman gain K mapping data residuals to model-space updates: 'data_space' K = Q A* N_d^-1; 'model_space' K = N_m^-1 A* R^-1 (or N_m^-1 A* without R). | `LinearGaussianInversion.gain (property); NormalOperator.gain(inverse, /)` | Now a property, not a method: the solver (and any preconditioner) is fixed at construction, so kalman_operator(solver, preconditioner=) becomes .gain; to change solver use with_solver(...). Formula unchanged (Q A* N^-1 / N^-1 A* R^-1, normal.py:487-496), matrix-free composition; built once and cached. NormalOperator.gain(inverse) lets a caller supply their own inverse. |
| `linear_bayesian.LinearBayesianInversion.model_posterior_measure` | Computes the posterior Gaussian measure p(u\|d): expectation mu_u + K(d - A mu_u - mu_e) and covariance, with an exact randomize-then-optimize sampler attached when both prior and noise can be sampled. | `LinearGaussianInversion.__call__(data) -> GaussianMeasure` | model_posterior_measure(data, solver, preconditioner=) becomes estimator(data). Covariance: data_space uses (I - K A) Q (normal.py:517-525; one fewer Q application than v1's Q - K A Q) with SELF_ADJOINT\|POSITIVE_SEMIDEFINITE traits; model_space still N^-1. Mean is mu + model_update(w) from the memoised residual solve. Sampler: attached as a CENTRED fluctuation taking an rng (gaussian.py:652-674), gated by prior.can_sample and error.can_sample (v1 sample_set); v1 attached a full sample() closure. Returned measure is GaussianMeasure(target_space, expectation=, covariance=, sample=) -- still no precision on the posterior. |
| `linear_bayesian.LinearBayesianInversion.posterior_expectation_operator` | Returns the map d -> posterior expectation, F(d) = mu_u + K(d - A mu_u - mu_e); if both prior and noise expectations are zero this is just the Kalman gain LinearOperator, otherwise an AffineOperator(linear_part=K, translation=mu_u - K(A mu_u + mu_e)). | `GaussianEstimator.mean_map (property) -> AffineOperator(gain, translation)` | Always an AffineOperator; v1 returned the bare Kalman LinearOperator when both means are zero. Translation mu_u - K(A mu_u + mu_e) computed once at construction (gaussian.py:118-123) with no zero-mean short-circuits. Solver fixed at construction (no solver/preconditioner arguments). Note gaussian.py docstring: mean_map computes the mean 'the plain way' (does not share the memoised solve). |
| `linear_bayesian.LinearBayesianInversion.mahalanobis_evidence_term` | Computes the data-dependent Mahalanobis term <v, (A Q A* + R)^-1 v> of the log-evidence for the shifted residual v; in 'model_space' it uses the Woodbury identity <v, R^-1 v> - <A* R^-1 v, N_m^-1 A* R^-1 v> to avoid the data-space inversion. | `LinearGaussianInversion.mahalanobis(data, /) -> float` | Renamed mahalanobis_evidence_term -> mahalanobis; solver and preconditioner are the estimator's (no per-call arguments). Same maths: <v, w> in data_space; Woodbury <v,R^-1 v> - <rhs, w> in model_space (gaussian.py:504-516). Raises ValueError without an error measure (as v1) and additionally if the model-space error has no precision. Uses the memoised _residual_solve so the solve is shared with __call__ (v1 always re-solved; v1 also used solver.solve_linear_system directly). |
| `linear_bayesian.LinearBayesianInversion._trace_log_slq` | Private matrix-free engine estimating Tr(ln(op)) = ln\|op\| via SLQ: wraps op in functional_calculus.LanczosOperatorFunction with f(x)=log(max(x,1e-15)) and delegates the Hutchinson trace to low_rank.random_trace. | `numerics.functional_calculus.log_determinant(operator, method='stochastic', samples=, rng=, max_iterations=40, rtol=1e-3, sample_rtol=None, max_samples=None) via operator_log + numerics.randomised.random_trace` | Same SLQ construction (OperatorFunction with np.log applied lazily by Lanczos, Hutchinson trace via random_trace) but: (1) no eigenvalue clamp -- v1 used log(max(x,1e-15)) (linear_bayesian.py:602-603), v2's operator_log applies np.log directly (functional_calculus.py:617-619), so a negative Ritz value gives NaN; (2) NO parallel/n_jobs: log_determinant has no n_jobs parameter and calls random_trace without one (functional_calculus.py:641-652, 780-786) although random_trace itself accepts n_jobs (randomised.py:760); (3) defaults: samples=100 fixed rather than v1's adaptive 10 probes -> rtol 1e-2 in blocks of 5 (adaptive route needs sample_rtol=; block_size fixed at 20); (4) the Lanczos degree is max_iterations=40 with early stop rtol=1e-3 (matches v1's 40/1e-3); v1's 'fixed'-degree mode (lanczos_rtol=None) has no documented equivalent, though passing rtol=0.0 reaches it in practice because the convergence test at functional_calculus.py:348 can then pass only on an exact zero change; (5) returns an Estimate (value, standard_error, samples) not a float; (6) requires the operator to claim POSITIVE_DEFINITE (functional_calculus.py:742); (7) probe distribution changed from Rademacher components (v1 low_rank.py:1123-1127) to Gaussian white noise on the space (randomised.py:812-813) -- both estimate tr(A_c), but Rademacher has lower Hutchinson variance, so at equal sample counts v2 is noisier. The unused `space` argument is gone. |
| `linear_bayesian.LinearBayesianInversion.estimate_log_determinant` | Estimates ln\|N\| of either the data-space normal operator (A Q A* + R) or the model-space normal operator (Q^-1 + A* R^-1 A) by Stochastic Lanczos Quadrature, independently of the instance's own formalism. | `LinearGaussianInversion.normal_log_determinant(*, method='auto', samples=100, rng=None, **kwargs) -> Estimate` | No operator_type argument: it uses the instance's own formalism (use with_formalism('model_space').normal_log_determinant() for the other), and in model_space returns ln\|N_m\|+ln\|Q\|+ln\|R\| (Sylvester) rather than ln\|N_m\| alone -- i.e. it always reports ln\|N_d\|. Default method='auto' FORMS THE DENSE Galerkin MATRIX and takes slogdet whenever the space has coordinates, dim <= 4000 and (matrix is readable or dim <= samples*max_iterations) (functional_calculus.py:733-771); v1 was always SLQ. Result memoised on (method, samples, kwargs). SLQ kwargs renamed: size_estimate->samples, rtol->sample_rtol, lanczos_degree->max_iterations, lanczos_rtol->rtol, block_size fixed at 20, method 'variable'/'fixed' -> sample_rtol set/None; parallel/n_jobs gone (passing them raises TypeError in log_determinant). Returns Estimate not float. Raises ValueError without an error measure (v1 did not). |
| `linear_bayesian.LinearBayesianInversion.log_evidence` | Approximate log marginal likelihood ln p(d) = -0.5 [ ln\|N_d\| + <v, N_d^-1 v> + M ln(2 pi) ], combining mahalanobis_evidence_term with an SLQ log-determinant estimate. | `LinearGaussianInversion.log_evidence(data, /, **kwargs) -> float; evidence_terms(data, **kwargs) -> (misfit, volume)` | Same formula -0.5[ln\|N_d\| + <v,N_d^-1 v> + M ln 2pi] with Sylvester in model_space (gaussian.py:587-611,627-635). Differences: solver/preconditioner are the estimator's; SLQ kwargs are those of normal_log_determinant (renamed, no parallel/n_jobs); DEFAULT method='auto' takes the dense route for dim <= 4000 (v1 always SLQ) -- pass method='stochastic' to stay matrix-free; log-det memoised across data. In model_space, Q and R are stamped POSITIVE_DEFINITE via with_traits before log_determinant (gaussian.py:597-605); with_traits now returns a shallow copy of the same class (algebra/operators.py:536-579), so a DiagonalLinearOperator prior or noise covariance still takes the exact O(dim) route (functional_calculus.py:734-742) -- REVIEW.md item 2's wrapper defect has been fixed. Added evidence_terms returning the two halves. |
| `linear_bayesian.LinearBayesianInversion.diagonal_normal_preconditioner` | Builds a diagonal (Jacobi-type) inverse preconditioner for the data-space normal operator A Q A* + R by computing diag(A Q A*) via <A* e_i, Q A* e_i> per data index (or per block of indices using the averaged basis vector) and adding the noise covariance diagonal. | `inference.preconditioners.NormalDiagonalPreconditioner(*, blocks=None, floor=1e-14) -- a LinearSolver applied to a NormalOperator` | Free-standing LinearSolver: NormalDiagonalPreconditioner(blocks=...)(inv.normal_operator) or CGSolver().with_preconditioner(NormalDiagonalPreconditioner()). Same identity <A* e, Q A* e>, same block-partition validation (preconditioners.py:110-125), same Galerkin diagonal of R. Lost: parallel/n_jobs (blocks loop is serial, :140-146; R diagonal via diagonals(form='galerkin') without n_jobs, :151). Changed floor semantics: entries with \|d\| <= floor are left UNINVERTED (inverse entry = 1.0, :154-155) where v1 set them to 0. Requires a FactoredNormalOperator in data_space formalism (TypeError/ValueError, :50-64) and coordinates on the data space. Returns an InverseOperator with SELF_ADJOINT trait (applies Gram then divides) -- correct on weighted data spaces where v1's component form was not. |
| `linear_bayesian.LinearBayesianInversion.sparse_localized_preconditioner` | Builds a sparse approximate inverse of the data-space normal operator by taking randomized low-rank (Nystrom/eigen) approximations of A Q A* restricted to user-supplied, possibly overlapping, index blocks, assembling them into a SciPy sparse matrix, adding the diagonal noise variance and factorizing with splu. | `inference.preconditioners.LocalisedPreconditioner(blocks, /, *, rank=10, rng=None)` | Free-standing LinearSolver on a data-space NormalOperator. Same construction: per block a randomised eigendecomposition of P (A Q A*) P* (random_eig, min(rank, size)), dense V diag(lambda) V^T scattered into COO, noise diagonal added, splu, self-adjoint solve. Changes: overlapping blocks are AVERAGED not summed (:302-311, documented as a v1 bug fix); the restriction is the Galerkin sub-block (apply_gram before indexing, :255-260) rather than v1's component projection; the solve applies the Gram first; rng argument added; rank must be >= 1 and blocks non-empty (:222-225,234-241); the two unconditional print() calls are gone; parallel/n_jobs dropped (serial loop :250). Parameters interacting_blocks -> blocks (positional-only), rank keyword-only. |
| `linear_bayesian.LinearBayesianInversion.woodbury_data_preconditioner` | Builds a data-space preconditioner via the Woodbury identity N_d^-1 = R^-1 - R^-1 A (Q^-1 + A* R^-1 A)^-1 A* R^-1, using existing inverse covariances where set and solver-inverting Q and/or R otherwise. | `numerics.preconditioners.WoodburyPreconditioner.from_normal(normal, *, solver=None, prior_solver=None, noise_solver=None) -> used as a LinearSolver (picks data_form when the operator lives on the data space) or .data_form() -> LinearOperator` | Same identity R^-1 - R^-1 A (Q^-1 + A* R^-1 A)^-1 A* R^-1 (preconditioners.py:697-715), matrix-free, with prior/error precisions picked up automatically from the NormalOperator (:649-650) and prior_solver/noise_solver fallbacks. Changes: solver is optional, defaulting to CGSolver(rtol=1e-3, maxiter=200, strict=False) (:663-671) -- v1 required one; the constructor takes (A, Q, R) operators directly and from_normal reads them off any object with forward/prior_covariance/error_covariance; which form is applied is decided by the dimension/space of the operator handed to the solver (:728-735); the inner operators are stamped POSITIVE_DEFINITE; raises ValueError without R (:636-641) as v1. Not tied to an inversion instance. |
| `linear_bayesian.LinearBayesianInversion.woodbury_model_preconditioner` | Builds a model-space preconditioner via the Woodbury identity N_m^-1 = Q - Q A* (R + A Q A*)^-1 A Q, requiring no inverses of Q or R. | `WoodburyPreconditioner.from_normal(normal, solver=...).model_form() or as a LinearSolver on a model-space operator` | Same identity Q - Q A* (R + A Q A*)^-1 A Q with no inverses of Q or R (preconditioners.py:684-695). solver optional (loose CG default) where v1 required one; result stamped SELF_ADJOINT; chosen automatically when the operator to precondition lives on the model space. Raises ValueError without R. |
| `linear_bayesian.LinearBayesianInversion.surrogate_inversion` | Constructs a new LinearBayesianInversion from optionally substituted forward operator, prior and data error measure (defaulting to the originals), inheriting the parent's formalism; intended for cheap surrogate problems used as preconditioners. | `LinearGaussianInversion.surrogate(*, forward=None, prior=None, error=None, formalism=None) -> NormalOperator; NormalOperator.surrogate(...)` | Returns a surrogate NormalOperator, not a LinearBayesianInversion: a surrogate posterior/evidence cannot be obtained from it (build LinearGaussianInversion(LinearForwardProblem(A~, error=R~), Q~, formalism=...) by hand for that). Keywords renamed alternate_forward_operator/alternate_prior_measure/alternate_data_error_measure -> forward/prior/error; a formalism override is added. Validation: codomain must equal the data space (as v1); a new forward on a different model space now REQUIRES a prior (normal.py:442-449) where v1 raised on domain mismatch; the v1 AttributeError when no error measure exists is fixed (error may be None, :441). The surrogate may live on a different model space (tested test_normal.py:111-124). |
| `linear_bayesian.LinearBayesianInversion.low_rank_surrogate` | Builds a surrogate inversion in which the forward operator, prior and/or data error measure are replaced by randomized low-rank approximations of the requested ranks. | `LinearGaussianInversion.low_rank_surrogate(*, forward_rank=None, prior_rank=None, error_rank=None, rng=None, **kwargs) -> NormalOperator` | Returns a NormalOperator not an inversion. data_error_rank -> error_rank; the three per-factor kwargs dicts (forward_kwargs/prior_kwargs/data_error_kwargs) collapse into one **kwargs forwarded to ALL of random_svd, prior.low_rank_approximation and error.low_rank_approximation, plus a shared rng. The accepted kwargs are a fixed set {oversampling, power, block_size, rtol, max_rank, n_jobs} validated by _range_options (randomised.py:120-140), so anything else raises TypeError. Forward truncation uses numerics.randomised.random_svd (v1 LowRankSVD.from_randomized); measures use GaussianMeasure.low_rank_approximation (random_cholesky, gives a covariance factor and no precision, gaussian.py:1221-1273 -- v1's likewise had no inverse covariance, so nothing lost there).
