| `linear_bayesian.LinearBayesianInversion.parameterized_inversion` | Builds a surrogate inversion on a parameter space via a parameterization operator P: parameter space -> model space, with a parameter prior that defaults to the pull-back of the model prior by P.adjoint. | `LinearGaussianInversion.parameterised(parameterisation, /, *, prior) -> LinearGaussianInversion` | Spelling parameterized -> parameterised. `prior` is now REQUIRED: v1's default pull-back model_prior.affine_mapping(operator=P.adjoint) is gone (docstring: 'not a pull-back and would be a different measure'); the same measure is obtainable as prior.push_forward(P.adjoint) (probability/base.py:293-315). Dropped keywords: dense, parallel, n_jobs, formalism override (inherits the parent's formalism and solver). No automatic densification of the parameter prior for model_space (call .with_dense_covariance() yourself). Delegates to problem.parameterised(P) which just composes A @ P (problem.py:393-412). Returns LinearGaussianInversion(...) not type(self); construction is eager, so the derived inversion factorises/resolves its own solver at creation. |
| `linear_bayesian.LinearBayesianInversion.data_reduced_inversion` | Builds a surrogate inversion on a reduced data space via a reduction operator (data space -> reduced data space), optionally with a supplied reduced data error measure. | `LinearGaussianInversion.data_reduced(reduction, /, *, error=None) -> LinearGaussianInversion` | reduced_data_error_measure -> error (may also be a Subset). Dropped keywords dense, parallel, n_jobs, formalism override; no automatic prior densification for model_space. Delegates to problem.data_reduced(reduction, error=) which pushes the error forward through the reduction when none is given (problem.py:414-441); returns LinearGaussianInversion with the parent's solver and formalism (eagerly constructed). |
| `linear_bayesian.dual_formalism` | A single instance-level switch selects which normal equations are assembled and solved: data-space N_d = A Q A* + R (M x M, K = Q A* N_d^-1) or model-space N_m = Q^-1 + A* R^-1 A (N x N, K = N_m^-1 A* R^-1). | `inference.normal.Formalism = Literal['auto','model_space','data_space']; choose_formalism(); NormalOperator(formalism=); LinearGaussianInversion(formalism='data_space')` | The switch survives with the same default 'data_space' and the same algebra in both branches (normal.py:265-296,487-555; mahalanobis and Sylvester branches gaussian.py:504-516,587-611), and 'auto' (smaller space) is added as opt-in (normal.py:52-97, DESIGN §27.2). Changes: model_space is REFUSED when there is no error measure (normal.py:246-258); data_space now also requires prior.covariance/error.covariance not None (:266-278); validation lives in NormalOperator so it applies to stand-alone normal operators and surrogates; a per-surrogate formalism override exists. The gates on the structure-aware preconditioners are enforced by _require_normal (preconditioners.py:58-63), which also means a solver carrying one cannot be switched to model_space via with_formalism. Tests: test_inference.py:219-233, test_normal.py:94-109 check the two formalisms agree. |
| `linear_bayesian.no_data_error_measure_branch` | When the forward problem carries no data error measure, all R terms are silently dropped: N_d = A Q A*, N_m = Q^-1 + A* A, K = N_m^-1 A*, rhs = A* v, residual not shifted by a noise mean, posterior sampler uses no noise sample, diagonal preconditioner adds no R diagonal, sparse preconditioner uses zero noise variance. | `NormalOperator with error=None (data_space only); LinearGaussianInversion on a LinearForwardProblem without error` | The data_space no-error branch is preserved: N = A Q A* (normal.py:271-278), K = Q A* N^-1, residual not shifted by a noise mean (error expectation only added when has_error, gaussian.py:152-153), sampler draws no noise (gaussian.py:670-673), NormalDiagonalPreconditioner adds no R diagonal (preconditioners.py:148-152), LocalisedPreconditioner adds no diagonal (:312-316). The model_space no-error branch (Q^-1 + A* A, K = N^-1 A*, rhs = A* v) is REMOVED: NormalOperator raises ValueError('The model-space formalism needs an error measure', normal.py:250-258) and 'auto' is forced to data_space. Still refused without R: mahalanobis (gaussian.py:498-503), normal_log_determinant/log_evidence (:567-568), WoodburyPreconditioner.from_normal (numerics/preconditioners.py:636-641), low_rank_surrogate(error_rank=) (gaussian.py:325-326). surrogate() no longer crashes when error is None (normal.py:441). |
| `linear_bayesian.preconditioner_forwarding` | kalman_operator, model_posterior_measure and mahalanobis_evidence_term pass the `preconditioner` kwarg to the solver only when it is an IterativeLinearSolver; direct solvers are called as solver(normal_operator) and the preconditioner is ignored. | `IterativeSolver(preconditioner=) / IterativeSolver.with_preconditioner(p); resolve_solver(factory, normal)` | The estimator never takes a preconditioner; it is attached to the solver (CGSolver().with_preconditioner(LinearSolver \| LinearOperator), solvers.py:686-726,728-762) and resolved against the normal operator when the solver is applied to it (_resolve_preconditioner inside _invert, :793-800,832-835) -- which, because LinearGaussianInversion.__init__ calls solver(normal), happens at construction. A preconditioner needing the assembled operator is supplied via a callable solver factory (resolve_solver, :150-206). Direct solvers have no preconditioner slot, so the v1 'ignored silently' case cannot arise. with_preconditioner refuses to replace an existing preconditioner (ValueError, :753-758). |
| `linear_bayesian.matrix_free_composition_no_caching` | Normal operators, Kalman gains, posterior covariances and Woodbury preconditioners are LinearOperator compositions (@, +, -) that never form a matrix; the normal_operator property and its solver inverse are rebuilt on every call. | `LinearGaussianInversion.__init__ builds normal/inverse/gain/covariance once; _residual_solve memo; _log_determinants memo` | Compositions remain matrix-free (normal.py:271-295,487-525; numerics/preconditioners.py:684-715), but the 'no caching' half is deliberately reversed: the normal operator, solver inverse, gain and posterior covariance are built once at construction (gaussian.py:107-116,132-141); the residual solve is memoised on data contents (:384-440, CoordinateSpace data spaces only; tested test_normal.py:863-901); the log-determinant is memoised per settings (:581-590). Consequence: with a direct solver the factorisation happens eagerly at construction (solvers.py:459-461) and is reused, and every derived inversion (with_formalism, with_solver, parameterised, data_reduced) is a fresh construction that repeats the factorisation / preconditioner resolution (gaussian.py:225-243,355-358,379-382); with an iterative solver each application of the InverseOperator re-runs the solve (solvers.py:230-233) as in v1. Dense matrices are still only formed in LocalisedPreconditioner blocks, in log_determinant(method='auto'/'dense') and via with_dense_covariance when the user asks. |
| `linear_bayesian.randomize_then_optimize_sampling` | model_posterior_measure attaches an exact posterior sampler u_post = u + K(d - A u - e), with u ~ prior and e ~ noise, whenever prior.sample_set and (no error measure or error.sample_set). | `LinearGaussianInversion._draw_fluctuation(rng) passed as GaussianEstimator(centred_sample=); GaussianMeasure.sample(rng=)` | Same algorithm (draw u ~ prior, e ~ noise, correct with the gain; one prior draw, one forward action, one noise draw, one gain action per sample) but written CENTRED (fluctuation only, mean added by GaussianMeasure.sample, probability/gaussian.py:633-646) and taking an explicit rng (gaussian.py:652-674) -- algebraically identical. Gate is prior.can_sample and (no error or error.can_sample) (:637-650; v1 sample_set). The sampler is carried through GaussianEstimator.push_forward (estimators.py:292-308), so property posteriors sample too (tested test_inference.py:650-700). |
| `linear_bayesian.slq_log_determinant` | ln\|N\| is estimated matrix-free as Tr(ln N) using LanczosOperatorFunction (per-probe Lanczos of degree up to 40, early stop at rtol 1e-3, eigenvalues clamped at 1e-15) and low_rank.random_trace (Hutchinson probes, adaptive to rtol 1e-2 in blocks of 5). | `numerics.functional_calculus.log_determinant defaults: method='auto', samples=100, dense_limit=4000, max_iterations=40, rtol=1e-3, sample_rtol=None, max_samples=None; random_trace block_size=20` | Default behaviour differs materially: (a) method='auto' goes DENSE (matrix + slogdet) for coordinate spaces with dim <= 4000 (functional_calculus.py:733-771) -- v1 always SLQ; (b) the stochastic route defaults to 100 fixed probes (v1: adaptive from 10 probes to rtol 1e-2 in blocks of 5); adaptive sampling needs sample_rtol=, block size is fixed at 20 (randomised.py:759), max_samples defaults to samples + 20*block_size; (c) Lanczos degree 40 with early-stop rtol 1e-3 matches v1, but there is no documented 'fixed'-degree mode (rtol=0.0 reaches it in practice, functional_calculus.py:348) and convergence is judged on quadrature weights; (d) no 1e-15 eigenvalue clamp before log; (e) no parallel/n_jobs; (f) probes are Gaussian white noise on the space (randomised.py:812-813) rather than v1's Rademacher components (low_rank.py:1123-1127) -- same expectation tr(A_c), higher variance per probe; (g) DiagonalLinearOperator gets an exact sum(log lambda) (functional_calculus.py:734-742, and with_traits no longer defeats it); (h) result is an Estimate with standard error; the model-space Sylvester route adds errors in quadrature (gaussian.py:606-609). In model_space log_evidence still runs three estimates (N_m, Q, R). |
| `linear_bayesian.joblib_parallel_options` | joblib (Parallel, delayed) is imported unconditionally; parallel=True with n_jobs runs the per-block loops of diagonal_normal_preconditioner and sparse_localized_preconditioner concurrently and is forwarded to extract_diagonal, random_trace, with_dense_covariance, parameterized_problem and data_reduced_problem. | `pygeoinf2.parallel.parallel_map(n_jobs=) and n_jobs keywords on GaussianMeasure.with_dense_covariance, DirectSolver(n_jobs=), LinearOperator.matrix/diagonals/apply_block, random_trace/random_svd/random_eig/random_diagonal` | The parallel=bool + n_jobs=-1 pair is replaced everywhere by a single n_jobs=None (serial unless set; joblib still a required dependency, parallel.py:20-23). Within this unit's entry points the option is LOST: NormalDiagonalPreconditioner and LocalisedPreconditioner loop serially and call diagonals() without n_jobs (inference/preconditioners.py:140-151,250-294,312-316); log_determinant/normal_log_determinant/log_evidence have no n_jobs and do not forward one to random_trace (functional_calculus.py:641-652,780-786); parameterised/data_reduced have no n_jobs. Retained indirectly: low_rank_surrogate(**kwargs) forwards n_jobs to random_svd/random_cholesky; with_dense_covariance(n_jobs=); DirectSolver(n_jobs=) for the matrix extraction of a direct solve. |
| `linear_bayesian.scipy_sparse_splu` | sparse_localized_preconditioner is the one place that forms an explicit sparse matrix (COO triplets from dense low-rank blocks plus a diagonal noise term) and factorizes it with scipy.sparse.linalg.splu; its returned operator applies splu.solve on component vectors and is declared self-adjoint (adjoint_mapping = same function). | `inference.preconditioners.LocalisedPreconditioner._invert: sparse.coo_matrix -> tocsr (averaging via a multiplicity matrix) -> + sparse.diags(noise) -> tocsc -> sparse_linalg.splu; InverseOperator self-adjoint` | Same scipy.sparse pipeline and splu factorisation, but the matrix that is factorised is not v1's: v1 let coo_matrix SUM duplicate entries from overlapping blocks (linear_bayesian.py:997-999) and restricted A Q A* in component form via EuclideanSpace.subspace_projection @ coordinate_projection (:945-960) with the solve acting on raw components (:1007-1010); v2 divides duplicates by a multiplicity matrix (preconditioners.py:302-311), restricts the Galerkin sub-block through apply_gram (:255-260) and applies the Gram before splu.solve (:320-322). On an overlapping cover or a non-orthonormal data space the assembled preconditioner therefore differs from v1's (an improvement: v1's summed seams were 'a different operator'). random_eig on a from_callables block operator replaces LowRankEig.from_randomized(method='fixed') (:278-289). Also used by InvariantDistancePreconditioner (:530-545). |
| `linear_bayesian.diagonal_preconditioner_thresholds` | diagonal_normal_preconditioner insists that blocks exactly partition the data indices (count, uniqueness and bounds checks with ValueError) and sets the inverse diagonal to zero wherever the estimated diagonal is <= 1e-14. | `NormalDiagonalPreconditioner(blocks=, floor=1e-14)` | Partition validation is the same (count, uniqueness, bounds; ValueError; preconditioners.py:110-125, tested test_normal.py:181-188) and the block probe is the averaged indicator broadcast to the block (:140-146). Threshold semantics changed: entries with \|diag\| <= floor are left uninverted -- inverse entry becomes 1.0 (:154-155) -- where v1 set them to 0 (linear_bayesian.py:887-889); the floor is now configurable and compared on \|d\| rather than d > 1e-14. |
| `linear_bayesian.stdout_printing` | sparse_localized_preconditioner prints 'Building sparse preconditioner over ... blocks (Rank ...)...' and 'Factorizing sparse matrix...' unconditionally; normal_residual_callback exposes a print_progress flag and message template for per-iteration residual output. | `No prints in inference/preconditioners.py; ProgressCallback(report=None) prints nothing unless a report callable is given; LeastSquares.residual_callback(report=print)` | The two unconditional print() calls in the sparse preconditioner are removed (grep 'print' in inference/preconditioners.py: none). Per-iteration residual reporting for the Gaussian inversion is done through CGSolver(callback=ProgressCallback(report=print)) (solvers.py:368-425), which is silent by default (v1 print_progress=True), has a fixed message format rather than v1's message template, and reports the solver's recurrence residual rather than a recomputed \|\|y - A x\|\|. The templated residual_callback(message=, report=) with {iteration}/{residual} fields exists only on LeastSquares (point.py:296-331). |

### linear_optimisation — `linear_optimisation.py`

| v1 | what it did | v2 | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| `linear_optimisation.LinearLeastSquaresInversion` | Tikhonov-regularised least-squares inversion minimising J(u) = \|\|A u - d\|\|^2_R + damping \|\|u\|\|^2, with a selectable 'model_space' (N x N normal equations) or 'data_space' (M x M dual/representer system) formalism. Subclass of LinearInversion. | `pygeoinf2.inference.point.LeastSquares (pygeoinf2/inference/point.py:71-331), on TikhonovNormalOperator (pygeoinf2/inference/tikhonov.py:46-318)` | Class renamed and re-shaped: v1 was a factory object holding only (forward_problem, formalism) whose methods took damping/solver per call; v2 LeastSquares(problem, /, *, damping=0.0, solver=None, formalism='data_space') fixes damping and solver at construction and IS the data->model affine operator (a LinearPointEstimator subclass), with .normal_operator, .inverse_normal_operator, .right_hand_side, .formalism, .damping, .problem, .solver properties and with_solver/with_formalism/with_damping/family/surrogate/parameterised/data_reduced/residual_callback methods. Formalism gains an 'auto' option (normal.py:44-88). Solver defaults to CG when None (solvers.py:150-205). The inverse normal operator is built eagerly in __init__ (point.py:111-112) and, when the problem has an error measure, one application of the operator to the error expectation is spent at construction even when that expectation is zero (point.py:120-124; v2 GaussianMeasure has has_zero_expectation at probability/gaussian.py:582 but it is not consulted). No assert_inverse_data_covariance(): the model-space precision requirement is enforced by TikhonovNormalOperator raising ValueError (tikhonov.py:80-86). Also new: the data-space formalism now refuses an error measure with no covariance (tikhonov.py:98-103). |
| `linear_optimisation.LinearLeastSquaresInversion.normal_operator` | Builds the regularised normal operator for the chosen formalism: model_space -> A* R^-1 A + damping I (or A* A + damping I without a data error measure); data_space -> A A* + damping R (or A A* + damping I). | `LeastSquares.normal_operator property (pygeoinf2/inference/point.py:142-150) returning a TikhonovNormalOperator (pygeoinf2/inference/tikhonov.py:46-130); free-standing TikhonovNormalOperator(forward, damping, *, error=, formalism=) and TikhonovFamily.at(damping) (tikhonov.py:402-409)` | No longer a method taking damping: the damping is fixed on the estimator, and a different damping means with_damping(t).normal_operator or TikhonovNormalOperator(A, t, error=R, formalism=...). Same matrix-free assembly (A* R^-1 A + t I, A A* + t R, or unweighted variants, tikhonov.py:80-109) and same damping<0 ValueError (tikhonov.py:71-72). The v2 object additionally carries its factors (forward, error_covariance, error_precision, prior_covariance = (1/t) I, base, shift) so structure-aware preconditioners can read them; prior_covariance raises ValueError at zero damping (tikhonov.py:188-209). |
| `linear_optimisation.LinearLeastSquaresInversion.normal_residual_callback` | Returns a ResidualTrackingCallback pre-configured with normal_operator(damping) and normal_rhs(data), for monitoring convergence of an iterative solver on the normal equations. | `LeastSquares.residual_callback(data, /, *, message='iteration {iteration}: normal residual {residual:.3e}', report=print) (pygeoinf2/inference/point.py:296-331)` | No damping argument (the estimator's fixed damping is used). Format keys renamed {iter}/{res} -> {iteration}/{residual}; print_progress bool replaced by a report callable. The residual is no longer computed by the callback from normal_operator and normal_rhs (v1 ResidualTrackingCallback printed the absolute \|\|y - N x\|\|, v1 linear_solvers.py:1098-1101); v2 returns a closure that takes the (iteration, residual) the IterativeSolver reports (solvers.py:814-817; CG records the absolute \|\|r\|\| at solvers.py:938,962) and divides by \|\|right_hand_side\|\|, so it prints a RELATIVE residual of whatever system the solver is running on. Usage differs too: the callback must be built from an estimator that already exists and then attached to a NEW solver via with_solver, and it also fires during that constructor's expectation solve when the problem has an error measure. Only on LeastSquares/MinimumNorm — not on ConstrainedLeastSquares. |
| `linear_optimisation.LinearLeastSquaresInversion.least_squares_operator` | Constructs the operator mapping observed data directly to the Tikhonov least-squares model: model_space -> N_m^-1 A* R^-1 (or N_m^-1 A*); data_space -> A* N_d^-1. | `The LeastSquares instance itself: LeastSquares(problem, damping=t, solver=CGSolver().with_preconditioner(P), formalism=...) (pygeoinf2/inference/point.py:79-136); linear part via .operator (estimators.py:107-110)` | Method (damping, solver, preconditioner=) -> class constructor. The preconditioner keyword is gone: preconditioners are attached to the IterativeSolver (solvers.py:728-772) as a ready LinearOperator or a deferred LinearSolver; a preconditioner built from other factors goes in as a callable solver factory resolved against the normal operator (solvers.py:150-205). Operator assembly is identical (N_m^-1 A* R^-1 / N_m^-1 A* / A* N_d^-1, point.py:114-117). Return type: always an affine LinearPointEstimator (translation = -L(z_bar) when non-zero, else zero translation) rather than LinearOperator-or-AffineOperator; it also carries resolution and propagated_covariance (estimators.py:120-160). |
| `linear_optimisation.LinearLeastSquaresInversion.woodbury_data_preconditioner` | Builds a data-space preconditioner for N_d = A A* + damping R via the Woodbury identity: (1/damping) [R^-1 - R^-1 A (A* R^-1 A + damping I)^-1 A* R^-1]. | `pygeoinf2.numerics.preconditioners.WoodburyPreconditioner.from_normal(lsq.normal_operator, solver=..., noise_solver=...).data_form() (pygeoinf2/numerics/preconditioners.py:592-651,697-715), or the WoodburyPreconditioner used directly as a solver's preconditioner (preconditioners.py:728-740)` | Moved off the inversion class into a free-standing LinearSolver. SEMANTIC DIFFERENCE, verified numerically: v1 returns (1/damping)[R^-1 - R^-1 A (A* R^-1 A + damping I)^-1 A* R^-1], the exact inverse of A A* + damping R; v2 data_form() with prior_precision = t I returns R^-1 - R^-1 A (t I + A* R^-1 A)^-1 A* R^-1, i.e. t * N_d^-1 (test: \|\|W N x\|\|/\|\|x\|\| = 0.3 at t = 0.3, model form gives 1.0; re-confirmed by both reviews). Harmless inside PCG (scale-invariant) but it is not an inverse and would mislead a residual-based or GMRES-style use. Default inner solver when solver=None is a loose CG (rtol=1e-3, strict=False; preconditioners.py:663-671), where v1 used the given solver exactly; noise_solver still defaults to solver. R^-1 taken from error_precision if the measure has one, else solved (preconditioners.py:646-651,673-681). Guards retained in different places: damping<=0 -> ValueError from TikhonovNormalOperator.prior_covariance (tikhonov.py:188-209); no error measure -> ValueError in from_normal (preconditioners.py:636-641). |
| `linear_optimisation.LinearLeastSquaresInversion.woodbury_model_preconditioner` | Builds a model-space preconditioner for N_m = A* R^-1 A + damping I via the Woodbury identity: (1/damping) [I - A* (damping R + A A*)^-1 A]. | `WoodburyPreconditioner.from_normal(lsq.normal_operator, solver=...).model_form() (pygeoinf2/numerics/preconditioners.py:592-651,684-695)` | Moved off the inversion class into numerics. Algebra identical and verified exact (Q - Q A* (R + A Q A*)^-1 A Q with Q = (1/t) I equals (1/t)[I - A* (t R + A A*)^-1 A]; numeric ratio 1.0). Still needs only R (never R^-1). Default inner solver when solver=None is loose CG rtol 1e-3, strict=False (v1 used the supplied solver). Same guards, raised from prior_covariance (zero damping) and from_normal (no error). |
| `linear_optimisation.LinearLeastSquaresInversion.surrogate_inversion` | Constructs a surrogate LinearLeastSquaresInversion with simplified physics and/or data errors, keeping the current formalism. | `LeastSquares.surrogate(*, forward=None, error=None, damping=None, formalism=None) -> TikhonovNormalOperator (pygeoinf2/inference/point.py:230-254; tikhonov.py:279-318)` | Keywords renamed alternate_forward_operator -> forward, alternate_data_error_measure -> error; damping/formalism overrides added. RETURN TYPE differs: v1 returned a full LinearLeastSquaresInversion; v2 returns only the surrogate normal operator (for preconditioner building). A surrogate estimator is written by hand: LeastSquares(LinearForwardProblem(A2, error=R2), damping=..., solver=..., formalism=...). v2 checks the surrogate shares the data space (tikhonov.py:305-312). |
| `linear_optimisation.LinearLeastSquaresInversion.data_reduced_inversion` | Surrogate inversion on a reduced data space, built from forward_problem.data_reduced_problem(reduction_operator, ...). | `LeastSquares.data_reduced(reduction, /, *, error=None) (pygeoinf2/inference/point.py:272-294) -> LinearForwardProblem.data_reduced (pygeoinf2/inference/problem.py:413-441)` | Renamed data_reduced_inversion -> data_reduced; reduction_operator -> reduction; reduced_data_error_measure -> error. | `linear_optimisation.LinearLeastSquaresInversion.parameterized_inversion` | INHERITED (not overridden in this file) from LinearInversion: surrogate inversion over a parameter space, via forward_problem.parameterized_problem(parameterization, dense=, parallel=, n_jobs=) and type(self)(new_fp, formalism=...). | `LeastSquares.parameterised(parameterisation, /) (pygeoinf2/inference/point.py:256-270) -> LinearForwardProblem.parameterised (pygeoinf2/inference/problem.py:393-411)` | Renamed parameterized_inversion -> parameterised (British spelling), parameterization -> parameterisation. dense/parallel/n_jobs flags dropped (no equivalent keyword anywhere in inference/); the composed operator A @ M stays matrix-free unless the user pre-assembles it with LinearOperator.assembled(n_jobs=) (operators.py:951). formalism override keyword dropped (use .with_formalism). Damping and solver are carried over (v1 rebuilt with formalism only). |
| `linear_optimisation.LinearLeastSquaresInversion.data_expectation_shift` | When the data error measure has a non-zero expectation z_bar, normal_rhs uses (v - z_bar) and least_squares_operator returns an AffineOperator whose translation is -L(z_bar), regardless of formalism. | `TikhonovNormalOperator.right_hand_side subtracts error.expectation (pygeoinf2/inference/tikhonov.py:259-263); LeastSquares sets translation = -L(z_bar) when \|\|L z_bar\|\| > 0 (pygeoinf2/inference/point.py:119-124); NOT propagated by ConstrainedLeastSquares (point.py:764-767)` | Ported for LeastSquares/MinimumNorm (translation -L z_bar on the estimator) and for DiscrepancyPrinciple/ConstrainedMinimumNorm (right_hand_side and chi_squared subtract the expectation), but LOST for ConstrainedLeastSquares: point.py:764 composes projector @ inner.operator — the LINEAR part of the inner LeastSquares — and rebuilds the translation from the subspace alone (t - operator(A t)), so the inner estimator's -L z_bar (computed at point.py:119-124) is discarded, and LinearPointEstimator (estimators.py:103-109) does not apply the expectation itself. In v1 the shift reached the constrained class automatically because shift_out @ reduced_op @ shift_in composed the AffineOperator that carried it (linear_optimisation.py:308-316,646-656). Verified: the v2 constrained answer is off from the dense constrained minimiser by exactly \|\|inner.translation\|\| (3.2519) in both formalisms; the hand composition t + P inner(d - A t) with the full affine inner estimator matches to 4e-15 (scratchpad/cls_shift.py, re-run). | `linear_optimisation.LinearLeastSquaresInversion.preconditioner_resolution` | Preconditioners may be supplied either as a ready LinearOperator or as a LinearSolver factory that is applied to the normal operator; the result is only used when the main solver is an IterativeLinearSolver. | `IterativeSolver(preconditioner=LinearSolver \| LinearOperator) / .with_preconditioner (pygeoinf2/numerics/solvers.py:679-801); resolve_solver for factories needing the operator (solvers.py:150-205)` | Resolution moved from the inversion into the solver: a LinearSolver preconditioner is deferred and applied to whatever operator is inverted (solvers.py:793-801), a LinearOperator is used as-is; DirectSolver has no preconditioner slot at all, so it cannot be 'silently ignored' — it cannot be passed. with_preconditioner refuses to replace an existing one (ValueError, solvers.py:728-762). Inside a damping sweep a deferred LinearSolver preconditioner is built once and only rebuilt when the damping moves by more than DampedSolves.refresh = 10x (numerics/root_find.py:386-389,467-481), not at every damping as in v1. |
| `linear_optimisation.LinearLeastSquaresInversion.woodbury_inverse_covariance_resolution` | Both Woodbury builders require damping > 0 and a data error measure (ValueError otherwise); the data-space variant obtains R^-1 from inverse_covariance when set, else by applying noise_solver (defaulting to solver) to R.covariance; the model-space variant never needs R^-1. | `WoodburyPreconditioner.from_normal picks up error_precision via getattr and otherwise solves R with noise_solver or the inner solver (pygeoinf2/numerics/preconditioners.py:646-651,673-681); guards at tikhonov.py:188-209 and preconditioners.py:636-641` | R^-1 resolution order preserved (precision if the measure has one, else noise_solver, else solver). Data form carries the extra factor t (see woodbury_data_preconditioner). |
| `linear_optimisation.ConstrainedLinearLeastSquaresInversion` | Tikhonov least-squares inversion with the solution confined exactly to an affine subspace (e.g. fixed mean value or boundary condition). Subclass of LinearInversion. | `pygeoinf2.inference.point.ConstrainedLeastSquares(problem, subspace, /, *, damping=0.0, solver=None, formalism='data_space') (pygeoinf2/inference/point.py:722-888)` | Renamed; constraint -> subspace; damping/solver fixed at construction; the instance is the affine data->model operator (LinearPointEstimator) with operator = P @ inner.operator and translation = t - operator(A t) (point.py:764-767). REGRESSION: ConstrainedLeastSquares returns the wrong model whenever the problem's error measure has a non-zero expectation, because the inner LeastSquares' translation (-L z_bar, point.py:119-124) is discarded when the outer affine operator is assembled from inner.operator alone (point.py:764-767); v1 composed the full AffineOperator (linear_optimisation.py:646-656). Verified: v1 matches the dense constrained minimiser to 1e-15 (scratchpad/cls_v1.py), v2 is off by \|\|inner.translation\|\| (3.25 / 3.09 with \|u_v1\| = 1.7) in both formalisms (scratchpad/cls_shift.py, cmn_v1v2.py); the test fixture's error is zero-mean (tests/test_point.py:253-278) and the constrained LS test checks only constraint.contains (test_point.py:636-639), so the suite cannot see it. ConstrainedMinimumNorm is not affected (v1/v2 agree to 3e-11). Unlike v1 it exposes reduced (the inner LeastSquares), normal_operator (the reduced one) and formalism, so a Woodbury/structure-aware preconditioner for the reduced system can be built through the public API. Domain check: subspace.domain must equal the model space (ValueError, point.py:754-755). No residual_callback and no surrogate/family/with_damping on the constrained class. |
| `linear_optimisation.ConstrainedLinearLeastSquaresInversion.least_squares_operator` | Operator mapping data to the constrained least-squares solution: shift_out @ reduced_op @ shift_in, where shift_in subtracts A(u_base) from the data, reduced_op is the inner unconstrained least_squares_operator, and shift_out adds u_base. | `The ConstrainedLeastSquares instance itself (pygeoinf2/inference/point.py:736-780)` | Method -> constructor (damping, solver, preconditioner-in-solver). Intended algebra u = t + P w with w from the reduced Tikhonov problem on d - A t, composed as one affine operator (linear part P @ inner.operator, translation t - P L (A t)) rather than v1's shift_out @ reduced_op @ shift_in; the translation costs one reduced solve at construction. Always affine, as v1. REGRESSION, verified numerically: the composition uses only the LINEAR part of the inner LeastSquares (point.py:764) and never its translation -L z_bar (point.py:119-124), and LinearPointEstimator (estimators.py:103-109) applies no expectation itself, so for an error measure with non-zero expectation the answer is u = t + P L (d - A t) instead of t + P [L (d - A t) - L z_bar]. v1's reduced_op was the AffineOperator carrying -L z_bar (linear_optimisation.py:308-316) and AffineOperator composition (affine_operators.py:139-149) kept it. Dense ground truth: \|u_v2 - u_true\| = 3.2519 in both formalisms = \|\|inner.translation\|\|; hand composition t + P*inner(d - A t) with the full affine inner estimator matches to 4e-15; unconstrained LeastSquares matches to 2e-15 (scratchpad/cls_shift.py, re-run); v1 on the same problem matches to 8e-15 (scratchpad/cls_v1.py); direct v1-vs-v2 on a second problem \|u_v2 - u_v1\| = 3.093 with \|u_v1\| = 1.716 (scratchpad/cmn_v1v2.py). The row's 'same algebra' holds only for zero-mean errors, which is all the test suite exercises (tests/test_point.py:253-278,636-639). |

| `linear_optimisation.LinearMinimumNormInversion` | Discrepancy-principle inversion: finds the minimum-norm model fitting the data to a statistically acceptable chi-squared (given a significance level), returning a NonLinearOperator (data -> model) with exact Frechet derivative and adjoint. (point.py:334-435)` | The v1 class-with-minimum_norm_operator(solver, ...) becomes: DiscrepancyPrinciple, which IS the non-linear data->model map (all search options fixed at construction); and MinimumNorm, a fixed-damping LeastSquares whose for_data returns a MinimumNorm at the damping the discrepancy principle finds (exposing the damping v1 hid). Failure: v1 RuntimeError('Discrepancy principle failed.') -> ValueError('The data cannot be fitted ...') (point.py:499-512). Zero-model shortcut retained (point.py:613-615).
