| `linear_optimisation.LinearMinimumNormInversion.discrepancy_search` | For each data vector: if chi_squared_from_residual(data) <= critical value, return the zero model with damping 0; otherwise start at damping = 1.0, halve until chi^2 <= critical (raising RuntimeError('Discrepancy principle failed.') if damping drops below minimum_damping) or double until chi^2 >= critical, each capped at maxiter steps; then bisect up to maxiter times until (upper - lower) < atol + rtol*(lower + upper), else RuntimeError('Bracketing search failed to converge.'). | `_discrepancy_search / _searched_damping (pygeoinf2/inference/point.py:438-513) on numerics.root_find.monotone_root (pygeoinf2/numerics/root_find.py:131-338) over a TikhonovFamily (tikhonov.py:320-449)` | Algorithm replaced: v1 halved/doubled the damping from 1.0 (capped at maxiter each way) then bisected up to maxiter times on the damping itself; v2 widens by factors of 10 from initial=1.0 in both directions (up to expansions=200), then runs Brent's method in log(t) with memoised probes (root_find.py:285-338), closing when high-low <= atol + rtol*(low+high). Zero-model shortcut when chi^2(0,d) <= critical kept (point.py:613-615). Unfittable data: v1 raised RuntimeError only if damping fell below minimum_damping (default 0, so effectively never — it ran maxiter halvings then bisected); v2 stops on solver breakdown and raises ValueError with the misfit reached (point.py:499-512). The 'every damping fits' end (exhausted='high') returns the largest damping probed rather than an error (root_find.py:271-276). Search cost and bracket are reported via RootResult (evaluations, inner_iterations, bracket, converged, exhausted, breakdown). Each evaluation still solves the full Tikhonov system at that damping and computes problem.chi_squared(model, data) (point.py:457-464); with a DirectSolver each such solve re-probes the full matrix (dim applications), as in v1 — see iterative_warm_start. |
| `linear_optimisation.LinearMinimumNormInversion.iterative_warm_start` | When solver is an IterativeLinearSolver, the search calls solver.solve_linear_system(normal_operator, preconditioner, rhs, sys_sol0) with sys_sol0 = the previous bisection step's raw system solution (model in model_space, dual variable in data_space), so successive solves start from the previous answer. | `monotone_root passes the previous probe's solution to every evaluate call (pygeoinf2/numerics/root_find.py:193-200); TikhonovFamily.solve(damping, rhs, x0=) -> DampedSolves.solve -> InverseOperator.solve(rhs, x0=) (tikhonov.py:370-380,429-449; root_find.py:396-416,483-499; solvers.py:283-295)` | Warm start now covers the bracketing phase as well as the bisection phase (v1 warm-started only the bisection loop), and works for any IterativeSolver through InverseOperator.solve(x0=) rather than the removed IterativeLinearSolver.solve_linear_system. Direct solvers ignore x0 and report zero iterations, as in v1. Can be switched off (warm_start=False on monotone_root, not exposed by DiscrepancyPrinciple). Additionally a deferred LinearSolver preconditioner is cached across the sweep (DampedSolves.refresh, root_find.py:386-389,467-481). CORRECTION to the earlier claim of once-only direct-solver matrix extraction: TikhonovFamily constructs DampedSolves with assemble=self.at (tikhonov.py:379) and DampedSolves.operator() takes the assemble branch before _sum_member (root_find.py:408-412), so _matrices()/_sum_member (root_find.py:418-465) are never reached on the Tikhonov path; every probe hands a DirectSolver a fresh TikhonovNormalOperator whose matrix is probed with dim applications — v1 parity, not a saving. Measured (scratchpad/sweep_count.py, re-run, dim 30 model / 20 data, CholeskySolver): TikhonovFamily.solve at t=1,2,3,4 costs 30,30,30,30 (model space) and 20,20,20,20 (data space) forward applications; a bare DampedSolves(base, shift, CholeskySolver()) costs 30,0,0,0 and 20,0,0,0. The once-only extraction fires only for a bare DampedSolves without assemble, which DiscrepancyPrinciple / MinimumNorm.for_data / discrepancy_search never use. |
| `linear_optimisation.LinearMinimumNormInversion.analytic_derivative` | The returned NonLinearOperator's derivative(data) re-runs the discrepancy search, then returns a LinearOperator (data_space -> model_space) with action delta_d -> L delta_d - <w, delta_d> H^-1 u and adjoint delta_u -> L* delta_u - <H^-1 u, delta_u> w, where L is the Tikhonov linear part at the found damping, H^-1 u the inverse normal operator applied to the model, and w = (L* u + R^-1 (A u - d)/damping) / <u, H^-1 u>. | `DiscrepancyPrinciple._derivative / _derivative_from (pygeoinf2/inference/point.py:658-719); _linearise shares one search between value and derivative (point.py:634-647)` | Same formula (du/dd = L - h (x) w, h = H^-1 u, w = (L* u + R^-1 r / t)/<u,h>, same adjoint; data-space push-through identity for h at point.py:690-695; zero operator at damping 0 at point.py:667-675). Differences: (1) NEW saturated case — when the search did not converge (damping pinned at the end of its range) the rank-one term is omitted and the derivative is the fixed-damping L alone (point.py:679-685); but _resolve uses found.converged as the 'damping moves with the data' flag (point.py:616-628), and converged is also False when Brent hits the iterations cap on an interior bracket (root_find.py:337), in which case the rank-one term is silently dropped although the damping is data-dependent — found.exhausted is the flag that means saturation; only bites with a small user-set iterations; (2) the residual is formed against data shifted by the error expectation (point.py:697-698), which v1 did not do; (3) Operator.at(data) computes model and derivative from ONE search (point.py:634-647) where v1 always ran two; calling __call__ and derivative separately still costs two searches; (4) the fixed-damping estimator is built once at the found damping and its inverse reused for h (point.py:677-694) where v1 built solver(normal_operator) twice (linear_optimisation.py:955-985). Requires error.precision as v1 required inverse_covariance (point.py:699). |
| `linear_optimisation.ConstrainedLinearMinimumNormInversion` | Discrepancy-principle minimum-norm inversion with the solution confined exactly to an affine subspace; also provides the non-linear mapping from constraint values to the resulting model with its derivative. Subclass of LinearInversion. | `pygeoinf2.inference.point.ConstrainedMinimumNorm(problem, subspace, /, *, level=0.95, solver=None, formalism='data_space', iterations=60, rtol=1e-6) (pygeoinf2/inference/point.py:948-1120), an Operator` | Renamed; constraint -> subspace; all search options fixed at construction; the instance IS the non-linear data->model map (v1 needed minimum_norm_operator(solver, ...)). Inner DiscrepancyPrinciple on A @ P built once (point.py:989-996) and exposed as .reduced. No with_formalism method. parameterised/data_reduced do not forward iterations/rtol (point.py:998-1002,1023-1043) so they silently revert to defaults. Requires an error measure (through the inner DiscrepancyPrinciple). Unlike ConstrainedLeastSquares it applies the inner operator's full non-linear map, so the error-expectation shift survives: v1 and v2 agree to 3e-11 on a non-zero-mean problem (scratchpad/cmn_v1v2.py). |
| `linear_optimisation.ConstrainedLinearMinimumNormInversion.minimum_norm_operator` | NonLinearOperator mapping data d to the constrained minimum-norm solution u_base + reduced_op(d - A u_base), with derivative(d) = reduced_op.derivative(d - A u_base). | `The ConstrainedMinimumNorm instance: __call__ = t + P inner(d - A t), derivative = P @ inner.derivative(d - A t) (pygeoinf2/inference/point.py:1045-1055)` | Method with (solver, preconditioner, significance_level, minimum_damping, maxiter, rtol, atol) -> the object's constructor with (level, solver, formalism, iterations, rtol); minimum_damping and atol gone; preconditioner lives in the solver. The projector P is applied explicitly to the reduced answer and to its derivative (v1 relied on the reduced solution already lying in range(P)). Always non-linear; no LinearOperator fallback for a noise-free problem (ValueError from DiscrepancyPrinciple). |
| `linear_optimisation.ConstrainedLinearMinimumNormInversion.constraint_value_mapping` | For a fixed dataset, returns a NonLinearOperator mapping a constraint value w (in the constraint operator's codomain) to the constrained minimum-norm model: u = B^+ w + reduced_op(data - A B^+ w), with derivative (I - D_unc @ A) @ B^+ where D_unc is the reduced operator's derivative at the shifted data. | `ConstrainedMinimumNorm.constraint_value_mapping(data, /) -> Operator (pygeoinf2/inference/point.py:1057-1120)` | Signature reduced to (data): solver, preconditioner, significance_level, minimum_damping, maxiter, rtol, atol are taken from the constructor. Same mapping u = B+ w + P D(d - A B+ w) and derivative (I - P D_red A) B+ (v1: (I - D_unc A) B+, without the explicit P). B+ is subspace.pseudo_inverse() (a method, geometry/subspaces.py:525-535) built with the subspace's own solver. Same ValueError without an explicit equation (point.py:1084-1089). Returned as Operator.from_callables(constraint_operator.codomain, model_space, value, derivative=...). Each evaluation still reruns the search. |
| `linear_optimisation.ConstrainedLinearMinimumNormInversion.parameterized_inversion` | Parameterised surrogate pulling the explicit constraint equation back to the parameter space, identical in logic to ConstrainedLinearLeastSquaresInversion.parameterized_inversion. | `ConstrainedMinimumNorm.parameterised(parameterisation, /) (pygeoinf2/inference/point.py:1014-1029) via _parameterised_subspace (point.py:891-931)` | Same pull-back and same NotImplementedError/ValueError guards; LOST the constraint's solver/preconditioner forwarding to from_linear_equation (point.py:929-931 passes no solver -> default CG) and the dense/parallel/n_jobs densification of new_B; formalism override dropped. BUG: iterations and rtol are not forwarded (point.py:1023-1029 pass only level/solver/formalism), so the parameterised estimator reverts to the defaults 60/1e-6. |
| `linear_optimisation.ConstrainedLinearMinimumNormInversion.data_reduced_inversion` | Surrogate on a reduced data space keeping the same constraint. | `ConstrainedMinimumNorm.data_reduced(*args, **kwargs) (pygeoinf2/inference/point.py:1031-1043)` | Renamed; keywords reduction / error; dense/parallel/n_jobs and formalism override gone; constraint kept. iterations and rtol are not forwarded (point.py:1037-1043), reverting to defaults. |
| `linear_optimisation.ConstrainedLinearMinimumNormInversion._get_reduced_operator` | Private helper that both minimum_norm_operator and constraint_value_mapping use to obtain the inner unconstrained NonLinearOperator; it is constructed afresh on every call, with no caching of search results. | `self._inner = DiscrepancyPrinciple(_reduced_problem(problem, subspace), ...) built once in __init__, exposed as .reduced (pygeoinf2/inference/point.py:989-996,1009-1012)` | The inner non-linear operator is constructed once at __init__ (with its TikhonovFamily and resolved solver) rather than afresh on every call; search results are still not cached between calls (each __call__/derivative/constraint_value_mapping evaluation reruns the search, point.py:1048-1055,1105-1113), except that Operator.at(data) on the inner operator shares one search (point.py:634-647). |
| `linear_optimisation.matrix_free_everywhere` | No dense or sparse matrix is formed anywhere in this module; normal operators, Woodbury preconditioners, affine shifts and derivatives are all compositions of LinearOperator/AffineOperator objects. Densification happens only when a user passes dense=True (with parallel/n_jobs) to parameterized_inversion/data_reduced_inversion, which delegate to LinearForwardProblem.parameterized_problem / data_reduced_problem and LinearOperator.with_dense_matrix. | `inference/point.py and inference/tikhonov.py form no matrices (grep 'dense\|matrix' finds none); DampedSolves (pygeoinf2/numerics/root_find.py:396-465)` | The estimators, normal operators, Woodbury forms, affine shifts and derivatives are all operator compositions as in v1. Two changes: (1) the opt-in dense=True/parallel/n_jobs flags on parameterised/data_reduced are gone — densification is now done by the user on the operator (LinearOperator.assembled(n_jobs=)/matrix(n_jobs=), algebra/operators.py:680-770,951-1000) before building the problem; (2) DampedSolves._sum_member/_matrices (root_find.py:418-465) can extract the dense base and shift matrices once for a DirectSolver and add them per damping, but this does NOT apply to the discrepancy sweep: TikhonovFamily passes assemble=self.at (tikhonov.py:379), which DampedSolves.operator() takes before _sum_member (root_find.py:408-412), so with a DirectSolver the summed operator is re-extracted at every damping exactly as v1 did (measured 30/30/30/30 applications per probe vs 30/0/0/0 for a bare DampedSolves, scratchpad/sweep_count.py). The once-only path is reachable only through a bare DampedSolves without assemble, which nothing in inference/ uses. |
| `linear_optimisation.solver_protocol` | Solvers are callable factories: solver(operator) -> inverse LinearOperator; IterativeLinearSolver additionally accepts solver(operator, preconditioner=...) and provides solve_linear_system(operator, preconditioner, rhs, x0) for warm-started solves; preconditioners are only forwarded to IterativeLinearSolver instances. | `numerics.solvers.LinearSolver.__call__(operator) -> InverseOperator with .solve(y, x0=) -> SolveResult (pygeoinf2/numerics/solvers.py:93-147,207-295); IterativeSolver carries the preconditioner (solvers.py:654-801); resolve_solver (solvers.py:150-205)` | Same factory idea (solver(operator) -> inverse operator) but: IterativeLinearSolver renamed IterativeSolver; the call form solver(operator, preconditioner=...) is gone — the preconditioner is a constructor argument / with_preconditioner; solve_linear_system(operator, preconditioner, rhs, x0) is gone — warm starts go through InverseOperator.solve(rhs, x0=) on any solver (direct ones ignore x0); solvers return a SolveResult carrying iterations/converged so the sweep can report cost; solvers validate traits and squareness (solvers.py:109-140). A callable operator->solver factory is also accepted wherever a solver is (resolve_solver). |

### backus_gilbert — `backus_gilbert.py, quadratic_form_quantile.py`

| v1 | what it did | v2 | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| `backus_gilbert.DualMasterCostFunction` | Subclass of NonLinearForm on the data space D implementing the Backus-Gilbert / dual-level-set master dual cost φ(λ; q) = (λ, d̃)_D + σ_B(T*q − G*λ) + σ_V(−λ); minimising φ over λ yields the support value h_U(q) of the property set U in direction q. | `pygeoinf2.inference.backus.DualFeasibleProperty.dual_cost(direction, data) -> Functional (backus.py:969-1092)` | No longer a class. v1's nine-argument NonLinearForm subclass is now a method on the route-(d) estimator returning a `Functional.from_callables(space, value, gradient=gradient)` closure per (direction, data). Inputs changed kind: `model_prior_support`/`data_error_support` (SupportFunction objects) became `prior`/`noise` ConvexSets passed to the estimator constructor, whose `.support_function()` and `.support_maximiser()` supply what v1's `__call__`/`support_point` did; `G`/`T` became `problem.forward_operator`/`target`; `observed_data`/`q_direction` became per-call `data`/`direction`. The subgradient is registered as `gradient=` (so `has_derivative` is True and LBFGS will accept the nonsmooth cost). Value and gradient share G*λ and −λ through a one-entry memo keyed on the certificate object (backus.py:1062-1076), replacing v1's explicit fused method — the closure is therefore stateful, not stateless as v1's was (see __call__ row for the in-place-mutation hazard). The finite-difference fallback for a set with no support point is gone: `support_maximiser` on a set without one raises (geometry/convex.py:113-131), and a set built by `ConvexSet.from_support_function(..., maximiser=)` raises too because `_OracleSet` names its hook `maximiser` and never overrides `support_maximiser` (convex.py:222-254). Constructor validation is reduced to `target.domain == model_space` (backus.py:1014). Also new: `smoothed_dual_cost` (Moreau-Yosida, balls/ellipsoids only, backus.py:1166-1221) and a `noise=None` default that requires the problem to carry a set-valued error rather than hardening a Gaussian (backus.py:1019-1023). DualFeasibleProperty is exported from `pygeoinf2.inference` (inference/__init__.py:25); the top-level __init__ exports BackusGilbert/BackusInference/FeasibleProperty only (__init__.py:80-86,132-137). |
| `backus_gilbert.DualMasterCostFunction.__call__` | Inherited from NonLinearForm; evaluates φ(λ; q) by dispatching to the registered _mapping: term1 = domain.inner_product(λ, d̃); term2 = σ_B(T*q − G*λ) using model_space.subtract; term3 = σ_V(−λ) using domain.negative. | `the `value` closure inside DualFeasibleProperty.dual_cost, reached as `cost(certificate)` (backus.py:1078-1084), behind the identity-keyed memo at :1064-1076` | Same three terms, same operator count: (λ, d) + h_prior(T*q − A*λ) + h_noise(−λ), one A* application, T*q precomputed at backus.py:1052. What changed is that v1's `_mapping` was stateless (G*λ recomputed on every call, v1 backus_gilbert.py:92-105) and v2's is not: the residual and −λ are answered from a one-entry memo keyed on the certificate OBJECT (`cache.get("certificate") is not certificate`, :1070). If the same array is mutated in place between two calls the memo returns the residual of the OLD contents and both value and gradient are silently wrong. v2's own `HilbertSpace.axpy` mutates its target in place (algebra/spaces.py:323-326, `y += a * x`), and the public `SubgradientDescent` (numerics/convex.py:516-537, exported from pygeoinf2.numerics) performs exactly the hazardous sequence `functional.subgradient(x)` -> `x = space.axpy(-step, subgradient, x)` -> `functional(x)`. Reproduced (re-run for this audit): on an 8x3 Euclidean problem `cost(lam)`, then `D.axpy(1.0, ones, lam)`, then `cost(lam)` gave 3.7787 where a fresh dual_cost gave 6.7621, and the gradients differed; `SubgradientDescent(max_iterations=20).minimise(cost, zeros)` reported best value −100.59 at a point where a fresh cost evaluates to −14.33. ProximalBundleMethod (the route's default) allocates a new candidate per step, so the estimator's own path is unaffected; the memo tests at tests/test_backus.py:769-829 cover address recycling only, not in-place mutation. |
| `backus_gilbert.DualMasterCostFunction.subgradient` | Inherited from NonLinearForm and wired to _subgradient at construction; returns an element g ∈ ∂φ(λ) = d̃ − G v − w where v ∈ ∂σ_B(T*q − G*λ) and w ∈ ∂σ_V(−λ) are obtained via SupportFunction.support_point(). | ``cost.subgradient(certificate)` / `cost.gradient(certificate)` on the Functional returned by dual_cost (backus.py:1086-1092; operators.py:1902-1915, 2080-2087)` | The analytic formula d − A x_prior − x_noise is ported, but registered as `gradient=` rather than `subgradient=`, so `has_derivative` is True, `gradient()` no longer raises, and `subgradient()` returns the gradient by the base-class default. It reads the residual from the same identity-keyed memo as the value, so it inherits the in-place-mutation hazard described in the __call__ row. No finite-difference fallback: where v1 silently fell back when a support point was None, v2's `ConvexSet.support_maximiser` raises NotImplementedError (convex.py:113-131). For a set built by `ConvexSet.from_support_function(domain, oracle, maximiser=...)` the situation is worse than 'no fallback': `_OracleSet` defines `maximiser` (convex.py:235) but never overrides `support_maximiser`, and nothing in the package calls `.maximiser(` (grep), so even an oracle set built WITH a user-supplied maximiser raises the base NotImplementedError inside the gradient. This includes the sets FeasibleProperty/DualFeasibleProperty themselves return from `__call__` (backus.py:239, :800, :1467), so a route output cannot be reused as a route-(d) prior. |
| `backus_gilbert.DualMasterCostFunction.value_and_subgradient` | Fused evaluation returning (φ(λ; q), g) in one pass, sharing G*λ and using SupportFunction.value_and_support_point() for both support functions so the value and subgradient cost one support evaluation each instead of two. | `implicit: the one-entry memo in dual_cost (backus.py:1058-1076) shares G*λ and −λ between `cost(x)` and `cost.gradient(x)` when called consecutively on the same certificate object` | No explicit fused method. Sharing depends on the caller evaluating value then gradient on the *same object* (identity test, backus.py:1070); ProximalBundleMethod does so (numerics/convex.py:966-968) so the saving of one A* application and one negation is realised there, and REVIEW2 3.3 fixed the earlier id()-keyed staleness bug (backus.py:1065-1071, tests test_backus.py:769-829). The identity keying is still a hazard for a caller that mutates the certificate in place between calls (see __call__ row: SubgradientDescent + axpy reproduces wrong values). What is NOT fused: the support *value* and support *maximiser* are separate calls (`prior_support(residual)` at :1082 vs `support_maximiser(residual)` at :1088), whereas v1's `SupportFunction.value_and_support_point` computed both in one pass — for an ellipsoid the covariance is now applied twice per oracle (review/geometry_plotting.md:33,90). No finite-difference fallback. |
| `backus_gilbert.DualMasterCostFunction._subgradient` | Computes g = d̃ − G v − w using support_point() of the two SupportFunctions; if either support_point returns None, silently falls back to a central finite-difference gradient of the whole cost. | `the `gradient` closure in dual_cost (backus.py:1086-1091)` | Analytic path ported: residual from memo, `forward(prior.support_maximiser(residual))`, `noise.support_maximiser(negated)`, then d − A v − w. The finite-difference fallback when a support point is unavailable is gone; such a set raises from `support_maximiser` instead — and so does an `_OracleSet` given a maximiser, because it exposes it under the name `maximiser`, which nothing calls (convex.py:235; grep). Registered as the gradient rather than the subgradient (see subgradient row). |
| `backus_gilbert.DualMasterCostFunction._gradient` | Defined as an alias of _subgradient 'for backward compatibility', but NonLinearForm.__init__ sets the instance attribute self._gradient = None, which shadows this method; consequently has_gradient is False and gradient() raises NotImplementedError. | ``cost.gradient(certificate)` on the Functional from dual_cost (operators.py:1882-1884 via _CallableFunctional._derivative, :2069-2073)` | v1's intended-but-dead alias is now the live behaviour: `gradient()` returns the subgradient because dual_cost registers it as `gradient=`. v1 as written raised NotImplementedError and had has_gradient False; v2 has_derivative True. Consequence: smooth optimisers (LBFGS etc., optimisation.py:154-158 check `has_derivative`) accept the nonsmooth dual cost without complaint. |
| `backus_gilbert.DualMasterCostFunction._validation` | Raises ValueError unless: the three spaces are HilbertSpace instances; G and T are LinearOperator instances with G: model_space→data_space and T: model_space→property_space (checked via domain/codomain equality); both supports are SupportFunction instances whose primal_domain equals model_space / data_space respectively; observed_data is an element of data_space and q_direction of property_space. | `DualFeasibleProperty.__init__ (backus.py:1013-1023)` | Only two checks remain: `target.domain != problem.model_space` -> ValueError (:1013-1014) and, when noise is omitted, that the problem's error is a ConvexSet -> ValueError (:1019-1023). Gone: isinstance checks on spaces/operators/support functions; the codomain checks (G: M->D, T: M->P) — G is validated by LinearForwardProblem only as being a LinearOperator; `prior.domain == model_space` and `noise.domain == data_space`; `data` element-of-data-space; `direction` element-of-property-space. A prior on the wrong space fails later with an arithmetic error inside dual_cost rather than at construction. |
| `backus_gilbert.BackusInference.prior_norm_bound` | Getter/setter for the prior bound on the model norm; the setter raises ValueError if value <= 0. | `the `prior: Ball` positional argument; stored as private `_radius` (backus.py:305, 528) / `_prior_radius` (BackusGilbert :204)` | The bound is now the radius of a Ball on the model space, passed at construction. No public getter and no setter on any of the three classes (grep `def prior_norm_bound\|def radius` in backus.py: none); the value is only reachable through the private `_radius`. Positivity: v1's setter raised ValueError for value <= 0. v2's Ball rejects only negative radii (convex.py:586-587); BackusGilbert additionally rejects radius <= 0 (backus.py:181-182) but BackusInference and FeasibleProperty accept radius 0 silently. To change the bound, construct a new estimator (`push_forward` rebuilds with the same radius, :469-475). |
| `backus_gilbert.BackusInference.significance_level` | Getter/setter for the significance level; the setter raises ValueError unless 0 < value < 1 and then recomputes the cached critical chi-squared via forward_problem.critical_chi_squared(...). | ``level: float = 0.95` keyword on BackusGilbert (backus.py:158) and FeasibleProperty (:524); absent from BackusInference and DualFeasibleProperty` | Route (a) BackusInference has no level at all (error-free). On BackusGilbert/FeasibleProperty `level` is a constructor keyword consumed once by `harden_error(problem, level=level)` (backus.py:93-133) -> `error_measure.ambient_ball(level=...)`, not stored, no getter/setter. Range validation: none in the constructor; an out-of-range level reaches `weighted_chi2_quantile` which raises ValueError 'A probability lies in (0, 1)' (quadratic_forms.py:243-244) — so v1's promised ValueError finally happens, but indirectly and only when the error is Gaussian. Semantics differ: v1's level set a chi-squared (Mahalanobis) threshold; v2's level sets the radius of a ball in the data space's OWN norm carrying that probability (weighted chi-square of the covariance eigenvalues). The two coincide only for isotropic covariance on an orthonormal data space; otherwise v2 route (c) uses a different data-compatibility set. Cost: where v1's threshold was one chi2.ppf, v2's ambient_ball on a covariance not diagonal in the data basis forms the dense Galerkin matrix and takes a generalised eigh (gaussian.py:1636-1652), then inverts a weighted chi-square by Imhof quadrature (see dense_regressions). The exact chi-squared set is available on route (d) by passing `noise=` an Ellipsoid (problem.consistency_set / error_measure.credible_set). v1's setter-ordering bug (critical value computed from the stale level) has no counterpart. |
| `backus_gilbert.BackusInference.test_data_compatibility` | Returns True if a model exists that is compatible with both the data (at the chi-squared significance level) and the prior norm bound: builds LinearMinimumNormInversion(forward_problem).minimum_norm_operator(solver, preconditioner=..., significance_level=..., minimum_damping=..., maxiter=..., rtol=..., atol=...), applies it to data, and compares model_space.norm(solution) <= prior_norm_bound. | ``is_feasible(data)` on BackusInference (backus.py:352-374), FeasibleProperty (:767-791) and DualFeasibleProperty (:1441-1457)` | Three predicates replace one method, none with v1's computation or options. (1) BackusInference.is_feasible: error-free — `\|\|A*(AA*)^-1 d\|\| <= r` via `budget(data) >= 0` (:340-374), one solver-based minimum-norm solve, matrix-free, no chi-squared level. (2) FeasibleProperty.is_feasible: attempts one support evaluation along basis_vector(0) and returns False on the bisection's ValueError (:789-791); this goes through `_data_gram`, a DENSE `eigh` of the dim(D)×dim(D) matrix of A A* formed by `.matrix(form="components")` (:568-589) and requires an orthonormal data space (:575-580) — v1 was matrix-free Krylov via LinearMinimumNormInversion. (3) DualFeasibleProperty.is_feasible: one bundle minimisation, False if `_check_bounded` raises, i.e. only when the run did NOT converge AND the value fell below −_UNBOUNDED = −1e6 (:34-36, :1421-1429, :1441-1457). This is a heuristic, not v1's exact norm comparison: an infeasible problem whose dual has not fallen below −1e6 within the bundle's iteration budget is reported feasible. All v1 keywords are gone: `solver` (required positional in v1), `preconditioner`, `minimum_damping`, `maxiter`, `rtol`, `atol`. v1's exact test (minimum-norm model at the chi-squared discrepancy, norm compared with the bound) is reproducible by hand as `problem.model_space.norm(DiscrepancyPrinciple(problem, level=level, solver=..., iterations=..., rtol=...)(data)) <= r` (inference/point.py:516-620), which raises ValueError rather than returning when no model fits (point.py:497-513). |
| `backus_gilbert.BackusInference.constructor_typo` | __init__ executes `self.signficance_level = significance_level` (missing 'i'), creating a stray public attribute instead of invoking the significance_level property setter; hence _significance_level and _critical_chi_squared are never initialised. | `BackusInference.__init__ (backus.py:285-318)` | The defect does not exist in v2: there is no `signficance_level` attribute (grep: no hits for 'signficance'), because the v2 constructor takes no significance level at all. The constructor validates `target.domain == model_space` (ValueError, :301-302) and that `prior` is a Ball (TypeError via _ball_radius, :80-90); it does not validate a level, so v1's docstring promise of ValueError for an out-of-range significance is moot on this class and is met only indirectly on BackusGilbert/FeasibleProperty (see significance_level row). |
| `quadratic_form_quantile.weighted_chi2_cdf` | Evaluates P(Q <= t) for the weighted chi-square variable Q = Σ_j w_j Z_j², Z_j iid N(0,1), by one of five methods: auto (picks saddlepoint or imhof from spectrum isotropy and tol), imhof (characteristic-function inversion), ws (Welch–Satterthwaite), saddlepoint (Lugannani–Rice), mc (Monte Carlo). | `pygeoinf2.numerics.quadratic_forms.weighted_chi2_cdf(weights, value, /, *, method="auto", tolerance=1e-10, samples=200_000, rng=None) -> float (quadratic_forms.py:153-209)` | Signature: `t` -> `value`, positional-only, SCALAR ONLY (`if value <= 0.0`, :185 — an array raises 'truth value ambiguous'); `rtol` -> `tolerance` with default 1e-8 -> 1e-10; `n_samples` -> `samples` with default 100_000 -> 200_000; `tol` removed. Methods: `imhof` kept, `ws` -> `matched`, `mc` -> `monte_carlo`, `saddlepoint` REMOVED, `auto` no longer a ν_eff-based choice — it is Imhof with a fallback to `matched` on ArithmeticError/ValueError (:199-207). Degenerate weights (empty/all-zero) now raise ValueError (:61-70) instead of returning the indicator. Equal-weights shortcut now fires for every method, including matched and monte_carlo, before the method name is validated (:191-192), with np.allclose default tolerances (rtol 1e-5) instead of v1's rtol=1e-12 — so weights within 1e-5 relative are treated as equal, and an unknown method name with equal weights returns silently. `value <= 0` returns 0.0 for all methods. Monte Carlo draws the full (samples × n) matrix at once (:197). Exported from `pygeoinf2.numerics` (numerics/__init__.py:73-75) — v1 exported nothing. |
| `quadratic_form_quantile.weighted_chi2_quantile` | Returns r such that P(Σ_j w_j Z_j² <= r) = probability, by inverting the chosen CDF method (imhof/saddlepoint via bracketed brentq), or directly via closed-form Welch–Satterthwaite (ws) or empirical np.quantile of Monte Carlo draws (mc). | `pygeoinf2.numerics.quadratic_forms.weighted_chi2_quantile(weights, probability, /, *, method="auto", tolerance=1e-10, samples=100_000, rng=None) -> float (quadratic_forms.py:212-285)` | Positional-only leading args; `rtol` -> `tolerance` (now the CDF's Imhof tolerance only; the root-finder tolerance is fixed at xtol=rtol=1e-12, :283-284, not user-settable — v1's default was 1e-6); `n_samples` -> `samples`; `tol` removed; `saddlepoint` removed; `ws` -> `matched`, `mc` -> `monte_carlo`. `method="matched"` no longer returns the closed form a·chi2.ppf: it root-finds on the matched CDF (:262-285), which is the same number more expensively. Empty/all-zero weights raise ValueError instead of returning 0.0. Equal-weights fast path now applies to all methods incl. matched/monte_carlo (:249-250), with loosened np.allclose defaults. Bracket loops capped at 60 steps with no RuntimeError on failure (:262-273); on failure brentq raises its own ValueError. Unknown method: raised from the first CDF probe (unless weights are equal, in which case it returns silently). Consumer changed: GaussianMeasure.ambient_ball / _ambient_ball_from_spectrum (probability/gaussian.py:1673-1685) with its own `quantile_method` and ν_eff rule. |
| `quadratic_form_quantile.auto_method_selection` | Computes effective degrees of freedom ν_eff = (Σw)²/Σw² (1.0 if Σw² == 0) and an empirical saddlepoint error estimate 0.1/ν_eff; returns 'saddlepoint' if 3 × that estimate < tol, else 'imhof'. | ``method="auto"` in quadratic_forms.py:199-207 (Imhof with fallback) and GaussianMeasure._quantile_method_for (probability/gaussian.py:1687-1716)` | Inside the quantile/cdf functions 'auto' is now: try Imhof; on ArithmeticError/ValueError return the moment-matched CDF (:199-207). There is no ν_eff rule and no `tol` keyword. A ν_eff rule exists only in the Gaussian-measure consumer: `_quantile_method_for` returns 'imhof' when there are <= 1000 positive weights, else 'matched' iff ν_eff > 100 (gaussian.py:1712-1716) — chosen for speed at long spectra, not for a user-stated accuracy. v1's rule (saddlepoint iff 0.3/ν_eff < tol) selected the cheap saddlepoint at ν_eff > 30 for the default tol; v2 has no saddlepoint to select, so in the 30 < ν_eff regime with <= 1000 weights every evaluation is a full Imhof quadrature. |
| `quadratic_form_quantile.degenerate_weights` | Both public functions treat a length-zero or all-zero weight array as the point mass at 0: the CDF returns 1 for t >= 0 and 0 otherwise; the quantile returns 0.0. | `_validate (quadratic_forms.py:61-70)` | Length-zero -> ValueError 'At least one weight is needed.'; all-zero -> ValueError 'At least one weight must be positive.' — v1 returned the point-mass-at-0 answers (indicator 1[t>=0]; quantile 0.0). Zero weights mixed with positive ones are now stripped (`live = values[values > 0]`, :67-70) rather than carried along, which is equivalent for the sums. Tested at tests/test_phase_four.py:984-985 as the intended contract. |
| `quadratic_form_quantile.equal_weights_fast_path` | If all strictly positive weights are equal (np.allclose(positive, positive[0], rtol=1e-12, atol=0)) the distribution is w·χ²_n exactly and scipy.stats.chi2 is used: in weighted_chi2_quantile (for imhof/saddlepoint/auto) and inside _imhof_cdf. | `quadratic_forms.py:186-192 (cdf) and :249-250 (quantile)` | Moved to the public entry points and made unconditional: it now fires for `matched` and `monte_carlo` too (v1 bypassed it for those), and fires BEFORE method-name validation. Criterion loosened from `np.allclose(..., rtol=1e-12, atol=0.0)` to `np.allclose(live, live[0])` (rtol 1e-5, atol 1e-8), so spectra differing by up to 1e-5 relative are treated as exactly chi-square. Inside `_imhof` there is no longer a shortcut (v1's `_imhof_cdf` had one) but it is unreachable from the public path anyway. Note: tests/test_phase_four.py:1415-1427 perturbs the weights by 1e-12 'so the short circuit does not fire' — with these tolerances it does fire, so that test exercises chi2.cdf against itself, not Imhof. |
| `quadratic_form_quantile.weight_validation` | Coerces weights to a flat float64 array (np.asarray(...).ravel()); raises ValueError 'weights must be finite.' on NaN/inf and 'weights must be non-negative.' on any negative entry. | `_validate (quadratic_forms.py:61-70)` | Still ravels to float; negative -> ValueError (message 'The weights must be non-negative.'). The finiteness check is gone: `inf` passes (v1 raised 'weights must be finite.'); `NaN` is not caught by `np.any(values < 0)` and only trips the 'At least one weight must be positive.' check if every entry is NaN — a NaN mixed with positive weights is silently dropped by `values > 0`. Returns only the positive entries, and raises on empty/all-zero (see degenerate row). |
| `quadratic_form_quantile.imhof_method` | Computes F(t) = 1/2 − (1/π)∫_0^∞ sin(θ(u))/(u ρ(u)) du by a vectorised fixed-step trapezoidal rule on a truncated domain [h, U], with Richardson-style step halving until the relative change is below rtol; returns 0 for t <= 0 and clips the result to [0, 1]. | `_imhof(weights, value, /, *, tolerance) and _imhof_integrand (quadratic_forms.py:73-141)` | Algorithm ported line for line (log-space integrand, doubling truncation from 4/w_max with 80 doublings, U >= 64π/t, h = 2π/t/32, 6 halvings, 200_000 step cap, f0 = ½(Σw − t), clip to [0,1]). Differences: keyword `rtol` -> `tolerance`, default 1e-8 -> 1e-10 (from the public cdf, :159) so the refinement loop runs more halvings; convergence test `<` -> `<=` (:132-134); the equal-weights shortcut moved out to the caller; `t <= 0` handled by the caller (:185); a `live.size == 0` indicator guard (:101-103) that the caller's validation makes unreachable. Docstring at :88-107 attributes the method to v1. |
| `quadratic_form_quantile.welch_satterthwaite_method` | Matches Q to a scaled chi-square a·χ²_ν with a = Σw²/Σw and ν = (Σw)²/Σw², then uses scipy.stats.chi2.cdf(t/a, df=ν) or a·chi2.ppf(p, df=ν). | `_matched (quadratic_forms.py:144-150), method name "matched"` | Renamed `ws` -> `matched` (docstring says 'Satterthwaite-Welch'). Only the CDF is ported (`chi2.cdf(value/scale, degrees)`); `_ws_params` and `_ws_quantile` have no counterpart — the quantile with `method="matched"` is obtained by brentq on `_matched` (quadratic_forms.py:262-285) instead of the closed form a·chi2.ppf(p, ν). The moment-matched quantile IS computed in closed form as the bracket seed (:257-259) but not returned. Uses: seed for inversion (kept), fallback for `auto` on an Imhof exception (:206-207; v1's saddlepoint fallbacks are gone with the saddlepoint). Not vectorised over t (scalar only). |
| `quadratic_form_quantile.monte_carlo_method` | Draws n_samples realisations of Q = Σ w_j Z_j² with a NumPy Generator (default np.random.default_rng()), in chunks of max(1, 1_000_000 // n_weights) rows so peak memory stays ≈ 8 MB regardless of spectrum length; the CDF is the sorted-sample fraction via np.searchsorted(side='right')/n_samples and the quantile is np.quantile(samples, probability). | `inline in weighted_chi2_cdf (quadratic_forms.py:195-198) and weighted_chi2_quantile (:252-256), method name "monte_carlo"` | Renamed `mc` -> `monte_carlo`, `n_samples` -> `samples`; cdf default 100_000 -> 200_000 (quantile stays 100_000). Chunking is gone: v2 allocates the full `(samples, n_weights)` standard-normal matrix in one call (`generator.standard_normal((samples, live.size))`), so peak memory is 8·samples·n bytes — 8 GB at 10^5 weights × 10^4 samples — where v1 capped it at ~8 MB. CDF uses `np.mean(draws**2 @ live <= value)` instead of sort+searchsorted (equivalent for a scalar). Quantile is the empirical np.quantile as in v1. Default rng np.random.default_rng() as in v1. Restored by REVIEW round (tests/test_phase_four.py:1451-1490 'v2's took no rng...'). |
| `quadratic_form_quantile.cdf_inversion` | Seeds a bracket [½ t_ws, 2 t_ws] from the Welch–Satterthwaite quantile (floored at 1e-12), widens it by halving lo / doubling hi until cdf(lo) <= p <= cdf(hi), then solves cdf(t) − p = 0 with scipy.optimize.brentq(rtol=rtol, xtol=rtol). | `inline in weighted_chi2_quantile (quadratic_forms.py:257-285)` | Same shape (moment-matched seed, [½·seed, 2·seed] bracket, halve/double until it brackets, brentq) with these differences: seed not floored at 1e-12; bracket loops are capped at 60 iterations each with no explicit failure — v1 returned 0.0 below 1e-300 and raised RuntimeError('Unable to bracket...') above 1e30, v2 silently hands whatever bracket it has to brentq, which raises its own ValueError; brentq tolerances are hard-coded xtol=rtol=1e-12 rather than the user's `rtol` (v1 default 1e-6); each probe goes through the PUBLIC cdf (:263, :269, :278-281) with tolerance 1e-10, so the equal-weights shortcut and method validation run per probe. Net: many more Imhof quadratures per quantile than v1 at defaults. |

### symmetric_space_base — `symmetric_space/symmetric_space.py`

| v1 | what it did | v2 | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| `symmetric_space.InvariantLinearAutomorphism` | A LinearOperator on a SymmetricHilbertSpace that is invariant under the symmetry group, i.e. a function f(Delta) of the Laplacian, diagonal in the eigenfunction basis. Subclasses DiagonalSparseMatrixLinearOperator. | `algebra.diagonal.DiagonalLinearOperator(domain, eigenvalues, *, traits=Traits.NONE)` | Stored as a numpy eigenvalue array rather than a scipy.sparse dia matrix (no longer a DiagonalSparseMatrixLinearOperator subclass); domain generalised from SymmetricHilbertSpace to any CoordinateSpace, with self-adjointness deduced only when the metric is diagonal; traits (SELF_ADJOINT/PSD/PD/INVERTIBLE/UNITARY/IDEMPOTENT) deduced from the values. Same closure under +, -, @, scalar *, neg, abs, pow and functional calculus via the specialisation protocol. |
| `symmetric_space.InvariantLinearAutomorphism.from_index_function` | Builds f(Delta) where the eigenvalue multiplier is given as a function g of the eigenvalue index rather than of the Laplacian eigenvalue. | `SymmetricSpace.spectral_operator(values, *, traits=)` | Takes an explicit array of one value per component instead of a callable on eigenvalue indices; moved from a staticmethod on the operator to a method on the space. There is no public index iteration, but a full per-(l,m)/wavevector index function is still expressible without private access by filling a pyshtools-shaped (or rfftn-shaped) coefficient array V and taking space.to_components(space.from_coefficients(V))/space.radius (== V[packing] exactly); degree-only functions use space.degrees directly. |
| `symmetric_space.InvariantLinearAutomorphism.from_function` | Builds f(Delta) for a scalar function f defined on the Laplacian spectrum. | `SymmetricSpace.invariant_operator(symbol, *, traits=)` | Moved to the space; `symbol` must be vectorised over the whole eigenvalue array (v1 called scalar f per eigenvalue); raises ValueError if the returned shape is not (dim,). No np.vectorize fallback. |
| `symmetric_space.InvariantLinearAutomorphism.inverse` | The inverse operator, formed from reciprocal eigenvalues. | `DiagonalLinearOperator.inverse` | Raises ZeroDivisionError instead of ValueError on a zero eigenvalue. |
| `symmetric_space.InvariantLinearAutomorphism.apply_function` | Functional calculus: applies func elementwise to the eigenvalues and returns f(A). | `DiagonalLinearOperator.apply_function(function)` | Function must be vectorised; the v1 fallback to np.vectorize on TypeError/AttributeError is gone and a shape mismatch raises ValueError. |
| `symmetric_space.InvariantGaussianMeasure` | A GaussianMeasure on a SymmetricHilbertSpace whose covariance is invariant under the symmetry group (a function of the Laplacian, diagonal in the eigenbasis), with Karhunen-Loeve sampling. | `SymmetricSpace.invariant_measure(spectral_variances, *, expectation=None, pointwise_std=None, norm_std=None) -> GaussianMeasure` | No longer a class: a factory returning a plain GaussianMeasure whose covariance/factor/precision are DiagonalLinearOperators. New validation (shape must be (dim,), variances must be non-negative -> ValueError; v1 had none). Gains pointwise_std/norm_std calibration keywords. Fast paths (spectral KL, exact norms, closure under +, scalar*, translate, diagonal affine maps) are now generic on any diagonal-covariance GaussianMeasure. |
| `symmetric_space.InvariantGaussianMeasure.from_function` | Builds an invariant measure with covariance f(Delta), f a function of the Laplacian eigenvalue. | `space.invariant_measure(callable, expectation=)` | Renamed and moved to the space; callable must be vectorised over the eigenvalue array. |
| `symmetric_space.InvariantGaussianMeasure.affine_mapping` | Override of GaussianMeasure.affine_mapping that keeps the result invariant when the map is a translation or an InvariantLinearAutomorphism, and otherwise injects a spectrally regularised block preconditioner before deferring to the base class. | `measure.affine_map(operator, *, translation=None); measure.translate(v); measure.push_forward(op); A @ measure` | Branches (1) translation and (2) diagonal operator are kept generically (diagonal factor/precision survive via _combine_affine/_mapped_precision). Branch (3) is dropped: the `inverse_solver` and `inverse_preconditioner` keyword arguments and the automatic water-filling + Jacobi-Schur block preconditioner no longer exist; a generic operator gives a GaussianMeasure with covariance op@C@op*, no precision. |
| `symmetric_space.InvariantGaussianMeasure.kl_divergence` | Override computing D_KL(self \|\| other); when both are InvariantGaussianMeasures on the same domain and method == 'auto', computes it exactly in O(N) from the spectral variances. | `GaussianMeasure.kl_divergence(other, *, method='auto'\|'spectral'\|'dense'\|'stochastic', solver=, samples=, sample_rtol=, max_samples=, n_jobs=, rng=, dense_limit=4000, **kwargs)` | O(dim) spectral route is generic for any two diagonal-covariance measures on the same space (not only same-class); singular reference raises ValueError (v1 divided by zero silently). 'auto' fallback changed: dense only when dim <= dense_limit, otherwise raises rather than v1's unconditional dense. 'randomized' renamed 'stochastic'. Also available as kl_divergence_estimate with error bar. |
| `symmetric_space.InvariantGaussianMeasure.nuclear_norm` | Override returning the exact nuclear (trace) norm of the covariance as covariance.trace. | `GaussianMeasure.nuclear_norm(*, method='auto', samples=100, rtol=None, rng=None, n_jobs=None)` | Exact sum of \|eigenvalues\| when covariance is diagonal (same result). Signature changed: v1's exact/size_estimate/method('variable'\|'fixed')/max_samples/block_size/parallel kwargs removed; new method/samples/rtol/rng/n_jobs. |
| `symmetric_space.InvariantGaussianMeasure.hilbert_schmidt_norm` | Override returning the exact Hilbert-Schmidt norm sqrt(Tr(C^2)) from the invariant covariance. | `GaussianMeasure.hilbert_schmidt_norm(*, method='auto', samples=, rtol=, rng=, n_jobs=)` | Exact sqrt(sum eig^2) on a diagonal covariance; same signature change as nuclear_norm. |
| `symmetric_space.InvariantGaussianMeasure.__mul__` | Scales the random variable by alpha: variances scale by alpha^2, mean by alpha. | `GaussianMeasure._combine_scale via ProbabilityMeasure.__mul__` | Diagonal covariance, factor and precision preserved, but the explicit O(dim) Karhunen-Loeve sampler is not carried: _combine_scale rebuilds without sample=, so the result samples through the DiagonalLinearOperator factor (white-noise synthesis + analysis + synthesis, three transforms per draw instead of one). v1 returned an InvariantGaussianMeasure whose constructor re-registered _kl_sample. |
| `symmetric_space.InvariantGaussianMeasure.__rmul__` | Right scalar multiplication; same as __mul__. | `ProbabilityMeasure.__rmul__` | As __mul__: the KL sampler is dropped and a draw costs three transforms instead of one. |
| `symmetric_space.InvariantGaussianMeasure.__truediv__` | Division by a scalar, implemented as multiplication by 1/alpha. | `ProbabilityMeasure.__truediv__` | Raises ZeroDivisionError on division by zero (v1 would produce inf). As __mul__, the KL sampler is dropped (runtime: (m/2)._sample_fn is None). |
| `symmetric_space.InvariantGaussianMeasure.__add__` | Sum of two independent measures; if other is invariant, adds spectral variances and expectations and stays invariant. | `GaussianMeasure._combine_add via ProbabilityMeasure.__add__` | Two diagonal covariances add to a diagonal one and factor/precision are rebuilt from it, but (1) when the summed variances are all positive _combine_add sets sample=None ('the factor is the better sampler'), so the one-synthesis KL draw becomes the three-transform factor route; (2) when any summed variance is zero (band-limited or degenerate invariant measures) _diagonal_inverse returns (None, None) because it requires values > 0, so the sum has NO covariance factor and no precision and samples as two independent draws added. v1 kept a single KL draw from sqrt of the summed variances and an inverse covariance whenever all were positive. |
| `symmetric_space.InvariantGaussianMeasure.__sub__` | Difference of two independent measures; invariant fast path ADDS spectral variances and subtracts expectations. | `ProbabilityMeasure.__sub__ -> self + (-1.0*other)` | self + (-1.0*other): inherits both the __mul__ and __add__ regressions (KL sampler dropped; factor/precision lost if any summed variance is zero). |
| `symmetric_space.InvariantGaussianMeasure._kl_sample` | Sampling is done by the Karhunen-Loeve expansion: xi = np.random.randn(dim); components = xi * sqrt(spectral_variances / metric_values); vector = domain.from_components(components) (+ expectation). | `sample closure inside SymmetricSpace.invariant_measure, registered as GaussianMeasure(sample=...)` | Same O(dim) Karhunen-Loeve draw sqrt(s/g)*xi in components, but draws from a numpy Generator passed as rng= (default_rng() when None) instead of the global legacy np.random.randn. |
| `symmetric_space.CorrelatedInvariantGaussianMeasure` | A GaussianMeasure for a tuple of n correlated random fields on a common SymmetricHilbertSpace, defined on the direct sum of n copies of the field space, with block covariance whose (i,j) block is the invariant operator with eigenvalues Sigma_ij(k), and joint Karhunen-Loeve sampling. | `SymmetricSpace.correlated_measure(spectral_cross_covariances, *, expectation=None, labels=None) -> GaussianMeasure on DirectSum([space]*n)` | Factory returning a plain GaussianMeasure rather than a class. Same (dim,n,n) shape, symmetry, PSD checks and per-slice eigh/clip; covariance and factor are a new SpectralBlockLinearOperator (one einsum per application instead of n^2 diagonal blocks — IMPROVED); precision built as slice-wise inverse only when min eigenvalue > 1e-10*max\|Sigma\| (v1: > 0). Expectation no longer validated for length n. The result has NO closure: +, -, scalar*, and affine maps return generic GaussianMeasures whose covariance forgets the spectral-block structure, and exact KL/norms are not available (see rows below). |
| `symmetric_space.CorrelatedInvariantGaussianMeasure.from_invariant_measures` | Builds the correlated measure with the given invariant marginals and spectral correlations: Sigma_ij(k) = R_ij(k) sqrt(sigma_i(k) sigma_j(k)). | `space.correlated_measure_from_correlations(variances, correlations, *, expectation=None, labels=None)` | Takes marginal variance arrays (or vectorised callables) instead of InvariantGaussianMeasure objects; marginal expectations are not inherited; correlation accepts only (n,n) or (dim,n,n) arrays — float, callable-of-eigenvalue and (dim,) forms raise (runtime: float -> ValueError 'Correlations must have shape', callable -> TypeError). Unit-diagonal check kept (atol default instead of 1e-8). |
| `symmetric_space.CorrelatedInvariantGaussianMeasure.marginal` | The marginal invariant measure of the i-th field, with variances Sigma_ii(k) and the i-th expectation component. | `GaussianMeasure.marginal(key)` | Generic to any measure on a DirectSum; accepts a label as well as an index; the diagonal block keeps its eigenvalues and gets a sqrt factor (only when the summand metric is diagonal). But v1 returned an InvariantGaussianMeasure with an explicit inverse covariance (when all marginal variances > 0) and the O(dim) KL sampler; v2 passes no precision= and no sample=, so the marginal has no density/log_density and samples through the factor. Invalid index raises IndexError (from DirectSum.index) rather than ValueError. |
| `symmetric_space.CorrelatedInvariantGaussianMeasure.spectral_correlations` | The spectral correlations rho_ij(k) = Sigma_ij / sqrt(Sigma_ii Sigma_jj) as a (dim,) array. | `space.spectral_correlations(measure, *, first=0, second=1)` | Moved from the measure to the space and takes the measure as argument; keyword names i,j -> first,second; zero-where-undefined rule kept. |
| `symmetric_space.CorrelatedInvariantGaussianMeasure.kl_divergence` | Override computing D_KL exactly in O(dim n^3) from the spectral cross-covariances when both measures are correlated invariant measures with the same field space and number of fields and method == 'auto'. | `GaussianMeasure.kl_divergence(other, method='auto')` | The exact O(dim n^3) spectral-block route is gone: SpectralBlockLinearOperator is not a DiagonalLinearOperator, so 'spectral' raises and 'auto' goes dense (forming two (n*dim)^2 Galerkin matrices) when n*dim <= 4000 and raises ValueError above that. Runtime: dim 2048 x 2 fields works densely; dim 4096 x 2 raises. |
| `symmetric_space.CorrelatedInvariantGaussianMeasure.nuclear_norm` | Exact trace norm as the sum of all eigenvalues of the spectral cross-covariance matrices. | `GaussianMeasure.nuclear_norm()` | No exact block route: _diagonal_eigenvalues is None for a SpectralBlockLinearOperator, so 'auto' assembles the dense (n*dim)x(n*dim) component matrix via BlockLinearOperator._known_matrix and takes its trace. | `symmetric_space.CorrelatedInvariantGaussianMeasure.hilbert_schmidt_norm` | Exact Hilbert-Schmidt norm as the root sum of squares of the per-slice eigenvalues. | `GaussianMeasure.hilbert_schmidt_norm()` | Same dense fallback as nuclear_norm: forms the full component matrix and computes sqrt(sum(M*M.T)). |
| `symmetric_space.CorrelatedInvariantGaussianMeasure.__neg__` | Negated expectation, covariance unchanged. | `(-1.0) * measure` | `-m` raises TypeError; `-1.0*m` works but the covariance becomes `_Composition` and the factor `_Scaled`: spectral-block structure (slices, exactness of later norms, marginal factors) is lost. |
| `symmetric_space.CorrelatedInvariantGaussianMeasure.__mul__` | Scales the fields by alpha: cross-covariances by alpha^2, mean by alpha. | `ProbabilityMeasure.__mul__ -> GaussianMeasure._combine_scale` | Result is a generic GaussianMeasure: covariance `_Composition`, factor `_Scaled`, precision None. Sampling still works; exact norms/KL and `.slices` no longer reachable. v1 stayed in class with alpha^2 * cross-covariances. |
| `symmetric_space.CorrelatedInvariantGaussianMeasure.__rmul__` | Right scalar multiplication. | `ProbabilityMeasure.__rmul__` | As __mul__. |
| `symmetric_space.CorrelatedInvariantGaussianMeasure.__truediv__` | Division by a scalar via multiplication by 1/alpha. | `ProbabilityMeasure.__truediv__` | As __mul__. |
| `symmetric_space.CorrelatedInvariantGaussianMeasure.__add__` | Sum of independent measures; fast path when other is a correlated invariant measure with the same field space and n adds cross-covariances and expectations. | `ProbabilityMeasure.__add__ -> GaussianMeasure._combine_add` | Result covariance is a generic `_Sum` (SpectralBlock + SpectralBlock has no specialisation), factor None (sampling falls back to two draws), precision None; slices/exact norms lost. v1 added the slice arrays and stayed in class. |

Float scalar, callable (vectorised or per-eigenvalue, scalar or matrix valued), (dim,) and (n,n,dim) forms are all gone. |
| `symmetric_space.CorrelatedInvariantGaussianMeasure._kl_sample` | Draws xi = np.random.randn(dim, n), forms coefficients = einsum('kij,kj->ki', kl_factor_array, xi), and maps each column through field_space.from_components to produce a list of n field vectors (+ expectation). | `sample closure in correlated_measure: space.from_components(factor._components_action()(space.white_noise_components(rng=rng)))` | Same joint KL draw (symmetric sqrt slices on white-noise components, one synthesis per field); uses a Generator rng= instead of the global RNG; the 1/sqrt(g) comes from DiagonalMetricSpace.white_noise_components. |
| `symmetric_space.SymmetricHilbertSpace` | Abstract base class (OrthogonalHilbertSpace, ABC) for Hilbert spaces of functions on symmetric manifolds, represented by expansion in the (orthogonal but not necessarily normalised) eigenfunctions of the Laplace-Beltrami operator. | `symmetric_space.base.SymmetricSpace[V](HilbertModule, DiagonalMetricSpace); __init__(metric_values)` | Constructor takes the Gram diagonal directly (no spatial_dim/degree/dim, no per-index Python loop over abstract methods). Abstract interface replaced: subclasses supply to_components/from_components, order, with_order, laplacian_eigenvalues (array), basis_at, degrees, reference_point, walk_from, spatial_dimension, gaussian_curvature, geodesic_distance/quadrature/ball_quadrature, project_function, random_point(rng=), _key. One class now covers both Lebesgue (order 0) and Sobolev orders; vectors are generic (sphere uses SHGrid). Gains coefficient_operator, spectral_projection_operator, power_spectrum, power_measure, pointwise_variance(_at), covariance_function, PreparedPoints. |
| `symmetric_space.SymmetricHilbertSpace.heat_kernel` | Returns the heat-kernel covariance function k -> exp(-scale^2 k). | `SymmetricSpace.heat_symbol(length_scale) -> np.ndarray` | Instance method returning the evaluated array over the space's eigenvalues instead of a static function factory; rejects negative length_scale. |
| `symmetric_space.SymmetricHilbertSpace.sobolev_kernel` | Returns the Sobolev covariance function k -> (1 + scale^2 k)^(-order). | `SymmetricSpace.sobolev_symbol(order, scale) -> np.ndarray` | Returns an array not a callable, AND the sign convention differs: v1 sobolev_kernel(order, scale) = (1+scale^2 k)^(-order); v2 sobolev_symbol(order, scale) = (1+scale^2 lambda)^(+order) (sobolev_measure passes -order itself). Rejects non-positive scale. |
| `symmetric_space.SymmetricHilbertSpace.laplacian_eigenvalue` | Abstract: the Laplacian eigenvalue for index k. | `SymmetricSpace.laplacian_eigenvalues (abstract property, array over components)` | Whole-array property instead of per-index method. |
| `symmetric_space.SymmetricHilbertSpace.random_point` | Abstract: a single random point on the manifold. | `SymmetricSpace.random_point(*, rng=None) (abstract)` | Adds rng Generator keyword. |

The box version rebuilds a Python dict of (wavevector, phase) -> position for both spaces on every call (O(dim) Python, uncached), unlike the sphere's cached _packing. |

| `symmetric_space.AbstractSymmetricLebesgueSpace.gradient_dot_product` | The pointwise dot product of the surface gradients of two fields, computed via the identity 0.5 (Delta(fg) - f Delta g - g Delta f). | `SymmetricSpace.gradient_dot_product(f, g)` | Sign convention flipped: v2 computes (f L g + g L f - L(fg))/2 with L the positive Laplacian and asserts v1's 0.5(L(fg) - f L g - g L f) had the wrong sign; result left on the grid (untruncated). | `symmetric_space.AbstractSymmetricLebesgueSpace.flexural_operator` | The exact 4th-order variable-coefficient thin-plate flexure operator Delta(D Delta w) - Delta(D_eff) Delta w + tr(Hess D_eff Hess w) + 2K grad D_eff . grad w - K D_eff Delta w + rho_g w on the manifold, as a formally self-adjoint matrix-free LinearOperator. | `SymmetricSpace.flexural_operator(rigidity, poisson_ratio, buoyancy) -> _FlexureOperator` | Arguments renamed (flexural_rigidity->rigidity, buoyancy_factor->buoyancy) and positional-only; implemented as a fused operator class (seven transforms per application instead of ~fifty, IMPROVED) with precomputed coefficient grids; claims SELF_ADJOINT; on a Sobolev space builds at order 0 and lifts. |
| `symmetric_space.AbstractSymmetricLebesgueSpace.inverse_flexural_operator` | The inverse of the flexure operator: exact spectral inverse 1/(D k^2 - K D_eff k + rho_g) as an InvariantLinearAutomorphism when all three coefficients are scalars; otherwise a preconditioned iterative solve of the variable-coefficient operator. | `SymmetricSpace.inverse_flexural_operator(rigidity, poisson_ratio, buoyancy, *, baseline_rigidity=None, baseline_buoyancy=None, solver=None)` | Same structure (exact diagonal inverse for constant coefficients; preconditioned CG otherwise). Non-iterative solver raises TypeError (v1 ValueError); preconditioner attached via solver.with_preconditioner only if the solver has none; operator tagged POSITIVE_DEFINITE; on Sobolev spaces the solve runs in L2 and is lifted. |
| `symmetric_space.SymmetricSobolevSpace` | The Sobolev space H^s over a symmetric Lebesgue space, built as a MassWeightedHilbertModule whose mass operator is the invariant automorphism (1 + scale^2 Delta)^order; also an AbstractSymmetricLebesgueSpace (abstract: with_order must be supplied by subclasses). | `fourier.Sobolev(shape, order, length_scale, *, lengths=) / sphere.Sobolev(lmax, order, length_scale, *, radius=, sampling=) — PeriodicBox/Sphere with order != 0` | Not a MassWeightedHilbertModule over a Lebesgue space: the same coordinate map with Gram diagonal (1+scale^2 lambda)^order (a DiagonalMetricSpace). The `safe` construction flag is gone; guards are per-call `unsafe=` keywords. with_order is concrete (returns Lebesgue at order 0). |
| `symmetric_space.SymmetricSobolevSpace.order_inclusion_operator` | The inclusion operator from this space into the same space with a lower order. | `SymmetricSpace.order_inclusion_operator(target: SymmetricSpace)` | Takes the target space rather than a target order; only checks dim equality — the v1 `safe` check refusing inclusion into a HIGHER order is gone (runtime: X.order_inclusion_operator(X.with_order(3.0)) succeeds). |

| `symmetric_space.SymmetricSobolevSpace.point_evaluation_operator` | An operator mapping a function to its values at a list of points, into EuclideanSpace(len(points)); the primary forward operator for point data. | `SymmetricSpace.point_evaluation_operator(points, *, dense=False, unsafe=False, eps=None, nthreads=None)` | Matrix-free by default via evaluate/accumulate (NUFFT on boxes, batched transforms on the sphere) with PreparedPoints conversion done once; the v1 dense (n_points x dim) matrix is opt-in via dense=True. [NEW semantics: divided by path length]` | NAME/SEMANTICS SWAP: the v2 method called path_average_operator normalises by path length, whereas v1's path_average_operator returned raw integrals; code ported by name will get different numbers. v1 semantics live in path_integral_operator. The uniform-random mesh on any geometry is a one-line comprehension. |
| `symmetric_space.SymmetricSobolevSpace.distance_localized_preconditioner` | Builds a sparse (or purely diagonal) approximate inverse of the normal matrix A Q A* + R for point-evaluation problems with an invariant prior, exploiting that the prior covariance between two points depends only on geodesic distance. | `inference.preconditioners.InvariantDistancePreconditioner(space, points, max_distance, *, taper=True) — a LinearSolver applied to the normal operator` | Now a solver class rather than a space method: prior and data-error covariance are read from the normal operator it is applied to (no prior_measure/data_error_measure args); apply_taper renamed taper and defaults True (v1 False); parallel/n_jobs removed (noise diagonal read via error_covariance.diagonals); Galerkin metric scaling G K G added for non-orthonormal data spaces; sparse splu kept; max_distance==0 diagonal case kept. Further restriction: v1 returned a free-standing LinearOperator on EuclideanSpace(n_data) usable with any solver or by hand; v2 is a LinearSolver whose _invert raises TypeError unless the operand is a FactoredNormalOperator (from an estimator's .normal_operator or .surrogate) and ValueError unless its formalism is 'data_space'. It cannot be built from a prior measure and a point list alone, nor applied outside the inference framework's normal-operator object. |
| `symmetric_space.SymmetricSobolevSpace.l2_products_operator` | Override: L2 inner products with weighting functions, computed in the underlying L2 space and lifted to this Sobolev space. | `SymmetricSpace.l2_products_operator(fields)` | Single implementation computing L2 components via with_order(0); dense (n x dim) matrix instead of v1's matrix-free lift. |
| `symmetric_space.SymmetricSobolevSpace.flexural_operator` | Override: the flexure operator built on the underlying L2 space and lifted as a formally self-adjoint operator on the Sobolev space. | `SymmetricSpace.flexural_operator (order != 0 branch lifts from with_order(0))` | v1 lifted with LinearOperator.from_formally_self_adjoint, so the H^s operator carried a self-adjoint claim usable directly by CG; v2 lifts with lift_formal_adjoint and traits=Traits.NONE, claiming nothing (v2 argues the v1 claim is false for variable coefficients, since the operator does not commute with the metric ratio, and routes CG through L2 in inverse_flexural_operator instead). For constant coefficients, where the claim was true, the trait is now absent unless passed explicitly. |
| `symmetric_space.SymmetricSobolevSpace.inverse_flexural_operator` | Override: the inverse flexure operator built on the underlying L2 space and lifted with from_formal_adjoint. | `SymmetricSpace.inverse_flexural_operator (order != 0 and variable coefficients: solved in L2 and lifted)` | Lifted operator maps self -> self (v1's codomain was the underlying Lebesgue space). Constant-coefficient case returns the diagonal symbol directly on the Sobolev space. |
| `symmetric_space.invariant_operator_fast_path` | All operators derived from the Laplacian (laplacian, identity_operator, zero_operator, invariant_automorphism, covariances/precisions of invariant measures, Sobolev mass and inverse-mass operators, the constant-coefficient inverse flexure operator and its preconditioner) are InvariantLinearAutomorphisms; sums, differences, compositions, scalar multiples and functional calculus between them stay in that class and cost O(dim) on the eigenvalue array. | `DiagonalLinearOperator specialisation protocol (_combine_add/_combine_compose/_combine_scale) + SymmetricSpace.laplacian/invariant_operator/spectral_operator` | Closure under +, -, @, scalar *, neg, abs, pow and calculus is kept and is now O(dim) on a numpy array (no scipy dia allocation). Lost: the identity/zero overrides, so `LinearOperator.identity(X) + D` is a generic `_Sum` (I@D and Z+D still specialise). Sobolev mass/inverse-mass operators no longer exist as operators (the metric is the Gram diagonal). |
| `symmetric_space.kl_divergence_auto_fallback` | Both invariant measure classes override kl_divergence with method='auto' default: an exact spectral formula when the other measure is of the same class on the same domain, otherwise 'auto' is translated to 'dense' before delegating to GaussianMeasure.kl_divergence (which also supports 'randomized'). | `GaussianMeasure.kl_divergence_estimate method resolution` | 'auto' -> 'spectral' when both covariances are DiagonalLinearOperators on the space; else 'dense' only if the domain has coordinates and dim <= dense_limit (4000); else raises ValueError instead of silently going dense. Block-diagonal (correlated) covariances never qualify for 'spectral'. |
| `symmetric_space.sobolev_safe_checks` | With safe=True (default), dirac, point_evaluation_operator and geodesic_integral raise NotImplementedError when order <= spatial_dimension / 2, and order_inclusion_operator raises ValueError when the target order exceeds the current order; safe=False disables these checks. | `SymmetricSpace._require_point_evaluation(what, unsafe=) called by dirac, point_evaluation_operator, covariance_function, pointwise_variance_at` | Per-call `unsafe=` instead of a construction-time `safe` flag; raises ValueError (v1 NotImplementedError); guards extended to covariance_function/pointwise_variance_at; REMOVED from path integrals/averages and ball averages (nodes evaluated with unsafe=True) and from order_inclusion_operator (no higher-order refusal). |

Still hard (in-function) imports, no optional branches; finufft/pyshtools live in the geometry modules. |
| `symmetric_space.global_rng_sampling` | Both KL samplers (InvariantGaussianMeasure._kl_sample, CorrelatedInvariantGaussianMeasure._kl_sample) draw with np.random.randn; random_point/random_points/random_source_receiver_paths depend on subclass implementations. No seed or Generator argument is exposed anywhere in this unit. | `rng: numpy.random.Generator \| None everywhere (sample(rng=), random_point(rng=), random_points(rng=), source_receiver_paths(rng=))` | No global legacy RNG; np.random.default_rng() when rng is None. IMPROVED reproducibility. |
