- random_trace -> random_trace: component Rademacher probes (variance-minimal for Hutchinson) replaced by Gaussian white-noise probes on the space (randomised.py:808-810 vs low_rank.py:1122-1127); same expectation, higher variance per sample, and on a non-orthonormal CoordinateSpace without a cheap white_noise_components override each probe needs G^{-1/2}, which the default forms by a dense Cholesky of the dim x dim Gram matrix cached once (spaces.py:364-381). Default mode changed from adaptive to fixed 100 samples.
- random_range -> random_range: the user-supplied `measure` (prior-weighted probes, v1 Path A low_rank.py:556-588; used live at v1 gaussian_measure.py:1895) is gone; probes are always white noise on the domain (randomised.py:89). The returned isometric LinearOperator became a list of vectors (randomised.py:233, 254-256).
- random_range (all from_randomized) -> random_range: power default 2 -> 1 (randomised.py:134, 228 vs low_rank.py:122, 272, 414, 501), so at equal settings v2 does one fewer subspace iteration by default.
- random_range Path B -> _range_with_columns/_adaptive_range_on_components: scipy.linalg.qr (Householder, backward stable) replaced by classical Gram-Schmidt with one conditional reorthogonalisation pass on component columns (spaces.py:531-593); numerically adequate with the 'twice is enough' test but not a QR factorisation. IMPROVED: the component path is now metric-aware (apply_gram) and therefore available on every CoordinateSpace, not only orthonormal codomains.
- LowRankSVD/LowRankEig factors -> _ColumnOperator: on coordinate spaces the U/V factors are materialised as dense (dim, k) component arrays (operators.py:1196-1226, 1537-1566) where v1 kept them as compositions Q_op @ U_tilde_op (low_rank.py:177-178, 191, 326-327); same O(nk) storage as v1's underlying from_vectors/from_matrix Q, so not a complexity regression, but the factor is no longer a lazy composition.
- The dense Gram Cholesky behind CoordinateSpace.white_noise_components (spaces.py:364-381: np.linalg.cholesky(self.gram_matrix()), with gram_matrix assembled column by column from dim apply_gram calls at spaces.py:400-408) is reached by every probe of random_range, random_eig, random_svd and random_cholesky (randomised.py:89 domain.white_noise(rng=rng)), not only random_trace. On a user-defined CoordinateSpace with a non-diagonal Gram matrix and no white_noise_components override, the first randomised call pays O(dim^2) memory and O(dim^3) time that v1's Gaussian component probes (np.random.randn / measure.samples) never did. The shipped spaces (DiagonalMetricSpace, OrthonormalSpace, ComponentView, DirectSum, MFEM) override it, so this bites only custom spaces.
- Adaptive range finding (random_range with rank=None, and hence adaptive random_eig/random_svd/random_cholesky) appends the final below-tolerance block before testing convergence (randomised.py:309-311, 369-371), where v1 broke first (low_rank.py:725-726, 841-842). The realised rank exceeds v1's by up to block_size directions below rtol; Review B measured 20 vectors instead of 10 at every rtol from 1e-1 to 1e-3 on a rank-5-dominant operator with a 1e-3 tail, and adaptive random_eig carrying 15 noise-floor eigenpairs. Not a dense formation, but a systematic rank inflation that enlarges every downstream factor.
- Generality: the generic MassWeightedSpace (spaces.py:802-950) implements random but not white_noise, so random_range/random_eig/random_svd/random_cholesky/random_trace (and GaussianMeasure.from_standard_deviation(...).sample) raise NotImplementedError on operators over it, where v1's guard (low_rank.py:547-548 with white_noise_measure) ran on every v1 space including MassWeightedHilbertSpace. Nothing in pygeoinf2 outside spaces.py and tests constructs one, so current exposure is low.
- IMPROVED: operator applications to a block of probes go through LinearOperator.apply_block (operators.py:804-825), one GEMM for matrix-backed operators and one parallel_map otherwise (randomised.py:90, 110, 114, 576, 644); v1 applied probes one at a time in Path A and only parallelised measure.samples.
- IMPROVED: orthonormalisation on coordinate spaces converts each vector to components once and works on (dim,k) arrays with apply_gram (spaces.py:531-593, 618-640; randomised.py:147-153, 315-373), where v1 Path A took O(k^2) inner products each costing two transforms on spectral spaces.
- IMPROVED: all randomness is from an explicit rng with per-probe spawned streams (randomised.py:806-815; parallel.py:80-82), so results are reproducible and independent of n_jobs; v1 used the global np.random state inside joblib workers.
- IMPROVED: the probe distribution on mass-weighted spaces is identity-covariance white noise (spaces.py:672-680) rather than v1's white_noise_measure with covariance G (DESIGN.md:1195-1224), fixing the range finder's anisotropic probes on every Sobolev space.
- IMPROVED: random_trace returns an Estimate with a standard error (randomised.py:50-67, 827-831) and the adaptive stopping, when requested, is on the standard error rather than on successive-estimate change (randomised.py:818-825, 1006-1015).
- IMPROVED: deflated_diagonal's exact part (randomised.py:890-905) is correct for both forms on a non-orthonormal space; v1's galerkin=False path used c_v where the component matrix needs G c_v (low_rank.py:1020-1025).

### nonlinear_optimisation

- IMPROVED: ScipyUnconstrainedOptimiser.minimize (hess via LinearOperator.matrix(galerkin=True), a matrix-free SciPy LinearOperator) -> NewtonCG/TrustRegionNewton + truncated_cg: the Hessian is applied as a v2 LinearOperator inside Steihaug CG with no SciPy object and no Galerkin assembly (optimisation.py:590-595, :717-725, :785-840).
- IMPROVED: ScipyUnconstrainedOptimiser.minimize jac/fun component round trip -> _DescentMethod/NewtonCG: no to_components/from_components/to_dual per evaluation; all arithmetic via space.axpy/inner_product/norm (optimisation.py:246-289), so the methods run on spaces without coordinates.
- IMPROVED (with offset): line_search (one SciPy f call + one myfprime call per trial, each with a from_components) -> StrongWolfeLineSearch: one functional.at per trial yields value and gradient together, and the model at the accepted point is returned to the optimiser (line_search.py:191-202, :225; optimisation.py:271-277), saving one value+gradient evaluation per outer iteration. Offset: _zoom re-evaluates the functional at the bracket's low end on entry (line_search.py:263-266), a value the caller already holds (`value` itself when low == 0.0, or previous_value from the bracketing loop); SciPy's _zoom takes phi_lo as an argument. One wasted value evaluation per zoom-entered search.
- IMPROVED: ScipyUnconstrainedOptimiser L-BFGS-B / CG in component space (metric-blind) -> LBFGS / NonlinearCG / SteepestDescent in the space's metric: implicit inverse Hessian and directions are preconditioned by G^-1 for free (optimisation.py:18-26, :446-511; examples/12_optimisation.py:60-77).
- REGRESSION (algorithmic, not dense): line_search zoom phase -> StrongWolfeLineSearch._zoom is pure bisection (line_search.py:268-287) where scipy.optimize.line_search's zoom uses cubic/quadratic interpolation; REVIEW.md:156 records this. More trials per line search on smooth problems.
- REGRESSION (capability): ScipyUnconstrainedOptimiser with 'Nelder-Mead'/'Powell' -> nothing: derivative-free minimisation is impossible (optimisation.py:153-157 raises); with 'L-BFGS-B' -> nothing: no bound constraints on the quasi-Newton methods; 'trust-exact'/'dogleg'/'BFGS' (full memory) -> nothing.
- QUALIFICATION (not a new regression): the 'no bound constraints' claim is correct but slightly overstated. v2 has a projected-gradient route for constraints given as a convex set: ProximalGradient.minimise(smooth, x0, nonsmooth=<set indicator>) at numerics/convex.py:555-625, with ConvexSet.project on Ball, Ellipsoid, HalfSpace, Hyperplane, Polytope and ConvexIntersection (geometry/convex.py:419, :561, :677, :741, :820, :1212). There is no Box set (grep 'class Box' in geometry/: no hits), so component-wise bounds like L-BFGS-B's can only be built as a ConvexIntersection of HalfSpaces projected by Dykstra iteration, and the smooth part is then first-order only (no quasi-Newton). review/numerics.md:51 already records this route as unadvertised.
- COUNTING: on both failure paths StrongWolfeLineSearch evaluates functional(trial) for the returned value without incrementing `evaluations` (line_search.py:243-244, :289-291); LineSearchResult.evaluations understates by one when converged is False. v1 returned SciPy's exact fc/gc counts.
- SEMANTIC: max_step is never actually tried. The bracketing loop does `step = min(2*step, max_step); if step >= max_step: break` (line_search.py:239-241), so it exits before evaluating at max_step and reports converged=False at that point. SciPy with amax clipped alpha to amax and evaluated there (scalar_search_wolfe2: alpha1 = min(alpha1, amax)).
- COST PER TRIAL: every Wolfe trial goes through Functional.at, which constructs the Hessian when the functional has one (operators.py:1878-1880), whereas v1's line search invoked only form() and form.derivative(). Harmless when _hessian returns a lazy LinearOperator, a regression when Hessian construction does work.
- ERROR BEHAVIOUR: v1 line_search raised ValueError('NonLinearForm must provide its gradient') up front (nonlinear_optimisation.py:164-165). v2 LineSearch.__call__ has no such check: a StrongWolfeLineSearch called directly on a derivative-less Functional fails at the first trial inside functional.at with NotImplementedError('No derivative or gradient was supplied.') (operators.py:2072); the guard exists only on Optimiser.minimise (optimisation.py:153-157).
- STALE REVIEW NOTE: review/numerics.md:51 lists '`ftol`-type stopping' as lost, but Optimiser.__init__ now has ftol (optimisation.py:89, :112-113, :129). The tol_handling row is right and that review line is out of date. Likewise review/numerics.md:111(b) says the _zoom low-end re-evaluation 'does not count it'; it is now counted (line_search.py:263-266), though the re-evaluation itself remains.
- NOTE: v2 LinearOperator.matrix(form='galerkin') is dense-only (operators.py:680-687) and there is no scipy.sparse.linalg.LinearOperator export anywhere in algebra/ or numerics/ (the only sparse_linalg uses are splu/spilu in the preconditioner modules and backends/mfem.py's _to_scipy for MFEM sparse matrices), so a user wanting to reproduce v1's SciPy bridge by hand would have to densify the Hessian where v1 did not.

### small_modules

- parallel_mat_mat / parallel_compute_dense_matrix_from_scipy_op (n_jobs=-1 default) -> LinearOperator.apply_block / LinearOperator.matrix (n_jobs=None default): every call site that relied on v1's default all-core parallelism now runs serially unless the caller passes n_jobs explicitly (pygeoinf2/parallel.py:144,163-166; pygeoinf2/algebra/operators.py:680-690,804). Deliberate per parallel.py:11-30 and pygeoinf2/review/parallel.md, but it is a lost default, not a lost option.
- parallel_compute_dense_matrix_from_scipy_op -> LinearOperator.matrix: v1 _compute_dense_matrix guarded its adjoint row-fill route with `not self.__using_default_dual_and_adjoint` (pygeoinf/linear_operators.py:99-105,832-847) and fell back to the dim(X)-column probe for an operator with no supplied adjoint; v2 dropped that guard, so A.matrix() (default by='auto', operators.py:725) on a wide from_callables operator without an adjoint raises NotImplementedError from the row route (operators.py:753-770,1663-1669) instead of assembling the matrix. Reproduced: v2 `LinearOperator.from_callables(EuclideanSpace(5), EuclideanSpace(2), f).matrix()` raises; `.matrix(by='columns')` succeeds; v1 `LinearOperator(X, Y, f).matrix(dense=True)` succeeds. Not a dense-vs-matrix-free regression, but a case where the dense assembly v1 could always do now fails by default.
- sample_earthquakes (smart refetch of max(2000, 1.2*n) events when the cache is short) -> Sphere.earthquakes: a request for more events than the 188-event seed file holds (after the magnitude filter) raises ValueError instead of fetching more (pygeoinf2/symmetric_space/sphere.py:1993-1994); the reachable catalogue is capped at the shipped table.
- load_gsn_stations / sample_earthquakes (stdlib-only, top-level, @staticmethod on Sphere) -> Sphere.stations / Sphere.earthquakes (instance methods): reading the shipped tables now requires constructing a Sphere, whose __init__ calls _require_pyshtools() (sphere.py:125-133,195), so the station and earthquake lists are gated behind the optional 'sphere' extra (pyproject.toml:22) and an lmax choice; the pyshtools-free readers _read_table/_subsample (sphere.py:1954-2000) are private.
- IMPROVED: parallel_mat_mat -> LinearOperator.apply_block: matrix-backed operators do one BLAS product for the whole block (pygeoinf2/algebra/operators.py:1810-1826), diagonal operators broadcast (pygeoinf2/algebra/diagonal.py:337-359), and sums/compositions/adjoints/scalings pass the block through their parts (pygeoinf2/algebra/nodes.py:91,200,304,375,514,715) instead of k separate applications.
- IMPROVED: parallel_compute_dense_matrix_from_scipy_op -> LinearOperator.matrix: `_known_matrix` (operators.py:773-790) skips probing entirely for matrix-backed and composed operators. (The row-fill-by-adjoint route for a smaller codomain is NOT an improvement over v1, which already did it at pygeoinf/linear_operators.py:835-847; see the regression above for what v2 changed there.)
- IMPROVED: joblib hard import at module load -> lazy import only on the parallel path (pygeoinf2/parallel.py:165-168); one BLAS/OpenMP thread per worker by default (parallel.py:181, measured in pygeoinf2/review/parallel.md); nested loops inside a worker are forced serial rather than silently becoming threads (parallel.py:121-126,165); n_jobs validated (parallel.py:107-118).
- IMPROVED: load_gsn_stations / sample_earthquakes unseeded stdlib random.sample -> Sphere.stations/earthquakes take an explicit numpy Generator (sphere.py:1995-1997), so point sets are reproducible; and minimum_magnitude now filters the cached table (sphere.py:1733) where v1 ignored it unless a download happened (inert at the new default of 0.0 on the bundled 5.0-7.5 data).

### gaussian_measure

- GaussianMeasure.with_sparse_approximation -> GaussianMeasure.with_sparse_approximation: v1 built the sparse matrix by N operator applications straight into COO/CSC and factorised with splu (never holding an N×N dense array); v2 forms the full dense matrix (covariance.matrix(form), gaussian.py:1421), symmetrises, runs np.linalg.eigvalsh O(N^3) (gaussian.py:1424), then csr_matrix; it also drops the sparse-LU precision, the correlation-based threshold, max_nnz, diag_rank/diag_samples and parallel (gaussian.py:1390-1440 vs v1 gaussian_measure.py:967-1099).
- GaussianMeasure.nuclear_norm(exact=True) -> GaussianMeasure.nuclear_norm(method='auto'\|'dense'): v1 summed covariance.extract_diagonal (O(N) applications, O(N) memory, fast for diagonal/dense operators); v2 forms the full component matrix and takes np.trace (O(N^2) memory) (gaussian.py:806). Default also flipped from stochastic to this dense route.
- GaussianMeasure.hilbert_schmidt_norm(exact=True) -> hilbert_schmidt_norm(method='auto'\|'dense'): v1 used extract_diagonal of C@C (O(N) memory); v2 forms the dense component matrix of C and computes sum(M*M.T) (gaussian.py:762-763). Default flipped from stochastic to dense.
- GaussianMeasure.credible_set (no inverse_covariance -> AttributeError) -> credible_set (no precision): v2 forms the dense Galerkin matrix and a Gram-weighted np.linalg.solve, O(N^3) (gaussian.py:1480-1495); v1 never densified here.
- GaussianMeasure.credible_set(geometry='ambient_ball', radius_method='auto') -> ambient_ball(method='auto'): v1 auto chose a randomised LowRankEig spectrum or Monte Carlo sampling (matrix-free); v2 auto chooses a dense generalised eigh of (C_gal, G), O(N^3), whenever the space has coordinates and dim <= 1024 (gaussian.py:1592-1600, 1629-1660). The user-supplied spectrum / LowRankEig / callable inputs are gone.
- GaussianMeasure.kl_divergence(method='dense' default) -> kl_divergence(method='auto'): dense remains the default for non-diagonal covariances up to dim 4000 (gaussian.py:1025), and 'auto' now REFUSES above that instead of falling back to the matrix-free route; the stochastic route additionally requires a covariance factor or precision factor (gaussian.py:1180-1191) where v1 needed only the reference precision.
- GaussianMeasure.affine_mapping(inverse_solver=...) -> (nothing): the matrix-free KKT/saddle-point push-forward precision with auto block-diagonal Jacobi-Schur preconditioner is gone; v2 keeps a precision only through identity/diagonal maps (gaussian.py:2208-2240).
- GaussianMeasure.deflated_pointwise_variance(method='variable', rtol, block_size, parallel) -> SymmetricSpace.pointwise_variance_at(rank, samples): adaptive stopping, rtol, block_size and the field-valued result are gone; restricted to SymmetricSpace and to listed points; requires CoordinateSpace for deflated_diagonal (symmetric_space/base.py:1143-1239; numerics/randomised.py:834-910).
- GaussianMeasure.sample_pointwise_variance / sample_pointwise_std -> (nothing): the general Monte-Carlo pointwise variance/std field on any HilbertModule is gone (grep).
- GaussianMeasure.as_multivariate_normal(parallel, n_jobs) -> as_multivariate_normal(): the N operator applications can no longer be parallelised, and the eigh-clipping retry on a non-PSD result is gone (gaussian.py:1717-1751).
- GaussianMeasure.with_regularized_inverse: lost the damping==0-with-existing-precision fast path (returned self) and the preconditioner keyword; the returned measure's covariance/sampler are no longer consistent with its precision when damping>0 (gaussian.py:1342-1388); it calls solver(...) directly (gaussian.py:1380) rather than through resolve_solver, so unlike condition() it does not accept solver=None or a factory.
- Sampler loss under the algebra (a capability regression rather than a dense one): v1 wrapped an explicit sampler through __neg__, __mul__, __sub__, zero_expectation, rescale_directional_variance and with_regularized_inverse; v2 _combine_scale never carries one (gaussian.py:2275-2318), so every measure whose only sampler is an explicit callable — condition() results, from_product/+ results built from samplers — becomes unsamplable after scaling, negation, subtraction or rescale_directional_variance. Verified with adv_gm.py ((2*mu), (-1*mu), (mu - mu), (2*cond), rescale all can_sample False).
- Root cause of the `cond + cond` ValueError recorded in the __add__ row lies in the operator algebra, not only in _combine_add: for two compositions re-traited with with_traits(SELF_ADJOINT\|POSITIVE_SEMIDEFINITE), (comp + comp).traits comes back as Traits.NONE (verified in adv_gm2.py) — Operator.__add__ (algebra/operators.py:346-355) dispatches to _combine_add/_combine_radd before make_sum, and the specialised sum discards with_traits claims (nodes.py sum_traits would have kept PSD). Any C1 + C2 of posterior covariances is affected, so summing conditioned Gaussians is impossible in v2 where v1 allowed it.
- ProbabilityMeasure.two_point_covariance (base.py:201-208) calls self.covariance(...) without a None check, so on a precision-only GaussianMeasure it raises TypeError ('NoneType' object is not callable) instead of the ValueError/_require_covariance message used elsewhere; v1 had no precision-only measures so no such path existed.
- IMPROVED: kl_divergence gains an exact O(dim) 'spectral' route for two DiagonalLinearOperator covariances (gaussian.py:1035-1053), a single-trace non-negative stochastic estimator with an error bar (gaussian.py:1073-1099, 1101-1191), and seedable/parallel probes.
- IMPROVED: nuclear_norm / hilbert_schmidt_norm / ambient_ball / log_normalising_constant take an O(dim) closed form when the covariance is a DiagonalLinearOperator (gaussian.py:657-664, 741-743, 789-791, 1580-1584, 2031-2035).
- IMPROVED: sampling is metric-correct — factor draws use factor.domain.white_noise (gaussian.py:638) and from_standard_deviation(s) therefore has covariance sigma^2 I on the space, fixing the v1 defect DESIGN §9 records; explicit rng everywhere, samples() reproducible independent of n_jobs (base.py:76-116).
- IMPROVED: from_covariance_matrix tries Cholesky before eigh (gaussian.py:42-102) and builds a metric-correct precision factor R^-1 G (gaussian.py:541-548); with_dense_covariance caches its result (gaussian.py:1300).
- IMPROVED: precision now survives translate, scalar scaling, invertible diagonal maps and diagonal sums (gaussian.py:2125-2147, 2208-2240, 2262-2264, 2291-2298); from_product propagates block factors and precision factors (gaussian.py:409-424).
- IMPROVED: as_multivariate_normal works on any CoordinateSpace with the correct component covariance G^-1 C_gal G^-1 (gaussian.py:1728-1751), not only EuclideanSpace.
- IMPROVED: ambient_ball's sampling route is now parallel and seedable (gaussian.py:1608); SymmetricSpace.pointwise_variance_at has an exact route (one application per point, parallel) and a vectorised closed form for invariant measures (symmetric_space/base.py:1189-1227).
- IMPROVED: new capabilities with no v1 counterpart in this module — condition() (Bayesian update with Matheron sampler), marginal(), cross_covariance(), mahalanobis_squared(), log_density(), grad_log_density(), log_normalising_constant(), kl_divergence_estimate() (gaussian.py:1753-2086).

### convex_analysis

- EllipsoidSupportFunction._mapping (A^{-1/2} route) -> _EllipsoidSupport._value: the direct \|\|A^{-1/2} q\|\| evaluation path via inverse_sqrt_operator is lost; only sqrt(<q, C q>) remains (geometry/convex.py:1039-1043 vs v1 convex_analysis.py:354-356). Not dense, but an option/fast path removed.
- SupportFunction.value_and_support_point / BallSupportFunction.value_and_support_point / EllipsoidSupportFunction.value_and_support_point -> (none): the fused value+maximiser entry point is gone, so a bundle method asking for value then subgradient pays two norms (ball), two covariance applications (ellipsoid) and two adjoint applications (_ImageSupport, numerics/convex.py:417-422). inference/backus.py:1055-1075 re-implements a one-entry memo at its own call site to recover part of the saving.
- ScaledSupportFunction._mapping alpha==0 short-circuit -> _ScaledSupport._value / _FunctionalScaled: the base is always evaluated (numerics/convex.py:402-403; algebra/nodes.py:968-975); v1 returned 0.0 without touching the base (v1 convex_analysis.py:892-893).
- Ellipsoid.support_maximiser (geometry/convex.py:883) omits the negative clamp that _EllipsoidSupport._maximiser (1048) and v1 (convex_analysis.py:382-383) apply; np.sqrt of a slightly negative <Cq,q> gives NaN on the route inference/backus.py:1088 uses.
- HalfSpaceSupportFunction (whole class, v1 convex_analysis.py:446-599) -> nothing: the extended-real half-space support function with configurable parallel tolerances and minimum-norm maximiser has no v2 counterpart; HalfSpace.support_function() raises (geometry/convex.py:98-111, 741-817).
- Set-level support_maximiser is implemented only on Ball (geometry/convex.py:592) and Ellipsoid (:863). _MinkowskiSum (:337-383), _Translated (:184-207) and _OracleSet (:222-258) inherit ConvexSet.support_maximiser (:113-131), which raises NotImplementedError, even when their support_function().subgradient() works (probe: (Ball+Ball).support_function().subgradient(y) -> vector, but (Ball+Ball).support_maximiser(y) -> NotImplementedError '_MinkowskiSum does not provide a support maximiser'; likewise _Translated). The v2 consumers call support_maximiser, not support_function().subgradient (inference/backus.py:1088-1089; numerics/convex.py:1910), and DualFeasibleProperty's docstring (backus.py ~1005-1010) admits 'any convex set ... with a support function and a support maximiser'. So v1's Phase-3 propagation of support points through Minkowski sums / translations (v1 convex_analysis.py:818-848) does not reach the Backus dual route for a composite prior such as the sum of two ellipsoids that ConvexSet.__add__'s docstring (geometry/convex.py:171-177) says route (b) returns. Not dense, but a functional regression adjacent to this unit.
- Ball.support_maximiser at a zero direction returns the stored centre object (geometry/convex.py:594-595; probe: B.support_maximiser(0) is B.centre -> True) while its twin _BallSupport._maximiser returns a copy (numerics/convex.py:352-353; probe -> False). The two implementations REVIEW.md:238 already flags as duplicated have diverged in aliasing behaviour; an axpy-based accumulator over Ball.support_maximiser results could mutate the ball's centre.
- Direct construction of the private combinators with mismatched spaces is unchecked and fails only at evaluation with a numpy shape error rather than a ValueError (probe: _ImageSupport(h, op_on_Y)(yy) -> ValueError 'shapes (3,) and (2,) not aligned'; _MinkowskiSupport((h_X, h_Y))(y) -> same). v1 raised a clear ValueError in the constructors (convex_analysis.py:733-738, :805-810). On an Opaque/non-numpy space the failure would be whatever that backend raises.
- CallableSupportFunction.support_point -> nothing reachable: the maximiser passed to ConvexSet.from_support_function is stored on _OracleSet but dropped by support_function() (geometry/convex.py:256-258), not exposed via support_maximiser (raises), and _OracleSet.maximiser has no caller in the tree; the v1 ability to give an oracle-defined set a usable support point (inner approximation, subgradient for bundle methods) is gone.
- IMPROVED: domain compatibility by HilbertSpace equality rather than identity (numerics/convex.py:294, :316; algebra/operators.py:336-345) — equal-but-distinct spaces compose.
- IMPROVED: _PointSupport._maximiser returns a copy (numerics/convex.py:368), so axpy-based accumulators in _MinkowskiSupport cannot corrupt the stored point; v1 handed out the stored object.
- IMPROVED: HalfSpace caches \|\|normal\|\|^2 at construction (geometry/convex.py:759) where v1 recomputed <a,a> on every _decompose_parallel call (v1 convex_analysis.py:527) — though the support function that benefited is gone.
- IMPROVED: Ball/Ellipsoid support functions are tested on a non-diagonal Gram (make_weighted_space) and on an Opaque space with no component map (tests/test_convex.py:157-214, :398; tests/test_geometry.py:570-660).
- IMPROVED: LinearOperator.adjoint is memoised (probe: A.adjoint is A.adjoint True; REVIEW.md:130), so _ImageSupport's per-call adjoint lookup (numerics/convex.py:418, :421) costs the same as v1's constructor-cached adjoint.

### convex_optimisation

- IMPROVED: ProximalBundleMethod._solve_master -> ProximalBundleMethod._solve_model/_gram: v1 allocated a dense (d+1)x(d+1) Hessian in component coordinates every iteration and used Euclidean dot products (metric-wrong off an orthonormal basis); v2 works in the k-cut dual with true inner products, an incrementally extended k x k Gram matrix and no d x d array (pygeoinf2/numerics/convex.py:1000-1076). Metric-correctness is by inspection: no bundle-method test runs on a non-Euclidean space (tests/test_convex.py:434-453, tests/test_quadratic_programming.py:98-190 all use EuclideanSpace).
- ProximalBundleMethod.qp_solver -> (none): v1 solved the master QP exactly with a QPSolver backend (SLSQP/OSQP/Clarabel); v2 solves the simplex dual by accelerated projected gradient (_minimise_on_simplex) whose accuracy floors on the ill-conditioned Gram matrices a converging bundle produces (it warns at residual > 1e-4; CURRENT_STATE.md:168-171 and REVIEW2.md:175/275 record wrong answers on tight-noise problems). Algorithmically cheaper per iteration but less accurate (pygeoinf2/numerics/convex.py:1092-1203).
- ProximalBundleMethod.minimise returns the stability centre's value, not the least value seen: a candidate with value < best but best - value < descent*gap is a null step and is discarded, so BundleResult.value ('The least value found', convex.py:845) can exceed the minimum evaluated. v1 tracked f_up/best_lam over every evaluation and returned those (pygeoinf2/numerics/convex.py:983-993 vs pygeoinf/convex_optimisation.py:938-944, 966-976).
- LevelBundleMethod._solve_level_master -> LevelBundleMethod._master: QP warm start x0=[lam_hat_c, t_warm] dropped (v2 passes no x0), so OSQP's warm-start advantage is unused (pygeoinf2/numerics/convex.py:1357-1363 vs v1 convex_optimisation.py:1211-1214).
- LevelBundleMethod._compute_lp_lower_bound -> LevelBundleMethod._lower_bound: the bounding box on lambda removed; the LP is unbounded (-inf) whenever the cuts do not span, so the first useful level step is delayed and the proximal fallback is taken instead (pygeoinf2/numerics/convex.py:1326).
- LevelBundleMethod.solve -> LevelBundleMethod.minimise: serious/null step classification removed (centre moves every iteration), which changes the method's stability behaviour (pygeoinf2/numerics/convex.py:1445-1447 vs v1 convex_optimisation.py:1369-1375).
- LevelBundleMethod iteration count on convergence is off by one relative to v1's definition ('master solves, excluding the initial evaluation'): v2 loops `for iteration in range(1, ...)` and returns `iteration` at the gap check before any master solve in that iteration, so converging at the first check reports iterations=1 where v1 reported 0 (pygeoinf2/numerics/convex.py:1406-1412 vs pygeoinf/convex_optimisation.py:1296-1311).
- LevelBundleMethod (both versions): still dense (d+1)x(d+1) in the data dimension and rebuilt per LP+QP call — same as v1, not a regression, but the only remaining O(d^2) convex solver (pygeoinf2/numerics/convex.py:1290-1364; CURRENT_STATE.md:111-114).
- QPSolver protocol tightened: LevelBundleMethod._master tests `result.solved`, a property only v2's QPResult has; a third-party backend returning a v1-style object with `.status` passes isinstance(obj, QPSolver) but raises AttributeError inside the bundle method (pygeoinf2/numerics/convex.py:1362; quadratic_programming.py:72-76).
- solve_support_values -> DualFeasibleProperty.support_values: lambdas (x_best per direction) and per-direction BundleResult diagnostics no longer returned; lambda0 cannot be supplied (pygeoinf2/inference/backus.py:1256-1389).
- solve_support_values(n_jobs) -> support_values(n_jobs): parallel branch exists only on route='dual'; on 'primal', 'kkt' and 'smoothed' the n_jobs argument is silently ignored (pygeoinf2/inference/backus.py:1325-1378). An API wart rather than a regression: v1's solve_primal_feasibility took no n_jobs either.
- SmoothedLBFGSSolver -> route='smoothed': geometric epsilon continuation (5 levels, warm-started) replaced by a single epsilon (default 1e-3); fewer, stiffer problems are not run, so the answer is only as close as one epsilon allows (pygeoinf2/inference/backus.py:1325-1337).
- IMPROVED: SmoothedLBFGSSolver (scipy L-BFGS-B on components, Euclidean metric) -> numerics.optimisation.LBFGS in the space's inner product: metric-correct on a non-orthonormal basis (pygeoinf2/inference/backus.py:1326-1333).
- IMPROVED: ChambollePockSolver._proj_B/_proj_V (ball only, NotImplementedError otherwise) -> ConvexSet.project: ellipsoids, polytopes and intersections (Dykstra) now work (pygeoinf2/numerics/convex.py:1640-1644; geometry/convex.py:633, 938, 387).
- IMPROVED: solve_primal_feasibility -> support_values(route='primal'): warm-starts the model across directions (v1 always started from zero) (pygeoinf2/inference/backus.py:1356-1367).
- ChambollePockSolver._compute_step_sizes -> _steps: the power-iteration start is an unseeded model_space.random(rng=None) draw (spaces.py:40 `_DEFAULT_RNG = default_rng()`), so default step sizes are not reproducible between runs unless rng is passed (v1 used default_rng(0)) (pygeoinf2/numerics/convex.py:1591).
- PrimalKKTSolver._woodbury_solve (cho_factor/cho_solve) -> PrimalKKTSolver._model (np.linalg.solve): LU instead of Cholesky on the M x M kernel, about 2x the factorisation cost per residual evaluation; IMPROVED in robustness since the component matrix of a self-adjoint operator is not symmetric on a non-Euclidean data space and Cholesky would have been wrong there (pygeoinf2/numerics/convex.py:1877-1884).
- PrimalKKTSolver: v1's constructor-time precompute of A_B u0 and G* A_V d_tilde (convex_optimisation.py:2355-2356) is gone; v2 _model recomputes both on every residual evaluation (pygeoinf2/numerics/convex.py:1861, 1865), one extra adjoint application and one extra weight application per fsolve evaluation.
- PrimalKKTSolver dense precompute: unchanged in kind (two dense M x M data-space matrices by column probing, O(M) operator applications and O(M^2) memory at construction); v2 probes the identity for a ball noise set where v1 wrote np.eye(M) directly — M wasted applications (pygeoinf2/numerics/convex.py:1819-1828).
- _get_value_and_subgradient -> (none): the fused value+subgradient oracle protocol is gone; bundle methods always make two calls. For the Backus dual cost the shared adjoint is recovered by a memo in dual_cost (pygeoinf2/inference/backus.py:1055-1076), but any other oracle pays the extra adjoint per iteration.

### subsets

- Ellipsoid (v1 no projection) -> Ellipsoid.project: new capability, but dense by default — each Newton step calls CholeskySolver()(identity + multiplier*precision) which factorises the dense Galerkin matrix (geometry/convex.py:985-1004; numerics/solvers.py:550-562). It does so TWICE per step, not once: convex.py:996 (the derivative at the old multiplier) and :1004 (the update at the new multiplier), so up to 2*iterations = 200 dense factorisations per projection; inside ConvexIntersection/Polytope Dykstra (iterations=1000) this nests to potentially 2e5 dense factorisations. Pass solver= an iterative solver to stay matrix-free — on a direct call only.
- ConvexIntersection.project / Polytope.project / _SetIndicator.prox cannot forward a solver to an Ellipsoid part: _dykstra (geometry/convex.py:386-416, line 410) calls part.project(shifted) bare and ConvexIntersection.project (1280-1293) passes only iterations, so every Dykstra cycle over an intersection containing an Ellipsoid runs Ellipsoid.project with the default dense CholeskySolver, and on a space without a component map the whole intersection projection raises TypeError (verified at runtime on OpaqueSpace for (Ellipsoid & Ball).project and .indicator().prox). v1's ConvexIntersection (subsets.py:737-781) needed only operator applications.
- Ellipsoid now requires an operator that declares Traits.SELF_ADJOINT\|POSITIVE_DEFINITE (geometry/convex.py:850-856, 1172-1178); an operator built with LinearOperator.from_matrix(..., form=...) carries Traits.NONE by default (operators.py:1431) and is refused with ValueError, whereas v1 Ellipsoid(domain, center, radius, operator) accepted any LinearOperator (subsets.py:955-979). Users must pass traits= or call .with_traits(...), which per operators.py:536-545 is a shallow class copy that drops the memoised adjoint.
- EllipsoidSupportFunction.value_and_support_point (v1 convex_analysis, one A^{-1} application for value and point) -> _EllipsoidSupport._value + _maximiser (geometry/convex.py:1039-1051): two covariance applications where one sufficed; Ellipsoid.support_maximiser (863-886) plus support_function()(q) likewise applies the covariance twice.
- Ellipsoid.support_function with inverse_sqrt_operator (v1 could evaluate h(q)=\|\|A^{-1/2}q\|\| when only the inverse square root was available) -> Ellipsoid.support_function(): the inverse_sqrt route is dropped; only covariance= works (geometry/convex.py:1009-1023), so a user holding only a square-root factor must form the covariance.
- ConvexSubset/Ball/Ellipsoid/HalfSpace support_function cached in _support_fn -> support_function() allocates a fresh SupportFunction object per call (geometry/convex.py:661-665,1009-1023); negligible compute, but per-call allocation in hot loops (inference/backus.py:1088-1089 calls support_maximiser per iteration).
- HalfSpace.is_element (v1: one inner product) -> HalfSpace.contains: one inner product plus two norms (\|\|x\|\| and \|\|normal\|\|, the latter recomputed each call although _squared_norm is cached) (geometry/convex.py:794-800).
- ConvexIntersection with the max-functional (v1: gradient/Hessian of the active constraint usable by a smooth constrained optimiser) -> ConvexIntersection.project by Dykstra (geometry/convex.py:386-416,1280-1293): constraint handling now goes through a first-order prox that cycles every part up to 1000 times; there is no second-order information about the feasible set at all.
- PrimalKKTSolver (numerics/convex.py:1878-1891) forms the KKT kernel as a dense data-space matrix (self._noise_covariance_matrix / mu + self._gram / lam) and solves it with np.linalg.solve; outside this unit and deliberate (data space is finite-dimensional), noted only because it is where the 'try the prior's support maximiser first' heuristic that resembles v1 feasible_lower_bound now lives (numerics/convex.py:1906-1920).
- IMPROVED: Intersection of convex sets gains a projection (Dykstra) and an indicator with a prox, so it can be used in ProximalGradient / primal-dual routes (geometry/convex.py:1212-1293; tests/test_geometry.py:775-870); v1 ConvexIntersection had no projection.
- IMPROVED: HalfSpace.project is now idempotent and the identity on feasible points (geometry/convex.py:802-814); v1 moved interior points onto the boundary plane, which would have been wrong as a prox.
- IMPROVED: Polytope.project and ConvexIntersection.project are true metric projections via Dykstra rather than cyclic projection (geometry/convex.py:386-416; tests/test_geometry.py:712-755).
- IMPROVED: ConvexIntersection now validates that all parts share a domain (geometry/convex.py:1257-1259); v1 did not.
- IMPROVED: Ball.contains and BallSurface.contains keep v1's one-norm fast path and Hyperplane/HalfSpace.project use a cached \|\|a\|\|^2 (geometry/convex.py:699,734,759,814) rather than recomputing it per call as v1 did (subsets.py:1326).

### subspaces

- AffineSubspace.from_linear_equation / LinearSubspace.from_kernel / pseudo_inverse default CholeskySolver(galerkin=True) -> _normal_inverse default CGSolver(rtol=1e-12) (pygeoinf2/geometry/subspaces.py:39-60): IMPROVED in that no dense m x m Galerkin matrix of A A* is formed by default; WORSE in per-application cost — every application of the kernel projector, the pseudo-inverse or the minimum-norm translation now runs a CG solve on A A* to rtol 1e-12, where v1 did one factorisation and a back-substitution per application. dimension() (275-295), OrthogonalProjector.basis() (102-114) and to_hyperplanes() (419-436) apply the projector dim times, i.e. dim CG solves for an equation-built subspace. Passing solver=CholeskySolver() restores v1's profile, except in from_hyperplanes which takes no solver.
- AffineSubspace.to_hyperplanes -> AffineSubspace.to_hyperplanes: v1 used the stored equation with m applications of B* (v1 subspaces.py:507-556); v2 ignores the stored equation and computes projector.complement().basis(), i.e. dim projector applications plus Gram-Schmidt of dim vectors, and requires coordinates (subspaces.py:419-436, 102-114). O(dim) operator applications where v1 was O(m), and each application is a CG solve under the default solver.
- AffineSubspace.from_hyperplanes constraint operator: v1 Python loop of inner products with hand-written adjoint (v1 subspaces.py:488-499) -> v2 LinearOperator.from_vectors(...).adjoint, which on a CoordinateSpace with component fast paths is a _ColumnOperator holding the normals' components as a (dim, m) dense array (algebra/operators.py:1138-1192, 1537-1597). Memory is the same order as storing the m normals themselves; IMPROVED: one matvec per action and the adjoint analyses y once instead of m times.
- IMPROVED: (A A*)^{-1} is built once in from_linear_equation / from_kernel and reused by the projector, the translation, pseudo_inverse(), with_constraint_value() and with_translation() (subspaces.py:320-328, 496-497, 516, 534, 637; tests/test_geometry.py:506-526 pin the solve count at 1). v1 pseudo_inverse and with_constraint_value re-formed and re-solved B B* on every access (v1 subspaces.py:240-258, 610-630).
- IMPROVED: OrthogonalProjector.complement() returns an OrthogonalProjector carrying SELF_ADJOINT \| IDEMPOTENT (subspaces.py:116-129) instead of a generic identity - P sum, and complement().complement() is the original object; LinearSubspace.complement no longer reaches into a private _mapping (574-582).
- IMPROVED: OrthogonalProjector.from_basis orthonormalises with domain.orthonormal_basis (algebra/spaces.py:220-244), which drops dependent vectors and reorthogonalises once, rather than v1's gram_schmidt which raised ValueError on any dependence; an empty family yields a working zero projector (subspaces.py:152-157).
- AffineSubspace.from_complement_basis -> AffineSubspace.from_complement_basis: not a dense change but a capability loss — v1 built an explicit constraint operator B: domain -> EuclideanSpace(m) with adjoint (v1 subspaces.py:400-433); v2 builds only the projector (subspaces.py:357-381), so pseudo_inverse, with_constraint_value, Bayesian conditioning and parameterised constrained inversion (inference/point.py:918-924) are unavailable on the result.
- AffineSubspace.get_tangent_basis -> OrthogonalProjector.basis(): not a dense change but a CORRECTNESS regression — v1's absolute 1e-10 floor on norm(P e_i) (v1 subspaces.py:188-196) was dropped; v2 passes every projected ambient basis vector to orthonormal_basis whose test is purely relative to the input's own norm (subspaces.py:110-114; algebra/spaces.py:242, 268), so rounding-noise images (~1e-16) of basis vectors in the complement are normalised and returned. Verified: len(basis()) == 6 vs dimension() == 5 on R^6 for the constraint <0.3 e_0, x> = 1; 131/200 (CG) and 55/200 (Cholesky) wrong ranks on random coordinate-aligned constraints in R^20, v1 0/200. dimension() and to_hyperplanes() unaffected in all sampled cases.
- GaussianMeasure.condition (pygeoinf2/probability/gaussian.py:1802-1811) asserts SELF_ADJOINT \| POSITIVE_DEFINITE on A C A* (+ R) by claim and inverts it with resolve_solver(solver, normal)(normal) (CG default); it accepts a solver or a factory callable, but there is still no route for a rank-deficient constraint operator (an implicit (I-P) constraint would stall CG, as in the subspace module). Confirms the loss of v1's implicit-constraint/MinRes conditioning path.

### forward_problem_inversion

- LinearForwardProblem.parameterized_problem(dense=True, parallel=, n_jobs=) -> LinearForwardProblem.parameterised(P): the option to materialise A@P and the error covariance densely (in parallel) is gone; the user must call forward_operator.assembled(n_jobs=) and error_measure.with_dense_covariance(n_jobs=) by hand (problem.py:393-412; operators.py:951; gaussian.py:1275). The v2 default (matrix-free) is unchanged.
- LinearForwardProblem.data_reduced_problem(dense=True, parallel=, n_jobs=) -> LinearForwardProblem.data_reduced(R, error=): same loss of the dense/parallel surrogate path (problem.py:414-441).
- The hand-built dense surrogate route (problem.parameterised(P) then LinearForwardProblem(p.forward_operator.assembled(n_jobs=k), error=p.error_measure.with_dense_covariance(n_jobs=k))) is real but never exercised in pygeoinf2/tests or pygeoinf2/examples for a forward problem or estimator: assembled() appears only on bare operators (tests/test_observation.py:53, tests/test_fourier_spaces.py:346, examples/19_observation.py:78) and with_dense_covariance() only in tests/test_probability.py:952-1000, so no test proves the v2 substitute reproduces v1's parameterized_problem(dense=True)/data_reduced_problem(dense=True) end to end.
- LinearInversion.parameterized_inversion / data_reduced_inversion (dense=, parallel=, n_jobs=, formalism=) -> LeastSquares/ConstrainedLeastSquares/ConstrainedMinimumNorm/LinearGaussianInversion .parameterised / .data_reduced: dense/parallel options and the per-call formalism override are gone (point.py:256-294, 827-889, 1014-1044; gaussian.py:332-382). parallel= is gone everywhere by decision D-6 (REVIEW.md:287,380; DESIGN.md:2992) — only n_jobs survives, and only on assembled()/matrix()/with_dense_covariance.
- ConstrainedLeastSquares.data_reduced(*args, **kwargs) (inference/point.py:875) and ConstrainedMinimumNorm.data_reduced (point.py:1031) forward keyword arguments to LinearForwardProblem.data_reduced, which accepts only error=; a v1-style dense=True/parallel=/n_jobs= call therefore fails with TypeError rather than being ignored or honoured.
- LOST (deliberate-dense step in v1, no v2 route): LinearBayesianInversion.parameterized_inversion / data_reduced_inversion densified the (parameter) prior with with_dense_covariance whenever dense=True OR the target formalism was 'model_space', guaranteeing a precision for Q^-1 + A* R^-1 A (linear_bayesian.py:1404-1408, 1462-1466). v2 LinearGaussianInversion.parameterised/data_reduced pass the prior through untouched (gaussian.py:332-382); with a precision-less prior and formalism='model_space' NormalOperator raises ValueError (normal.py:281-286). The user must call prior.with_dense_covariance() themselves.
- LOST: v1 LinearBayesianInversion.parameterized_inversion defaulted parameter_prior to the pull-back model_prior_measure.affine_mapping(operator=parameterization.adjoint) (linear_bayesian.py:1389-1392); v2 LinearGaussianInversion.parameterised requires prior= (gaussian.py:332-358). The v2 docstring and review/inference.md:44 argue the default was not a true pull-back ('defensible'), but there is no D-decision, so it is an unrecorded dropped convenience.
- LOST: parameterised / data_reduced / with_formalism / formalism on DiscrepancyPrinciple. Its v1 counterpart LinearMinimumNormInversion had all four (with_formalism at linear_optimisation.py:816; the other three inherited from LinearInversion because its constructor is (fp, formalism=), linear_optimisation.py:794-810, inversion.py:123-232). v2 DiscrepancyPrinciple exposes only .problem and .level (point.py:543-600).
- LOST: dense materialisation of the pulled-back constraint operator (new_B.with_dense_matrix(parallel=, n_jobs=)) in the constrained surrogates (linear_optimisation.py:728-730, 1288-1290); v2 _parameterised_subspace always leaves B @ M matrix-free (point.py:890-930).
- PARITY (originally misreported as IMPROVED): LinearForwardProblem.data_measure_from_model -> translate() keeps the error measure's precision (gaussian.py:2208-2227), but v1's affine_mapping(translation=) already returned GaussianMeasure(..., inverse_covariance=self._inverse_covariance, inverse_covariance_factor=self._inverse_covariance_factor) (gaussian_measure.py:1150-1157). chi_squared on the induced measure works in both.
- PARITY (originally misreported as IMPROVED): GaussianMeasure.from_product (joint_measure/from_direct_sum) builds a block-diagonal precision when every factor has one (gaussian.py:428-436); v1 GaussianMeasure.from_direct_sum already did this (gaussian_measure.py:350-356, BlockDiagonalLinearOperator of inverse_covariance when all inverse_covariance_set).
- PARITY (originally misreported as IMPROVED): the surrogate builders on the constrained classes pull the constraint back as (B M) p == w (point.py:827-889, 890-930, 1014-1044); v1 ConstrainedLinearLeastSquaresInversion and ConstrainedLinearMinimumNormInversion implemented parameterized_inversion and data_reduced_inversion with the same construction (linear_optimisation.py:683-775, 1244-1330) and raised NotImplementedError only for basis-defined subspaces, which v2 still does. The v2 surrogates also carry damping/solver/level/prior, as the stateful v1 overrides did; only v1's stateless base contract type(self)(fp, formalism=) is gone.
- IMPROVED: synthetic_data/chi_squared/critical_chi_squared/chi_squared_test now live on ForwardProblem and work for a nonlinear forward operator (problem.py:152-233); synthetic_data has an error-free fallback and all sampling takes an rng.
- IMPROVED: scipy.stats is imported lazily in critical_chi_squared (problem.py:208-211) rather than at module import.
- IMPROVED: GaussianMeasure.with_dense_covariance(n_jobs=) now caches the result and attaches covariance_factor/precision/precision_factor (probability/gaussian.py:1275-1340), where v1's version produced only a dense covariance plus inverse.
- NEUTRAL (not dense, but worth knowing): chi_squared_from_residual now goes through GaussianMeasure.mahalanobis_squared, which refuses to fall back to a dense solve when the measure has no precision (gaussian.py:1972-1997) — same requirement as v1's inverse_covariance, different exception type (NotImplementedError vs AttributeError).
- NEUTRAL: NormalOperator (LinearGaussianInversion) refuses formalism='model_space' without an error measure (normal.py:250-258) where v1 silently solved Q^-1 + A*A; TikhonovNormalOperator (LeastSquares/MinimumNorm/DiscrepancyPrinciple/constrained) still assembles unweighted A*A + tI as v1 did (tikhonov.py:79-90).

### linear_bayesian

- LinearBayesianInversion.estimate_log_determinant / log_evidence -> LinearGaussianInversion.normal_log_determinant / log_evidence: the default method='auto' forms the dense Galerkin matrix of the normal operator (and, in model_space, of Q and R) and calls np.linalg.slogdet whenever the space has coordinates, dim <= 4000 and either the matrix is readable or dim <= samples*max_iterations (=4000); v1 was SLQ-only and never formed a matrix (pygeoinf2/numerics/functional_calculus.py:733-771; pygeoinf2/inference/gaussian.py:586-605). Documented and deliberate (DESIGN §26, docstring), but the matrix-free behaviour now requires method='stochastic'.
- LinearBayesianInversion._trace_log_slq(parallel=, n_jobs=) -> numerics.functional_calculus.log_determinant: no n_jobs parameter and random_trace is called without one, so Hutchinson probes are always serial; random_trace itself supports n_jobs (pygeoinf2/numerics/functional_calculus.py:641-652,780-786; pygeoinf2/numerics/randomised.py:760).
- LinearBayesianInversion._trace_log_slq log(max(x,1e-15)) -> operator_log: np.log applied to the Lanczos Ritz values with no clamp; a negative Ritz value on a near-singular normal operator yields NaN instead of a floored value (pygeoinf2/numerics/functional_calculus.py:617-619; v1 linear_bayesian.py:602-603).
- Hutchinson probe distribution changed: v1 random_trace drew Rademacher (+-1) component probes (pygeoinf/low_rank.py:1123-1127); v2 random_trace draws Gaussian white noise on the space (pygeoinf2/numerics/randomised.py:812-813). Both estimate tr(A_c), so the log-determinant is the same quantity, but Rademacher probes have strictly lower Hutchinson variance, so at equal sample counts v2's SLQ estimate of ln\|N\| is noisier; v2 partly compensates by defaulting to 100 probes where v1 started from 10.
- LinearBayesianInversion.diagonal_normal_preconditioner(parallel=, n_jobs=) -> NormalDiagonalPreconditioner: the per-block adjoint/prior loop is serial and the R diagonal is extracted via diagonals() without n_jobs (pygeoinf2/inference/preconditioners.py:140-151).
- LinearBayesianInversion.sparse_localized_preconditioner(parallel=, n_jobs=) -> LocalisedPreconditioner: the per-block randomised eigendecompositions run serially (pygeoinf2/inference/preconditioners.py:250-294).
- LinearBayesianInversion (lazy) -> LinearGaussianInversion.__init__: solver(normal) runs at construction, so with a direct solver (CholeskySolver/LUSolver) the dim x dim matrix of the normal operator is extracted and factorised as soon as the estimator is built, even if it is never applied; v1 deferred the factorisation until a method was called (pygeoinf2/inference/gaussian.py:113-114; pygeoinf2/numerics/solvers.py:459-461).
- Every derived inversion -- with_formalism, with_solver, parameterised, data_reduced -- constructs a fresh LinearGaussianInversion and therefore eagerly runs solver(normal) and resolves any deferred preconditioner (pygeoinf2/inference/gaussian.py:225-243,355-358,379-382; numerics/solvers.py:793-800,832-835): with a direct solver each derived object extracts and factorises its own dim x dim normal matrix at creation, and a structure-aware preconditioner is rebuilt (its adjoint/prior loop or block eigendecompositions re-run) for each one, where v1 deferred all of that to the first method call.
- LinearBayesianInversion.parameterized_inversion / data_reduced_inversion (dense=, parallel=, n_jobs=) -> parameterised / data_reduced: the option to pre-assemble the reduced forward operator and prior densely (in parallel) is gone; only GaussianMeasure.with_dense_covariance(n_jobs=) survives, by hand (pygeoinf2/inference/gaussian.py:332-382; pygeoinf2/probability/gaussian.py:1275-1340).
- LinearBayesianInversion._compute_data_residual (skips A(mu) when prior.has_zero_expectation) -> LinearGaussianInversion._data_shift: A is always applied to the prior expectation, one extra forward action per residual and one at construction for zero-mean priors (pygeoinf2/inference/gaussian.py:118-119,148-154,433-435).
- The _residual_solve memo requires a CoordinateSpace data space and costs one to_components plus a buffer copy per __call__/mahalanobis (pygeoinf2/inference/gaussian.py:384-406); on a data space without coordinates the memo is simply off and est(data) followed by mahalanobis(data) costs two solves, as in v1.
- IMPROVED: normal operator, its inverse, the gain and the posterior covariance are built once and cached instead of being rebuilt (and re-inverted) on every kalman_operator/model_posterior_measure/posterior_expectation_operator/mahalanobis call (pygeoinf2/inference/gaussian.py:107-116).
- IMPROVED: the residual solve is memoised so est(data) followed by mahalanobis(data)/log_evidence(data) costs one solve, and a mixture costs one solve per component (pygeoinf2/inference/gaussian.py:384-440; tests/test_normal.py:863-901,932).
- IMPROVED: the log-determinant is memoised per settings, and a DiagonalLinearOperator log-determinant is exact O(dim) with no applications -- including after with_traits, which now preserves the class (pygeoinf2/inference/gaussian.py:581-590; numerics/functional_calculus.py:734-742; algebra/operators.py:536-579).
- IMPROVED: posterior covariance written (I - K A) Q applies Q twice per action instead of v1's three for Q - K A Q (pygeoinf2/inference/normal.py:498-525).
- IMPROVED: LocalisedPreconditioner averages overlapping blocks instead of summing duplicates (a v1 defect), restricts in the Galerkin form so it is right on weighted data spaces, and drops the unconditional stdout prints (pygeoinf2/inference/preconditioners.py:255-260,302-311).
- IMPROVED: the surrogate may live on a different (coarser) model space, and Woodbury picks up known precisions automatically (pygeoinf2/inference/normal.py:399-461; numerics/preconditioners.py:642-651); the surrogate no longer crashes when there is no error measure (v1 AttributeError at linear_bayesian.py:1176).
- IMPROVED: randomised routines (random_svd/random_eig/random_cholesky used by low_rank_surrogate and LocalisedPreconditioner) apply the operator to a block of probes at once via apply_block, with an n_jobs hook (pygeoinf2/numerics/randomised.py:537-660).
- IMPROVED: log-determinant estimates return an Estimate with a standard error, and the model-space Sylvester route combines errors in quadrature (pygeoinf2/numerics/randomised.py:51-67; inference/gaussian.py:606-609).
- IMPROVED (cost): the v2 solver callback reports the CG recurrence residual already in hand rather than re-applying the operator once per iteration as v1's ResidualTrackingCallback did (pygeoinf2/numerics/solvers.py:814-818; v1 linear_solvers.py:1066-1100) -- at the price of no independent residual check.

### linear_optimisation

- REGRESSION (wrong answer, not dense): ConstrainedLeastSquares ignores a non-zero error expectation — point.py:764-767 composes projector @ inner.operator and rebuilds the translation from the subspace alone, dropping the inner LeastSquares' translation -L z_bar (point.py:119-124); v1's shift_out @ reduced_op @ shift_in carried it (pygeoinf/linear_optimisation.py:308-316,646-656). Verified: v1 matches the dense constrained Tikhonov minimiser to 1e-15 (scratchpad/cls_v1.py), v2 is off by exactly \|\|inner.translation\|\| (3.25 / 3.09 with \|u\| ~ 1.7) in both formalisms (scratchpad/cls_shift.py, cmn_v1v2.py, re-run); ConstrainedMinimumNorm is unaffected (v1/v2 agree to 3e-11). Not covered by tests: the fixture error is zero-mean (pygeoinf2/tests/test_point.py:253-278) and the constrained LS test checks only the constraint (test_point.py:636-639).
- LinearLeastSquaresInversion.woodbury_data_preconditioner -> WoodburyPreconditioner.from_normal(TikhonovNormalOperator).data_form(): returns t * N_d^-1 instead of N_d^-1 (the 1/damping factor of v1 is absent because prior_inverse = t I from tikhonov.py:211-214 is substituted into the Gaussian identity without rescaling); verified numerically \|\|W N x\|\|/\|\|x\|\| = 0.3 at t = 0.3, model form 1.0 (pygeoinf2/numerics/preconditioners.py:697-715; pygeoinf2/inference/tikhonov.py:188-214; scratchpad/wood.py, adv_lo_check.py). Carries over unchanged to the surrogate construction that replaces surrogate_woodbury_data_preconditioner (WoodburyPreconditioner.from_normal(lsq.surrogate(...)).data_form() gives 0.300 at t = 0.3 on the surrogate operator). Harmless for PCG iterates, wrong as an inverse.
- LinearLeastSquaresInversion.woodbury_*_preconditioner -> WoodburyPreconditioner: the inner solve defaults to CGSolver(rtol=1e-3, maxiter=200, strict=False) when no solver is given, where v1 used the caller's solver exactly (pygeoinf2/numerics/preconditioners.py:663-671).
- ConstrainedLinear{LeastSquares,MinimumNorm}Inversion.parameterized_inversion -> _parameterised_subspace: AffineSubspace.from_linear_equation is called without the original subspace's solver/preconditioner, so (B M)(B M)* is always inverted by the default CG regardless of the solver the constraint was built with (pygeoinf2/inference/point.py:929-931; geometry/subspaces.py:298-329; v1's own default was CholeskySolver(galerkin=True), pygeoinf/subspaces.py:285-328); the dense=True/parallel/n_jobs densification of new_B is gone.
- LinearInversion.parameterized_inversion/data_reduced_inversion(dense=, parallel=, n_jobs=) -> LeastSquares.parameterised/data_reduced: the opt-in dense assembly with joblib parallelism is gone from the estimators and the forward problem (pygeoinf2/inference/problem.py:393-441); the replacement is manual: LinearOperator.assembled(n_jobs=) on the composed operator before building the problem (algebra/operators.py:951).
- ConstrainedMinimumNorm.parameterised/data_reduced do not forward iterations/rtol, so the rebuilt estimator silently reverts to the defaults 60/1e-6 (pygeoinf2/inference/point.py:998-1002,1023-1043).
- LeastSquares.__init__ applies the freshly built estimator to the error expectation even when it is zero, costing one normal-equation solve per construction (and per DiscrepancyPrinciple.estimator_at in every derivative) (pygeoinf2/inference/point.py:119-124; GaussianMeasure.has_zero_expectation exists at probability/gaussian.py:582 but is unused here).
- DiscrepancyPrinciple: a deferred LinearSolver preconditioner is reused while the damping stays within a factor 10 of where it was built (DampedSolves.refresh, pygeoinf2/numerics/root_find.py:386-389,467-481) — an approximation v1 did not make (it rebuilt preconditioner(normal_operator) at every damping); refresh is not exposed on DiscrepancyPrinciple.
- DiscrepancyPrinciple._resolve uses found.converged as the 'damping moves with the data' flag (pygeoinf2/inference/point.py:616-628,679-685). converged is also False when Brent hits the iterations cap on an interior bracket (numerics/root_find.py:337), in which case the rank-one derivative term is silently dropped and the derivative is the frozen-damping L alone although the damping is data-dependent; found.exhausted is the flag that means saturation. Only bites with a small user-set iterations.
- NOT AN IMPROVEMENT (withdrawn): the once-only direct-solver matrix extraction in DampedSolves._sum_member/_matrices (pygeoinf2/numerics/root_find.py:418-465) is dead code on the Tikhonov path — TikhonovFamily builds DampedSolves with assemble=self.at (inference/tikhonov.py:379) and DampedSolves.operator() takes assemble before _sum_member (root_find.py:408-412), so with a DirectSolver every probe of DiscrepancyPrinciple / MinimumNorm.for_data / discrepancy_search re-probes the full matrix (dim applications per damping; measured 30/30/30/30 vs 30/0/0/0 for a bare DampedSolves, scratchpad/sweep_count.py). v1 parity, not a saving.
- MinimumNorm.for_data has no zero-model shortcut (only DiscrepancyPrinciple._resolve does, pygeoinf2/inference/point.py:613-615), so data the zero model already fits drive monotone_root through all 200 upward expansions (200 solves) and return a MinimumNorm at damping 1e200. New-API observation, no v1 counterpart.
- IMPROVED: LinearMinimumNormInversion.discrepancy_search -> monotone_root: Brent's method in log(t) with memoised probes replaces bisection on t, bracketing widens in both directions, and the search reports evaluations/inner_iterations/bracket/converged (pygeoinf2/numerics/root_find.py:131-338); DESIGN.md:4285-4290 measures 10-13 solves per root against 23-28.
- IMPROVED: iterative_warm_start: warm starts now cover the bracketing phase as well as the bisection (pygeoinf2/numerics/root_find.py:193-200), and work through InverseOperator.solve(x0=) for every IterativeSolver rather than a special solve_linear_system path.
- IMPROVED: DiscrepancyPrinciple.at(data) computes the model and its derivative from a single damping search (pygeoinf2/inference/point.py:634-647), and the derivative reuses one inverse normal operator (point.py:677-694) where v1 built solver(normal_operator) twice (pygeoinf/linear_optimisation.py:955-985).
- IMPROVED: the found damping and the search diagnostics are exposed (MinimumNorm.for_data(...).damping, discrepancy_search, DiscrepancyPrinciple.search; pygeoinf2/inference/point.py:344-435,593-602) where v1 hid them; a saturated search no longer adds a spurious rank-one derivative term (point.py:679-685) — subject to the converged-vs-exhausted caveat above.
- IMPROVED: the reduced normal operator of the constrained least-squares estimator is public (ConstrainedLeastSquares.normal_operator/.reduced, pygeoinf2/inference/point.py:792-800), so Woodbury/structure-aware preconditioners for the reduced system can be built through the public API, which v1 did not allow.

### backus_gilbert

- quadratic_form_quantile._draw_q_samples -> weighted_chi2_cdf/weighted_chi2_quantile method='monte_carlo': v1 drew in chunks of 1_000_000//n rows (~8 MB peak); v2 allocates the whole (samples × n_weights) normal matrix at once (numerics/quadratic_forms.py:197, :254) — O(samples·n) memory, prohibitive for long spectra.
- quadratic_form_quantile.weighted_chi2_cdf (array t, one shared MC sample) -> weighted_chi2_cdf (scalar only): v1 evaluated ws/mc vectorised over t and drew the Monte Carlo sample once for all thresholds; v2 accepts one threshold (quadratic_forms.py:185) so many thresholds cost many calls and, for Monte Carlo, many redraws.
- quadratic_form_quantile._auto_select_method + _saddlepoint_cdf -> weighted_chi2_*(method='auto'): v1 'auto' picked the O(1)-per-evaluation Lugannani–Rice saddlepoint whenever 0.3/ν_eff < tol (ν_eff > 30 at the default tol); v2 has no saddlepoint and 'auto' is always a full Imhof quadrature (quadratic_forms.py:199-207), with the moment match chosen only by the Gaussian-measure consumer above 1000 weights and ν_eff > 100 (probability/gaussian.py:1712-1716). gaussian.py:1691-1694 measures the consequence: 0.8 s at 500 weights, 10.4 s at 2000.
- quadratic_form_quantile._invert_cdf(rtol=1e-6) -> weighted_chi2_quantile: brentq now runs at xtol=rtol=1e-12 (quadratic_forms.py:283-284) on a CDF at tolerance 1e-10 (:218) instead of the user's rtol (v1 default 1e-6, shared by the inner quadrature); each of the extra root-finder steps is a full Imhof pass, and the tolerance is no longer settable.
- quadratic_form_quantile._ws_quantile (closed form) -> weighted_chi2_quantile(method='matched'): v1 returned a·chi2.ppf(p, ν) directly; v2 root-finds on the matched CDF (quadratic_forms.py:262-285) — the same number by a bracket search plus brentq.
- backus_gilbert.BackusInference.test_data_compatibility (matrix-free damped Krylov minimum-norm solve) -> FeasibleProperty.is_feasible: goes through _data_gram, a dense scipy eigh of the dim(D)×dim(D) matrix of A A* built by `.matrix(form="components")` (inference/backus.py:568-589), and refuses non-orthonormal data spaces (:575-580). BackusInference.is_feasible (error-free) and DualFeasibleProperty.is_feasible remain matrix-free.
- backus_gilbert.DualMasterCostFunction.value_and_subgradient (fused support value + support point via SupportFunction.value_and_support_point) -> DualFeasibleProperty.dual_cost: the residual and −λ are shared by a memo (backus.py:1062-1076), but the support value and the support maximiser are separate calls (:1082 vs :1088-1089), so an ellipsoid prior/noise applies its covariance twice per oracle call where v1 applied it once (review/geometry_plotting.md:33,90).
- backus_gilbert.DualMasterCostFunction._finite_difference_gradient -> (none): the O(dim) fallback is gone; a set without a support maximiser now raises inside the gradient (geometry/convex.py:113-131) rather than degrading to finite differences — a loss of generality, not of speed.
- backus_gilbert.BackusInference.critical_chi_squared / significance_level (O(1) chi2.ppf(level, dim D)) -> harden_error -> GaussianMeasure.ambient_ball (pygeoinf2/inference/backus.py:133; probability/gaussian.py:1503-1652): for a data-error Gaussian whose covariance is not diagonal in the data basis, the 'auto' route forms the dense Galerkin covariance matrix and takes a generalised eigh (gaussian.py:1636-1652, O(dim(D)^3)), then inverts the weighted chi-square by full Imhof quadrature for up to 1000 weights (gaussian.py:1712-1716); above dense_limit=1024 with no sampler and no rank= it raises ValueError instead (gaussian.py:1596-1612). This is paid by every BackusGilbert/FeasibleProperty constructed without noise= on a correlated Gaussian error; v1 never formed a matrix to get a threshold.
- Recovering v1's exact chi-squared data set for route (d): GaussianMeasure.credible_set on a measure built from a covariance alone densely inverts the Galerkin matrix with np.linalg.solve (probability/gaussian.py:1476-1497) to obtain the precision an Ellipsoid requires; v1's chi-squared test needed only chi2.ppf and the measure's Mahalanobis form.
- IMPROVED: DualFeasibleProperty.support_values(directions, data, warm_start=True, n_jobs=None, route='dual'\|'primal'\|'kkt'\|'smoothed') (backus.py:1256-1389) sweeps directions with the previous certificate as the start and can run directions in parallel via parallel_map; v1's cost object needed convex_optimisation's driver for this and had no parallel option in this unit.
- IMPROVED: BackusInference.__call__ (backus.py:407-427) returns the exact feasible property set as an Ellipsoid in dim(P)+1 matrix-free solves, and _joint_spectrum (dense eigh) is cached once per estimator (cached_property, :430-447) rather than rebuilt per inclusion_norm call.
- IMPROVED: harden_error (backus.py:93-133) derives the data ball radius from the measure's ambient_ball quantile in the space's own norm instead of REVIEW.md's earlier metric-wrong `sqrt(chi2_crit × mean diagonal)`; and quadratic_forms.py:24-36 makes scipy.stats/optimize lazy imports (0.26 s off import time).

### symmetric_space_base

- CorrelatedInvariantGaussianMeasure.nuclear_norm -> GaussianMeasure.nuclear_norm: v1 summed the per-slice eigenvalues in O(dim n); v2 has no block-spectral route, so 'auto' assembles the dense (n*dim)x(n*dim) component matrix via BlockLinearOperator._known_matrix and traces it (/home/david/dev/pygeoinf/pygeoinf2/probability/gaussian.py:793-806, algebra/direct_sum.py:598-599).
- CorrelatedInvariantGaussianMeasure.hilbert_schmidt_norm -> GaussianMeasure.hilbert_schmidt_norm: same dense (n*dim)^2 assembly (/home/david/dev/pygeoinf/pygeoinf2/probability/gaussian.py:740-763).
- CorrelatedInvariantGaussianMeasure.kl_divergence -> GaussianMeasure.kl_divergence: v1 exact O(dim n^3) slice-wise formula; v2 forms two dense Galerkin matrices when n*dim <= 4000 and raises ValueError above that (runtime: 2 fields x dim 4096 raises) (/home/david/dev/pygeoinf/pygeoinf2/probability/gaussian.py:999-1030, 1049-1062).
- CorrelatedInvariantGaussianMeasure.__add__/__sub__/__mul__/__truediv__/__neg__ -> generic ProbabilityMeasure algebra: v1 stayed in class with slice arithmetic; v2 returns covariance `_Sum`/`_Composition` and factor None/`_Scaled`, so slices, exact norms, spectral marginal factors and a one-draw sampler are lost after any arithmetic (runtime; /home/david/dev/pygeoinf/pygeoinf2/probability/gaussian.py:2242-2318; SpectralBlockLinearOperator defines no _combine_* at base.py:2427-2555).
- SymmetricHilbertSpace.l2_products_operator -> SymmetricSpace.l2_products_operator: v1 matrix-free LinearOperator.from_vectors; v2 stacks a dense (n_fields x dim) row matrix and uses from_matrix(form='galerkin') (/home/david/dev/pygeoinf/pygeoinf2/symmetric_space/base.py:451-476). Mild: same memory as the fields themselves.
- SymmetricHilbertSpace.identity_operator -> LinearOperator.identity: `identity + D` is a generic `_Sum` rather than a DiagonalLinearOperator, so expressions like `I + s^2 * Laplacian` lose the O(dim) functional calculus (inverse, sqrt) v1 had via the identity override (runtime; /home/david/dev/pygeoinf/pygeoinf2/algebra/operators.py:1108-1112).
- InvariantGaussianMeasure.affine_mapping branch 3 -> GaussianMeasure.affine_map: the automatic spectrally regularised block preconditioner for iterative inverse solves (inverse_solver/inverse_preconditioner kwargs) is gone; no replacement in probability/ (grep 'water\|jacobi_schur\|inverse_solver' empty).
- SymmetricHilbertSpace.estimate_truncation_degree -> SymmetricSpace.estimate_truncation_degree: v2 can only return a degree present in the current space (bounded by degrees.max()); v1 walked upward without bound to propose an lmax (/home/david/dev/pygeoinf/pygeoinf2/symmetric_space/base.py:478-514 vs v1 :2010-2056). Sphere.truncation_degree_for partially covers this.
- IMPROVED: InvariantLinearAutomorphism -> DiagonalLinearOperator stores a numpy array, no scipy.sparse dia allocation per derived operator; eigenvalues cached (/home/david/dev/pygeoinf/pygeoinf2/algebra/diagonal.py:39-97).
- IMPROVED: SymmetricSobolevSpace.point_evaluation_operator -> SymmetricSpace.point_evaluation_operator is matrix-free by default (NUFFT on boxes, batched Legendre on the sphere, points prepared once); the dense (n_points x dim) matrix is opt-in (/home/david/dev/pygeoinf/pygeoinf2/symmetric_space/base.py:1582-1651).
- IMPROVED: pairs_within_distance uses a cKDTree over the geometry embedding (O(n log n), periodic wrap) instead of v1's O(n^2) Python loop (/home/david/dev/pygeoinf/pygeoinf2/symmetric_space/base.py:1262-1322).
- IMPROVED: cluster_points computes the condensed distance vector vectorised through _embedding instead of a Python double loop (/home/david/dev/pygeoinf/pygeoinf2/symmetric_space/base.py:1340-1403).
- IMPROVED: flexural_operator is a fused _FlexureOperator (seven transforms per application vs ~fifty term-by-term) with a components action for Krylov loops (/home/david/dev/pygeoinf/pygeoinf2/symmetric_space/base.py:2557-2655).
- IMPROVED: correlated covariance/factor is a SpectralBlockLinearOperator applied as one einsum (n analyses + n syntheses) instead of n^2 diagonal blocks; sampling is one synthesis per field (/home/david/dev/pygeoinf/pygeoinf2/symmetric_space/base.py:2427-2555, :929-938).
- IMPROVED: path/ball operators use sparse quadrature weight matrices and a cached Gauss-Legendre rule; dense assembly is opt-in (/home/david/dev/pygeoinf/pygeoinf2/symmetric_space/base.py:2256-2383, :2688-2735).
- IMPROVED: covariance_function/pointwise_variance use a closed form (sum over basis, Legendre series on the sphere) instead of applying the covariance to a Dirac representer (/home/david/dev/pygeoinf/pygeoinf2/symmetric_space/base.py:1092-1141, sphere.py:1135-1190).
- IMPROVED: SymmetricHilbertSpace.__init__ no longer runs a Python loop over dim calling two abstract methods per index; the metric array is computed vectorised in the geometry constructor (/home/david/dev/pygeoinf/pygeoinf2/symmetric_space/fourier.py:159-165, sphere.py:208-214).
- Per-draw cost regression (not dense): every algebraic operation on an invariant measure (scalar *, /, +, -, translate, the zero-mean and post-hoc norm_std recipes) discards the explicit one-synthesis Karhunen-Loeve sampler registered by SymmetricSpace.invariant_measure, so the result samples through the DiagonalLinearOperator factor at one analysis plus three (translate: four) syntheses per draw (runtime circle Sobolev(64): m.sample -> from_components x1; (2*m).sample -> to_components x1, from_components x3; m.translate(v).sample -> to x1, from x4) (/home/david/dev/pygeoinf/pygeoinf2/probability/gaussian.py:2178-2205, :2251-2272, :2311-2317; base.py:740-755 documents the factor route as 'three transforms for the same numbers').
- Sum of two invariant measures with any zero spectral variance (band-limited priors) loses its covariance factor and precision entirely because _diagonal_inverse requires values > 0, so sampling becomes two draws added; v1 kept a single KL draw and an inverse covariance where possible (/home/david/dev/pygeoinf/pygeoinf2/probability/gaussian.py:2125-2148, :2263).
- CorrelatedInvariantGaussianMeasure.marginal -> GaussianMeasure.marginal: the marginal carries no precision and no KL sampler (v1's InvariantGaussianMeasure had both), so log_density is unavailable and a draw costs three transforms (/home/david/dev/pygeoinf/pygeoinf2/probability/gaussian.py:1917-1922).
- PeriodicBox.degree_transfer_operator builds a Python dict of dim (wavevector, phase) -> position entries via _component_index() on BOTH spaces on every call (/home/david/dev/pygeoinf/pygeoinf2/symmetric_space/fourier.py:741-782); O(dim) Python per call and not cached, unlike the sphere's cached _packing-based version at sphere.py:1894-1934. Mild.
- SymmetricHilbertSpace.estimate_truncation_degree on Sobolev spaces: v2 measures L2 power (bare symbol) where v1 measured metric-weighted (H^s) power, so the returned degree can differ on Sobolev spaces (/home/david/dev/pygeoinf/pygeoinf2/symmetric_space/base.py:501-504 vs v1 :2036-2039, :3055-3059). Semantic, not a cost change.

### sphere

- Sobolev.point_evaluation_operator(parallel=True, n_jobs=) -> SymmetricSpace.point_evaluation_operator: joblib parallelism over forward/adjoint chunks lost; only NUFFT nthreads (default 1) remains, and the direct basis_matrix route is single-threaded (pygeoinf2/symmetric_space/base.py:1582-1651, sphere.py:1009-1017, 1069-1076)
- Sobolev.path_average_operator(parallel=True, n_jobs=) -> path_integral_operator/path_average_operator: quadrature precomputation and forward/adjoint chunk parallelism lost (base.py:2256-2313)
- Sobolev.path_average_operator(lazy_quadrature=True) -> none: bounded-memory mode for very large path sets lost; nodes and CSR W always materialised at construction (base.py:2265-2290)
- Lebesgue.invariant_covariance_function -> Sphere.covariance_function: refuses on any space of order <= 1 (ValueError via _require_point_evaluation with no unsafe override), so the sparse-covariance construction v1 supported on a Lebesgue space needs a Sobolev space in v2 (sphere.py:1186, base.py:1464-1501)
- Sphere.covariance_function requires the spectrum packaged as an invariant GaussianMeasure on exactly this space (DiagonalLinearOperator covariance, domain == self); the array-in/callable-out form of v1 is gone, and a non-isotropic spectrum drops to the O(dim)-per-distance basis-matrix route (pygeoinf2/symmetric_space/sphere.py:1174-1184; base.py:1076-1090)
- Lebesgue.from_covariance / from_heat_kernel_prior / from_sobolev_kernel_prior (and Sobolev variants) -> SymmetricSpace.estimate_truncation_degree: cannot search beyond the lmax of an existing space (bincount over self.degrees, capped at per_degree.size-1), where v1 iterated upward to convergence (base.py:478-514 vs v1 symmetric_space.py:2027-2055)
- Lebesgue.to_coefficient_operator(lmax > self.lmax) -> coefficient_operator: zero-padding to a larger lmax lost, ValueError instead (base.py:382-392)
- Sobolev.path_average_operator order guard -> _path_operator: the safe/order refusal is bypassed (unsafe=True) so a Lebesgue path operator is built silently (base.py:2309-2311)
- Sphere.from_coefficients silently assumes 'ortho'/csphase=1 for any SHCoeffs passed in (reads `.coeffs` raw), where v1's `ulm.expand()` honoured the object's own normalization; pyshtools' default is '4pi', so models loaded with SHCoeffs.from_file synthesise wrong (off by sqrt(4 pi), verified numerically) in v2 with no error (pygeoinf2/symmetric_space/sphere.py:654 vs pygeoinf/symmetric_space/sphere.py:316-319)
- path_integral_operator/path_average_operator with count=None on a Lebesgue sphere: node count is 2*arc/length_scale with length_scale silently 1.0, so on a radius-6371 sphere each path gets O(10^4) nodes (a (nodes x 2) prepared array plus CSR W of the same size, and a NUFFT/basis_matrix over all of them per application), and on a unit sphere at most 7 nodes whatever lmax; v1 had no path operator on Lebesgue and used the Sobolev scale (pygeoinf2/symmetric_space/base.py:2143-2146; sphere.py:157-166, 2011-2025; v1 symmetric_space.py:2595-2607, 2632-2655)
- Lebesgue inner_product/squared_norm on grid-level fields (products, sqrt, domain_mask, from_grid_values) now differ from the component route by the documented 0.05-2%, so `squared_norm(x) != sum(to_components(x)**2)` off the span; v1 always used components (pygeoinf2/symmetric_space/sphere.py:404-465; v1 hilbert_space.py:618-621)
- Sphere.grid_values (pygeoinf2/symmetric_space/sphere.py:338-356) returns any bare ndarray unchanged with no shape check; only to_components (sphere.py:481-483) and _own_grid_values (sphere.py:386-387) check grid_shape, so a wrong-shaped array passes through the inner-product-by-quadrature path until a transform is hit. Confirms the is_element loss is not compensated by shape validation at the boundary.
- The v2 grid never carries the south-pole row: tests/test_sphere_transform.py:67-79 pin that the pole row has zero quadrature weight and the pole value is reconstructed internally by _south_pole_kernel (sphere.py:827-934) for the NUFFT doubling only. So there is no route to a user-visible extended (pole-inclusive, 360-degree-column) grid; the v1 extend=True default is not reproducible without a user-side pyshtools expand(extend=True) round trip.
- n_jobs survives on the sphere only indirectly: SymmetricSpace.pointwise_variance_at(measure, points, rank=, samples=, rng=, n_jobs=) (base.py:1145-1240) and SymmetricSpace.apply_block (base.py:2540, 'accepted for the protocol and unused'). Neither restores parallelism inside point_evaluation_operator or the path operators.
