- Sphere._embedding: builds the (n,3) embedding with a Python loop of _to_vector per point, where v1 pairs_within_distance vectorised the conversion (sphere.py:1830 vs v1 sphere.py:661-693) - minor
- IMPROVED: Sobolev.point_evaluation_operator default -> matrix-free by default (v1 default matrix_free=False formed the operator through the base machinery); NUFFT route O(dim log dim + n) for >= 200 points and dim >= 256 (sphere.py:981-1092)
- IMPROVED: spherical_cap_integral -> cap_integral_components: closed-form Legendre integral batched over centres instead of SHCoeffs.from_cap + rotation per centre (sphere.py:1539-1611)
- IMPROVED: Lebesgue inner_product/squared_norm -> grid quadrature with no transforms (sphere.py:404-465); see the semantic caveat above for off-span fields
- IMPROVED: geodesic_quadrature / geodesic_ball_quadrature -> vectorised slerp/ring construction and lru-cached Gauss-Legendre nodes (sphere.py:1388-1500, base.py:2688-2699)
- IMPROVED: _ylm_index_maps -> module-level lru_cache shared across instances of the same lmax (sphere.py:87-122)
- IMPROVED: pairs_within_distance now on the base for every geometry (base.py:1262-1322)
- IMPROVED: degree_transfer_operator adjoint derived with the target metric (sphere.py:1926-1934)
- IMPROVED: plotting.plot pcolormesh rolled to the dateline with explicit cell edges; plot_paths as one LineCollection (plotting/sphere.py:223-291, 405-472)

### fourier_spaces

- IMPROVED: circle/line.Sobolev.point_evaluation_operator -> SymmetricSpace.point_evaluation_operator: v1 was dense-only on circle/line (base-class matrix from laplacian_eigenvectors_at_point); v2 is matrix-free via finufft type-2/type-1 on every box in 1-3 D (base.py:1582-1651, fourier.py:455-561).
- IMPROVED: torus/plane.Sobolev.point_evaluation_operator(matrix_free=False default) -> point_evaluation_operator(dense=False default): matrix-free by default, dense only on request (base.py:1582-1651).
- IMPROVED: torus/plane.Sobolev.path_average_operator (dense from_linear_forms default) -> path_integral_operator/path_average_operator: always W E with sparse CSR weights and NUFFT evaluation by default (base.py:2256-2313).
- IMPROVED: torus.finufft hard import -> lazy optional import with direct-sum fallback (fourier.py:388-394).
- IMPROVED: torus.Lebesgue._build_index_map (Python loop over dim at construction) -> _FourierPacking vectorised (fourier.py:38-104).
- IMPROVED: torus.Lebesgue.degree_transfer_operator construction O(dim_src*dim_tgt) np.where loop -> O(dim_src+dim_tgt) label dicts (fourier.py:746-799).
- IMPROVED: torus/plane invariant_covariance_function (NotImplementedError) -> covariance_function closed form (base.py:1092-1141).
- IMPROVED: geodesic_quadrature leggauss per call -> lru_cached _gauss_legendre (base.py:2688-2699).
- NOT AN IMPROVEMENT OVER v1 (corrects the earlier 'IMPROVED: _points_to_angle_arrays per application -> prepare_points once per operator' claim): v1 already converted the points once per operator (plane.py:629, torus.py:1101, outside the closures) with a vectorised _points_to_angle_arrays (plane.py:379-386). v2's Box.prepare_points is a per-point Python loop calling _to_enclosing (box.py:187) plus a second per-point loop in PeriodicBox.prepare_points (fourier.py:441-443): 0.168 s vs 0.001 s vectorised for 1e5 points. The REVIEW2 4.2.7 saving is relative to an earlier v2. Construction-time regression relative to v1 on Box (line/plane); application cost unchanged.
- path_integral_operator / path_average_operator / geodesic_ball_average_operator with dense=True: `sparse @ self.basis_matrix(nodes)` (base.py:2296-2301) materialises a (total_quadrature_nodes x dim) dense array via np.stack of basis_at rows (base.py:1548-1554) before reducing to (n_paths x dim). v1's dense route (SymmetricSobolevSpace.path_average_operator via geodesic_integral, symmetric_space.py:2596-2613, 2632-2660) accumulated weight*eigenvector into one dim-vector per path and never held more than (n_paths x dim). Peak memory is larger by the nodes-per-path factor (default max(2, ceil(2*arc/length_scale))).
- torus.Lebesgue.zero (np.zeros property) -> CoordinateSpace.zero() method: one irfftn per call instead of an allocation (algebra/spaces.py:640-642).
- circle.Lebesgue.degree_transfer_operator (vectorised rfft slice, no per-component Python) -> PeriodicBox.degree_transfer_operator: builds a Python dict of size dim for each space at construction (fourier.py:746-752, 780-782); application remains O(dim).
- circle.Lebesgue.invariant_covariance_function (Chebyshev series, O(kmax) per distance, no dim-length vectors) -> covariance_function: basis_matrix(points) forms an (n_distances x dim) dense array per call (base.py:1139-1141); on a torus dim = n0*n1 per distance.
- *.from_covariance / from_sobolev_parameters (scalar loop, no space built) -> estimate_truncation_degree on an over-sized space: requires constructing the large space first (packing + eigenvalues + metric, O(dim)) and cannot grow beyond it (base.py:478-514).
- torus/plane.Sobolev.path_average_operator(lazy_quadrature=True) memory escape hatch -> removed; all pooled nodes are held as a list of ndarrays plus the CSR (base.py:2256-2313). DESIGN.md 20.8 records 'replaced'.
- torus/plane.Sobolev.path_average_operator matrix-free branch checked order > d/2 -> _path_operator passes unsafe=True, so no order check on the path operators (base.py:2307-2312).

### plot

- plot_corner_distributions(parallel=, n_jobs=) -> plot_corner: the dense n x n covariance is still formed (moments -> as_multivariate_normal -> covariance.matrix(form='galerkin') + 2n solve_gram, pygeoinf2/probability/gaussian.py:1738-1751) but the parallel option is gone: LinearOperator.matrix() accepts n_jobs (pygeoinf2/algebra/operators.py:686) and as_multivariate_normal does not pass it (gaussian.py:1743-1745), so plot_corner has no way to parallelise the n covariance applications v1 could (v1 plot.py:1835-1847).
- plot_1d_distributions stat extraction -> moments(): a single component's variance is still obtained by forming the WHOLE dense covariance (distributions.py:87-89), as in v1 (plot.py:106); no matrix-free e_i^T G^-1 C_gal G^-1 e_i path was added even though only covariance[index,index] is read (:405). Not worse than v1, but a missed matrix-free opportunity noted as review C3 (review/geometry_plotting.md:199).
- as_multivariate_normal costs more than v1's dense read, not less: v1 formed the component matrix with n covariance applications (pygeoinf/linear_operators.py:848-857); v2 forms the Galerkin matrix with n applications and then does 2n solve_gram calls, one per column, twice (pygeoinf2/probability/gaussian.py:1738-1747), so plot_densities on an n-component measure to read one variance costs n applies + 2n Gram solves. Metric-correct, and trivial for the 1-D measures this is normally called on, but strictly more work than v1 when the index component is all that is read.
- plot_corner_distributions 2-D panels -> plot_corner: fixed 160 x 160 mesh (distributions.py:679-680) replaces v1's adaptive clamp(25*eval_span, 100, 500) per axis (plot.py:2015-2016); diagonal 500-point grid (:652) replaces clamp(50*eval_span, 200, 5000) (plot.py:1934). Fewer points (faster) but lower resolution on wide windows; no evaluation beyond the display window.
- moments() sampling route (new, no v1 counterpart): draws `samples`=20000 samples one at a time in a Python loop (distributions.py:99-101); when each sample is a solve (a conditioned or RTO posterior) this is 20000 solves with no warning or cap (review C3).
- SubspaceSlicePlotter exact paths (pulled-back quadratic slice, plot.py:1037-1124; halfspace-intersection polyhedral slice, plot.py:1438-1706) -> nothing: the exact O(k) inner-product slices of Ball/Ellipsoid/PolyhedralSet and the plotly 3-D backend are entirely absent from v2; the only way to see a set's cross-section would be hand-written oracle sampling.
- IMPROVED: plot_1d_distributions/plot_corner_distributions read covariance.matrix(dense=True) (the raw component matrix A_c, wrong on a non-orthonormal basis since the component covariance is A_c G^-1; linear_operators.py:848-857) -> v2 moments() reads as_multivariate_normal(), the metric-correct component covariance G^-1 C_gal G^-1 (gaussian.py:1729-1750; DESIGN.md §30.2).
- IMPROVED: plot_densities per-curve grid (_grid, distributions.py:126-156) resolves a posterior orders of magnitude narrower than its prior, which v1's single shared linspace capped at 10000 points could miss (plot.py:136-149).
- IMPROVED: both v2 plotters accept any measure with can_sample (push-forward through a non-linear map, RTO posteriors) and draw it by binned KDE (histogram + one convolution, distributions.py:181-270), ~2000x faster than scipy gaussian_kde, which is also offered as density='kde'; v1 refused non-Gaussian input (plot.py:1829-1833).
- IMPROVED: plot_corner accepts axes= to draw into an existing N x N grid (distributions.py:527, :623-627); v1 always made its own figure (plot.py:1904-1910).

### checks

- check_traits (new, no v1 counterpart) -> testing.check_traits INVERTIBLE branch: forms the full dense matrix via operator.matrix(form='components') and computes np.linalg.matrix_rank on it, O(dim^2) memory and O(dim^3) time, whenever an operator claims Traits.INVERTIBLE on CoordinateSpaces (pygeoinf2/testing.py:553-561); matrix_rank is computed once on the success path and a second time inside the failure message (:557,:560). review/r2_algebra_solvers.md:30 (A Consider-19) records this as only 'partial' — the dense rank test was never replaced by a matrix-free probe. v1 had no such check, so this is new dense work rather than a regression of a v1 path, but it makes check_traits unusable on large invertible operators.
- HilbertSpaceAxiomChecks._check_riesz_representation (dormant) -> check_coordinates: forms the dense Gram matrix via space.gram_matrix() and runs np.linalg.eigvalsh on it, O(dim^3) (pygeoinf2/testing.py:248-260), where v1's space-level check was matrix-free (but the Riesz check itself never ran). check_coordinates is CoordinateSpace-only and should not be run on large spaces.
- IMPROVED: NonLinearOperatorAxiomChecks._check_derivative_finite_difference -> check_derivative: central differences with step 1e-6 (O(h^2) truncation) replace forward differences with h=1e-7, at the same two operator evaluations per direction, and the 1e-4 relative-tolerance floor is removed (pygeoinf2/testing.py:605-614 vs pygeoinf/checks/nonlinear_operators.py:264-280).
- IMPROVED: HilbertSpaceAxiomChecks._check_basis_and_expectation -> check_coordinates basis loop: checks min(dim, 4) basis vectors instead of all dim, O(dim) instead of O(dim^2) allocations (pygeoinf2/testing.py:296-301 vs pygeoinf/checks/hilbert_space.py:157-165).
- IMPROVED: HilbertSpaceAxiomChecks comparison scheme -> _assert_close: comparisons are made in the space's own norm (metric-aware) instead of on component arrays, and sample_expectation/mean is checked without going through components, so check_space now works on non-coordinate (e.g. PETSc/MFEM-backed) spaces (pygeoinf2/testing.py:45-58,210-216; DESIGN.md:2090-2091).
- IMPROVED: all checks take a numpy Generator (`rng=`) so failures are reproducible; v1 used the global RNG with no seed argument (pygeoinf2/testing.py:88,431,591).
- IMPROVED: LinearOperatorAxiomChecks.check -> check_operator: adds adjoint domain/codomain, memoisation and involution-by-identity checks (pygeoinf2/testing.py:446-455) and check_traits verifies claimed traits (:467-561); check_white_noise (:344-402) catches the v1 white-noise covariance bug on mass-weighted spaces; check_gradient (:621-671) catches the derivative-vs-gradient trap; check_measure and check_projection are new.
- REGRESSION (lost fast path of a different kind): LinearOperatorAxiomChecks.check / NonLinearOperatorAxiomChecks.check `measure` / `domain_measure` / `codomain_measure` -> check_operator / check_derivative: there is no way to draw test vectors from a smooth GaussianMeasure; every check uses space.random (pygeoinf2/testing.py:435,458,602). REVIEW.md:74 (item 8), review/r2_packaging_tests_docs.md:43 (U 8) and REVIEW2.md:135 record this as an open regression blocking pyslfp's adjoint tests, which need heat-kernel-smooth fields.
- DESIGN-vs-implementation gap (not a dense regression): DESIGN.md:1170-1172 specifies check_space(space, rng, n=10) and check_operator(op, rng) covering 'derivative by finite differences'; the implementation ships trials=5 and a check_operator with no derivative call (pygeoinf2/testing.py:69-74, 410-464). The implementation is narrower than the DESIGN-recorded contract; the 'inherited_nonlinear_checks: subsumed (user must opt in)' row is therefore an unrecorded deviation, not a decision.
- REGRESSION (coverage, not cost): the v2 copy check is vacuous against an aliasing copy and the in-place checks test return values only, so a space whose copy returns its argument, or whose axpy/scale_inplace do not mutate, passes check_space where v1's .check() failed (pygeoinf2/testing.py:182-197; scratchpad/probe.py, probe2.py). compat.py:150-152 and testing.py:196 still depend on mutation.

### data_assimilation

- get_independent_gaussian_pdf -> GaussianMeasure.from_standard_deviations(...).as_multivariate_normal(): v1's diagonal product-of-1-D-Gaussians fast path is replaced by a full dense component covariance handed to scipy multivariate_normal (pygeoinf2/probability/gaussian.py:1717-1740); negligible at teaching sizes but the fast path is gone.
- LinearKalmanFilter._update -> LinearGaussianInversion.__call__ / GaussianMeasure.condition: v1 fell back to np.linalg.pinv(S) with a warning when the innovation covariance was singular (v1 core.py:~900); v2 has no pinv/LinAlgError fallback anywhere in inference/ or numerics/solvers.py (LinAlgError appears only in numerics/root_find.py:56,124 for Newton breakdown and probability/gaussian.py:74 for the Cholesky-then-eigh fallback), so a singular S is a hard failure.
- plot_gaussian_ellipsoid -> plot_corner: v1 drew one Ellipse patch from a 2x2 eigendecomposition; v2 evaluates a 160x160 Mahalanobis field with np.linalg.inv of the 2x2 block and contours it (pygeoinf2/plotting/distributions.py:672-690). Trivial cost, but it is dense grid evaluation where v1 was closed-form.
- IMPROVED: LinearKalmanFilter._update/_predict -> LinearGaussianInversion / GaussianMeasure.condition / GaussianMeasure.push_forward: the Kalman update and the covariance propagation F C F* are matrix-free operator compositions with a pluggable solver and a choice of data-space or model-space formalism (pygeoinf2/inference/gaussian.py:4-16, probability/gaussian.py:1753-1846, :2150-2172), where v1 formed dense (I-KH)P and F P F^T with np.linalg on ndarrays.
- IMPROVED: solve_ensemble (serial Python loop, prints to stdout) -> ProbabilityMeasure.samples(n, rng=, n_jobs=) draws in parallel with per-draw spawned generators and no printing (pygeoinf2/probability/base.py:76-115) — though this samples a measure rather than integrating dynamics, so it is not a like-for-like replacement.
- IMPROVED: package import no longer pulls in matplotlib.pyplot (v1 core.py:14 imported it at module level; v2 imports it lazily inside plotting functions, distributions.py:590).
- OBSERVATION (not a regression): pygeoinf2/inference/problem.py:189-193 chi_squared_from_residual subtracts measure.expectation from the residual and adds it straight back before calling mahalanobis_squared — a no-op round trip costing two extra data-space vector ops per call. Harmless for correctness.
- GaussianLikelihood singular R: v1 core.py:523 raised ValueError at construction; v2 from_covariance_matrix (probability/gaussian.py:60-100, :540-560) accepts a singular PSD R with precision=None, so the error surfaces later (when precision/log_density/chi_squared is asked for) and with a different message. Semantic difference, not a performance regression.

Not a like-for-like port: the class, its properties (observed_data, direction), set_direction, value_and_subgradient and the finite-difference fallback are gone; what exists is a differently-shaped, stateful oracle inside DualFeasibleProperty. |
| `backus_gilbert.BackusInference` | subsumed | V1_CATALOGUE.md:265 `BackusInference \| Ported \| M5 stages 5.7 and 5.9, with four routes (§18.3)`. The name now denotes only route (a), error-free; the `method=` selector the catalogue and DESIGN §18.8 imply was never built (REVIEW.md:223,251). The v1 class's noisy chi-squared semantics are reachable only through the differently named FeasibleProperty/DualFeasibleProperty, the former with a different hardening (ambient ball rather than chi-squared ellipsoid). |
| `backus_gilbert.BackusInference.test_data_compatibility` | ported_changed | V1_CATALOGUE.md:268 `test_data_compatibility \| Ported \| is_feasible(data) on all three noisy routes`. Two of the three carriers are noisy (FeasibleProperty, DualFeasibleProperty); BackusInference's is the error-free route; the noisy route (b) BackusGilbert has none. None of v1's solver/preconditioner/damping/iteration options survive, FeasibleProperty's version forms a dense A A* where v1 was matrix-free, and DualFeasibleProperty's is a −1e6 heuristic — so 'Ported' overstates it. |

No Wood saddlepoint`. ## 9. Terminology changes

### hilbert_space

- Vector (module TypeVar) -> V (PEP 695 class type parameter, `HilbertSpace[V]`) (algebra/spaces.py:51)
- HilbertSpace.zero (property) -> zero() (method) (algebra/spaces.py:106-108)
- HilbertSpace.multiply(a, x) -> scale(a, x) (algebra/spaces.py:155); `multiply` now means pointwise product on HilbertModule (757)
- HilbertSpace.ax -> scale_inplace (algebra/spaces.py:122-124)
- HilbertSpace.sample_expectation -> mean (algebra/spaces.py:171)
- HilbertSpace.identity_operator() -> LinearOperator.identity(space) (algebra/operators.py:1108)
- HilbertSpace.zero_operator(codomain) -> LinearOperator.zero(domain, *, codomain=None) (algebra/operators.py:1115)
- HilbertSpace.check(n_checks=, measure=) -> testing.check_space(space, *, rng=, trials=, rebuild=) + check_coordinates/check_representer/check_white_noise (testing.py:69, 219, 304, 344)
- HilbertSpace.__eq__ (abstract) -> _key() (abstract) with concrete __eq__/__hash__ (algebra/spaces.py:76-85, 130-138)
- HilbertSpace.coordinate_inclusion / coordinate_projection (properties) -> CoordinateSpace.coordinate_inclusion() / coordinate_projection() (methods) (algebra/spaces.py:687-720)
- HilbertSpace.to_dual(x).components -> CoordinateSpace.apply_gram(to_components(x)) / LinearFunctional.derivative_components (algebra/spaces.py:356; algebra/operators.py:2165)
- HilbertSpace.from_dual(xp) -> CoordinateSpace.representer(g) / LinearFunctional.representer (algebra/spaces.py:722; algebra/operators.py:2142)
- LinearForm -> LinearFunctional (algebra/operators.py:2113)
- LinearForm(domain, mapping=...) -> LinearFunctional.from_callables(domain, value, *, representer=None, derivative_components=None) — exactly one reading required (algebra/operators.py:2178-2235)
- DualHilbertSpace.from_components(c) -> LinearFunctional.from_derivative_components(space, g) (algebra/operators.py:2242)
- DualHilbertSpace.from_dual(x) -> LinearFunctional.from_representer(space, x) (algebra/operators.py:2237)
- HilbertModuleMixin -> HilbertModule (algebra/spaces.py:733)
- HilbertModuleMixin.vector_multiply -> HilbertModule.multiply (algebra/spaces.py:757)
- HilbertModuleMixin.vector_sqrt -> HilbertModule.sqrt (algebra/spaces.py:761)
- new: HilbertModule.multiplication_operator(f) (algebra/spaces.py:765-777); SymmetricSpace overrides it to lift the L2 operator through its metric
- OrthogonalHilbertSpace(dim, metric_values) -> DiagonalMetricSpace(metric_values) (algebra/spaces.py:953-968)
- OrthogonalHilbertSpace.metric / inverse_metric -> apply_gram / solve_gram (actions) (algebra/spaces.py:995-1001)
- OrthonormalHilbertSpace(dim) -> OrthonormalSpace (no constructor) (algebra/spaces.py:1119)
- EuclideanSpace.subspace_projection(indices) -> no name; v2 inlines restrict/extend closures at the call site (inference/preconditioners.py:255-268)
- HilbertSpace.basis_vector(i): v1 accepted negative indices with NumPy wrap-around (c[-1] = 1 gives the last basis vector); v2 CoordinateSpace.basis_vector raises IndexError for i < 0 (algebra/spaces.py:658-659)
- MassWeightedHilbertSpace(underlying_space, mass_operator, inverse_mass_operator) -> MassWeightedSpace(base, mass, /, *, mass_solver=None) (algebra/spaces.py:829-836)
- MassWeightedHilbertSpace.underlying_space -> MassWeightedSpace.base (algebra/spaces.py:876)
- MassWeightedHilbertSpace.mass_operator -> MassWeightedSpace.mass (algebra/spaces.py:881)
- MassWeightedHilbertSpace.inverse_mass_operator -> MassWeightedSpace.mass_inverse (algebra/spaces.py:886)
- HilbertSpace.random() -> random(*, rng=None) (algebra/spaces.py:274)
- is_element (membership checks) -> require_coordinates(*spaces) (algebra/operators.py:189-210) and require_module(*spaces) (algebra/spaces.py:780-799), guards on capability rather than membership
- internal: _relating_mass(target, base) (algebra/operators.py:95-160) is the route by which from_formal_adjoint reads M and M^{-1} off a MassWeightedSpace, a DirectSum of them, or two CoordinateSpaces sharing a component map
- new: HilbertSpace.white_noise, orthonormal_basis, shares_vectors_with; CoordinateSpace.apply_gram, solve_gram, gram_matrix, gram_diagonal, has_diagonal_metric, uses_component_fast_paths, components_of, vectors_from, representer; ArrayVectorMixin; Reals; ComponentView; require_module (algebra/spaces.py)

### operators

- Scalar multiplication is order-dependent for numpy scalars: np.int64(2) * h yields _ScaledSupport (numpy object arithmetic unboxes the scalar to a Python int and calls h.__rmul__(2)), but h * np.int64(2) yields a generic _FunctionalScaled because SupportFunction.__mul__ (numerics/convex.py:299) tests isinstance(alpha, (int, float)) while Operator.__mul__ (algebra/operators.py:366) accepts np.floating/np.integer too. The claim that numpy-integer scalars always give _FunctionalScaled holds only for right-multiplication.

- EllipsoidSupportFunction(primal_domain, center, radius, shape_operator, inverse_operator, inverse_sqrt_operator) -> Ellipsoid(domain, precision, /, *, centre, covariance).support_function() / _EllipsoidSupport(domain, covariance, centre) (geometry/convex.py:833, :1029); shape_operator -> precision; inverse_operator -> covariance; radius and inverse_sqrt_operator removed
- HalfSpaceSupportFunction.normal_vector -> HalfSpace.normal (geometry/convex.py:761) [set, not support function]
- CallableSupportFunction(primal_domain, fn, support_point_fn) -> _OracleSupport(domain, oracle, /) + _OracleSet.maximiser (geometry/convex.py:326, :235); support_point_fn -> maximiser
- PointSupportFunction -> _PointSupport (numerics/convex.py:357)
- LinearImageSupportFunction -> _ImageSupport (numerics/convex.py:409)
- MinkowskiSumSupportFunction(left, right) -> _MinkowskiSupport(parts: tuple) (numerics/convex.py:371); left/right -> parts
- ScaledSupportFunction -> _ScaledSupport (numerics/convex.py:394)
- NonLinearForm -> Functional (algebra/operators.py:1848)
- has_gradient -> has_derivative (algebra/operators.py:271; note it is True for every SupportFunction)
- HilbertSpace.multiply(alpha, x) -> HilbertSpace.scale(alpha, x) (algebra/spaces.py:155; v2 multiply is a pointwise vector product, spaces.py:758)
- HilbertSpace.zero (attribute) -> HilbertSpace.zero() (method, algebra/spaces.py:107)

- DESIGN.md §11.8 (line 1730) records 'compose_with had its domains backwards' as a bug in v2's own early implementation found by v2's tests; the V1_CATALOGUE.md:199 row attributes that defect to v1 ('v1's domain/codomain were the wrong way round (§9)'). v1 LinearImageSupportFunction (convex_analysis.py:733-745) has the same, correct orientation as v2 _ImageSupport; DESIGN.md §9 has no such entry, and §11.8 describes v2.

- The 'inner bound' vocabulary moved: v1's feasible_lower_bound -> v2's DualFeasibleProperty/FeasibleProperty.inner_hull returning Polytope(..., outer=False) (inference/backus.py:905-955), built from admissibility tests rather than from parts' support maximisers.

- Ball.radius and BallSurface.radius properties survive unchanged (convex.py:609-612, 1079-1082); the classification has no per-member row for them

- Ellipsoid inverse_operator= -> covariance= (convex.py:840); inverse_sqrt_operator= removed
- Ellipsoid/EllipsoidSurface radius (ctor arg and property) removed — folded into the precision (level fixed at 1); radius 0 no longer expressible
- Ball(domain, center, radius, open_set=True) -> Ball(domain, /, *, radius=1.0, centre=None) (convex.py:564-571)
- Sphere(domain, center, radius) -> BallSurface(domain, /, *, radius=1.0, centre=None) (convex.py:1064-1066)
- HyperPlane(domain, normal_vector, offset) / HalfSpace(domain, normal_vector, offset, inequality_type) -> Hyperplane/HalfSpace(domain, normal, /, *, offset=0.0) (convex.py:684-686,744-746)

- open_set / is_open / is_closed / closure: removed (all v2 convex sets closed)
- Ellipsoid.normalized / EllipsoidSurface.normalized: removed (always normalised)

## 10. Added in v2 (no v1 counterpart)

### algebra

| v2 | kind | what it does | nearest v1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `traits.Traits` | class (enum.Flag) | A flag enum of mathematical claims about a linear operator (SELF_ADJOINT, POSITIVE_SEMIDEFINITE, POSITIVE_DEFINITE, INVERTIBLE, ISOMETRY, UNITARY, IDEMPOTENT) carried by every LinearOperator and used for dispatch. Verified: v1 has no trait or flag of any kind; LinearOperator.self_adjoint / self_adjoint_from_matrix only wire the adjoint mapping to the forward one (linear_operators.py:123-128, 441-481) and nothing downstream can ask an operator whether it is self-adjoint. | none (closest: LinearOperator.self_adjoint / self_adjoint_from_matrix constructors, which carry no flag) |
| `traits.close` | function | Closes a trait set under implication rules (POSITIVE_DEFINITE => SEMIDEFINITE\|INVERTIBLE\|SELF_ADJOINT; IDEMPOTENT&SELF_ADJOINT => PSD; ISOMETRY&INVERTIBLE => UNITARY, etc.) to a fixed point, so no inconsistent set is representable. | none |
| `traits.sum_traits / scale_traits / adjoint_traits / compose_traits / inverse_traits` | functions | Propagation rules giving the traits of A+B, alpha*A, A*, A@B and A^-1 from the operands' traits (sign of alpha matters for definiteness; adjoint drops bare ISOMETRY; composition keeps only isometry/unitary/invertible; inverse drops bare PSD). | none |
| `traits.congruence_traits / gramian_traits` | functions | The trait halves of the palindrome rules: S A S* preserves self-adjointness/semidefiniteness of A (definiteness only if S invertible), and L L* is always PSD (PD if L is full rank). Consumed by nodes._Composition._palindrome_traits. | none |
| `algebra.spaces.HilbertSpace (coordinate-free base) + ArrayVectorMixin` | class / architecture | The abstract core is now dim, _key, zero(), copy, inner_product, axpy, scale_inplace; to_components/from_components/to_dual/from_dual are no longer required, so a PETSc/MFEM-backed space implements HilbertSpace alone. axpy/scale_inplace return their result (in-place contract for immutable vector types such as Reals). Coordinates move to the optional CoordinateSpace capability; ArrayVectorMixin supplies the NumPy defaults v1 had as base-class fallbacks (x.copy(), y += a*x). | hilbert_space.HilbertSpace (to_dual/from_dual/to_components/from_components all abstract, hilbert_space.py:72-138; array defaults at 216-242) |
| `algebra.spaces.HilbertSpace.__eq__/__hash__/_key` | behaviour | Spaces are structurally hashable via a subclass-supplied _key; equality is by type and key. Verified: v1 defines __eq__ abstractly without __hash__, so every v1 space is unhashable (TypeError: unhashable type) and cannot key a dict or set. | HilbertSpace.__eq__ (abstract, per-class; hilbert_space.py:130-138) |
| `algebra.spaces.HilbertSpace.shares_vectors_with` | method | Declares that two spaces hold the same vectors and differ only in inner product, so transfers between them (in from_formal_adjoint) are no-ops rather than round trips through components. Overridden by MassWeightedSpace and DirectSum. | none (v1 from_formal_adjoint hard-codes the MassWeighted/DirectSum cases via isinstance, linear_operators.py:159-183) |
| `algebra.spaces.HilbertSpace.orthonormal_basis + reorthogonalising gram_schmidt` | method + algorithm change | Rank-revealing Gram-Schmidt that drops numerically dependent vectors (relative rtol) instead of raising. Both it and gram_schmidt use a 'twice is enough' (DGKS 1/sqrt2) second pass and a relative dependence threshold; CoordinateSpace runs them on (dim,k) component arrays with the metric entering only through apply_gram, and _orthonormalise_columns(against=) can project off an already-orthonormal block for incremental range finding. v1's range finder achieved the 'drop dependent' behaviour only by catching gram_schmidt's ValueError at the call site (low_rank.py:596-600) and the twice-is-enough pass existed only inside Lanczos. | HilbertSpace.gram_schmidt (single-pass MGS, absolute 1e-12 threshold, raises on dependence; hilbert_space.py:353-382); twice-is-enough only in functional_calculus.iter_lanczos_tridiagonalize (functional_calculus.py:460-475) |
| `algebra.spaces.HilbertSpace.white_noise / CoordinateSpace.white_noise_components` | methods (and a correctness fix) | A draw whose covariance is the identity in the space's own inner product: components are N(0, G^-1) via a cached Cholesky factor of the Gram matrix (a divide on DiagonalMetricSpace, standard normal on OrthonormalSpace, blockwise on DirectSum). This is not merely v1's white_noise_measure relocated: verified empirically that v1's white_noise_measure(domain) = from_standard_deviation(domain, 1.0) samples through _sample_from_factor, which draws domain.random() = from_components(randn) and applies the identity factor, so on a space with metric diag(1,4,9) the component variances come out (1,1,1) instead of (1,0.25,0.11) -- covariance G, not I -- while the measure's covariance operator claims the identity. v2's method is the correct draw; random() is documented as not white noise. | low_rank.white_noise_measure(domain) / GaussianMeasure.from_standard_deviation(domain, 1.0).sample() (low_rank.py:34-47, gaussian_measure.py:144-170, 1786-1793) -- a measure whose sampler is metric-incorrect on non-orthonormal spaces |
| `algebra.spaces.HilbertSpace.random(rng=) / white_noise(rng=) / spaces.default_rng` | keyword | random() and white_noise() accept a numpy Generator for reproducible draws; a module-level default_rng is used otherwise. v1 HilbertSpace.random used the global np.random.randn (the only rng= keywords in v1 are on Monte-Carlo routines in quadratic_form_quantile and gaussian_measure, not on spaces). | HilbertSpace.random() (no rng; hilbert_space.py:244-253) |
| `algebra.spaces.CoordinateSpace Gram interface (apply_gram, solve_gram, gram_matrix, gram_diagonal, apply_gram_to_columns, solve_gram_to_columns, has_diagonal_metric)` | methods/properties | The metric is expressed as the action of G and G^-1 directly on component arrays, plus column-batched variants for (dim,k) arrays, gram_matrix()/gram_diagonal() for spaces that hold their metric, and has_diagonal_metric, which DiagonalLinearOperator consults to decide self-adjointness. What is genuinely new is the batched column API, gram_diagonal/gram_matrix and has_diagonal_metric; a general (non-diagonal) Gram matrix was already supported in v1 through to_dual/from_dual on any HilbertSpace (LinearForm.components == G c, from_dual == G^-1) and MassWeightedHilbertSpace.to_dual, so 'general Gram supported by default' is not itself new. | HilbertSpace.to_dual/from_dual (hilbert_space.py:78-104, general), MassWeightedHilbertSpace.to_dual/from_dual (808-826), OrthogonalHilbertSpace.metric/inverse_metric (sparse diagonal only, 596-604) |
| `algebra.spaces.CoordinateSpace.components_of / vectors_from / uses_component_fast_paths / squared_norm (one conversion)` | methods/property + fast path | Batch conversion of many vectors to one (dim,k) array and back, an opt-out flag for spaces whose coordinate map is too expensive, and a squared_norm that converts once instead of twice; used so Gram-Schmidt, Lanczos and low-rank adjoints pay O(k) transforms instead of O(k^2) inner products on any coordinate space. v1 had the idea only as the scipy-LinearOperator wrapper matrix(dense=False).matmat and low_rank's Path B component fallback, which was taken only when the codomain is orthonormal and otherwise fell back to abstract inner products. | LinearOperator.matrix(dense=False).matmat (linear_operators.py:629-657) and low_rank.random_range Path B (low_rank.py:590-629, orthonormal codomain only) |
| `algebra.spaces.HilbertModule.multiplication_operator / require_module` | method + function | Pointwise multiplication by a field as a LinearOperator on any HilbertModule with no self-adjointness claimed (it holds only in L2; v1's version used LinearOperator.self_adjoint even on a Sobolev MassWeightedHilbertModule, which is a wrong adjoint there), plus a checker raising TypeError by name when a space is not a module. | AbstractSymmetricLebesgueSpace.spatial_multiplication_operator (symmetric spaces only, claims self-adjointness; symmetric_space.py:2344-2353); MassWeightedHilbertModule's isinstance check (hilbert_space.py:911-912) |
| `algebra.spaces.MassWeightedSpace(mass_solver=) / mass_inverse` | keyword + property | The inverse mass operator is no longer a required constructor argument: it is derived lazily from a LinearSolver (CG by default) or an explicit inverse operator. The constructor also validates that the mass operator is an endomorphism of the base claiming SELF_ADJOINT\|POSITIVE_DEFINITE. Works over a coordinate-free base. | MassWeightedHilbertSpace(underlying_space, mass_operator, inverse_mass_operator) (inverse required, nothing checked; hilbert_space.py:758-773) |
| `algebra.spaces.ComponentView` | class | A CoordinateSpace whose vectors are another space's component arrays with that space's metric, so iterative solvers can run Krylov loops in array arithmetic with one conversion in and one out. Public class name but not in __all__/algebra.__init__; used by numerics.solvers. | LinearOperator.matrix(dense=False) (a scipy LinearOperator wrapper over components used to run scipy solvers; linear_operators.py:600-665) |
| `algebra.spaces.Reals` | class | The real line as a one-dimensional OrthonormalSpace whose vectors are plain floats, so that a functional is an Operator into Reals and evaluates to a number rather than a length-1 array. | EuclideanSpace(1) (used as the codomain in from_linear_form / as_linear_operator; linear_operators.py:253-291, linear_forms.py:110-126) |
| `algebra.operators.Functional / LinearFunctional as Operator / LinearOperator subclasses` | architecture | Scalar-valued maps are now operators into Reals rather than a parallel form hierarchy: a Functional has the full Operator algebra and can be a block in a Column/Block operator, and a LinearFunctional has an adjoint (gradient == adjoint(1.0)), traits, matrix(), and stays a LinearFunctional under +, *, @ via the node subclasses. v1's NonLinearForm was not a NonLinearOperator and LinearForm was a components-array dual vector; the bridge was LinearForm.as_linear_operator / LinearOperator.from_linear_form(s) into EuclideanSpace(1) or R^n. | LinearForm.as_linear_operator, LinearForm.from_linear_operator, LinearOperator.from_linear_form / from_linear_forms (linear_forms.py:88-126, linear_operators.py:222-291) |
| `algebra.linearisation.Linearisation` | class (result type) | Frozen record of (point, value, derivative) returned by Operator.at(x), with as_affine() giving the tangent affine map. Lets a backend compute value and Jacobian in one call. | none (v1 NonLinearOperator has separate __call__ and derivative(x); nonlinear_operators.py:84-105) |
| `algebra.linearisation.QuadraticModel` | class (result type) | Linearisation specialised to scalar-valued operators: stores derivative (a LinearFunctional) and optional Hessian; gradient is derived lazily as derivative.adjoint(1.0) so the metric enters exactly once. | none (NonLinearForm.gradient/hessian are separate calls with gradient as the stored primitive; nonlinear_forms.py:95-148) |
| `algebra.operators.Operator.at / second_derivative / has_second_derivative` | methods | at(x) returns a Linearisation (value+derivative together); second_derivative(x, dx) returns F''(x)[dx,.] as a LinearOperator, enabling exact Newton Hessians of composed functionals. Propagated through sums, scalings and compositions in nodes.py (differentiated chain rule). Grep of v1 for second_derivative finds nothing. | NonLinearOperator.derivative(x) only (nonlinear_operators.py:88-105); no second derivative anywhere |
| `algebra.operators.Operator.from_callables(linearise=, second_derivative=)` | keywords | A nonlinear operator can be built from a single callable that returns value and derivative together, and/or from a second-derivative callable. | NonLinearOperator(domain, codomain, mapping, derivative=) (nonlinear_operators.py:33-55) |
| `algebra.operators specialisation protocol (_combine_add/_combine_radd/_combine_compose/_combine_rcompose/_combine_scale)` | behaviour / extension protocol | Before building a generic expression node, +, * and @ ask both operands whether they can stay in their own class. This is how AffineOperator, DiagonalLinearOperator, _Identity and _Zero keep their structure without v1's string-based type check (type(other).__name__ == 'AffineOperator'). | Ad-hoc isinstance overrides in InvariantLinearAutomorphism.__add__/__matmul__ (symmetric_space.py:214-258) and AffineOperator.__add__/__matmul__ (affine_operators.py:75-174); the string check at linear_operators.py:918, 956, 998 |
| `algebra.operators.LinearOperator.traits / with_traits` | property + method | Every linear operator carries claimed Traits; with_traits returns a same-class shallow copy with extra claims (not a wrapper, so fast paths survive). SELF_ADJOINT on a non-endomorphism is rejected at construction. | none |
| `algebra.operators.LinearOperator.adjoint (memoised) / adjoints_are_linked / _link_adjoint` | behaviour + static method | adjoint is memoised so A.adjoint is A.adjoint, and adjoints_are_linked reads the memo without constructing anything. This identity link is what lets nodes._Composition recognise L@L.adjoint and S@C@S.adjoint as PSD after the fact, and _block_traits recognise a self-adjoint block grid. | LinearOperator.adjoint (built a fresh operator each call; adjoint_base only made adjoint.adjoint return the base; linear_operators.py:556-567) |
| `algebra.operators.LinearOperator.matrix(form='auto', by=) with _known_matrix through expression nodes` | keywords + behaviour | Genuinely new: form='auto' picks Galerkin when SELF_ADJOINT is claimed (trait-driven); by= makes the column-vs-row choice explicit; and the expression nodes (_Sum, _Scaled, _Adjoint, _Composition) answer _known_matrix by combining their parts, so (A + t I).matrix() or (B @ A).matrix() on matrix-backed A is a read rather than dim probes. Not new: the galerkin/components distinction, automatic transposition when the codomain is smaller, and stored-matrix reads on Matrix/Block operators all existed in v1 (linear_operators.py:831-861, 1105-1115; direct_sum.py:306-322). | LinearOperator.matrix(dense=True, galerkin=bool) with _compute_dense_matrix overrides on MatrixLinearOperator and the block classes |
| `algebra.operators.LinearOperator.diagonals(probe='banded') and the _known_diagonals hook` | keyword / new algorithm | Banded probing: obtains the requested diagonals with one application per residue class of width max(offsets)-min(offsets)+1, independent of dimension, exact when the operator is banded within the offsets. _Notes:_ ADVERSARIAL PASS. Read all seven v2 files in full and v1 hilbert_space, linear_operators, nonlinear_operators, nonlinear_forms, linear_forms, affine_operators, direct_sum, symmetric_space (InvariantLinearAutomorphism, spatial_multiplication_operator), low_rank (white_noise_measure, random_range), functional_calculus (Lanczos), parallel, preconditioners (Banded), gaussian_measure (from_standard_deviation, _sample_from_factor), convex_analysis/optimisation and subsets (prox candidates). Ran v1 under `poetry run python` to verify four claims empirically.  REMOVED from the claimed list (v1 had it): 1. CoordinateSpace.representer -- v1 HilbertSpace.from_dual(LinearForm(domain, components=g)) (hilbert_space.py:92-104; OrthogonalHilbertSpace 614-616) is exactly G^-1 g. The first pass's own notes already list 'representer = domain.from_dual(form)' as a rename; a method that takes the raw array instead of a LinearForm is not an addition. 2. LinearOperator.from_derivative_callables -- v1 LinearOperator(domain, codomain, mapping, dual_mapping=...) (linear_operators.py:60-114) with _adjoint_mapping_from_dual (826-829) doing to_dual(y) -> dual_mapping -> from_dual is the same information: v2's derivative_components(y) is v1's dual_mapping with the Riesz map of y already taken. The first pass's notes already say 'from_derivative_callables is v1's dual_mapping= keyword under a new name'; it was listed as an addition and a rename at once. 3. LinearOperator.from_component_columns -- v1 low_rank.random_range Path B builds exactly this: LinearOperator.from_matrix(EuclideanSpace(k), operator.codomain, q_matrix, galerkin=False) (low_rank.py:626-629), whose adjoint through the dual is one analysis + G + one product. The only new part is the orthonormal= ISOMETRY claim, which belongs to the from_vectors/_ColumnOperator entry (kept, rewritten).  REWRITTEN as partial (v1 had a real version; summaries now say only what is new): - CoordinateSpace Gram interface: general non-diagonal Gram was already supported through to_dual/from_dual on any v1 HilbertSpace and MassWeightedHilbertSpace.to_dual; new are the batched column ops, gram_diagonal/gram_matrix, has_diagonal_metric. - MatrixLinearOperator: v1 already returned its stored matrix when the form matched (linear_operators.py:1105-1115) and SparseMatrixLinearOperator read diagonals off the sparse array without densifying (1308-1339). VERIFIED: v1 re-probes column by column when matrix(galerkin=other) is asked (0 applications same form, 4 applications other form at dim 3), so v2's on-demand Gram conversion is the genuine addition, plus required form= and traits. - DiagonalLinearOperator: VERIFIED that v1 DiagonalSparseMatrixLinearOperator.from_diagonal_values on a non-orthonormal OrthogonalHilbertSpace already has a metric-correct adjoint ((Dx,y)==(x,D*y) holds), so 'handles a non-diagonal Gram correctly' is a port. New: calculus + closure on any CoordinateSpace, trait deduction, spectrum-gated calculus, _rebuild hook. - matrix(form=, by=): galerkin bool, auto-transpose and stored-matrix reads on Matrix/Block classes all existed; new are trait-driven 'auto', explicit by=, and _known_matrix through the expression nodes. - from_vectors/_ColumnOperator: merged with from_component_columns; new is the ISOMETRY claim, lazy columns, single class, apply_block. Direction flip noted below. - components_of/vectors_from: v1 nearest is matrix(dense=False).matmat and low_rank Path B (orthonormal codomain only), not 'none'. - orthonormal_basis: v1's range finder got 'drop dependent vectors' by catching gram_schmidt's ValueError (low_rank.py:596-600). - multiplication_operator: v1's spatial_multiplication_operator claimed self-adjointness via LinearOperator.self_adjoint even on Sobolev (MassWeighted) spaces, which is wrong there; v2 refusing the claim is a correction.  CORRECTNESS FINDING (upgrades the white_noise claim): v1 white_noise_measure(domain) = from_standard_deviation(domain, 1.0) samples via _sample_from_factor (gaussian_measure.py:1786-1793), which draws domain.random() (standard-normal COMPONENTS, hilbert_space.py:244-253) through an identity factor. VERIFIED on a space with metric diag(1,4,9): sampled component variances (1.00, 0.99, 1.02) versus the (1, 0.25, 0.11) that identity covariance in the space's inner product requires, while m.covariance is the identity operator. So v1's white noise was wrong on every non-orthonormal space (its randomised range finder was therefore sampling with covariance G, biased toward heavy-metric directions), and v2's white_noise_components = N(0, G^-1) is a fix, not a relocation.  ADDED (missed by the first pass): Functional/LinearFunctional as subclasses of Operator/LinearOperator (v1 NonLinearForm was not a NonLinearOperator; bridge was LinearForm.as_linear_operator / from_linear_form(s) into EuclideanSpace(1)). Also folded into existing entries: ArrayVectorMixin, CoordinateSpace.squared_norm single conversion, _orthonormalise_columns(against=), DirectSum.__len__, _accumulate, DiagonalLinearOperator._rebuild, LinearOperator.__mul__ returning self for alpha==1. Minor and not listed separately: EuclideanSpace(0) is now allowed (v1 required dim>=1); from_tensor_product claims PSD when u is v (a trait detail); _Identity/_Zero claim their traits.  CONFIRMED NEW with no v1 trace (grep and reading): Traits and all propagation functions; __hash__/_key (v1 spaces verified unhashable); shares_vectors_with; rng= on space draws; second_derivative (no hit anywhere in v1); Linearisation/QuadraticModel/at(); prox/conjugate (grep 'def prox\|conjugate\|fenchel' empty; subsets.project is on a Subset, not a form); DirectSum labels (grep 'labels' hits only plot.py); nonlinear block operators (grep 'class .*Block' finds only direct_sum's four linear classes); banded residue-class probing (BandedPreconditioningMethod calls extract_diagonals, one application per column); fused component actions; expression nodes; chain-rule Hessian (v1 __matmul__ drops it); MassWeightedSpace(mass_solver=); ComponentView; Reals.  Ported-with-rename (NOT additions; from the first pass, all checked and correct): mean = sample_expectation; multiply -> scale, ax -> scale_inplace; DiagonalMetricSpace = OrthogonalHilbertSpace; OrthonormalSpace = OrthonormalHilbertSpace; HilbertModule.multiply/sqrt = HilbertModuleMixin.vector_multiply/vector_sqrt; MassWeightedSpace.base/mass = underlying_space/mass_operator; coordinate_inclusion/coordinate_projection now methods; LinearOperator.identity/zero = identity_operator/zero_operator; assembled() = with_dense_matrix(); diagonals() = extract_diagonals() (returns array only, spdiags-aligned); is_endomorphism = is_automorphism; Functional = NonLinearForm; LinearFunctional = LinearForm (representer = from_dual(form), derivative_components = form.components, from_derivative_components = LinearForm(components=), from_representer = to_dual(v)); AffineOperator.translation = translation_part; DirectSum.subspaces/inclusion/projection = subspaces/subspace_inclusion/subspace_projection; DiagonalLinearOperator calculus = InvariantLinearAutomorphism's; MatrixLinearOperator.stored_form/stored_matrix = is_galerkin/is_dense/sparse_array.  DROPS OBSERVED in these files (the owner's stated worry; not additions but worth flagging): (a) from_vectors direction is flipped -- v1 maps space -> R^n by inner products, v2 maps R^n -> space; ported code needs .adjoint. (b) from_tensor_product takes one (u, v) pair; v1's list-with-weights form and self_adjoint_from_tensor_product are gone (v1 gaussian_measure.from_samples used the latter). (c) from_matrix no longer accepts a scipy.sparse.linalg.LinearOperator; matrix(dense=False) is gone; Dense/Sparse/DiagonalSparse classes, from_operator diagonal-approximation factory, is_strictly_diagonal/offsets are gone. (d) DualHilbertSpace, LinearOperator.dual, riesz/inverse_riesz, duality_product, canonical_dual_isomorphism have no counterpart; everything is Riesz-identified. (e) HilbertSpace.is_element is gone; v1 used it in gram_schmidt/sample_expectation and AffineOperator's constructor to validate the translation -- v2 AffineOperator does no such check. (f) EuclideanSpace.subspace_projection(indices) has no counterpart. (g) LinearOperator.from_linear_forms / from_linear_form / from_vector (stack of functionals into R^n / R^1) have no direct counterpart; the route is ColumnLinearOperator of LinearFunctionals or from_vectors(representers).adjoint. (h) A linear operator built without an adjoint now raises NotImplementedError on .adjoint; v1 derived the dual numerically by default (_dual_mapping_default, dim evaluations per application). Deliberate, but silently-working v1 code will now fail. (i) with_dense_matrix(galerkin=True) option is gone: assembled() always stores components form (direct solvers convert on demand). (j) BlockDiagonalLinearOperator.block(i, j) and BlockStructure index checks are gone; only .operators remains. (k) LinearForm(parallel=, n_jobs=) component evaluation and __iadd__/__imul__ are gone. (l) gram_schmidt numerical behaviour changed (relative rtol, second pass) -- an improvement, not identical. (m) LinearFunctional.from_callables shadows LinearOperator.from_callables with a different signature. (n) ComponentView is public-named but not exported. (o) v1 checks/ axiom mixins are not mixed in; docstrings point to pygeoinf2.testing (not audited here).

### numerics_linear

| v2 | kind | what it does | nearest v1 |

CG's non-positive-curvature check existed in v1 as FloatingPointError; MinRes's indefinite-preconditioner check existed as ValueError (kept as ValueError in v2). | CGSolver FloatingPointError on breakdown (linear_solvers.py:520-531); MinResSolver ValueError on non-PD preconditioner (linear_solvers.py:633-634); no counterpart for the iteration-cap case |

Note the warm start itself is not new: v1's solve_linear_system(operator, preconditioner, y, x0) was a public solver method taking x0; what is new is reaching it (with diagnostics) through the inverse operator. | IterativeLinearSolver.__call__ / DirectLinearSolver._build_inverse_operator building a bare LinearOperator (linear_solvers.py:59-97, 315-322); IterativeLinearSolver.solve_linear_system(..., x0) for the warm start (linear_solvers.py:240-266); 'InverseLinearOperator' exists only in a comment (preconditioners.py:197) |

The adjoint-factor reuse is NOT new: v1 LUSolver already passed lu_solve(factor, c, 1) as the rmatvec/adjoint mapping. | LUSolver apply_inv_adj via lu_solve(factor, c, 1) (linear_solvers.py:125-131) for the adjoint reuse; DirectLinearSolver._build_inverse_operator ScipyLinOp route (linear_solvers.py:88-97) with no matrix shortcut |

In v1 only CGSolver had a native callback and it received the iterate x, not a residual; MinRes/BICGStab/LSQR/FCG had none; residual tracking required ResidualTrackingCallback to re-apply the operator per step. Partial precedent: ScipyIterativeSolver forwarded a callback to scipy and, for gmres, defaulted callback_type='pr_norm', so a residual-norm callback did exist for the scipy GMRES wrapper only. | CGSolver(callback=) receiving x (linear_solvers.py:456, 574-575); ScipyIterativeSolver callback passthrough with gmres pr_norm (linear_solvers.py:395-412); ResidualTrackingCallback (linear_solvers.py:1064) |

What is genuinely new is the immutable copy-with semantics, the refusal to replace, and the property. | `numerics.solvers.resolve_solver / SolverLike` | function + type alias | Accepts a LinearSolver, a callable operator -> LinearSolver (a factory deferred until the operator to be inverted exists, for preconditioners built from different factors such as a coarse surrogate), or None (default CG), and returns a LinearSolver, type-checking the factory's result. No callable-factory protocol exists in v1; the nearest idea is LinearBayesianInversion.surrogate_*_preconditioner, which took the surrogate pieces as arguments and built the operator internally rather than deferring via a callable. | none as a protocol; LinearBayesianInversion.surrogate_normal_preconditioner / surrogate_woodbury_*_preconditioner (linear_bayesian.py:1200-1290) address the same sequencing problem by a different mechanism |
| `numerics.solvers.GMRESSolver` | class (new algorithm implementation) | Native, coordinate-free restarted GMRES (Arnoldi + Givens rotations, residual known without forming the iterate), with left preconditioning (tolerance measured in the preconditioned norm), callback and strict handling. v1 offered GMRES only by wrapping scipy.sparse.linalg.gmres on operator.matrix(), which requires a component map and runs in the Euclidean component norm. | GMRESMatrixSolver / ScipyIterativeSolver('gmres') (linear_solvers.py:325-436) |
| `numerics.solvers.LeastSquaresSolver` | abstract class | Sibling ABC of LinearSolver for rectangular systems solved in the least-squares sense; __call__ returns an InverseOperator with Traits.NONE. LSQRSolver derives from it. In v1 LSQRSolver subclassed IterativeLinearSolver and inherited its __call__'s `assert operator.is_automorphism`, so the one rectangular solver could not be used through the operator interface on a rectangular operator. | LSQRSolver(IterativeLinearSolver) (linear_solvers.py:816) inheriting IterativeLinearSolver.__call__ (linear_solvers.py:281-299) |
| `numerics.solvers.LSQRSolver(damping=) constructor keyword + damped-warm-start refusal + relative normal-residual tolerance` | keyword/behaviour | Damping is a constructor option so a damped LSQR is usable through the operator interface (v1 exposed damping only as an extra positional argument of solve_linear_system, which __call__ never passed). A damped warm start is refused with an explanation (it would penalise the correction, not the solution), and both stopping tests are relative to the data (\|\|b\|\|, \|\|A* b\|\|) rather than the shifted residual; v1's normal-residual test was absolute (arnorm <= atol). | LSQRSolver.solve_linear_system(..., damping=0.0) (linear_solvers.py:836-843) and its stopping tests (linear_solvers.py:932-940) |
| `numerics.preconditioners.WoodburyPreconditioner` | class (relocated and generalised) | Standalone LinearSolver implementing both Woodbury identities (model form needing only Q and R applications; data form needing Q^-1 and R^-1), choosing which by the dimension/space of the operator it is asked to invert; takes surrogate A, Q, R directly, optional closed-form prior_inverse/noise_inverse, per-factor solvers, defaults the inner solve to loose non-strict CG (rtol 1e-3, maxiter 200), validates the operator's dimension, and has from_normal() to read the factors (and precisions) off a NormalOperator. v1 had the same two identities and the surrogate variants, but as methods on LinearBayesianInversion returning a bare operator, with the inner solver mandatory and the identity chosen by the caller. | LinearBayesianInversion.woodbury_data_preconditioner / woodbury_model_preconditioner / surrogate_woodbury_data_preconditioner / surrogate_woodbury_model_preconditioner (linear_bayesian.py:1019-1125, 1220-1290) |
| `numerics.preconditioners.BandedPreconditioner(probe='banded', form='auto'\|'components'\|'galerkin')` | keywords (capability) | probe='banded' obtains the band with one operator application per residue class of columns rather than one per column (exact when the operator is banded, otherwise folds out-of-band entries in). The probe itself is implemented in LinearOperator.diagonals (algebra/operators.py:861-948), so this module's contribution is surfacing it plus the `form` choice with self-adjointness of the result deduced honestly by _sparse_inverse_traits. v1 always probed every column (extract_diagonals) and always used the Galerkin matrix; v1's matrix-backed operators could read their own diagonals without probing (a capability v2's _known_diagonals keeps). v1's incomplete-LU and parallel options on this class are dropped. | BandedPreconditioningMethod (preconditioners.py:201-284) with LinearOperator.extract_diagonals(galerkin=True) column probe (linear_operators.py:708-770) |
| `numerics.preconditioners.ColumnThresholdedPreconditioner pattern symmetrisation` | behaviour | After per-column thresholding the sparsity pattern is symmetrised (a position is kept if either column wants it) and the missing values are filled from the transpose of the Galerkin matrix, so the factorised preconditioner is symmetric as CG requires; v1 factorised the asymmetric thresholded pattern directly. The column-at-a-time probe that avoids holding the dense matrix is NOT new: v1 called operator.matrix(galerkin=...) with the default dense=False, a matrix-free ScipyLinOp, and probed scipy_op @ e_j per column. v1's galerkin=False choice and parallel option are dropped; incomplete-LU is kept. | ColumnThresholdedPreconditioningMethod (preconditioners.py:408-549), probing via operator.matrix(galerkin=...) which is matrix-free by default (linear_operators.py:569-580) |
| `numerics.functional_calculus.operator_function` | function (dispatch) | f(A) for any operator claiming self-adjointness, dispatching on storage: a DiagonalLinearOperator evaluates f on its eigenvalues exactly; anything else becomes a lazily-applied Lanczos OperatorFunction. The caller supplies the trait claim for f(A). v1 had the exact route only as InvariantLinearAutomorphism.apply_function (symmetric spaces) and LowRankEig.apply_function, and the Lanczos route only as the explicit LanczosOperatorFunction class; there was no unified entry point. | InvariantLinearAutomorphism.apply_function (symmetric_space/symmetric_space.py:168-190); LanczosOperatorFunction (functional_calculus.py:40-135); LowRankEig.apply_function (low_rank.py:335) |
| `numerics.functional_calculus.operator_sqrt / operator_inverse_sqrt / operator_exp / operator_log / operator_power` | functions | Named operator functions for general self-adjoint operators, each gated on the trait the maths needs (sqrt/fractional power: POSITIVE_SEMIDEFINITE; inverse sqrt/log: POSITIVE_DEFINITE) and attaching the right trait to the result. v1 had sqrt/exp/log/__pow__ only on InvariantLinearAutomorphism (with eigenvalue-sign checks), and built fractional powers of a general covariance by hand via LanczosOperatorFunction(cov, lambda x: np.power(x, p)). | InvariantLinearAutomorphism.sqrt/exp/log/__pow__ (symmetric_space/symmetric_space.py:148-200); GaussianMeasure fractional powers via LanczosOperatorFunction (gaussian_measure.py:2110-2130) |
| `numerics.functional_calculus trait gating of the Lanczos routines (_require_self_adjoint, OperatorFunction(traits=))` | behaviour | iter_lanczos_tridiagonalise, apply_operator_function, operator_quadratic_form and OperatorFunction refuse an operator that does not claim SELF_ADJOINT, with a message pointing at with_traits()/check_traits(); OperatorFunction accepts a traits= claim for f(A) and closes it with SELF_ADJOINT. v1's LanczosOperatorFunction checked only domain == codomain and assumed self-adjointness silently. | LanczosOperatorFunction.__init__ automorphism check (functional_calculus.py:97-100) |
| `numerics.functional_calculus.log_determinant` | function | log det of a positive-definite operator returning an Estimate, with method='auto'\|'dense'\|'stochastic': exact sum(log lambda) for a DiagonalLinearOperator; dense slogdet of the Galerkin matrix with the metric's own log det subtracted (so the component-matrix determinant is returned, matching the stochastic route) when dim <= dense_limit and the matrix can be read or probed within the SLQ application budget; otherwise stochastic Lanczos quadrature via random_trace(operator_log(A)) with a standard-error stopping rule (sample_rtol). v1 had only the SLQ route, as a method on LinearBayesianInversion restricted to its two normal operators and returning a bare float; dense slogdet appeared only inline inside KL-divergence code. | LinearBayesianInversion.estimate_log_determinant / _trace_log_slq (linear_bayesian.py:560-687); inline np.linalg.slogdet in GaussianMeasure._kl_divergence_dense (gaussian_measure.py:2163-2164) and symmetric_space.py:521, 1177 |
| `numerics.functional_calculus Lanczos component fast path + small-order eigh switch` | behaviour (fast path) | On a CoordinateSpace with uses_component_fast_paths the Krylov basis is kept as component columns and reorthogonalisation is classical Gram-Schmidt against the whole basis with one apply_gram per pass (Kahan second pass when the norm drops by more than 1-1/sqrt(2)), against 2k+4 analyses per step through the abstract inner product; plus a switch to np.linalg.eigh below order 32 for the per-step convergence test. Kahan's 'twice is enough' second pass is NOT new: v1's abstract loop already had it (threshold 0.707); v2's abstract loop actually drops it to a single modified-Gram-Schmidt pass on a measurement. What is new is the column route with batched metric application and the dense-eigh switch. | iter_lanczos_tridiagonalize abstract loop with twice-is-enough reorthogonalisation (functional_calculus.py:392-509, second pass at 450-462); eigh_tridiagonal always (functional_calculus.py:225, 340) |
| `numerics.randomised.Estimate` | class (result type) | Frozen dataclass (value, standard_error, samples) returned by random_trace and log_determinant so a Monte Carlo estimate carries its uncertainty; the dense log-det route reports standard_error 0 so callers treat both uniformly. v1 random_trace and estimate_log_determinant returned a float with no error estimate. | none (random_trace -> float, low_rank.py:1053-1156; estimate_log_determinant -> float, linear_bayesian.py:640-687) |
| `numerics.randomised.random_trace(rtol=) standard-error stopping + random_diagonal(rtol=) norm-ratio standard-error stopping` | behaviour | Adaptive sampling stops when the standard error (random_trace) or the norm of the per-entry standard errors over the norm of the estimate (random_diagonal) falls below rtol, with a max_samples ceiling defaulting to samples + 20 blocks. v1's 'variable' method stopped when the running mean moved by less than rtol between successive blocks, a noisy test of a noisy quantity. Also random_trace probes with HilbertSpace.white_noise and the space's inner product rather than Rademacher components and a Euclidean dot, and random_diagonal always uses Rademacher probes (v1 defaulted to Gaussian with a use_rademacher flag). | random_trace / random_diagonal method='variable' running-mean tests (low_rank.py:940-952, 1140-1152) |
| `numerics.randomised.* rng= keyword (seedable probes) and per-probe spawned streams` | keyword (capability) | random_range, random_eig, random_svd, random_cholesky, random_trace, random_diagonal, deflated_diagonal and the preconditioners built on them (Jacobi, Spectral) take a numpy Generator; random_trace spawns one child stream per probe in order so the estimate depends on the seed alone whether run serially or with n_jobs. v1 low_rank used the global np.random.randn/choice throughout, and HilbertSpace.random used np.random.randn, with no seeding hook. | none in low_rank.py (np.random global state at low_rank.py:760, 808, 828, 911, 1123) or HilbertSpace.random (hilbert_space.py:244-256) |
| `numerics.randomised.random_range(oversampling=) + white-noise probes on any space + component-column route through the factorisations` | keyword + behaviour (fast path) | Genuinely new: (1) an oversampling= keyword, so rank=k draws k+oversampling probes in one block (v1's fixed method drew exactly size_estimate with no oversampling parameter); (2) probes drawn as HilbertSpace.white_noise on every space, with the basis carried as component columns on any CoordinateSpace with fast paths, through power iteration and straight into random_eig/random_svd/random_cholesky (k analyses, not k^2) -- v1 routed every non-orthonormal codomain to the abstract per-vector Python path and used its component/QR path only when codomain.is_orthonormal; (3) power iteration is applied to the final adaptive basis with reorthonormalisation at each half step (v1's component variable-rank path power-iterated only the initial block and did not reorthonormalise between the A^T and A half steps, low_rank.py:815-823); (4) the adaptive component route projects the block off the basis twice. NOT new, contrary to the first pass: the 'orthogonalise only the new block and extend by its residuals' loop -- v1's abstract and component adaptive paths already did exactly that (low_rank.py:701-736 and 828-850), so the 'linear vs cubic' comparison does not hold against pygeoinf v1. | random_range with method='fixed'/'variable' (low_rank.py:492-636); _abstract_variable_rank_random_range (low_rank.py:669-737); _component_variable_rank_random_range (low_rank.py:787-852); HilbertSpace.gram_schmidt (hilbert_space.py:354-380) |

_Notes:_ Method: all four v2 files read in full; v1 linear_solvers.py, preconditioners.py and functional_calculus.py read in full; low_rank.py read for the LowRank classes, random_range and all three estimators; targeted reads of linear_bayesian.py (SLQ, Woodbury, surrogates), symmetric_space.py (InvariantLinearAutomorphism calculus), gaussian_measure.py (Lanczos powers, dense KL), linear_operators.py (from_matrix, matrix(), extract_diagonal(s)), hilbert_space.py (random, gram_schmidt); v2 algebra/operators.py for the _known_matrix/_known_diagonals/_components_action/diagonals(probe=) hooks the numerics fast paths rely on.  Corrections to the first pass (none removed outright, but four overstated): (a) random_range 'linear vs cubic' -- v1's abstract variable-rank loop projected each test vector off q_basis, kept the residuals, Gram-Schmidted only those and extended (low_rank.py:701-736); the component loop did the same with QR (828-850). The v2 comment attributing the rebuild-everything arrangement to 'v1' evidently refers to an earlier v2 draft, not to pygeoinf v1. Rewritten around what is new (oversampling=, white-noise probes on any coordinate space, column route into the factorisations, power iteration on the final basis with half-step reorthonormalisation). (b) Lanczos 'Kahan second pass' -- v1 already had twice-is-enough (functional_calculus.py:450-462); v2's abstract loop drops it. (c) ColumnThresholded 'never holds the dense matrix' -- v1 already probed a matrix-free ScipyLinOp column by column (preconditioners.py:437-449; matrix() defaults to dense=False). Only the symmetrisation is new. (d) resolved_for 'no reuse-across-family facility' -- v1 __call__(preconditioner=P) accepted a pre-built operator, so reuse was possible by hand; the new parts are copy-with semantics, refuse-to-replace and the .preconditioner property. Also corrected v1_nearest for InverseOperator (x0 existed on solve_linear_system), the callback item (ScipyIterativeSolver forwarded scipy's pr_norm residual callback for gmres) and ConvergenceError (MinRes raised ValueError on an indefinite preconditioner).  Added by this pass: random_range(oversampling=) (folded into the random_range item) and the Lanczos-side trait gate (_require_self_adjoint / OperatorFunction(traits=)); v1 LanczosOperatorFunction checked only domain == codomain.  Ports, not additions (renames/near-renames): LUSolver/CholeskySolver/EigenSolver (galerkin flag -> per-class form; v2 symmetrises the matrix 0.5*(M+M.T) before cho_factor/eigh, which v1 did not); CGSolver; MinResSolver (preconditioned in v1 too, same ValueError on indefinite preconditioner); BiCGStabSolver (v1 BICGStabSolver); FlexibleCGSolver (v1 FCGSolver -- beta formula differs: v1 -(z_new, Ap)/(p, Ap), v2 Polak-Ribiere (r_new - r_old, z)/(r, z); both legitimate flexible variants, but a rewrite); LSQRSolver (rtol default 1e-5 -> 1e-10, atol dropped, maxiter 2*max(dim) -> 4*dim); ProgressCallback (v1 printed and had reset/finalize; v2 records residuals, prints only via report=); IdentityPreconditioner; JacobiPreconditioner (v1 JacobiPreconditioningMethod; default changed from 20-probe estimate to exact diagonal; floor= keyword exposes v1's hardcoded 1e-14); SpectralPreconditioner (v1 SpectralPreconditioningMethod -- formula differs: v1 returns (U S U* + d^2 I)^-1 = (1/d^2)(I - U diag(s/(s+d^2)) U*); v2 returns (1/d) I + U (1/s - 1/d) U*, i.e. the inverse of U S U* + d (I - U U*). A rewrite to check; v2 exposes only rank/damping/rng where v1 had method/max_rank/power/rtol/block_size/parallel); BandedPreconditioner; BlockPreconditioner (v1 ExactBlockPreconditioningMethod -- overlap and missing-index-to-diagonal already existed in v1 (preconditioners.py:333-341) despite the v2 docstring's 'v2 required a partition'; v2 drops incomplete/galerkin=False/parallel, uses array-based pattern assembly); ColumnThresholdedPreconditioner; OperatorFunction (v1 LanczosOperatorFunction); apply_operator_function; operator_quadratic_form (v1 operator_function_quadratic_form; v1 also stopped early under method='variable'); lanczos_tridiagonalise / iter_lanczos_tridiagonalise (spelling; breakdown_tol keyword replaces v1's _BREAKDOWN_TOL constant); LowRankEig/LowRankSVD/LowRankCholesky (accessor renames u_factor->factor/left_factor, v_factor->right_factor, l_factor->factor; d_factor/sigma_factor dropped; LowRankEig now deduces POSITIVE_SEMIDEFINITE from its eigenvalues); random_eig/random_svd/random_cholesky (v1 from_randomized classmethods; random_svd now assembles the k x k Gram of A* Q rather than forming Q* A and its dense matrix -- same cost class; random_eig requires the SELF_ADJOINT claim, random_cholesky the POSITIVE_SEMIDEFINITE claim); random_diagonal (operator + form= instead of matrix + galerkin=); deflated_diagonal (v1 deflated with a randomised SVD, v2 with a randomised eig); random_range rank=None (v1 method='variable').  v1 capabilities absent from these v2 files (confirm elsewhere or record as removals): ScipyIterativeSolver and the CG/BiCG/BiCGStab/GMRES matrix-solver factories (plain BiCG has no v2 counterpart); IterativePreconditioningMethod (subsumed by any LinearSolver being a deferred preconditioner, but its override of the inner solver's maxiter/rtol is gone); SolutionTrackingCallback and ResidualTrackingCallback (the callback no longer receives the iterate, so tracking the solution path is impossible); incomplete/drop_tol/fill_factor on Banded and Block preconditioners (kept only on ColumnThresholded); Spectral's method/power/max_rank/rtol/block_size range-finder options; galerkin=False on Block/ColumnThresholded (Block keeps form=; ColumnThresholded is Galerkin-only); parallel= on every v1 preconditioning method (v2 Banded/Block/ColumnThresholded have no n_jobs); LanczosOperatorFunction's method='fixed'/check_interval/atol; random_range's measure= argument (v2 always draws HilbertSpace.white_noise -- by design per DESIGN.md 9) and its return as an isometry LinearOperator (v2 returns a list of vectors); white_noise_measure (moved to HilbertSpace.white_noise); LowRankEig.apply_function's regularization= keyword; LowRankCholesky.from_randomized's direct-Cholesky-then-eig fallback (v2 always via eig); CholeskySolver check_finite; random_diagonal's use_rademacher=False Gaussian option and method='fixed' name (v2: rtol=None). v1 random_range silently clamped size_estimate to min(dim); v2 raises on rank <= 0 and clamps rank+oversampling.  Other observations: IterativeSolver default rtol 1e-5 -> 1e-8 and default maxiter 10*dim -> max(2*dim, 20); MINRES default atol 1e-8 -> 0; direct solvers' n_jobs replaces v1's parallel+n_jobs pair. The v2 module docstrings' 'v1 did X' claims are mixed: the Jacobi one (v1 estimated by default) is right; the BlockPreconditioner partition claim and the random_range 'that is v1's arrangement' comment describe an earlier v2 draft, not pygeoinf v1.

### numerics_nonlinear

| v2 | kind | what it does | nearest v1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `numerics.optimisation.OptimisationResult` | class (result type) | Frozen dataclass returned by every optimiser: minimiser, value, gradient_norm, iterations, evaluations, converged, message, value history. Verified: v1's ScipyUnconstrainedOptimiser.minimize discarded SciPy's OptimizeResult and returned only domain.from_components(result.x) (nonlinear_optimisation.py:111-112), so no diagnostics reached the caller. | none (ScipyUnconstrainedOptimiser.minimize returns a bare Vector, nonlinear_optimisation.py:50-112) |
| `numerics.optimisation.Optimiser` | abstract base class | Common base for all minimisers with its own stopping design: gtol (absolute), rtol (relative to initial gradient norm), ftol (relative value-decrease test), max_iterations, pluggable LineSearch; minimise() validates has_derivative; a line-search failure with \|\|g\|\| <= sqrt(eps)*(1+\|f\|) is reported as 'precision-limited' success. The shared _DescentMethod loop (direction rule + line search + ftol test + steepest-descent fallback on a non-descent direction) also lives here. Verified: v1 had no base class and no stopping criteria of its own; it forwarded 'tol'/'gtol' to SciPy (nonlinear_optimisation.py:92-97). | nonlinear_optimisation.ScipyUnconstrainedOptimiser (thin scipy.optimize.minimize wrapper) |
| `numerics.optimisation.SteepestDescent` | class (algorithm) | Native steepest descent in the space's metric with a strong Wolfe default line search and the Nocedal-Wright slope-ratio initial-step heuristic (_slope_ratio_step). Verified: v1's method set was {Newton-CG, trust-ncg, trust-krylov, trust-exact, dogleg, BFGS, L-BFGS-B, CG, Nelder-Mead, Powell} (nonlinear_optimisation.py:29-39); no steepest descent. | none (closest: ScipyUnconstrainedOptimiser('CG')) |
| `numerics.optimisation.NonlinearCG` | class (algorithm; native rewrite of a SciPy-reached capability) | Native nonlinear CG in the space's inner product with strong Wolfe c2=0.1 and slope-ratio initial step. Genuinely new: the 'fletcher-reeves' variant switch (SciPy's CG is Polak-Ribiere+ only) and metric awareness. NOT new: Polak-Ribiere+ CG itself, which v1 reached via ScipyUnconstrainedOptimiser('CG') on components — and there with gradient components passed as jac (nonlinear_optimisation.py:70-73), i.e. the wrong convention on a non-Euclidean space. | ScipyUnconstrainedOptimiser('CG') (nonlinear_optimisation.py:37) |

NOT new: the L-BFGS capability (v1 via SciPy 'L-BFGS-B'/'BFGS' on components, same gradient-vs-derivative convention issue at nonlinear_optimisation.py:70-73) and the memory size, which v1 could pass as SciPy's 'maxcor' through **kwargs. v1 also had SmoothedLBFGSSolver (convex_optimisation.py:2120-2228), a SciPy L-BFGS-B on a Moreau-Yosida-smoothed dual, which v2 drops. | ScipyUnconstrainedOptimiser('L-BFGS-B' \| 'BFGS'); convex_optimisation.SmoothedLBFGSSolver |

NOT new: Newton-CG itself (v1 via SciPy). Verified the v2 docstring's charge: v1 passed domain.to_components(form.gradient(x)) as jac (nonlinear_optimisation.py:70-73) but hessian_op.matrix(galerkin=True) as hess (line 80-83), mixing gradient and derivative conventions in one call; v1's own line_search correctly passed dual components (lines 174-182). | ScipyUnconstrainedOptimiser('Newton-CG') |
| `numerics.optimisation.TrustRegionNewton` | class (algorithm; native rewrite of a SciPy-reached capability) | Native trust-region Newton solved by Steihaug-CG with the standard radius update (initial_radius, max_radius, acceptance ratio), coordinate-free. NOT new: trust-region Newton capability (v1 via SciPy 'trust-ncg'; v1 also offered 'trust-krylov', 'trust-exact' and 'dogleg', which v2 drops). | ScipyUnconstrainedOptimiser('trust-ncg') |
| `numerics.optimisation.truncated_cg` | function (algorithm) | Public, coordinate-free Steihaug truncated CG on a LinearOperator: stops on residual tolerance, negative curvature, or trust-region boundary (radius keyword, _to_boundary root), returning the step and a reason string; handles indefinite operators. Verified: v1's CGSolver raises FloatingPointError on non-positive p^T A p (linear_solvers.py:531-535), and no other truncated/trust-region CG exists in v1. | none (linear_solvers.CGSolver is nearest but raises FloatingPointError on indefiniteness, linear_solvers.py:531-535) |
