Makes 'no root in range' a reported answer carrying the endpoint, and distinguishes a singular probe (LinAlgError -> saturation) from a solver that ran out of iterations (ConvergenceError -> breakdown). v1 returned (model, damping) or raised RuntimeError (linear_optimisation.py:915, 946). | none (v1 discrepancy search returned (model, damping) or raised RuntimeError, linear_optimisation.py:915,946) |
| `numerics.root_find.monotone_root` | function (algorithm) | Generic scalar root find for a monotone quantity in a positive multiplier, shared by inference/point.py, inference/backus.py and tikhonov.py. Genuinely new versus v1: Brent's method in log(t) with memoised probes after bracketing (v1: geometric bisection at 0.5*(lo+hi)); decade-wise widening with 'expansions' cap and exhaustion reported with the endpoint rather than raised (v1 raised RuntimeError below minimum_damping and, in the upward loop, silently accepted the maxiter endpoint as a bracket); breakdown vs saturation distinction; 'decreasing=False' sign flip for increasing quantities; convergence judged on the bracket criterion. NOT new: bracketing at both ends — v1 halved while chi2 > critical and doubled while chi2 < critical (linear_optimisation.py:908-924) — and warm-starting the bisection phase from the previous solution (linear_optimisation.py:930-932). | LinearMinimumNormInversion.minimum_norm_operator -> _solve_discrepancy (linear_optimisation.py:896-947) |
| `numerics.root_find.DampedSolves` | class | Manages solves of (base + t*shift) x = b along a multiplier sweep. Genuinely new: caches each assembled member; keeps a LinearSolver-valued preconditioner and rebuilds it only when the multiplier moves by more than 'refresh' (default 10x) — v1 re-resolved preconditioner(normal_operator) on every damping value (linear_optimisation.py:872-876); an 'assemble' hook so structure-aware preconditioners still see A/Q/R factors; applies traits; and for a DirectSolver extracts base and shift matrices once and forms the sum as a matrix. NOT new: passing x0 to warm-start an iterative solver, which v1 did (linear_optimisation.py:879-881). | get_model_for_damping closure in LinearMinimumNormInversion.minimum_norm_operator (linear_optimisation.py:860-894) |
| `numerics.convex.SquaredDistance` | class (Functional) | 0.5\|\|x - centre\|\|^2 in the space's norm, with gradient, identity Hessian (POSITIVE_DEFINITE trait) and closed-form prox (x + t*centre)/(1+t). Prox is new to the library (no 'prox' anywhere in v1). Partial precedent: v1's subsets._EllipsoidalGeometry builds the quadratic form <A(x-c),x-c> as a NonLinearForm with gradient and hessian (subsets.py:884-930), but as a set's defining functional with no prox. | subsets._EllipsoidalGeometry quadratic form (subsets.py:884-930; value/gradient/hessian only, no prox) |
| `numerics.convex.NormFunctional` | class (Functional) | weight*\|\|x\|\| with closed-form prox (shrinkage along the vector). Genuinely new: the prox. NOT new: value and subgradient — v1's BallSupportFunction centred at 0 with radius r evaluates to r\|\|q\|\| and its subgradient (support_point) is r*q/\|\|q\|\| (convex_analysis.py:247-303), which is the same function with the same subgradient. | convex_analysis.BallSupportFunction at centre 0 (convex_analysis.py:247-303; value and subgradient, no prox) |
| `numerics.convex.BallIndicator` | class (Functional) | Indicator of a closed ball (0 inside, inf outside) whose prox is the projection onto the ball, plus conjugate() returning the ball's SupportFunction. v1 had subsets.Ball (membership only; no project method — only HyperPlane/HalfSpace have project, subsets.py:1310,1475) and an inline ball projection inside ChambollePockSolver._proj_B (convex_optimisation.py:1653-1680), but no indicator functional, no prox, and no Fenchel-conjugate method. | subsets.Ball (set, no projection) / convex_optimisation.ChambollePockSolver._proj_B (inline projection) |
| `numerics.convex.SubgradientDescent(rule=..., target_value=...) and subgradient-norm stop` | keyword adding capability on a ported class | Diminishing step rules 'sqrt' (a/sqrt(k), default), 'inverse' (a/k) and 'polyak' ((f-f*)/\|\|g\|\|^2 with a known target_value) alongside v1's constant step; a stopping test on \|\|subgradient\|\| <= gtol, which v1 lacked (v1 stopped only on max_iterations or an optional stagnation_window); returns an OptimisationResult with the best point seen. Verified v1 was constant-step only and its docstring said convergence was not guaranteed (convex_optimisation.py:51-160). Dropped: store_iterates, stagnation_window, x_final/f_final. | convex_optimisation.SubgradientDescent (convex_optimisation.py:51-160, constant step only) |
| `numerics.convex.ProximalGradient` | class (algorithm) | Proximal gradient / FISTA for smooth f + nonsmooth g with prox: optional fixed step or monotone backtracking on the quadratic upper bound with a two-point Lipschitz initial estimate, Nesterov momentum when accelerated=True, prox taken in the space's norm. minimise(smooth, x0, *, nonsmooth=None). Verified: no proximal, FISTA or Nesterov method anywhere in v1; SmoothedLBFGSSolver (convex_optimisation.py:2120-2228) is Moreau-Yosida smoothing plus L-BFGS-B, a different approach. | none (v1's SmoothedLBFGSSolver is a Moreau-Yosida smoothing + L-BFGS-B approach, not a proximal method) |

Verified v1 solved the primal (d+1)-variable QP in components through a QPSolver backend (convex_optimisation.py:842-895). Dropped: qp_solver and rho_factor options, f_low/num_serious_steps/function_values/iterates fields. | convex_optimisation.ProximalBundleMethod (convex_optimisation.py:761-1011, component-space QP via QPSolver) |
| `numerics.convex.ProximalBundleMethod.minimise / LevelBundleMethod.minimise (subgradient=... override)` | keyword adding capability on ported methods | Both bundle methods accept a callable 'subgradient' override so the oracle need not be attached to the Functional. Also new: 'rng' keyword for the power-iteration norm estimate (v1 hard-coded default_rng(0), line 1631); validation that the sets live in the operator's spaces and theta >= 0; SaddlePointResult carries the support value. NOT new: the warm start — v2's 'start' is a rename of v1's solve(c, m0=None) (convex_optimisation.py:1709-1713). | convex_optimisation.ChambollePockSolver (convex_optimisation.py:1542-1820, balls only) |

_Notes:_ Adversarial pass over the first-pass list. Method: read all six v2 files in full (/home/david/dev/pygeoinf/pygeoinf2/numerics/{optimisation,line_search,root_find,quadratic_forms,quadratic_programming,convex}.py); grepped v1 (/home/david/dev/pygeoinf/pygeoinf) for lbfgs, newton, trust region, wolfe, armijo, steihaug, truncated, gauss/jacobian, brent, bisect, warm, prox, fista, moreau, fenchel, dykstra, polyak, nesterov, momentum, steepest, polak, fletcher, indicator, project; read v1 nonlinear_optimisation.py in full, linear_optimisation.py:840-960 (discrepancy search), convex_optimisation.py (SubgradientDescent, QP classes, BundleResult, ProximalBundleMethod, LevelBundleMethod, ChambollePock, PrimalKKTSolver), convex_analysis.py listing, subsets.py listing, quadratic_form_quantile.py signatures, linear_solvers.py CG breakdown checks, backus_gilbert.py test_data_compatibility.  REMOVED: nothing. No claimed item has a full v1 counterpart. Every v1 optimiser capability was reached through SciPy on component arrays; none of the native, coordinate-free implementations, result types, or abstractions existed.  CORRECTED (summaries rewritten because the first pass overstated novelty): - NonlinearCG: SciPy's 'CG' already is Polak-Ribiere+; only the Fletcher-Reeves switch and metric awareness are new. - LBFGS: the 'memory' keyword is not new capability — v1 could pass SciPy's 'maxcor' via **kwargs (nonlinear_optimisation.py:41-48). - truncated_cg: v1's CGSolver raises FloatingPointError, not ValueError, on non-positive p^T A p (linear_solvers.py:531-535). - gauss_newton_hessian: v1 has the linear special case (LinearLeastSquaresInversion.normal_operator, linear_optimisation.py:116-150) and a J*-based gradient composition without Hessian (nonlinear_forms.py:319-341); set as v1_nearest. - monotone_root: v1 DID bracket in both directions (halve while chi2 > critical, double while chi2 < critical, linear_optimisation.py:908-924) and DID warm-start the bisection phase (line 930-932). What is new is Brent in log t with memoisation, exhaustion reported rather than raised, the breakdown/saturation distinction, decreasing=False, and reuse across four callers (inference/point.py:466, inference/backus.py:713, inference/tikhonov.py:370 via DampedSolves). The v2 module docstring's claim that 'widening only upwards' was the prior state does not match v1's code. - DampedSolves: x0 warm-starting is not new (linear_optimisation.py:879-881); preconditioner reuse with refresh, the assemble hook, member caching and the direct-solver matrix-sum path are. - NormFunctional: v1's BallSupportFunction at centre 0 already gives r\|\|q\|\| with subgradient r q/\|\|q\|\| (convex_analysis.py:247-303); only the prox is new. - SquaredDistance: v1's subsets._EllipsoidalGeometry has a quadratic form with gradient and Hessian (subsets.py:884-930); the prox is new. - SubgradientDescent: added the \|\|g\|\| <= gtol stop, which v1 lacked (v1: stagnation_window only, convex_optimisation.py:105-160). - ChambollePockSolver: 'start' is a rename of v1's m0 (convex_optimisation.py:1709-1713), not a new warm start; rng, set-domain/theta validation, general ConvexSet projection and the value field are new. - ProximalBundleMethod: also drops rho_factor; serious-step test in v1 was f_next < f_hat with no fraction (line 954); v1 gap tolerance was absolute (line 987).  VERIFIED CLAIMS FROM THE FIRST PASS: the v2 docstring's charge that v1's ScipyUnconstrainedOptimiser mixed conventions is correct — jac = domain.to_components(form.gradient(x)) (nonlinear_optimisation.py:70-73) while hess = hessian_op.matrix(galerkin=True) (lines 80-83); v1's own line_search passed domain.dual.to_components(form.derivative(x)) with a comment explaining why (lines 174-182). v1 had no 'prox', 'indicator' functional, 'fenchel/conjugate', 'fista', 'polyak', 'armijo' implementation, 'steepest descent', or 'steihaug/truncated CG' (grep confirmed; 'truncated' hits are low_rank spectral truncation and the Imhof domain).  NO MISSED ADDITIONS WORTH A ROW. Minor non-capability changes seen in the v2 read, recorded here only: QPResult.solved property and a shared _validate shape check in quadratic_programming.py (v1 had no shape validation; v1 SciPyQPSolver hard-coded ftol=1e-9/maxiter=1000, which v2 exposes as tolerance/iterations); ClarabelQPSolver raises ValueError with zero constraints; KKTResult and SaddlePointResult gain a 'value' field (v1's KKTResult/ChambollePockResult had none, convex_optimisation.py:1493-1540); BundleResult gains 'message' and 'evaluations'; LevelBundleMethod defaults to best_available_qp_solver() (v1: SciPyQPSolver) and enforces require_coordinates with a TypeError; SupportFunction.compose_with validates operator.domain (v1's image() documents the same ValueError, convex_analysis.py:156-175); quadratic_forms lazy-imports scipy. quadratic_forms.py: confirmed NO additions — v1 already had imhof/ws(=matched)/mc(=monte_carlo)/rng/n_samples (quadratic_form_quantile.py:58-70, 122-135) and a brentq inversion; v2 drops 'saddlepoint', the tol-driven 'auto' selection, array-valued t, and accepts fewer degenerate weight sets (v2 raises on all-zero weights; v1 only rejected negative/non-finite, line 196-203).  DROPS relative to v1 in this module group, for the owner's attention: derivative-free methods (Nelder-Mead, Powell), full BFGS, trust-krylov/trust-exact/dogleg, line_search's amax and extra_condition; store_iterates everywhere; SubgradientDescent stagnation_window; Cut/Bundle public classes; BundleResult f_low/num_serious_steps/function_values/iterates; ProximalBundleMethod qp_solver and rho_factor; value_and_subgradient duck typing; solve_support_values (joblib multi-direction sweep), solve_primal_feasibility, SmoothedDualMaster, SmoothedLBFGSSolver; EllipsoidSupportFunction, HalfSpaceSupportFunction, CallableSupportFunction, SupportFunction.translate/scale/value_and_support_point/primal_domain; quantile 'saddlepoint' method and tolerance-driven 'auto'. Also the convex.py module docstring (lines 22-24) still says the KKT and Chambolle-Pock machinery is 'deliberately left behind' while both are in the file — stale.

Verified in v1: HilbertSpace.random (hilbert_space.py:253) uses np.random.randn, GaussianMeasure._sample_from_factor (gaussian_measure.py:1786-1793) draws through it, from_samples (318) uses np.random.randn, the randomized KL (2231) and random_trace (low_rank.py:1123) use np.random.choice; credible_set(rng=) (760) forwards rng to _resolve_spectrum (1884) which never passes it on, and _sampling_radius (1761) takes no rng. _Notes:_ REMOVED FROM THE CLAIMED LIST (v1 had it):  1. `GaussianMeasure.condition(operator, value, noise=, solver=)` -- v1 already conditioned a Gaussian on A x = value, exactly or with noise, with the same Kalman-gain posterior and the same Matheron / randomise-then-optimise sampler x + K(value - A x - e). It lived in the inference layer rather than on the measure: `LinearBayesianInversion.model_posterior_measure` (/home/david/dev/pygeoinf/pygeoinf/linear_bayesian.py:293-397; sampler at 362-397) and, for the exact-constraint case, `AffineSubspace.condition_gaussian_measure(prior, geometric=False)` (/home/david/dev/pygeoinf/pygeoinf/subspaces.py:632-690), which wraps the constraint operator in a LinearForwardProblem with no data-error measure and delegates to model_posterior_measure. v2's method is a relocation with a narrower scope: it is the 'data_space' formalism only (v1 also had 'model_space', linear_bayesian.py:339-351), it defaults the solver to conjugate gradients where v1 required one, and it orders the posterior covariance as (I - C A* N^-1 A) C to save one application of C. Not an addition.  2. The quantile-selection half of the `ambient_ball` claim ("quantile method chosen by effective rank, 'matched' new in numerics.quadratic_forms") -- v1's `quadratic_form_quantile._auto_select_method` (/home/david/dev/pygeoinf/pygeoinf/quadratic_form_quantile.py:210-240) already chose by effective degrees of freedom nu_eff = (sum w)^2 / sum w^2, and v1's "ws" method (lines 30, 355-372, `_ws_quantile`) is the Welch-Satterthwaite moment-matched chi-square that v2 renames "matched". The entry is kept for the 'diagonal' and 'dense' spectrum routes only, which are genuinely new.  KEPT WITH TIGHTENED v1_nearest (partial v1 versions): the spectral KL route and the O(dim) norm shortcut existed in v1 for `symmetric_space.InvariantGaussianMeasure` / `CorrelatedInvariantGaussianMeasure` (symmetric_space.py:493-616, 1139-1229) and are generalised in v2 to any DiagonalLinearOperator covariance on the base class; `marginal` and `cross_covariance` existed for `CorrelatedInvariantGaussianMeasure` (symmetric_space.py:1044-1073) and are generalised to any DirectSum measure with label access; `push_forward` of a non-Gaussian measure through a nonlinear map existed only as `data_assimilation.core.ProbabilityGrid.push_forward` (core.py:376), a numpy-grid Liouville advection through an ODE, which is not comparable machinery; `ProbabilityMeasure` as a base has `ProbabilityGrid` (core.py:182) as the only v1 non-Gaussian probability object, on no HilbertSpace and with no shared interface.  ADDED (missed by the first pass): (a) `credible_set` now works on a covariance-only measure (dense Gram-corrected inverse) and on a precision-only measure; v1's `_credible_set_chi2_ellipsoid` (gaussian_measure.py:1824-1843) read `self.inverse_covariance`, which raises AttributeError when unset (391-396). (b) Factor/precision propagation through the algebra: v2 `_combine_scale` keeps the precision and precision factor, `_mapped_precision` keeps the precision through translation and invertible diagonal maps, and `_combine_add` regains a factor and precision when two diagonal covariances are summed; v1 `__mul__` (gaussian_measure.py:1674-1697) dropped inverse_covariance and `__add__`/`__sub__` (1707-1758) dropped both factor and inverse, keeping only a sample closure. The first pass had buried this in the notes. Minor additions not worth their own entry: `with_dense_covariance` memoises its result (v1 recomputed every call, gaussian_measure.py:878-904); the constructor validates operator domains and SELF_ADJOINT\|POSITIVE_SEMIDEFINITE trait claims (v1 checked nothing); `ProductMeasure.factor(key)`; `GaussianMixture.__len__`.  VERIFIED CLAIMS: v1 constructor required covariance or covariance_factor (gaussian_measure.py:112-115); v1 from_covariance_matrix was Galerkin-only (from_matrix(..., galerkin=True) at 262), always eigh, and attached a pseudo-inverse factor built without the Gram matrix (Li = Di @ U.T at 259); v1 randomized KL required other.inverse_covariance_set (2197-2201) and summed three per-probe estimates (2230-2266); v1 had no Estimate type; v1 sampling used np.random global state throughout (hilbert_space.py:253, gaussian_measure.py:318, 643, 1786-1793, 2231, low_rank.py:760-934, 1123); v1 credible_set(rng=) was forwarded to `_resolve_spectrum` (1884) which never used it, and `_sampling_radius` (1761) took no rng; no v1 mixture, log density on a measure, normalising constant on a measure, or has_expectation/has_covariance notion exists.  RENAMES (ported, not additions): sample_set -> can_sample; inverse_covariance -> precision; inverse_covariance_factor -> precision_factor (both now return None instead of raising AttributeError); from_direct_sum -> from_product (adds `labels`, a v2 DirectSum feature; builds a block-diagonal covariance *factor* and precision_factor when every component has one, where v1 composed samplers and only built a block precision); affine_mapping(operator=, translation=, affine_operator=) -> affine_map(operator, translation=) plus push_forward(AffineOperator); bare translation -> `translate(v)`; credible_set(probability, geometry='ellipsoid') -> credible_set(level=); ambient_ball(probability, radius_method=, spectrum_size=) -> ambient_ball(level=, method=, rank=); kl_divergence 'randomized' -> 'stochastic', hutchinson_size_estimate -> samples, rtol -> sample_rtol; nuclear_norm/hilbert_schmidt_norm `exact=` -> `method=`; low_rank_approximation(size_estimate, ...) -> low_rank_approximation(rank=, rng=); two_point_covariance uses `space.dirac(point).representer` instead of `dirac_representation`; directional_covariance/directional_variance/two_point_covariance moved to the base class; `sample=` callables now take `rng`. `low_rank.white_noise_measure` has no v2 counterpart in this module (white noise is now `HilbertSpace.white_noise(rng=)`). v2 `_stochastic_trace` draws probes as white noise on the space; v1 `low_rank.random_trace` (low_rank.py:1053-1140) already handled the metric by working in components, so this is not a correctness addition.  SEMANTIC CHANGES ON PORTED THINGS: from_standard_deviation(s) now draw white noise with respect to the space's inner product and from_standard_deviations builds a DiagonalLinearOperator on the space (v1 mapped from a Euclidean coefficient space, gaussian_measure.py:172-211), so results differ on any non-orthonormal space; from_covariance_matrix attaches no precision for a singular covariance (v1 attached a pseudo-inverse factor); as_multivariate_normal works on any CoordinateSpace with Gram correction; with_regularized_inverse no longer adds damping noise to the sampler (v1 906-965 did) nor accepts `preconditioner`, and no longer short-circuits when damping == 0 and a precision exists; with_sparse_approximation is drastically reduced (absolute threshold on a dense matrix + PSD check; no sparse LU inverse, max_nnz, correlation threshold, deflated diagonal or parallel; v1 967-1100) and reads `self._covariance.matrix` directly so it fails with AttributeError rather than a message on a precision-only measure.  DROPPED FROM V1 GaussianMeasure (the owner's worry): directional_statistics (1362), zero_expectation (1405), __neg__ (1649), sample_pointwise_variance/std (502-558), deflated_pointwise_variance/std (560-735), from_samples with a single sample (304-310), credible_set geometries 'cameron_martin' and 'weakened_ellipsoid' plus weakened_ellipsoid() (872) and the whole fractional-operator machinery (1982-2121), open_set and rank kwargs on credible_set, callable/LowRankEig `spectrum=` input to ambient_ball (1879-1917), affine_mapping(inverse_solver=) KKT construction of a pushforward precision with its Jacobi-Schur preconditioner (1178-1210, 1795-1822; InvariantGaussianMeasure's water-filling preconditioner at symmetric_space.py:466-484), the 'model_space' formalism of conditioning, the randomized KL's ability to run with only other.inverse_covariance (v2 needs a square root on one side or a solver), and v1 kl 'auto' silently falling back to dense for non-invariant measures (v2 raises above dense_limit).  SMALL DEFECTS NOTICED WHILE READING: ProbabilityMeasure.two_point_covariance's docstring says NotImplementedError but raises TypeError, and calls self.covariance(...) without a None check; GaussianMeasure.mahalanobis_squared and grad_log_density docstrings say ValueError but raise NotImplementedError; the `_combine_*` specialisation protocol is private but is the extension point subclasses (invariant measures) must override to stay in class.

_Notes:_ Adversarial pass: every claimed addition was checked against v1 by grep (names, synonyms, the maths: dykstra/alternating/POCS/nearest point, minkowski, secular, prox/proximal/indicator, oracle/certificate, outer/inner bound, sample/random point, trace, __and__/__or__/__invert__/__contains__) and by reading the v1 candidates in pygeoinf/subsets.py, subspaces.py, convex_analysis.py, convex_optimisation.py, hilbert_space.py, linear_operators.py. Runtime claims were verified in the poetry env (/home/david/.cache/pypoetry/virtualenvs/pygeoinf-0ZCu7S8P-py3.12).  Nothing was removed outright — none of the 20 claims turned out to exist in v1 as such — but three were overstated and are rewritten above: (a) OrthogonalProjector.complement: v1 already accepted an explicit complement projector (`complement_projector=`, subspaces.py:32-48) and from_complement_basis supplied a real OrthogonalProjector (396-404); only the lazy fallback was `identity - self`; the traits and the back-link are what is new. (b) to_hyperplanes: v1 from_complement_basis built an explicit EuclideanSpace-codomain B (406-437), so the first pass's 'verified' example (from_complement_basis(X,[e0]).to_hyperplanes()) would have worked in v1 too; the new case is from_tangent_basis / bare-projector subspaces (v1 raised at 529-533), re-verified with from_tangent_basis. (c) cached (AA*)^-1: v1 from_linear_equation already built G_inv once for both translation and P_perp (300-320); the duplication was in pseudo_inverse/with_constraint_value, and v2's own _normal_inverse docstring ('three times over', 'two of those happen in the one constructor call') overstates v1. Two more were sharpened: support_bound's tolerance for unbounded parts matters mainly because v1 could not put a HalfSpace into a ConvexIntersection at all; the projection-based default `contains` had a one-class precedent in v1 AffineSubspace.is_element (568-586).  One genuine addition the first pass missed is added: ConvexSet.intersect now yields a ConvexIntersection for any two ConvexSets, and since HalfSpace, Hyperplane, Polytope and AffineSubspace are ConvexSets in v2 (they were plain Subsets in v1, subsets.py:1223/1354/1569, subspaces.py:96; v1 Subset.intersect at 141-157 required every part to be a ConvexSubset), mixed intersections such as `ball & half_space` gain projection, indicator and support_bound. Verified at runtime.  v2 docstring inaccuracies about v1 (not additions, for the owner's benefit): subspaces.LinearSubspace.from_kernel says the equation 'did not [get recorded] before' — v1 from_kernel did record _constraint_operator/_constraint_value (subspaces.py:736-741); the remark refers to an earlier v2 state. The _normal_inverse docstring's 'three times over' claim is discussed above.  Renames / moves, NOT additions: Subset.is_element -> contains (default rtol 1e-6 -> 1e-9); Sphere -> BallSurface; HyperPlane -> Hyperplane (now ConvexSet); ConvexSubset -> ConvexSet; ConvexSubset.directional_bound / SupportFunction.support_point -> ConvexSet.support_maximiser (returns the point only; v1 returned (point, value)); ConvexIntersection.support_upper_bound -> support_bound; Ellipsoid(center, radius, operator, inverse_operator=) -> Ellipsoid(precision, centre=, covariance=) with NormalisedEllipsoid folded in (v2 Ellipsoid is always the unit level set; the radius parameter is gone); Ellipsoid.form(x) -> mahalanobis_squared(x); AffineSubspace.tangent_space -> tangent; get_tangent_basis() -> OrthogonalProjector.basis() (now on any projector, so a complement basis is one call); OrthogonalProjector.from_basis(orthonormalize=True) -> from_basis(orthonormal=False) (inverted flag; v2 returns an OrthogonalProjector for an empty family where v1 returned a plain zero_operator); projection_operator / pseudo_inverse properties -> methods; LinearSubspace.complement property -> method; HalfSpace.normal_vector -> normal; HalfSpace.project (boundary) -> HalfSpace.boundary.project.  Behaviour changes worth a reviewer's eye: v1 Ball defaulted to open_set=True (subsets.py:1122), v2 Ball is always closed; Ball.contains tolerance is radius*(1+rtol) (v2) vs rtol*max(1,radius) (v1), so a zero-radius v2 ball admits only the exact centre; Hyperplane/HalfSpace.contains scale rtol by max(\|offset\|, \|\|x\|\|·\|\|normal\|\|, 1) where v1 used max(1,\|offset\|) (subsets.py:1290); ConvexIntersection.support_function raises NotImplementedError where v1 returned None; ConvexIntersection raises TypeError for a non-convex part (v1 did not check); AffineSubspace.boundary() returns self where v1 returned EmptySet; from_linear_equation / from_kernel default to CGSolver(rtol=1e-12) where v1 defaulted to CholeskySolver(galerkin=True); Complement/Intersection/Union no longer apply De Morgan; constructors flatten nested Intersection/Union (v1 flattened only via intersect/union); AffineSubspace.constraint_operator / constraint_value now raise AttributeError without an explicit equation where v1 fell back to (I-P) and (I-P)x0 (subspaces.py:216-237).  Dropped v1 functionality visible from these files (owner's stated worry): SublevelSet, LevelSet and the form/level/open_set machinery (open sets, closure(), is_open/is_closed, _warn_if_open, ConvexSubset.check() randomised convexity check); ConvexIntersection's max-functional with gradient/Hessian of the active constraint and feasible_lower_bound(); Ellipsoid radius parameter, normalized property and inverse_sqrt_operator; HalfSpace inequality_type '>=' and HalfSpace.support_function (HalfSpaceSupportFunction), distance_to, is_bounded, is_empty; HyperPlane.distance_to, normal_norm, dimension; Subset.is_empty; Subset.plot / SubspaceSlicePlotter hooks (plot.py's exact PolyhedralSet slice path); domain=None subsets; AffineSubspace.condition_gaussian_measure (Bayesian conditioning on a subspace), the solver/preconditioner properties and every preconditioner= keyword, from_tangent_basis(orthonormalize=, solver=); from_complement_basis no longer records a constraint operator (v1 built explicit B; v2 has_explicit_equation False, verified, so with_constraint_value/pseudo_inverse/constraint_operator are unavailable on such subspaces); LinearSubspace.from_complement_basis / from_tangent_basis / from_linear_equation as usable entry points (verified: LinearSubspace.from_complement_basis(X,[e0]) raises TypeError: LinearSubspace.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'translation', because the inherited AffineSubspace classmethods call cls(projector, translation=...)).  Duplication to watch (both in v2): Ball.indicator() returns numerics.convex.BallIndicator rather than the generic _SetIndicator (verified: Ball -> BallIndicator, HalfSpace -> _SetIndicator) — same semantics, two classes; Ball.support_function delegates to numerics.convex.SupportFunction.of_ball while Ellipsoid carries its own _EllipsoidSupport in geometry/convex.py; v1 kept all support functions in convex_analysis. Polytope.contains has a stray hasattr(plane, 'contains') guard that makes a non-Subset entry evaluate False rather than error.

_Notes:_ Adversarial pass: all ten v2 files read in full; v1 checked by reading forward_problem.py, inversion.py, linear_bayesian.py (core, evidence, preconditioners, surrogates, parameterised/data_reduced), linear_optimisation.py (least squares, minimum norm, both constrained classes), backus_gilbert.py in full, convex_optimisation.py (BundleResult, solve_support_values, KKTResult, ChambollePockResult, solve_primal_feasibility, PrimalKKTSolver, SmoothedDualMaster), nonlinear_optimisation.py defs, preconditioners.py defs, symmetric_space.py distance_localized_preconditioner, gaussian_measure.py credible_set/ambient_ball/sample, low_rank.py random_trace; plus GNU-grep sweeps of v1 for mixture, laplace, MAP/log_posterior, nystrom, gaspari, 'auto', inclusion/inner_hull/polytope/admissible, certificate, family, warm, discrepancy, prior_only/budget/is_feasible, extremal, resolution/averaging, push_forward/propagat. (Note: the shell's grep is ugrep; --include behaves differently, so /usr/bin/grep was used for the counts that matter.)  REMOVED OR DOWNGRADED because v1 had it: (1) DualFeasibleProperty.certificate is not new. v1 solve_support_values (pygeoinf/convex_optimisation.py:1393-1440) returned (values, lambdas, diagnostics) with lambdas = the optimal lambda per direction, and BundleResult (:704-731) carries x_best. v2's certificate() re-exposes that for a single direction. Worse, v2 support_values (backus.py:1197-1330) returns only the values array, dropping the lambdas and diagnostics v1 returned -- a small loss. (2) FeasibleProperty's 'extremal model' is not new. v1 KKTResult.m (convex_optimisation.py:1493-1510) and ChambollePockResult.m (:1519-1540) return the optimal primal model; PrimalKKTSolver already solved the same two-multiplier ball/ball problem via Woodbury. What is new in FeasibleProperty is the mechanics (nested monotone bisection replacing fsolve; one cached eigendecomposition of A A* making each probe O(dim D)), plus inclusion_norm/admits/inner_hull. Entry rewritten; v1_nearest set to PrimalKKTSolver. (3) ForwardProblem.consistency_set is data_measure_from_model(model).credible_set(p) (forward_problem.py:178-197 + gaussian_measure.py:737) in one call. Kept only as a named convenience, not a capability. (4) normal_log_determinant: sampling to a tolerance was in v1 (method='variable', rtol) and the Sylvester split for the model-space formalism was in v1 log_evidence (:735-765). Kept for the dense/auto route, Estimate error bar and memo. v1's parallel/n_jobs for the probes have no counterpart in pygeoinf2/numerics/functional_calculus.py:641-652 log_determinant. (5) DiscrepancyPrinciple: the zero-model shortcut (chi^2 <= critical -> zero model, damping 0) and the rank-one Frechet derivative are both v1's (linear_optimisation.py:896-900, 953-1035); only the saturation-aware derivative and estimator_at are new, as the entry says.  ADDED (missed by the first pass): rng threading on synthetic_data / synthetic_model_and_data and general ProbabilityMeasure inputs on data_measure_from_model_measure / joint_measure (v1 sample() took no generator and everything was GaussianMeasure-typed); DiscrepancyPrinciple._linearise sharing one damping search between value and derivative (v1 mapping and derivative each re-ran _solve_discrepancy).  Confirmed ports (not additions), beyond those the first pass listed: LinearGaussianInversion.gain = kalman_operator; data_prior / joint_prior; mahalanobis incl. the Woodbury reduction (linear_bayesian.py:539-556); randomise-then-optimise sampler; surrogate / low_rank_surrogate (v1 :1126-1190, :1292-1351; v2 takes one rng/**kwargs rather than per-factor kwargs dicts); LeastSquares = least_squares_operator incl. the affine shift for a non-zero error expectation (v1 :306-320); the solver-factory argument (resolve_solver) = v1's preconditioner-as-LinearSolver on least_squares_operator/minimum_norm_operator (:275-284); ConstrainedLeastSquares / ConstrainedMinimumNorm = ConstrainedLinear*Inversion (:547-776, :1040-1330) incl. constraint_value_mapping and the (B M) p == w parameterisation pull-back; MinimumNorm(damping=0) = v1's error-free A*(AA*)^-1 fallback (:1032-1037); InvariantDistancePreconditioner's max_distance == 0 diagonal shortcut (symmetric_space.py:2772-2795). New but trivial accessors not listed as additions: ConstrainedLeastSquares.reduced / normal_operator / subspace and ConstrainedMinimumNorm.reduced (v1 kept _unconstrained_inversion private); LinearGaussianInversion.with_solver / inverse_normal_operator / solver (a consequence of the solver moving to the constructor); LeastSquares.residual_callback's report= callable and relative residual (v1 normal_residual_callback had message/print_progress); NormalOperator.assembled; TikhonovNormalOperator.base/shift.  Naming caution for the reviewer: v2 docstrings call both BackusInference.is_feasible and FeasibleProperty.is_feasible 'v1's test_data_compatibility'. v1's test (backus_gilbert.py:353-399) ran the discrepancy-principle minimum-norm inversion at a significance level and compared that model's norm with the bound -- a noisy-data test with a chi-squared threshold. v2 BackusInference.is_feasible is the error-free budget test r^2 - \|A*(AA*)^-1 d\|^2 >= 0, and FeasibleProperty.is_feasible is one support-value probe with a hardened noise ball. The v1 semantics (min-norm model at a chi-squared level vs bound) survive only as a composition: MinimumNorm(problem).for_data(data, level=...) then compare the model's norm to the bound. BackusInference keeps the v1 class name but is a different object.  Corrections to the first pass's 'deliberate removals' list: (a) the Woodbury preconditioners were NOT dropped -- pygeoinf2/numerics/preconditioners.py:483 WoodburyPreconditioner exists (out of scope here, but the note that they 'may be dropped' is wrong); the surrogate_* preconditioner factories collapse into surrogate(...) + any preconditioner; (b) the joblib parallel/n_jobs flags on the diagonal and localised preconditioners and on log-determinant probes are absent in v2's versions -- a real loss for large data spaces; (c) FeasibleProperty raises NotImplementedError on a non-orthonormal data space (backus.py:562-567) whereas v1 PrimalKKTSolver worked on any data space by forming P = G G* densely; (d) v2 support_values returns values only (see (1) above). The other removals the first pass listed are confirmed from the sources: model_space formalism without an error measure refused (v1 linear_bayesian.py:192-193 built Q^-1 + A* A); from_direct_sum refusing mixed error/no-error problems (v1 forward_problem.py:160-166 silently dropped errors); parameterised/data_reduced losing dense/parallel/n_jobs (v1 :334-432); parameterised requiring an explicit parameter prior (v1 :1353-1410 pulled the model prior back through parameterization.adjoint by default); ValueError rather than v1's RuntimeError when no damping reaches the chi-squared target (v1 :915, :947).  Headline genuinely new capabilities after checking: the estimator hierarchy with push_forward to property spaces (incl. sampler transport, and on set estimators); factored normal operators (NormalOperator, TikhonovNormalOperator, TikhonovFamily with warm-started sweeps); 'auto' formalism; dense/auto log-determinant with Estimate error bars and memoisation; the shared posterior/misfit solve; MAP/Laplace for nonlinear problems; Gaussian-mixture posteriors; the classical Backus-Gilbert optimal-averaging estimator with split error bars; the closed-form ellipsoid feasible set, budget and prior_only bracket; the nested-bisection primal route's spectral reduction; exact set-inclusion tests and inner polytopes; emptiness detection on the dual route; set-valued data errors on ForwardProblem; and the three v1 Bayesian preconditioners re-homed as LinearSolvers that also precondition Tikhonov operators, with the overlap-averaging, Galerkin-form and default-taper fixes.

_Notes:_ Verification method: listed every def in v1 (symmetric_space.py, sphere.py, circle.py, torus.py, line.py, plane.py) and v2, grepped all of v1 (including gaussian_measure.py, datasets.py, direct_sum.py) for each claimed name, its synonyms and the underlying maths, and read the candidate v1 implementations and all eight v2 files in full.  Result: no claimed addition was found fully present in v1, so none was removed. Several were partial and their summaries/v1_nearest were corrected: (a) PreparedPoints -- v1 already converted points once per operator (torus.py:1101, sphere.py:1566), so the new thing is the public reusable object, not the once-per-operator conversion; (b) pointwise_variance_at -- the exact per-point route was available in v1 as `directional_statistics(dirac_representation(p))` (gaussian_measure.py:1363); (c) covariance_function's non-invariant fallback is built on v1's `GaussianMeasure.two_point_covariance` (gaussian_measure.py:1340); (d) source_receiver_paths -- v1 shipped the same catalogues via `iris_stations`/`random_earthquakes`, new is the pairing + separation filter; (e) power_spectrum -- on the sphere v1 users had pyshtools' `spectrum()` one call away.  Genuine additions the first pass missed, now added: `PeriodicBox.geodesic_ball_quadrature` (1-D/2-D; v1 base raised NotImplementedError for everything but the sphere, symmetric_space.py:1629-1641), the KD-tree `_embedding` generalisation of `pairs_within_distance`/`cluster_points` to boxes with periodic wrap (v1 base was O(n^2), symmetric_space.py:1992/1929), and the `amplitude=` keyword on the kernel measures.  Corrections to the first pass's notes: behaviour-change item (5) is wrong as stated -- v1 sphere `vector_multiply` already returned the untruncated grid product `x1 * x2` (sphere.py:819), so leaving products on the grid is a change relative to an earlier v2 revision, not to v1. Also v2's `random_points` docstring says it \"lived on the sphere\" in v1; it was on the v1 base (symmetric_space.py:1743). Additional behaviour changes worth a look: `Sphere.random_point` now draws longitude in [-180,180) (v1 [0,360), sphere.py:468) and `project_function` hands the callback longitudes in [-180,180); `Sphere.geodesic_distance` uses atan2 rather than arccos (numerically better, same maths); `Sphere.earthquakes(minimum_magnitude=)` filters the cached table, whereas v1's `min_magnitude` only affected a fresh download (datasets.py:186-234); `Sphere.geodesic_quadrature`'s antipodal rejection and zero-length handling are ports of sphere.py:480-513.  Trivial new properties not listed as additions: `Sphere.area`, `grid_shape`, `colatitudes`, `longitudes`, `PeriodicBox.volume`, `grid_axes` (v1 circle/torus/line/plane had `points()` for grid coordinates; the sphere had none), `Box.domain_volume`, `correlated_measure(labels=)`.  v1 functionality confirmed absent from these v2 files (may live elsewhere in v2; flagging): `matrix_free`/`parallel`/`n_jobs`/`lazy_quadrature` on point-evaluation and path operators (v2 has only finufft `nthreads`, and `n_jobs` in pointwise_variance_at); `random_domain_points`; `distance_localized_preconditioner` (with its Gaspari-Cohn taper); `geodesic_integral`/`geodesic_integral_representation` as single LinearForms; `dirac_representation` (now `dirac(p).representer`); `wavevector_indices`; the `from_covariance`/`from_heat_kernel_prior`/`from_sobolev_kernel_prior` classmethod constructors; `InvariantGaussianMeasure`/`CorrelatedInvariantGaussianMeasure` arithmetic, `kl_divergence`, `nuclear_norm`, `hilbert_schmidt_norm`, `sample_power_measure`; `InvariantLinearAutomorphism.apply_function/exp/log`; `extend=`/`grid=` options on the sphere (only DH with sampling 1 or 2 remains); `iris_stations(include_names=)`; per-geometry `plot*`/`create_map_figure`/`plot_error_bounds` helpers. The earlier notes' rename/wrapper list (spectral_operator, invariant_operator, invariant_measure merging the norm_scaled/point_value_scaled families, sobolev_measure/heat_measure, correlated_measure family, coefficient_operator, multiplication_operator, multiply/sqrt, dirac(unsafe=), lift_formal_adjoint, truncation_degree_for incl. `power_of_two`, stations/earthquakes/domain_mask(ocean=), sampling=2 == DH2, pointwise_multiply duplicating multiply) was checked and stands.

| `plotting.distributions.plot_densities / plot_corner: sampled (non-Gaussian) measures` | behaviour (new capability on ported functions) | Both entry points accept any measure that can be sampled, not only a GaussianMeasure: marginals and pairwise panels are drawn from draws by kernel density estimation, with 2D contour levels chosen to enclose the same probability mass as the sigma contour (chi2.cdf(levels**2, df=2)); `samples=` and `rng=` keywords control the draws. Confirmed new: v1 plot_corner_distributions raised TypeError for anything but a GaussianMeasure and v1 has no KDE anywhere (grep gaussian_kde/histogram: none). The draws are taken serially one sample() call at a time with no n_jobs. | pygeoinf/plot.py:28 plot_1d_distributions and plot.py:1788 plot_corner_distributions (Gaussian only; TypeError at plot.py:1831-1835) |
| `plotting.distributions density='binned' \| 'kde'` | keyword (new algorithm) | Kernel density for sampled measures by binning draws onto the plot grid and convolving once with the Scott's-rule kernel (gaussian_filter1d in 1D; an anisotropic fftconvolve kernel in 2D via _binned_density_2d), with density='kde' selecting exact scipy.stats.gaussian_kde evaluation and a ValueError for any other string. | none (no KDE, histogram or fftconvolve in v1) |
| `plotting.distributions.plot_densities index=` | keyword (new capability) | Selects which component of a multi-component measure is drawn as the 1D marginal, with IndexError when out of range. | pygeoinf/plot.py:104-110 (plot_1d_distributions hard-codes expectation[0] and covariance[0,0]) |
| `plotting.distributions._grid (per-curve adaptive grid)` | behaviour (new algorithm, private helper behind public functions) | Each density curve is evaluated on the union of a coarse grid over the shared window and a fine grid over its own +/- width standard deviations, so a posterior far narrower than the prior on the twin axis is resolved whatever the ratio. v1 used one uniform grid sized at 25 points per std of the narrowest peak, clamped to [1000, 10000] points, which aliases at extreme ratios. | pygeoinf/plot.py:139-149 (uniform x_axis, n_pts = min(10000, max(1000, span/min_std*25))) |
| `plotting.distributions.plot_corner prior density on a twin axis; legend/posterior_label/prior_label/truth_label; axes=` | behaviour + keywords (partly new) | New: the prior is drawn as a dotted density (from draws if sampled) on a twinx of each diagonal panel instead of v1's secondary x-axis in prior-sigma units; the legend labels are configurable (posterior_label/prior_label/truth_label) and the key is built from synthetic Line2D handles; and `axes=` lets the corner plot be drawn into an existing N x N grid (v1 always called plt.subplots itself). Not new: having a legend in the empty top-right panel (v1 plot.py:2143-2151 did that with fixed labels 'Posterior PDF' / 'True Value'), the truth marker, the Mahalanobis widening of contour levels, and the 1.05 buffer to keep the truth in frame. | pygeoinf/plot.py:1963-1985 (secondary_xaxis 'Distance from Prior Mean'), 1911-1917 (own plt.subplots), 2134-2158 (legend with fixed labels) |
| `plotting.fourier.plot_error_bounds (lower, upper, centre=)` | function (ported with changed signature; centre= and validation new) | Shades the band between two explicit bound fields on a 1D PeriodicBox, optionally drawing the estimate as a centre line (left on the axes as .centre_line), validating each field's shape against the space, and raising ValueError on a box of more than one dimension. v1 took (u, u_bound) and shaded u - u_bound .. u + u_bound with no centre line and no validation; a v1 call site must now pass u - s, u + s. v1 line.py's full= (show the tapered padding) is gone. | pygeoinf/symmetric_space/circle.py:787 plot_error_bounds and line.py:773 plot_error_bounds |
| `plotting.sphere renderer: dateline rolling fast path` | behaviour (new performance path) | Rolls the [0,360) grid to [-180,180) and builds explicit cell edges (the first cell drawn as two halves at each map edge) so no pcolormesh cell straddles cartopy's antimeridian cut, keeping the mesh on cartopy's fast path (documented 1.3 s -> ~0.1 s per map at lmax 128); contour routes close the seam by repeating the first column at +180. v1 handed u.lons()/u.lats() straight to pcolormesh/contourf. | pygeoinf/symmetric_space/sphere.py:1993-1997 (contourf/pcolormesh on lons, lats directly) |
| `plotting.sphere renderer and plot_points: colorbar=None auto-on with colorbar_label, title=` | keywords (minor capability) | A colorbar_label implies a colourbar unless colorbar=False, and title= sets the axes title. Also new: the renderer accepts a bare grid array as well as an SHGrid (via space.grid_values) and validates its shape; set_global is applied when no map_extent is given. Not new: vmin/vmax (v1 accepted them through **kwargs and read them back with kwargs.get), levels (v1 accepted levels in kwargs), lat_interval/lon_interval in gridlines_kwargs (v1 had them with a 30-degree default and LongitudeFormatter/LatitudeFormatter, both of which v2 drops), and attaching the bar as .colorbar. | pygeoinf/symmetric_space/sphere.py:1957-1958, 1980-1988, 2009-2023, 2025-2032 (colorbar=False, colorbar_kwargs, vmin/vmax via kwargs, lat/lon_interval default 30) |
| `plotting.sphere.plot_paths` | function (ported with new implementation) | Draws a set of great-circle paths as one LineCollection (documented 528 ms -> 36 ms for 960 paths on PlateCarree), sampling each path with Sphere.geodesic_quadrature(count=) and splitting at dateline crossings so no piece is drawn across the whole map. What is new is the batching, the explicit sampling and the dateline split. Not new: following the great circle — v1's plot_geodesic used transform=ccrs.Geodetic(), which cartopy also renders along the geodesic. Dropped relative to v1: the sources/receivers scatter (plot_sources/plot_receivers/source_kwargs/receiver_kwargs), the automatic coastline, and a single-path plot_geodesic. | pygeoinf/symmetric_space/sphere.py:2156 plot_geodesic_network (one ax.plot per path via plot_geodesic at sphere.py:2133 with ccrs.Geodetic) |
| `parallel.resolve_jobs` | function | Normalises an n_jobs request: None/1 -> serial, -1 -> joblib.cpu_count() (affinity/container aware), ValueError for 0 or below -1. v1 had no validation: n_jobs=-1 went straight to joblib.Parallel, gated by a separate parallel=False flag (`jobs = n_jobs if parallel else 1`). | none (pygeoinf/linear_operators.py:691, 737 `jobs = n_jobs if parallel else 1`; gaussian_measure.py:477-480) |
| `parallel.parallel_map` | function | Generic `[f(x) for x in items]` under joblib.Parallel when n_jobs > 1 and there are >= 2 items, otherwise a plain comprehension with joblib never imported. Replaces v1's two column-specific helpers and the ~20 ad hoc Parallel(n_jobs)(delayed(...)) calls scattered through gaussian_measure, linear_operators, linear_forms, low_rank, linear_bayesian, preconditioners, convex_optimisation and sphere.py. v1's parallel_mat_mat and parallel_compute_dense_matrix_from_scipy_op have no direct equivalent. | pygeoinf/parallel.py:20 parallel_mat_mat and parallel.py:41 parallel_compute_dense_matrix_from_scipy_op; ad hoc Parallel at gaussian_measure.py:480, linear_operators.py:639/654/703/764, linear_forms.py:242, low_rank.py:1130, linear_bayesian.py:865/983, preconditioners.py:365/511, convex_optimisation.py:1452, sphere.py:1585/1618/1682 |
| `parallel: nesting guard (serial inside a worker)` | behaviour | parallel_map detects via joblib's get_active_backend().nesting_level that it is already inside a worker and runs serially, so n_jobs can be forwarded between loops without joblib turning the inner request into threads inside a worker (which crashes pyshtools). No counterpart in v1 (grep nesting/get_active_backend: none). | none |
| `parallel: one-thread-per-worker default and parallel_config passthrough` | behaviour | Unless a joblib.parallel_config context is already active, parallel_map wraps the run in parallel_config(backend='loky', inner_max_num_threads=1) so workers do not oversubscribe BLAS/OpenMP; an active context is respected entirely (backend, thread budget, dask/ray). v1 offered only a global, manual utils.configure_threading (threadpoolctl) and let joblib default to cores // n_jobs. _context_is_set reads joblib's private `_backend` thread-local and `default_parallel_config`, which is version-fragile. | pygeoinf/utils.py:4-14 configure_threading (threadpool_limits applied globally by the user) |
| `testing.check_space: equality/hash/rebuild= and a fuller axiom set` | keyword / behaviour (on ported check) | New relative to v1's HilbertSpaceAxiomChecks: asserts a space equals itself and is hashable, and with rebuild= that an independently built space compares equal and hashes equally (v1 spaces are unhashable); checks the axpy/scale_inplace return-value contract (v1's mutate and return None); checks commutativity, associativity, negation, scaling by one, scalar associativity and distributivity over scalar addition, positive-definiteness of the inner product, and norm == sqrt(squared_norm); compares vectors in the space's own norm rather than by np.allclose on components. Not new: the mean() check (v1 _check_basis_and_expectation checked sample_expectation), gram_schmidt orthonormality, copy independence, in-place ops agreeing with out-of-place. Dropped: the triangle-inequality check, the measure= sampler for test vectors, and v1's printed progress. | pygeoinf/checks/hilbert_space.py:13 HilbertSpaceAxiomChecks (check at :175; sample_expectation check at :167-173; no __hash__ anywhere in v1) |
| `testing.check_coordinates` | function | Checks a CoordinateSpace: Gram matrix symmetric and positive definite, identity Gram iff is_orthonormal, components of shape (dim,), coordinate map additive/homogeneous and round-tripping both ways, inner product equal to c_x^T G c_y, apply_gram/solve_gram consistent with the matrix and each other, basis_vector components, plus check_representer per trial. v1 had only the round trips, the basis-vector check and a disabled Riesz check; nothing on the Gram matrix. Forms the dense Gram matrix, so it is a small-space check. | pygeoinf/checks/hilbert_space.py:75-87 _check_mapping_identities, :156-165 basis_vector check, :58-72 _check_riesz_representation (commented out at :219) |
| `testing.check_representer` | function | Checks that representer(g) for derivative-convention components g satisfies (v, x) == g . c_x for random x, i.e. that the Riesz map is applied and a derivative is not being passed off as a gradient. | none (closest: pygeoinf/checks/hilbert_space.py:58 _check_riesz_representation on to_dual/duality_product, disabled in check()) |
| `testing.check_white_noise` | function | Statistical check that space.white_noise has identity covariance on the space, E[(x,u)(x,v)] == (u,v), with rtol meant to scale as 1/sqrt(samples); the failure message names the N(0,I)-components-vs-N(0,G^-1) error. v1 HilbertSpace has no white_noise method (grep: only low_rank.white_noise_measure, never checked). | none (pygeoinf/low_rank.py:34 white_noise_measure exists but is unchecked) |
| `testing.check_operator: adjoint space, memoisation and involution-by-identity checks` | behaviour (on ported check) | Beyond linearity and the adjoint identity (both in v1), asserts the adjoint's domain/codomain are the right spaces, that A.adjoint is the same object on each access, and that A.adjoint.adjoint is A by identity (v1 checked (A*)* == A by value only, and rebuilt the adjoint on each access). Dropped: v1's (A+B)* == A*+B*, (aA)* == aA*, (AB)* == B*A* and the dual-operator identities with a second operator. | pygeoinf/checks/linear_operators.py:27 _check_linearity, :58 _check_adjoint_definition, :75-120 _check_algebraic_identities ((A*)* == A by value at :112) |
| `testing.check_traits` | function | Verifies every Traits flag an operator claims: SELF_ADJOINT symmetry and endomorphism, POSITIVE_SEMIDEFINITE / POSITIVE_DEFINITE quadratic forms, ISOMETRY norm preservation, IDEMPOTENT A A == A, UNITARY and INVERTIBLE squareness, INVERTIBLE full rank via the dense component matrix. v1 has no trait system; LinearOperator.self_adjoint(...) etc. were constructors that recorded nothing and verified nothing. | none (pygeoinf/linear_operators.py:124 self_adjoint, :204 from_formally_self_adjoint, :442 self_adjoint_from_matrix are unverified constructor conveniences) |
| `testing.check_derivative: central differences, has_derivative guard, seeded rng and step=` | behaviour (on ported check) | The finite-difference derivative check now uses central differences along unit-normalised random directions with a documented step default near sqrt(eps), fails cleanly when the operator has no derivative, and draws its directions from an explicit rng. v1 used a one-sided forward difference with fixed h=1e-7, an effective rtol floor of 1e-4, and NumPy's global random state. Dropped: v1's sum/scalar/chain-rule derivative checks against a second operator (op2=) and the AffineOperatorAxiomChecks. | pygeoinf/checks/nonlinear_operators.py:16-63 _check_derivative_finite_difference (forward difference; check() at :152 uses np.random.randn) |
| `testing.check_gradient` | function | Checks a Functional's gradient against central differences of the functional along random unit directions, (grad, d) vs (f(x+hd)-f(x-hd))/2h; the message explains a Gram-factor mismatch as a derivative passed where a gradient was wanted. v1's NonLinearForm had gradient/hessian but no check method at all. | none (pygeoinf/nonlinear_forms.py:95 gradient exists; no check anywhere for forms) |
| `testing.check_second_derivative` | function | Checks operator.second_derivative(point, d)(e) against central differences of operator.derivative(.)(e) along d, with a looser tolerance than the first-derivative check. | none (pygeoinf/nonlinear_forms.py:131 hessian existed unchecked; no Hessian check in checks/) |
| `testing.check_measure` | function | Draws samples from a ProbabilityMeasure and compares the sample mean against the declared expectation (six standard errors) and the sample covariance along probe directions against (C u, v) with a sqrt(C_ii C_jj)-scaled tolerance; unclaimed moments are skipped. v1 GaussianMeasure has no self-consistency check between sampler and covariance (grep 'def check' in gaussian_measure.py: none). | none |
| `testing.check_projection` | function | Checks a ConvexSet's project(): the image lies in the set, projecting twice equals projecting once, and no sampled nearby point of the set is closer (the nearest-point / variational inequality property). | none (pygeoinf/subsets.py:682 ConvexSubset.check tests only the convexity inequality of the defining functional; project at subsets.py:1310, 1475 is unchecked) |
| `testing: explicit rng= on every check` | behaviour (cross-cutting) | Every check takes a numpy Generator and draws its probe vectors and scalars from it, so a failing check is reproducible; v1's mixins used np.random.randn / np.random.uniform global state and space.random() with no seed argument. | pygeoinf/checks/hilbert_space.py:213 (np.random.randn), nonlinear_operators.py:171-173, subsets.py:709 (np.random.uniform), hilbert_space.py:244 random() with no rng |
| `compat.AdaptedSpace` | class | Presents a v1 HilbertSpace as a v2 CoordinateSpace by delegating to_components/from_components/inner_product/axpy/ax, reading apply_gram off v1's to_dual and solve_gram off from_dual, supplying an rng-driven random() (v1's ignores any generator), and drawing corrected white noise N(0, G^-1) rather than v1's N(0, I) components. Takes gram='auto'\|'diagonal'\|'dense'. __init__ does not call CoordinateSpace.__init__; _V1SpaceKey hashes on dim only. | none (the wrapped objects are v1's; v1 had no adapter layer) |
| `compat.AdaptedSpace.has_diagonal_metric / _probe_is_diagonal` | property / behaviour | Detects whether the wrapped v1 space's Gram matrix is diagonal with two seeded random probes G s == diag(G 1) * s (a few Gram applications, not O(dim^2)), caches the diagonal, and under gram='auto' warns before falling back to a dense factorisation for white noise. | pygeoinf/hilbert_space.py is_orthonormal / OrthogonalHilbertSpace metric (declared by the class, never detected) |
| `compat.AdaptedOperator` | class | Presents a v1 LinearOperator as a v2 LinearOperator over adapted spaces, caching v1's adjoint once (v1 rebuilds it on every attribute access) and accepting caller-claimed Traits since v1 records none. | none |
| `compat.adapt_space / adapt_operator / adapt_form` | functions | Idempotent wrappers returning v2 objects for v1 spaces, operators and LinearForms (a LinearForm becomes LinearFunctional.from_derivative_components since v1 stores form components in the derivative convention); already-v2 inputs pass through. | none |

_Notes:_ Method: read all seven v2 files in full and the v1 counterparts (pygeoinf/plot.py plot_1d_distributions and plot_corner_distributions; pygeoinf/parallel.py; pygeoinf/utils.py; pygeoinf/checks/{hilbert_space,linear_operators,nonlinear_operators,affine_operators}.py; the plotting sections of symmetric_space/{sphere,circle,line,plane,torus}.py; subsets.ConvexSubset.check). Grepped v1 for every claimed name and for the underlying mechanisms (gaussian_kde/histogram/fftconvolve/chi2, LineCollection/Geodetic, singledispatch, plt.show/get_backend, joblib Parallel/parallel_config/cpu_count/nesting_level/threadpool, white_noise, __hash__, self_adjoint/trait flags, hessian, project/check, adapt/compat).  REMOVED from the claimed list: - "plotting.fourier PeriodicBox renderer (1D and 2D in one)": not an addition. v1 already plotted 1D boxes (circle.py:760 plot, line.py:741 plot) and 2D boxes (plane.py:757 plot, torus.py:1229 plot); merging them behind one registration is the dispatch mechanism already listed under plotting.base.plot. The only genuinely new bits are a shape ValueError and a NotImplementedError above two dimensions, which are too small to stand as an addition. What this merge DROPS from v1's box renderers is more notable: contour=, contour_lines=, contour_lines_kwargs, num_levels (plane/torus), full= (line/plane: show the tapered padding), the float form of symmetric=, and v1's horizontal colourbar default.  CORRECTED (kept, summary rewritten): - check_space: the mean() check is NOT new (v1 hilbert_space.py:167-173 checked sample_expectation); moved that to "not new" and listed the genuinely new axioms and the dropped triangle inequality / measure= sampler. - plot_paths: v1's plot_geodesic used transform=ccrs.Geodetic(), so v1 already followed the great circle; the new part is the LineCollection batching, explicit sampling and dateline split, and v1's sources/receivers scatter is dropped. - sphere renderer keywords: vmin/vmax were accepted in v1 via **kwargs (sphere.py:1980-1988), and lat_interval/lon_interval existed in v1 with a 30-degree default and coordinate formatters that v2 drops; only colorbar_label auto-on, title=, bare-array input and the shape check are new. - plot_corner legend: v1 plot.py:2143-2151 already drew a legend in the empty top-right panel (fixed labels), so only the configurable labels, the twin-axis prior density and axes= are new (the v2 docstring's "v1 had one; v2 lost it" refers to an intermediate v2 state, not to v1). - colour_limits: the symmetric option existed inline in all four v1 2D renderers; only the factoring, the explicit-limit-wins rule and the exact (non-1.2x) extent are new. - moments: v1 also accepted scipy frozen multivariate normals (plot.py:106-109); v2 does not, and a frozen distribution now fails with AttributeError on .can_sample rather than the documented TypeError.  ADDED (missed by the first pass): - plot_corner axes= (draw into an existing N x N grid); v1 always built its own figure (plot.py:1911-1917). Folded into the plot_corner entry. - check_derivative: central differences with a documented step, has_derivative guard, unit-normalised directions (v1 nonlinear_operators.py:16-63 used forward differences with h=1e-7 and a 1e-4 floor). - testing: explicit rng= across every check (v1 mixins used np.random global state). - Deferred cartopy import with an install hint, and symmetric_space no longer importing matplotlib/cartopy at all (v1 sphere.py imports cartopy at module top) — folded into the plot registry entry.  Drops/narrowings a "what was dropped" audit should confirm, sitting beside these additions: - plotting.sphere: no plot_points/plot_paths registrations for box spaces (v1 plane.py:861/939/968 and torus.py:1298/1362/1407 had plot_points, plot_geodesic, plot_geodesic_network); no single-path plot_geodesic; plot_points lost coasts/borders/rivers/gridlines/map_extent and its default zorder/edgecolors; contour_lines_kwargs and num_levels gone (contour-line style fixed to black 0.5); the v1 float scale factor for symmetric= is gone; gridline default interval (30) and Longitude/LatitudeFormatter are gone; colourbar default orientation changed from horizontal to vertical. - plotting.fourier: see the removed item above; plot_error_bounds signature changed from (u, u_bound) to (lower, upper). - plotting.distributions: show_true_value_in_legend and legend_position gone; plot_densities title defaults to None (v1 had a default string, fontsize 16); prior_labels/labels must be sequences (v1 accepted a bare str and wrapped it); plot_corner refuses fewer than two components (v1 handled n_dims == 1 at plot.py:1919, 2152-2157); v1's filled mode drew pcolormesh + figure colourbar + a red 1-sigma dashed contour, v2 fills with contourf levels and no colourbar; v1's prior secondary x-axis in prior-sigma units is replaced by a dotted prior density; v1's parallel=/n_jobs on the dense covariance build are gone and sampled draws are serial. - plotting.base.plot: docstring claims strict type dispatch with no inheritance, but singledispatch follows the MRO, so subclasses of Sphere/PeriodicBox do inherit the registration. - parallel: parallel_mat_mat and parallel_compute_dense_matrix_from_scipy_op have no direct equivalent; utils.configure_threading (threadpoolctl) is not here; _context_is_set relies on joblib private internals. - testing: v1's _check_algebraic_identities (sum/scalar/composition adjoint and dual identities), _check_add_derivative/_check_scalar_mul_derivative/_check_matmul_derivative, the whole AffineOperatorAxiomChecks (translation recovery, affine combination, derivative consistency), the triangle-inequality check and the measure= sampler have no counterpart; check_coordinates forms the dense Gram (small spaces only). - compat: entirely new; CURRENT_STATE.md calls it a parity shim to be deleted at the rename.

### backends

| v2 | kind | what it does | nearest v1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `backends.mfem.MfemSpace` | class | A CoordinateSpace over a PyMFEM FiniteElementSpace whose vectors are mfem.Vector objects and whose Gram matrix is the assembled mass matrix, read once into SciPy CSR and factorised once with spla.factorized. Optionally restricted to the subspace vanishing on essential (Dirichlet) dofs; to_components/from_components map to and from the free dofs only, copying out of MFEM-owned memory. Genuinely new: v1 has no foreign vector type, no FEM space, and no space whose Gram matrix is a non-diagonal sparse matrix (v1 MassWeightedHilbertSpace makes the caller hand in mass and inverse-mass operators; OrthogonalHilbertSpace is diagonal only). | hilbert_space.MassWeightedHilbertSpace (/home/david/dev/pygeoinf/pygeoinf/hilbert_space.py:746) and hilbert_space.EuclideanSpace |
| `backends.mfem.MfemSpace.restrict / restrict_vector / essential_dofs / free_dofs / is_constrained / mass_matrix` | methods and properties | Index-based essential-boundary-condition machinery: restrict takes an mfem.SparseMatrix or ndarray over all dofs to its free-free block (sparse via CSR row-then-column slicing); restrict_vector copies the free entries of a full load vector; properties expose the constraint and the full assembled mass matrix. v1's only constrained-subspace notion (subspaces.LinearSubspace / AffineSubspace) is basis- or projector-based, not an index set. Note restrict_vector is never called directly by the tests (only through the form constructors). | subspaces.LinearSubspace (basis/projector based) |
| `backends.mfem.MfemSpace.white_noise_components` | method (override of CoordinateSpace hook) | Components with covariance M^-1, i.e. identity covariance in the space's own inner product, drawn by assembling MFEM's white-noise load (covariance M) and doing one mass solve; no Cholesky of M is formed. Genuinely new in substance, not only in mechanism: v1's white_noise_measure draws through covariance_factor.domain.random() (gaussian_measure.py:1789), which is HilbertSpace.random = from_components(randn) (hilbert_space.py:244) and is not overridden by MassWeightedHilbertSpace, so on a mass-weighted v1 space the draw is white in components, not in the metric, despite the docstring's claim (low_rank.py:34-47). | low_rank.white_noise_measure(domain).sample() (/home/david/dev/pygeoinf/pygeoinf/low_rank.py:34; metric-correct only when the Gram matrix is trivial) |
| `backends.mfem.essential_dofs_of` | function | Asks MFEM (GetEssentialTrueDofs) for the true-dof indices on a set of boundary attributes (all by default), validating attribute numbers against the mesh; produces the essential_dofs list both MfemSpace and MfemDofSpace accept. | none |
| `backends.mfem.operator_from_bilinear_form` | function | Turns an assembled, finalised mfem.BilinearForm into a LinearOperator by handing its (free-block) sparse matrix to LinearOperator.from_matrix in Galerkin form, so the adjoint's mass solve is done by the core. Only the FEM entry point and the essential-dof restriction are new; the Galerkin-matrix interpretation itself is v1's from_matrix(galerkin=True). | linear_operators.LinearOperator.from_matrix(..., galerkin=True) (/home/david/dev/pygeoinf/pygeoinf/linear_operators.py:378) |
| `backends.mfem.solver_from_bilinear_form` | function | Wraps an MFEM solver (default CGSolver + GSSmoother on the restricted system rebuilt as an mfem.SparseMatrix) as a LinearOperator equal to the inverse of the form's operator, applying the mass matrix first so a function rather than its coefficients is the right-hand side. New relative to v1: a foreign solver wrapped as an operator, a make_solver hook for user MFEM solvers/preconditioners (v1's analogue is CGSolver(preconditioning_method=...) on pygeoinf operators only), strict=True raising RuntimeError on non-convergence (v1 CGSolver silently returns after maxiter, linear_solvers.py:577-578), and keepalive references against MFEM's raw-pointer ownership. strict= is not exercised by the tests. | linear_solvers.CGSolver(rtol, maxiter)(operator) (/home/david/dev/pygeoinf/pygeoinf/linear_solvers.py:439) |
| `backends.mfem.functional_from_linear_form` | function | Turns an assembled mfem.LinearForm (a load vector) into a LinearFunctional via from_derivative_components, so its representer is M^-1 b. Mathematically v1 already does this: LinearForm(domain, components=b) on a MassWeightedHilbertSpace gets its representer through from_dual = M^-1 R_X^-1 (hilbert_space.py:815-824). New is only the MFEM entry point: free-dof restriction and the copy out of MFEM-owned memory. | linear_forms.LinearForm(domain, components=...) with MassWeightedHilbertSpace.from_dual (/home/david/dev/pygeoinf/pygeoinf/hilbert_space.py:815) |
| `backends.mfem.operator_from_linear_forms` | function | Stacks several assembled MFEM linear forms (sensor footprints) into one observation operator onto a Euclidean (or supplied) data space as a Galerkin-form matrix. v1 has the same construction generically: LinearOperator.from_linear_forms(forms) stacks LinearForm.components into a dense matrix with a metric-correct dual mapping (linear_operators.py:223-252). New here: the MFEM load-vector entry point, essential-dof restriction, and the codomain argument (v1 always uses EuclideanSpace(len(forms))). | linear_operators.LinearOperator.from_linear_forms (/home/david/dev/pygeoinf/pygeoinf/linear_operators.py:223) |

_Notes:_ Adversarial pass over v1 (/home/david/dev/pygeoinf/pygeoinf, current tree on branch refactor). Nothing was removed from the list: the current v1 tree has no mfem, finite element, mesh-based space, mass-matrix-as-Gram space, Matern/SPDE field, essential-dof machinery, or foreign vector type (grep over all v1 .py files including symmetric_space/ and data_assimilation/; only hits are 'mass matrix' in docstrings of MassWeightedHilbertSpace and low_rank.py:1071, and np.meshgrid). Four v1_nearest fields were corrected and summaries narrowed: (a) operator_from_linear_forms (both backends): the real v1 analogue is LinearOperator.from_linear_forms (linear_operators.py:223-252), which already stacks form components into a dense matrix with a metric-correct dual mapping, not point_evaluation_operator; what is new is the MFEM entry point, essential-dof restriction, the codomain argument, and (mfem_hilbert only) never forming the matrix. (b) functional_from_linear_form: v1 LinearForm(domain, components=b) + MassWeightedHilbertSpace.from_dual (hilbert_space.py:815-824) already yields M^-1 b; only the MFEM entry point is new. (c) white_noise_components / MfemHilbertSpace.white_noise: verified that v1 white_noise_measure samples via covariance_factor.domain.random() (gaussian_measure.py:1786-1793) -> HilbertSpace.random = from_components(np.random.randn(dim)) (hilbert_space.py:244-253), and MassWeightedHilbertSpace does not override random (hilbert_space.py:746-886), so on a mass-weighted v1 space the draw has component covariance I, i.e. covariance M in the space's metric -- the v1 docstring claim at low_rank.py:42-46 that it 'perfectly respects ... mass matrices' is not borne out. The v2 N(0, M^-1) draw is therefore a genuine addition in substance, not just mechanism; worth telling the owner since it is a silent v1 bug. (d) matern_measure: v1 sobolev_kernel_gaussian_measure(order, scale, expectation=) and norm_scaled_ variant (symmetric_space.py:1856-1895) is the same covariance family; v2 loses real order and the expectation keyword, gains meshes/BCs/anisotropy. Two entries added that the first pass missed: the Matern parameterisation helpers (_matern_parameters/_anisotropy/_matern_normalisation, mfem.py:863-948; unit pointwise variance via MFEM's normalisation is a different convention from v1's norm-scaled measure) and the PyMFEM memory-safety helpers (_to_scipy Finalized guard, _to_mfem entry-by-entry rebuild, keepalive tuples; mfem.py:73-97, 466-523). Historical precedent, not in current v1: git history shows a hand-rolled 1-D FEM package pygeoinf/interval (Lebesgue space with hat-function basis and cached Gram matrix, GeneralFEMSolver for -Laplace u = f with Dirichlet/mixed BCs, KL_sampler; commits bbfd494 'removed dolfinx solver' through 3c7aba2), deleted 2025-12-16 in 89f2c60, so an earlier v1 did have an FEM space with a mass-matrix Gram on an interval; v2's MFEM backends are its first general-mesh successor. Test coverage gaps (grep of pygeoinf2/tests/test_backends.py and test_mfem_hilbert.py): strict=, rotation, dot=, dimension=, essential_dof_array, restrict_vector (direct) and _System.apply_transpose have zero direct references; partial assembly, new_system, essential_dofs_of, white_noise_load, matern_measure, correlation_length and constrain are exercised. Verified previous-pass reviewer points: v1 MassWeightedHilbertSpace.__eq__ compares by operator equality (hilbert_space.py:837-850) whereas both v2 spaces key on id(finite_element_space); MfemHilbertSpace._key deliberately overrides the core MassWeightedSpace._key (spaces.py:903-913) which keys on the mass operator object. Stray 'rtol:' line in the matern_measure docstring at mfem.py:815-816 confirmed. Both v2 modules export six same-named functions dispatched by import, with mfem_hilbert importing four private helpers from mfem.py. Examples: pygeoinf2/examples/16_mfem_backend.py, 27_mfem_inverse.py, 29_mfem_hilbert.py.

## 11. Reviewer notes per unit

**hilbert_space.** FINAL after two adversarial reviews. Review A proposed no row changes and its extra findings (mass_inverse has no diagonal shortcut anywhere on the solver path; preconditioners.py:255-270 re-inlines subspace_projection; tests pin MassWeightedSpace as non-CoordinateSpace) were verified against the code and merged into the affected rows and dense_regressions. Review B proposed three status tightenings, all ACCEPTED after reading the cited code: (1) EuclideanSpace.subspace_projection subsumed -> lost: grep finds no v2 symbol; the only occurrence of the logic is the local restrict/extend closure in inference/preconditioners.py:255-268; from_matrix/from_vectors are generic escape hatches, not counterparts, and both review rounds record 'not done'. (2)/(3) MassWeightedHilbertSpace.to_components/from_components subsumed -> lost: MassWeightedSpace (spaces.py:802) bases HilbertSpace only and defines no component map; require_coordinates (operators.py:203) is an isinstance(CoordinateSpace) test so library dispatch refuses the weighted space regardless of what its vectors are; _relating_mass special-cases it (operators.py:114-116); tests/test_mfem_hilbert.py:125-127 asserts the non-composition; DESIGN.md:372-375 and the docstring (816-818) claim the opposite, so it is not a recorded decision. Calling base.to_components on shared vectors is a workaround outside the weighted space, which under this classification's usage of 'subsumed' (a named v2 symbol on the same object covering the capability) does not qualify. The MassWeightedHilbertModule.vector_multiply/vector_sqrt rows stay 'subsumed' because the parent-class row already carries 'lost' and the base's method is a real call on the same vectors; Review A flagged them as the weakest subsumptions and the row text now says so. Review B's extra behavioural note (basis_vector negative indices) was verified against v1 hilbert_space.py:398-399 and added to that row; its check_space observations (min(3,dim) vs min(5,dim), hard failure on dependent draws) were verified at testing.py:200 and added to the check row. The unit is largely re-expressed rather than ported one-to-one: the dual-space layer (DualHilbertSpace, to_dual/from_dual, riesz/inverse_riesz, duality_product) is removed by a recorded design decision (DESIGN.md §1 decision 1) and its capabilities are reachable through LinearFunctional (from_representer / from_derivative_components / representer / derivative_components) and CoordinateSpace.apply_gram/solve_gram/representer; component maps moved to CoordinateSpace; is_element removed by design. Those are agreed changes. Findings the owner should weigh: (1) EuclideanSpace.subspace_projection is lost, missing from the catalogue entirely, and v2 re-inlines it privately; v1 used it in linear_bayesian.py:956, torus.py:296, gaussian_measure.py:1218. (2) MassWeightedSpace is not a CoordinateSpace, so v1's delegated to_components/from_components (and with them basis_vector, is_orthonormal, coordinate_inclusion/projection, white_noise, matrix()) are lost on a weighted space over a coordinate base, even though its docstring and DESIGN.md:372-375 say the two compose and the catalogue marks it Ported. Its default M^{-1} is a CG solve per application with no diagonal shortcut (numerics/solvers.py:103-106, 834-862, 927-978), unlike the docstring's 'free when diagonal' claim; passing mass_solver=<inverse operator> restores v1 cost. (3) MassWeightedHilbertModule is lost with no agreed decision (catalogue 'Not ported', owner wants the functionality); DESIGN.md:1892 only argues it is unnecessary for v2's Sobolev spaces. Smaller points: sparse CSR metric/inverse_metric objects are gone and DiagonalMetricSpace.gram_matrix() is a dense n x n build (A Consider-15 not done) that _Identity's Galerkin matrix also reaches; testing.check_space lost the measure= sampler option (A Consider-19 partial); @final markers are gone (no record, but v2's fast paths rely on overriding those methods); `multiply` changed meaning (scalar -> pointwise) which silently misroutes v1 calls on a SymmetricSpace (REVIEW.md:215); basis_vector no longer accepts negative indices; EuclideanSpace now accepts dim 0; equality is exact-type rather than isinstance; zero is a method. compat.AdaptedSpace (compat.py:89-263) documents the v1->v2 mapping for the Riesz machinery and is a reliable cross-reference.
