**operators.** FINAL after two adversarial reviews. Written to /tmp/claude-1000/-home-david-dev-pygeoinf/d93e5baf-8aac-4918-917c-1c45c7801ad1/scratchpad/audit/operators.json. Review A (lost/subsumed/dropped rows) proposed no status changes; its one evidence nit -- the stacking block in algebra/direct_sum.py is ColumnLinearOperator (:665, DirectSum codomain), not RowLinearOperator (:747, DirectSum domain) -- was verified and applied to the from_linear_forms row. Review B (ported rows) proposed ten corrections; all ten were verified by reading the cited v1/v2 code and re-running a call-counting probe (poetry run python), and all were accepted: (1) derivative(x) -> at(x).derivative evaluates the value first on Operator (operators.py:303-305), LinearOperator (655-659), AffineOperator (2355-2356) and Functional (1878-1880, also the Hessian; (f+f).gradient runs the Hessian callable 4 times), so the rows nonlinear_operators.derivative, linear_operators.derivative_is_self, affine_operators.constant_derivative and nonlinear_forms.gradient move from ported to ported_changed and nonlinear_forms.derivative gains the cost note; (2) the __matmul__ row's claim that v2 saves a re-application of other(x) was inverted for derivative-only queries -- v2 evaluates the outer value too (probe Fv 1 vs v1 Fv 0); (3) has_derivative is unconditionally True for subclass-defined Functionals because Functional overrides _linearise (operators.py:270-281 vs 1878-1880), so NormFunctional + NormFunctional reports has_subgradient True and raises on use -- the subgradient regression is masked rather than merely reported absent; (4) from_formal_adjoint's coordinate path (1343-1399) performs no same-vectors check: an unrelated dense-metric space of matching dimension is accepted and check_operator passes (probe), whereas v1 raised 'Domain mismatch'; (5) v1's base extract_diagonals already padded to min(domain.dim, codomain.dim) (linear_operators.py:736, 775), so that 'change' was removed from the base-class row (it stays on the MatrixLinearOperator/Sparse/DiagonalSparse override rows, where it is genuine). Review B's two side observations are recorded in the derivative_info_propagation row and here: (phi @ AffineOperator).has_hessian is False because AffineOperator declares no second derivative (nodes.py:1013-1022) -- a v2-only gap since v1 propagated no Hessian through @; and DiagonalLinearOperator's domain == codomain requirement (already in the from_diagonal_values row) removes v1's ability to build a diagonal operator between two different spaces of equal dimension, e.g. a space and its mass-weighted counterpart, where the fallback is a dia_array through from_matrix with no calculus. No correction was rejected. ORIGINAL METHOD AND FINDINGS (retained): every row was established by reading pygeoinf2/algebra/operators.py, nodes.py, diagonal.py, linearisation.py, parallel.py, testing.py and compat.py in full, grepping the whole pygeoinf2 tree for v1 names, and a runtime probe of the algebra. The probe confirmed: Affine @ Affine -> _OperatorComposition; (f+g), 2*f, -f, f@A lose subgradients for subgradient-only from_callables functionals; from_callables without adjoint raises NotImplementedError on .adjoint(y); a LinearOperator into Reals is not a LinearFunctional; str(A) is a cheap repr; diagonals() returns 2-D; U @ D @ U.adjoint is recognised SELF_ADJOINT\|PSD; from_matrix keeps a dia_array sparse; AffineOperator accepts a mis-sized translation. Overall: the unit is present in v2 with a better algebra (structured nodes, traits, known-matrix propagation, fused component chains, functional calculus that v1 only documented) and stricter validation (domain/codomain checks on every operation). Genuine losses: (1) the scipy.sparse.linalg.LinearOperator interchange format and its parallel matmat (DESIGN.md:1386/1504 record it as deferred to M3, so 'lost' not 'dropped_deliberately'); (2) automatic adjoint derivation when none is supplied (and a stale from_callables docstring claiming otherwise, operators.py:1066-1069); (3) subgradient propagation through the functional algebra, masked for subclass functionals by a spurious has_derivative; (4) Affine @ Affine closure; (5) LinearForm in-place ops, copy, and the mapping-probing constructor; (6) the op2 algebraic identity checks and GaussianMeasure sampling in check(); (7) matrix(by='auto')/assembled() fail on adjoint-less operators with codomain.dim < domain.dim where v1 fell back to columns; (8) derivative-only queries now evaluate the value (and Hessian) as well; (9) from_formal_adjoint's space-mismatch check on coordinate spaces. Default changes a v1 user will notice: matrix()/diagonals() default form='auto' returns the GALERKIN form for operators claiming SELF_ADJOINT (v1 default was always the standard form); extract_diagonal is now 2-D; from_matrix requires form=; from_vectors is transposed; assembled() always stores components. Catalogue corrections: line 383 names from_derivative_matrix, which no longer exists (D-4 renamed it to from_matrix; DESIGN.md:713 is also stale) and no v2 helper stacks functionals into an R^N operator (ColumnLinearOperator gives a DirectSum codomain); line 295 claims check_operator handles affine operators, but it is typed LinearOperator, reads .adjoint and asserts linearity; line 382 'Ported' hides that from_tensor_product lost its multi-pair/weights form; line 110 'AffineOperator Ported' hides the F @ G regression. Dropped-deliberately rows (dual, self_dual, dual<->adjoint conversion) rest on DESIGN.md:35 decision 1 and DESIGN.md:1254-1261 plus V1_CATALOGUE.md:88/367/386; the owner's notes column on those rows is empty, so the agreement is via DESIGN.md rather than an explicit owner note. compat.py (adapt_space/adapt_operator/adapt_form) provides adapters for v1 objects and confirms v1 LinearForm.components are derivative components.

**direct_sum.** FINAL after two adversarial reviews. Review A proposed no row corrections; its three extra dense regressions and three terminology items were verified and merged (the Galerkin round-trip through _known_block_matrix at direct_sum.py:413/:420 and MatrixLinearOperator._in_form at operators.py:1766-1774; no apply_block on Block/Column/Row; the compat.py to_dual note; the empty-list IndexError-vs-ValueError inconsistency; block-index access). One factual point in Review A's third item was corrected: while no test or example calls .matrix() on a Column/Row operator, production code does — inference/backus.py:408-411 builds a ColumnLinearOperator and _self_adjoint_spectrum (:57) takes .matrix(form='galerkin') of joint @ joint.adjoint, so the Column/Row dense regression is exercised in a shipped code path. Review B's six corrections were all verified against the code and accepted: (1-2) ColumnLinearOperator._compute_dense_matrix and RowLinearOperator._compute_dense_matrix moved from 'subsumed' to 'lost' — neither ColumnLinearOperator/ColumnOperator (direct_sum.py:618-693) nor RowLinearOperator/RowOperator (:696-769) defines _known_matrix, the base hook returns None (operators.py:772-787) and matrix() probes (:733-770); the v1 method's entire content was the vstack/hstack fast path, and the cited v2 'replacement' is code the user writes, matching the standard already applied to _check_block_indices. The generic probe still yields a correct matrix, which is recorded in the row so the loss is not overstated. (3-5) _subspace_inclusion_mapping, ColumnLinearOperator._mapping and BlockDiagonalLinearOperator._mapping moved from 'ported' to 'ported_changed' for the list->tuple return change, consistent with copy/from_components/zero. (6) inner_product_via_dual keeps ported_changed but its description was corrected: DirectSum overrides only inner_product (:194) and not squared_norm/norm (:186-220), and _CoordinateDirectSum's MRO (DirectSum, CoordinateSpace, HilbertSpace) resolves squared_norm to CoordinateSpace.squared_norm (spaces.py:420-430) with uses_component_fast_paths inherited True (spaces.py:449-456), so on every all-coordinate sum the norm goes through concatenated components — not worse than v1, but not the coordinate-free route the original text claimed. StrictSpace (tests/doubles.py:132) is confirmed a CoordinateSpace, so a sum containing it does dispatch to _CoordinateDirectSum as Review B stated. Unit as a whole: the core capabilities (direct sum space, four block operators, matrix-free action and adjoint, projections/inclusions) are all present in /home/david/dev/pygeoinf/pygeoinf2/algebra/direct_sum.py and in several respects better (direct inner product, zero-block skipping, structured/linked adjoints with trait propagation, blockwise Gram operations, apply_block on block-diagonal, labelled summands, nonlinear block operators with derivatives). The genuine regressions are concentrated in dense-matrix extraction: v1's per-block assembly hooks (np.block / vstack / hstack / block_diag, always taken) became a conditional _known_matrix that fires only when every block already holds a matrix, asks blocks for 'components' only (so Galerkin-stored blocks pay two metric passes), and for Column and Row was not ported at all. Second, the uniform BlockStructure interface is gone: block(i, j), row_dim, col_dim survive only on BlockOperator/BlockLinearOperator (unvalidated); the other three classes expose .operators. Third, API-breaking surface changes a v1 user will hit immediately: vectors are tuples (see review/pyslfp_usage.md:55), zero is a method, ax->scale_inplace, multiply->scale, number_of_subspaces->len(S), subspace_projection/inclusion->projection/inclusion, negative indices rejected by subspace(). The dual-space methods and is_element are gone by recorded DESIGN.md decisions (DESIGN.md:35, :211, :1272). Minor constructor inconsistencies: empty-list errors are ValueError only on the nonlinear-base path but IndexError when the *LinearOperator class is constructed directly or reached by dispatch from an empty list (direct_sum.py:668-670, :750-752, :819-821); BlockDiagonalLinearOperator now rejects empty lists where v1 accepted them. The catalogue (V1_CATALOGUE.md:116-121, :504-512) marks every class 'Ported' and BlockStructure 'Subsumed'; this audit disagrees on the Column/Row dense hooks (lost), the block()/row_dim/col_dim accessors on Column/Row/BlockDiagonal (gone), and the block-index validation (gone). Aside from _known_matrix reading stored matrices and the base matrix() probe, nothing in this unit forms a dense or sparse matrix; v1's matrix(dense=False) scipy wrapper is a base-class removal, not specific to this unit. **preconditioners.** FINAL after two adversarial reviews. Review A (lost/subsumed/dropped rows) proposed no status corrections; its runtime confirmation of the IterativePreconditioningMethod idiom (converges; 36 RuntimeWarnings over two solves) and its test-coverage observation (no v2 test passes a bare IterativeSolver as preconditioner=) are folded into that row and dense_regressions. Review B (ported rows) proposed four text corrections, all keeping the original status; I re-read the cited code and re-ran the reproduction for each, and ACCEPT ALL FOUR: (1) _probe_columns aliasing — reproduced in the project venv exactly as described (v2 Block/ColumnThresholded on LinearOperator.identity(EuclideanSpace(4)) raise 'Factor is exactly singular'; v1 returns [1,2,3,4]); cause is basis[index]=0.0 at preconditioners.py:354 before the yield while `image` aliases `basis` through EuclideanSpace's documented zero-copy to_components/from_components and _Identity._value returning x. This is the single most important finding in the unit: a new correctness defect, not a dropped option. (2) The Jacobi __call__ row's 'mathematically the same as v1' was false — v1's _mapping_galerkin (linear_operators.py:1058-1062) is G^-1 M, so v1's Jacobi acted as G^-1 D^-1 on components while v2 acts as D^-1 G; v2 is correct, v1 was right only on an identity Gram; the row now says so and agrees with the dense_regressions entry. (3) The SELF_ADJOINT requirement on Jacobi (:65) is a generality loss, not stricter validation: GMRESSolver has requires NONE (:1063) and BiCGStabSolver inherits NONE, diagonals()/random_diagonal need no trait, and v1's random_diagonal capped samples at n (low_rank.py:906-909) where v2's does not. (4) ColumnThresholded's SELF_ADJOINT requirement plus transpose-based symmetrisation removes the v1 use case of preconditioning a non-symmetric system; v1 offered galerkin=False, an asymmetric pattern and trans='T'. Also accepted Review B's minor points: the 'v1 always probed dim columns' improvement was overstated (v1 MatrixLinearOperator.extract_diagonal had a dense-matrix fast path at linear_operators.py:1129) — softened in dense_regressions; and test paths corrected to /home/david/dev/pygeoinf/pygeoinf2/tests/ (there is no top-level tests/ directory). No correction was rejected. No status changed: all seven v1 preconditioning methods still have a v2 counterpart (six classes plus the IterativeSolver-as-preconditioner idiom), nothing is 'lost' outright, and only Identity, the diagonal-fill behaviour and the zero-diagonal fallback are clean 'ported'. Summary of what the owner should know, in order of importance: (a) the _probe_columns basis-aliasing defect breaks Block/ColumnThresholded on zero-copy identity-like operators — trivial fix, needs a test; (b) Jacobi and ColumnThresholded can no longer precondition non-symmetric systems even though v2 provides GMRES/BiCGStab; (c) SpectralPreconditioner is a different preconditioner from v1's (exact inversion of resolved modes + 1/d tail, expecting the already-damped operator, vs v1's Woodbury inverse of U S U* + d^2 I expecting the undamped A*WA) and `damping` is no longer squared; (d) the Jacobi default flipped from ~20 stochastic probes to exact, costing dim applications on any composed operator; (e) systematic option losses — ILU from Banded/Block (REVIEW.md:110 flagged as undecided, still absent), parallel probing from everything but Jacobi (incomplete D-6 port, hooks exist one call down), the adaptive modes of random_diagonal/random_eig unreachable from Jacobi/Spectral, and the transposed-solve adjoint on the sparse-LU classes (harmless while SELF_ADJOINT is claimed, a full re-probe otherwise). Genuine improvements: correct Gram handling on non-identity metrics in all four coordinate-based preconditioners (Jacobi's included, which v1 got wrong), conditional rather than asserted self-adjointness claims, deduplicated overlapping blocks, symmetrised column thresholding, the O(bandwidth) banded probe, broader known-diagonal reads, and lazy joblib import. WoodburyPreconditioner (numerics/preconditioners.py:483-740) and the structure-aware classes in pygeoinf2/inference/preconditioners.py belong to the inversion-class unit, not to this v1 module. **functional_calculus.** FINAL after two adversarial reviews. Review A proposed no row corrections (no row is lost/subsumed/dropped_deliberately); its two extra notes (DESIGN.md 5.7 documents the SELF_ADJOINT gate; Traits lives in traits.py) were verified against pygeoinf2/DESIGN.md:1036-1042 and traits.py:30 and are merged into the automorphism_check row, the LanczosOperatorFunction row and terminology_changes. Review B's two corrections were both verified by reading the code and re-running its repro scripts, and are ACCEPTED: (1) the coordinate-free iter_lanczos_tridiagonalise path mutates the operator's output in place (axpy at :139) so an argument-returning operator -- including v2's own LinearOperator.identity (nodes.py:65-66) -- has its first Krylov vector zeroed; reproduced: basis norm 3.4e-16, sqrt(I)x rel err 1.0 on StrictSpace, 0.0 on the component path. This is a genuine silent wrong-answer regression versus v1's out-of-place subtract (v1 :461-463) and is now recorded on the iter, lanczos, apply, OperatorFunction, quadratic-form and breakdown rows and in dense_regressions; status stays ported_changed as both reviewers and I agree. (2) The component path's 'Kahan second pass' baseline is \|\|A q\|\| before the three-term subtraction (:208), so it fires essentially every step; reproduced: 91 apply_gram calls in 30 steps (3.03/step). The reorthogonalisation row's earlier claim that the component path 'retains' v1's Kahan criterion was wrong and is corrected; v2 has no path implementing v1's conditional re-pass. Review B's default-cost measurement (all 50 applications used even at cond 1e2) is merged into the apply_operator_function and convergence_schedule rows and dense_regressions. Otherwise the original assessment stands: everything in this unit exists in v2 and the core mathematics (Lanczos on an abstract Hilbert space, f(T)e_1 in coefficient space, Gauss quadrature for the quadratic form, lazy self-adjoint operator) is faithfully carried, with real improvements (early stopping in the quadratic form, coefficient-space check retained, exact diagonal dispatch, component fast path, yield-aliasing fix, breakdown_tol exposed, named operator_sqrt/log/exp/power helpers, log_determinant). Nothing forms a dense or sparse matrix of A or f(A) on either path. The catalogue overstates: all five 'Ported' rows (V1_CATALOGUE.md:158-162) hide that every public signature changed argument order, that size_estimate/method/max_k/atol/check_interval were removed with no owner decision recorded (REVIEW.md:110: 'dropped things that were not decided'), that rtol default went 1e-3 -> 1e-10 and the iteration cap from space.dim to a hard 50/30 (measured to mean ~50 applications per default f(A)x), that neither path implements v1's conditional Kahan re-pass, that every routine now refuses an operator lacking the SELF_ADJOINT trait (owner-designed in DESIGN.md 5.7, mitigated by with_traits), and the in-place aliasing bug. Two further correctness regressions found by running the code: max_iterations < 1 is no longer validated (IndexError on the component path, silent empty result on the coordinate-free path; v1 raised ValueError), and the component path preallocates dim x max_iterations doubles regardless of early termination. Recommended fixes for the owner: copy w when it is basis[-1] (or space.copy the operator output) at numerics/functional_calculus.py:135-139; take the Kahan baseline after the three-term subtraction at :208; restore a max_iterations >= 1 check. v1's internal consumers (gaussian_measure sampling/log-density, linear_bayesian matrix log) are served in v2 through operator_function/operator_sqrt and log_determinant (probability/gaussian.py:1072, inference/gaussian.py:565), so the capability is reachable end-to-end, but on a coordinate-free space with an aliasing covariance those consumers would inherit the zero-result bug. **nonlinear_optimisation.** FINAL classification after two adversarial reviews. Review A (lost/subsumed/dropped rows) proposed no corrections; its two qualifications (the ProximalGradient projected-gradient route as a partial answer to bound constraints, and the stale 'ftol lost' line in review/numerics.md:51) were verified and folded into the _GRADIENT_METHODS row, the ScipyUnconstrainedOptimiser row, the tol_handling row and dense_regressions. Review B (ported rows) proposed one correction to line_search.gradient_recomputation, which I verified line by line and ACCEPTED: line_search.py:263-266 re-evaluates functional at the bracket's low end on zoom entry, and since previous_step starts at 0.0 (:204) and zoom is called with low=previous_step from the Armijo branch (:213-222), a first-trial Armijo failure re-evaluates f(point) — the very `value` the caller was required to pass. The original row's 'never recomputes f(x) ... at the start point' was false; status stays ported_changed but the change text and the IMPROVED verdict are now qualified. Review B's four further findings (failure-path evaluations uncounted at :243-244 and :289-291; max_step never evaluated at :239-241; Functional.at building the Hessian at every Wolfe trial, operators.py:1878-1880; v1's up-front has_gradient ValueError replaced by a NotImplementedError deep inside functional.at, operators.py:2072) were all confirmed and added to dense_regressions, and the max_step and error-behaviour points were also added to the line_search row's change text. One thing neither review caught: review/numerics.md:111(b) says the zoom re-evaluation is uncounted, but the code now counts it (the comment at :263-264 records the fix), so that review line is half stale.  No status changed. The whole v1 unit was a 218-line SciPy adaptation layer; v2 replaces it with native, coordinate-free optimisers and line searches and imports nothing from scipy.optimize for general functionals. The drop of ScipyUnconstrainedOptimiser is recorded in V1_CATALOGUE.md:180 with the owner's 'yes, drop', and DESIGN.md:1650-1658 plus the v2 module docstring (optimisation.py:1-27) give the reason: v1 handed SciPy primal-gradient components as jac alongside a Galerkin Hessian, which is metrically inconsistent unless G = I. The v2 design removes the failure mode structurally (gradient = derivative.adjoint(1.0), slopes are inner products), and the tests include a non-diagonal Gram matrix (tests/test_optimisation.py:628-644), which is the right test per the metric-bug rule.  Three things the owner should weigh. (1) Real capability losses that the catalogue's 'Replaced by bespoke coordinate-free methods' does not surface: derivative-free minimisation (Nelder-Mead/Powell) is impossible in v2, bound constraints (L-BFGS-B) exist only as an unadvertised first-order ProximalGradient route with no Box set, and full-memory BFGS / trust-exact / dogleg are absent. The owner's own note on V1_CATALOGUE.md:182-184 asks about constrained optimisation, so this is already on the radar. (2) The catalogue's 'Ported' for line_search is too generous: the function became a class with a different signature (value and slope now required; extra_condition, amax=None, old_old_fval gone), a different return type, different defaults (max_iterations 30 vs 10; max_step 1e8 vs unbounded, and never actually evaluated), a bisection zoom instead of SciPy's interpolating zoom (REVIEW.md:156), a redundant evaluation on zoom entry, an evaluation miscount on failure, and no up-front derivative check. extra_condition in particular is lost with no hook other than subclassing LineSearch. (3) Net improvements are substantial and should be recorded as such: convergence status, iteration/evaluation counts and value history are returned (v1 discarded them); the Wolfe search returns the model at the accepted point so the outer loop saves an evaluation per iteration (partly offset by the zoom re-evaluation); the Hessian is consumed matrix-free inside Steihaug CG; and all methods run on spaces without a component map and are metric-aware. The v1 UnboundLocalError bug in line_search (extra_condition omitted) is gone by removal of the feature rather than by a fix.  A minor point for anyone who wants a SciPy bridge back: v2 LinearOperator.matrix() is dense-only and no scipy.sparse.linalg.LinearOperator export exists, so v1's matrix-free Galerkin Hessian export (matrix(galerkin=True, dense=False)) has no v2 equivalent. No file under /home/david/dev/pygeoinf was modified.  Overall the GaussianMeasure class is substantially ported and in several respects better (metric-correct sampling, explicit RNG, precision propagation, spectral fast paths, KL error bars, new condition/marginal/density methods), but the catalogue's blanket 'Ported' rows hide real losses and three defects that tests do not cover.  Confirmed defects in v2 (reproduced with `poetry run python` on scratch scripts under /tmp/claude-1000/-home-david-dev-pygeoinf/d93e5baf-8aac-4918-917c-1c45c7801ad1/scratchpad/): (1) DOUBLE MEAN — GaussianMeasure.sample adds the expectation after calling an explicit sampler (gaussian.py:637-650), but the sampler closures built by _combine_affine (gaussian.py:2178-2184), _combine_add (gaussian.py:2252-2255) and from_product (gaussian.py:427-431) call the public self.sample() which already includes the mean. Any measure with an explicit sampler and no factor — notably every result of condition() — therefore has its mean doubled after translate(v) with v != -m, affine_map(), +, or from_product. Measured: mean [10,20,30] -> translate(0) samples with mean [20,40,60]; cond.translate(0).sample() == 2m. condition() itself is correct because it centres explicitly, and translate(-m) is correct because the new mean is zero. (2) SAMPLER LOSS — _combine_scale (gaussian.py:2275-2318) never passes a sampler to _rebuild, so scaling, -1.0*mu, subtraction and rescale_directional_variance make explicit-sampler, factor-less measures unsamplable; v1 wrapped the sampler through each of __neg__, __mul__, __sub__, zero_expectation. (3) TRAIT LOSS ON SUMS — _combine_add builds total = C1 + C2 without re-claiming POSITIVE_SEMIDEFINITE, and the operator-sum specialisation discards with_traits claims on compositions ((comp+comp).traits == Traits.NONE; operators.py:346-355), so `cond + cond` raises ValueError from the constructor (gaussian.py:2262, :210-216). Factor-backed measures are unaffected by all three.  Genuinely lost capabilities: the KKT saddle-point push-forward precision (affine_mapping(inverse_solver=...)) and its Jacobi-Schur preconditioner; the Cameron-Martin and weakened/fractional credible-set geometries with their spectrum/Lanczos options; credible_set's rank and open_set; sample_pointwise_variance/std (Monte-Carlo pointwise variance field on a HilbertModule); directional_statistics; __neg__; user-supplied spectra for the ambient ball; the sparse-LU precision, correlation thresholding and max_nnz of with_sparse_approximation; parallel assembly in as_multivariate_normal; the None zero-mean sentinel under algebra. None of these is recorded as a deliberate drop in V1_CATALOGUE.md 'Your notes' or DESIGN.md, so they are classed 'lost', not 'dropped_deliberately'.  Semantic shifts users will hit: from_standard_deviations now means diag(sigma) as an operator in the space's basis (agrees with v1 only on orthonormal spaces); from_standard_deviation samples differ from v1 on any non-identity Gram matrix (v2 is the correct one); from_covariance_matrix gives no precision for singular matrices; from_samples refuses n=1; kl_divergence 'auto' raises for large non-diagonal spaces instead of going stochastic, and the stochastic route needs a factor; nuclear/HS norms default to exact-dense rather than Hutchinson; with_regularized_inverse leaves the covariance and sampler at C while the precision is (C+dI)^-1; credible_set silently densifies when no precision exists; the constructor rejects covariance/precision operators lacking SELF_ADJOINT\|POSITIVE_SEMIDEFINITE traits; from_product always stores a tuple expectation.  Catalogue corrections needed: from_standard_deviation(s) (two methods, array refused), with_dense_covariance and low_rank_approximation (are Ported methods, not Subsumed), deflated_pointwise_variance (now reachable via SymmetricSpace.pointwise_variance_at, catalogue says Not ported), sample_pointwise_variance (Not ported, not Subsumed), credible_set / weakened_ellipsoid / affine_mapping (overstated as Ported), directional_statistics (absent), with_sparse_approximation (weakened). V1_CATALOGUE.md:415-419 and tests/test_code_practice.py:274-279 encode some of these stale statuses.

**convex_analysis.** FINAL classification after two adversarial reviews. Review A (lost/subsumed rows) proposed no status corrections and its re-verification of every lost/subsumed row is accepted; its one extra finding — numpy-scalar multiplication is order-dependent (np.int64(2)*h -> _ScaledSupport, h*np.int64(2) -> _FunctionalScaled) — reproduced in the poetry environment and has been folded into the scale, __mul__ and __rmul__ rows and the terminology list. Review B (ported rows) proposed three corrections, all accepted after reading the code and re-running the probes: (1) CallableSupportFunction.support_point is 'lost', not 'ported_changed' — the maximiser passed to ConvexSet.from_support_function is stored on _OracleSet but discarded by support_function() (geometry/convex.py:256-258), _OracleSupport has no _maximiser so subgradient() returns None, _OracleSet does not override support_maximiser (grep 'def support_maximiser' -> :113, :592, :863 only) so the ConvexSet API raises, and the only accessor, _OracleSet.maximiser, has no caller anywhere in pygeoinf2 while the consumers (inference/backus.py:1088-1089, numerics/convex.py:1910) call support_maximiser; a capability reachable from nothing is lost. (2) SupportFunction.point and (3) PointSupportFunction move from 'ported' to 'ported_changed' under the rule that a row naming a breaking change (rename, classmethod->staticmethod, positional-only, private class absent from every __all__) cannot carry 'ported'; the semantics are unchanged so these are renames, not losses. The method-level _mapping rows (Ball, Callable, Point, LinearImage, MinkowskiSum) stay 'ported' because the _mapping -> _value hook rename is charged once to the SupportFunction._mapping row and the computations are identical (Review B considered and rejected changing these, and I agree). Review B's three extra regressions all reproduced and are merged: set-level support_maximiser exists only on Ball and Ellipsoid so composite sets ((Ball+Ball), _Translated, _OracleSet) raise NotImplementedError on the route the Backus dual code uses even though their functional-level subgradient works; Ball.support_maximiser returns the stored centre object at a zero direction while _BallSupport._maximiser returns a copy (the duplicated pair REVIEW.md:238 flags has diverged); direct construction of _ImageSupport/_MinkowskiSupport with mismatched spaces fails only at evaluation with an opaque numpy shape error. Review B's DESIGN.md §11.8 finding is confirmed: line 1730 records 'compose_with had its domains backwards' as v2's own early bug, which is the sharper evidence that V1_CATALOGUE.md:199 misattributes the defect to v1; the image/LinearImageSupportFunction rows and catalogue notes now cite it. Overall picture unchanged from the original: the unit was re-architected rather than ported — v1's nine public NonLinearForm subclasses became one public abstract Functional subclass (numerics.convex.SupportFunction, exported from pygeoinf2.numerics but not from the package top level) plus eight private implementations, with the user-facing entry points moved onto geometry.convex.ConvexSet. Ball, Point, Minkowski sum, scaling and linear image survive with the same matrix-free formulas. Genuinely lost: HalfSpaceSupportFunction in its entirety (REVIEW.md:134; catalogue 'Ported \| HalfSpace' is false; the docstring rationale 'no dependence on the inversion layer' does not cover it); the fused value_and_support_point entry point and its Ball/Ellipsoid overrides; the Ellipsoid radius parameter and the A^{-1/2} evaluation route; the alpha==0 short-circuit; and the callable support-point capability. Confirmed correctness hazards: _OracleSupport and _ShiftedSupport never define _maximiser (Operator is not an ABC so @abstractmethod is unenforced), so their subgradient returns None while has_subgradient claims True and a Minkowski sum containing such a part raises TypeError; 0.0*h, -h, h-g and h*np.int64 fall through to generic _FunctionalScaled/_FunctionalSum whose has_subgradient is True but whose subgradient() raises NotImplementedError; has_derivative is True for every SupportFunction though gradient() raises; Ellipsoid.support_maximiser lacks the negative clamp its functional twin has (geometry/convex.py:883 vs 1048). Domain checks by equality instead of identity and adjoint memoisation are improvements. The catalogue has no rows for value_and_support_point, the operator overloads, or the package exports. **convex_optimisation.** FINAL after two adversarial reviews. Review A (lost/subsumed rows) proposed no corrections and its verification of the subsumed constructions and the three harmless 'lost' Bundle helpers was confirmed; those rows stand. Review B (ported rows) proposed three status changes, all verified against the code and accepted: (1) QPSolver ported -> ported_changed: LevelBundleMethod._master tests `result.solved` (convex.py:1362), a property only v2's QPResult has, so the protocol contract tightened beyond spelling; (2) OSQPQPSolver.solve ported -> ported_changed: `_validate` at quadratic_programming.py:304 raises ValueError where v1 passed arrays straight to osqp.setup, the same change that already marked SciPyQPSolver.solve ported_changed; (3) PrimalKKTSolver._woodbury_solve ported -> ported_changed: v1 cached A_B u0 and G* A_V d_tilde at construction (convex_optimisation.py:2355-2356) while v2 _model recomputes both on every residual evaluation (convex.py:1861, 1865). Review B's three extra regressions were each confirmed by reading the code and merged: ProximalBundleMethod reports the stability centre's value rather than the least value evaluated (convex.py:989-991 vs v1 938-944); the lost KKT vector cache; and the off-by-one Level iteration count (v2 `range(1, ...)` returning `iteration` at convex.py:1406-1412 vs v1 `num_iterations=k` with k from range(0, ...) at 1296-1311) — the original LevelBundleMethod.solve row's '(same as v1)' was wrong and is corrected. Review B's two non-status factual corrections were also adopted: the joblib row overstated the loss (v1's ImportError fallback at convex_optimisation.py:1461-1465 was unreachable because seven other v1 modules import joblib at module level and pyproject.toml:16 already required it), and 'n_jobs honoured only on route=dual' is an API wart rather than a regression since v1's solve_primal_feasibility had no n_jobs. No correction was rejected. Substance unchanged from the original: nothing in this unit is unreachable except trivial never-used Bundle helpers, but very little is a straight port either. The catalogue's 'Ported' rows (208, 210, 211, 216, 218) understate the changes: ProximalBundleMethod was re-derived (k-cut simplex dual via FISTA, metric-correct, no QPSolver) and lost rho_factor/qp_solver/store_iterates, with accuracy now limited by the projected-gradient subproblem (REVIEW2 3.1, CURRENT_STATE.md:168-171); LevelBundleMethod lost serious/null classification, its QP warm start and the LP box, and defaults to best_available_qp_solver while remaining dense in the data dimension; SmoothedLBFGSSolver's continuation schedule was dropped for a single epsilon; solve_support_values returns only values (no lambdas, diagnostics or lambda0); the fused value_and_subgradient oracle REVIEW.md:302 asked to restore was replaced by a memo covering only the Backus cost. Genuine improvements: ProximalBundleMethod and the smoothed route are metric-correct and free of O(d^2) allocations (by inspection — no bundle-method test runs on a non-Euclidean space, contrary to the owner's metric-bug rule); Chambolle-Pock projects onto any ConvexSet and warm-starts across directions; the KKT solver validates spaces and its data-space solve is correct on non-Euclidean data spaces. All three REVIEW/DESIGN documents say 'Mag's API, not redesigned, nothing cut' (REVIEW.md:304-312, CURRENT_STATE.md:165-167) — the code shows otherwise for ProximalBundleMethod and LevelBundleMethod, so the owner should review those two in particular. Tests (tests/test_convex.py, tests/test_quadratic_programming.py, tests/test_backus.py:698-766) cover happy paths and cross-route agreement on loose-noise problems, on Euclidean spaces only. pyproject.toml still declares osqp and clarabel extras; joblib is a hard dependency in both versions. **subsets.** FINAL classification after two adversarial reviews; also written to /tmp/claude-1000/-home-david-dev-pygeoinf/d93e5baf-8aac-4918-917c-1c45c7801ad1/scratchpad/audit/subsets.json. Review B (ported rows) proposed eight corrections; all eight were verified against the cited code and accepted: (a) EmptySet.is_element and UniversalSet.is_element -> ported_changed (sets.py:95,115 have rtol=1e-9 vs v1 subsets.py:266,286 rtol=1e-6, the same change the sibling rows already call ported_changed); (b) Ellipsoid.center and EllipsoidSurface.center -> ported_changed (v1 subsets.py:905-906 raised unless domain.is_element(center); v2 convex.py:861,1180 accept anything and default to zero; EllipsoidSurface.__init__ 1172-1179 also lacks Ellipsoid's precision-domain check at 857-858); (c) PolyhedralSet and Subset.intersect keep ported_changed but now record that Polytope.__and__ (convex.py:511-522) is unguarded — `Polytope & Ball` raised AttributeError 'Ball' object has no attribute 'is_outer' at runtime while .intersect(Ball) returned ConvexIntersection; (d) Ellipsoid.radius stays subsumed but the subsumption is partial since v1 accepted radius 0 (subsets.py:908-909) and 1/r**2 cannot express it; (e) behaviour.matrix_free now records that _dykstra (convex.py:410) calls part.project bare, so solver= cannot reach an Ellipsoid inside ConvexIntersection/Polytope/indicator prox. Nothing was rejected. Row count unchanged (116 rows, all original ids retained). Overall shape: the unit was redesigned around 'a convex set knows its metric projection' (ConvexSet.project abstract; contains defaults to \|\|x-P(x)\|\|) instead of v1's 'a set is a sublevel set of a functional'. Consequences: (1) the whole functional family — SublevelSet, LevelSet, ConvexSubset.form/level/is_open/closure/check, the ellipsoidal NonLinearForm with gradient 2A(x-c) and Hessian 2A, and ConvexIntersection's max-functional — has no v2 counterpart; the catalogue says LevelSet/SublevelSet are 'Not ported' and planned for M5 5.8, and tests/test_code_practice.py:274-281 pins them as ABSENT_FROM_V2, so this is a known gap, not a deliberate drop. (2) Every v2 convex set is closed; open sets and Ball's open-by-default quirk are gone without a recorded decision. (3) Sets gained: projections (including a Newton secular-equation projection for ellipsoids and Dykstra for intersections/polytopes), indicator functionals with prox, Minkowski sums, oracle sets from support functions, translate, operator overloads, inner/outer polytopes. (4) Things silently missing that the catalogue still marks Ported: Subset.is_empty, Subset.boundary as a base contract (only Ball/HalfSpace/Ellipsoid have it), Subset.plot (plot_slice is 'Planned'), ConvexSubset.check, ConvexIntersection.feasible_lower_bound, HalfSpace.support_function (catalogue row 197 is false and was already flagged twice in review/), HalfSpace '>=' form, HyperPlane/HalfSpace.distance_to, HyperPlane.dimension, Ellipsoid inverse_sqrt_operator route, the _support_fn cache, the centre-membership validation on all four ellipsoidal/ball sets, and Ellipsoid radius 0. (5) Tolerance semantics changed per class and the default rtol moved 1e-6 -> 1e-9; v1's floor of max(1, level) is gone for Ball/BallSurface, so small-radius sets are tested much more tightly than before (verified: Ball(radius=1e-3).contains(r*(1+1e-8)) is False in v2). (6) v2 defects noticed while reading, in the replacement paths users are pointed at: Polytope.__and__ breaks for any non-Polytope right operand (a regression against v1 intersect); Ellipsoid.support_maximiser raises AttributeError where its docstring promises ValueError (convex.py:872-881) and _OracleSet.maximiser likewise vs NotImplementedError (250-254); Ellipsoid.support_function raises NotImplementedError vs docstring ValueError (1015-1019); Ball.boundary raises ValueError at radius 0 via BallSurface's radius>0 check although Ball allows radius 0 (convex.py:586-590,1074-1075; tests confirm intended, test_geometry.py:324-330); _Translated does not override support_maximiser so ConvexSet.translate(ball, v).support_maximiser raises NotImplementedError while Ball.translate works; per Review B, SupportFunction._maximiser is @abstractmethod but Functional is not an ABC, so _ShiftedSupport (convex.py:210) and _OracleSupport (326) instantiate without it and .subgradient returns None while has_subgradient reports True (numerics/convex.py:148-155) — inference/backus.py:1088-1089 would hit this if a translated or oracle set were used as a prior; ConvexIntersection.support_bound's NotImplementedError catch (1319-1324) also swallows evaluation-time failures. (7) Matrix-free status is preserved everywhere except the new Ellipsoid.project, whose default CholeskySolver is dense (two factorisations per Newton step) and whose solver= override cannot be forwarded through Dykstra, so any intersection containing an ellipsoid is coordinate-bound; a new capability, not a regression of an existing one, but it cuts against the library's matrix-free-by-default aim. (8) Examples/tests evidencing v2 behaviour: examples/17_sets.py, tests/test_geometry.py (TestSetAlgebra, TestConvexProjections, TestEllipsoid, TestBoundaries, TestTheMetricEntersEveryProjection, TestPolytopeProjection, TestConvexIntersection).

**subspaces.** FINAL after two adversarial reviews. Review A proposed no row corrections; its confirmation of every subsumed row (solver= keyword locations, CGSolver(preconditioner=) inheriting IterativeSolver.__init__, no conditioning method anywhere in geometry/probability/inference, both from_complement_basis replacement constructions real, _combine_affine zero-translation path, REVIEW.md:134 and review/pyslfp_usage.md:174 asking for the subspace conditioning method to be restored) has been folded into the change/evidence text, and its extra dense regression and terminology item are merged. Review B's two corrections are ACCEPTED after independent re-verification: OrthogonalProjector.basis() (the get_tangent_basis port) over-reports rank and returns out-of-range vectors because v1's absolute 1e-10 norm floor on P e_i was dropped in favour of orthonormal_basis's purely relative test (norm > 1e-10 * norm(input), input floored at 1e-300); re-running the scripts in this audit gave len(basis()) == 6 vs dimension() == 5 with norm(P e_0) = 1.1e-16 on R^6 for <0.3 e_0, x> = 1, and 131/200 (CG) / 55/200 (Cholesky) wrong ranks vs v1 0/200 in R^20; dimension() and to_hyperplanes() were 0/200 wrong. Statuses of both rows stay ported_changed but the change text now records a correctness regression. Review B's note about the original classification's own notes is also ACCEPTED: the claim that the from_linear_equation docstring's 'pass a least-squares solver' advice is 'not supported by _normal_inverse's square-solver call protocol' was wrong — _normal_inverse does a plain solver(normal) call with no isinstance check and LeastSquaresSolver.__call__ returns a LinearOperator, so LSQRSolver() duck-types through (verified: rank-2 3-row A on R^10, consistent b, \|\|A x - b\|\| = 1.5e-14, dimension() == 8); only the type hint LinearSolver \| None does not admit it. That claim has been removed and the corrected observation recorded on the from_linear_equation and default_cholesky_galerkin_solver rows. No corrections were rejected. Summary: the module is genuinely ported in shape — projector + translation, explicit/implicit dichotomy, one Gram solve, hyperplane round-trip — and several things are better (shared (A A*)^{-1}, projector-typed complement, rank-tolerant orthonormalisation, working zero projector, matrix-free default). Six real losses or regressions hide behind catalogue 'Ported' rows: (1) from_complement_basis (both classes) no longer produces an explicit constraint operator, so such subspaces cannot be conditioned, pseudo-inverted, shifted by constraint value, or used in a parameterised constrained inversion; (2) the implicit-constraint fallback (I-P)u = (I-P)x0 and the MinRes route for conditioning implicit subspaces are gone — constraint_operator/constraint_value raise AttributeError, and GaussianMeasure.condition's POSITIVE_DEFINITE assertion closes the manual route too; (3) condition_gaussian_measure has no counterpart on the subspace: the Bayesian mode is GaussianMeasure.condition(A, b, solver=) and the geometric mode is prior.affine_map(P, translation=...), with the caller supplying the pieces; (4) solver/preconditioner are no longer readable and from_hyperplanes cannot take a solver at all; (5) boundary() now returns the subspace itself where v1 returned EmptySet — a semantic reversal, not a rename; (6) OrthogonalProjector.basis() is rank-incorrect for coordinate-aligned constraints (the one-line fix is to drop projected vectors below an absolute or largest-projected-norm-relative floor before orthonormalising, as v1 did). Behavioural drifts to watch: default Gram solve is CG to 1e-12 (a CG solve per projector application, so dimension()/basis()/to_hyperplanes() become dim solves), A A* is asserted POSITIVE_DEFINITE so rank-deficient constraints stall CG silently (though LSQRSolver() can be passed as a workaround despite the type hint), contains() default rtol is 1e-9 not 1e-6, translation is no longer validated against the domain, ~subspace on a LinearSubspace gives the orthogonal complement rather than the set complement, and the exception type for explicit-only operations changed from ValueError to AttributeError. V1_CATALOGUE.md's Part 2 table for AffineSubspace is wrong or incomplete on get_tangent_basis (location and correctness), boundary (reversed answer), from_complement_basis (lost equation), LinearSubspace.from_complement_basis (absent) and condition_gaussian_measure (not on the subspace). The owner's only note in that table (V1_CATALOGUE.md:520, 'All these methods below have been useful, and so they are either needed or the functionality provided elsewhere') supports keeping the functionality, and no DESIGN.md or owner-notes decision records dropping any of these, so none qualify as dropped_deliberately; DESIGN §21.16 (lines 3386-3390) does record the decision that constraint_operator should raise rather than invent an equation, which explains loss (2) but was not signed off in the catalogue's 'Your notes' column. Final JSON written to /tmp/claude-1000/-home-david-dev-pygeoinf/d93e5baf-8aac-4918-917c-1c45c7801ad1/scratchpad/audit/subspaces.json.

SILENT DEFAULT CHANGES worth flagging to the owner: circle.Lebesgue/Sobolev default to circumference 1.0 (v1 radius 1 = circumference 2*pi; the generic pygeoinf2.Lebesgue((n,)) keeps 2*pi, so the two circle spellings disagree) — combined with physical-coordinate arguments, EVERY v1 circle call site that passed angles (project_function, geodesic_distance, point_evaluation_operator, path operators) silently computes something else unless length=2*pi is given; line/plane Sobolev padding defaults to 0.1*extent, no longer 6*scale (v1 tied padding to the correlation length); line/plane Lebesgue padding is relative (0.1*extent) not absolute 0.1; 2-D plots are transposed relative to v1 (axis 0 vertical) with cmap viridis and colorbar on. CONFIRMED v2 DEFECT (runtime): Box does not override PeriodicBox._wrap, which reduces points modulo `lengths` in domain coordinates, so geodesic_quadrature nodes, walk_from points and geodesic_ball_quadrature nodes on any bounded domain whose padded range is not inside [0, L) per axis are displaced by a period (line.Lebesgue(32, lower=2, upper=5): nodes for [2.5, 4.5] -> [2.73, 3.5, 0.67]; walk_from 3.0 by 1.0 -> 0.4). Integrals are still correct because the basis is periodic, but the returned coordinates — and anything fed to path_*_operator's weight= callable or to a user's plot — are wrong. tests/test_space_parity.py only uses lower=0 and so does not catch it. Second confirmed v2 defect-in-kind: the transfer operator's handling of the mode that becomes Nyquist is not the orthogonal projection in either version, but the factor changed (0.5/2 -> 1/sqrt2/sqrt2) and the derived adjoint makes T*T non-idempotent at that mode. v1 defects that v2 fixes: line derivative's extra 2*pi; line geodesic_quadrature wrapping through the padding; circle.Sobolev.angles() AttributeError; plane.Sobolev kwargs leak in from_sobolev_parameters; safe not forwarded by with_order/with_degree (no longer a space attribute). **checks.** FINAL classification after two adversarial reviews. Review A (attacking lost/subsumed/dropped rows) proposed no status corrections; I re-verified its supporting evidence (AffineOperator without .adjoint at operators.py:2320-2395, check_operator typed LinearOperator and dereferencing .adjoint at testing.py:446, DESIGN.md:35/1254 for the dual drop, REVIEW2.md:135 for U 8 still open) and merged its two extra dense-regression notes and two extra terminology notes. Review B (attacking ported rows) proposed three corrections, all accepted after reading the code and re-running its probe scripts: (1) hilbert_space._check_copy is re-classified ported_changed -> LOST: testing.py:194-197 compares x against copy(x) after scaling a second copy, so if copy returns x (or a shared-buffer view) every object aliases and x == original holds trivially; probe2.py confirms an aliasing copy with pure out-of-place ops passes check_space(trials=20) while v1 fails with 'copy() returned the same object'. The original classification's claim that a same-object copy 'would still be caught' was wrong. Only value preservation survives, which is not what the v1 check was for. (2) hilbert_space._check_inplace_operations keeps ported_changed but the change text is rewritten: v2 tests the RETURN VALUE only (testing.py:185-186,190-191; `target` unused afterwards) and never verifies mutation or `result is target`; an out-of-place axpy/scale_inplace passes v2 and fails v1 (probe.py). This is deliberate per DESIGN.md:1325-1329 (Reals is immutable) but was mis-described as an added guarantee; compat.py:150-152 and testing.py:196 still rely on mutation. (3) linear_operators...inherited_nonlinear_checks keeps subsumed, with the reason corrected: DESIGN.md:1172 specified check_operator would include 'derivative by finite differences' and DESIGN.md:1170 kept n=10, so the missing derivative call and the trials=5 default are implementation deviations from the design document, not recorded decisions; 'the user must opt in' was not intended. The DESIGN.md:1170 point is also now noted on the HilbertSpaceAxiomChecks.check row. Everything else stands as originally classified. Summary for the owner: the move to pygeoinf2/testing.py free functions is DESIGN-recorded (§8, DESIGN.md:1162-1175) and the new checks (check_traits, check_white_noise, check_gradient, check_representer, check_measure, check_projection, second derivatives, rng seeding, metric-aware norm comparisons) are genuine gains. Quietly lost and not recorded in the catalogue: (a) the GaussianMeasure sampling option on every check (open item U 8; needed by pyslfp); (b) the op2 two-operator identity checks (derivative sum/scalar/chain rules, adjoint algebra; the dual one is gone by DESIGN decision 1) — reachable only indirectly by checking the composite; (c) the whole of AffineOperatorAxiomChecks — the catalogue's 'Subsumed: check_operator handles affine operators' (V1_CATALOGUE.md:295) is false; (d) the deep-copy/independence check, now vacuous; (e) verification that axpy/scale_inplace actually mutate (deliberate, DESIGN.md:1325); (f) check_operator's inherited finite-difference derivative check, contrary to DESIGN.md:1172. Smaller losses: derivative type/domain assertions, the named `subtract` identity, the triangle inequality, user-settable tolerances on check_space/check_coordinates/check_operator, halved default trial counts (contrary to DESIGN.md:1170 for spaces). check_coordinates (dense Gram + eigvalsh) and check_traits' INVERTIBLE branch (dense matrix_rank, computed twice on failure) must not be run on large spaces. The v1 quirks the inventory flagged (sampler attribute side effect, dormant Riesz check, O(dim^2) basis loop, chain-rule domain caveat, zero-vector spurious copy failure) are all resolved in v2 — the last one only because the independence test itself was removed. **data_assimilation.** The whole data_assimilation unit is absent from pygeoinf2: no data_assimilation or pendulum directory exists, and every unit-specific symbol grepped (ProbabilityGrid, AssimilationEngine, *KalmanFilter, GaussianLikelihood, solve_trajectory/solve_ensemble, solve_ivp, wrap_angle, trapezoid, RegularGridInterpolator, expm, tangent_linear, propagator, pendulum, the plotting helpers) hits only Markdown, docstring mentions of 'Kalman gain/formulas' (inference/gaussian.py:158, inference/normal.py:488, inference/mixture.py:12), the Imhof trapezoid quadrature in numerics/quadratic_forms.py, or an expm test oracle. This is a recorded, owner-agreed decision: V1_CATALOGUE.md:323-333 marks the module Dropped and the owner's note on :329 reads 'This is actually just a teaching module included for convenience. It is not part of the core library, though as noted above we will eventually add in stuff for sequentual data assimilation. For the moment al this is droped from V2'; V1_CATALOGUE.md:55-57 and DESIGN.md:3058-3059 defer sequential assimilation to a later dynamical_system module; REVIEW.md:365 and FUNCTIONALITY_AUDIT.md:14 record the same agreement. Hence 55 of 64 rows are dropped_deliberately (8 subsumed, 1 ported_changed), none is a silent loss. What genuinely survives is the part that was never really teaching-specific: a Gaussian observation model (ForwardProblem / LinearForwardProblem with a GaussianMeasure error), one Kalman analysis step (LinearGaussianInversion, or GaussianMeasure.condition, both matrix-free with a pluggable solver), one Kalman prediction step (GaussianMeasure.push_forward through a LinearOperator gives F m and F C F*), synthetic data with an explicit rng, the Gaussian pdf factories via as_multivariate_normal() or log_density, and a 2-D covariance ellipse via plot_corner's exact-Gaussian branch. Two things a user porting the teaching notebooks would notice: (1) there is no ODE integration of any kind in v2, so neither the Liouville advection nor the EnKF forecast nor the pendulum examples can be reconstructed without scipy.integrate called by hand; (2) the singular-innovation pinv fallback of the v1 KF has no v2 counterpart. The catalogue's 'Subsumed' verdict for GaussianLikelihood/LinearGaussianLikelihood (:331) is accurate; its blanket 'Dropped' for core.py plotting (:333) is slightly too strong for plot_gaussian_ellipsoid, which plot_corner covers. No v2 file was modified. Applied evidence corrections, each verified by me: (1) from_covariance_matrix's form= is NOT required — it defaults to 'galerkin' (gaussian.py:456-464), fixed in core.get_gaussian_pdf and core.GaussianLikelihood; (2) a singular R does not raise at construction in v2 — _semidefinite_factors (gaussian.py:60-100) falls back to eigh and returns no inverse root, from_covariance_matrix then sets precision=None (:540-560), so the failure moves to first use of precision/log_density/chi_squared, unlike v1's ValueError at core.py:523; fixed in core.GaussianLikelihood; (3) GaussianMeasure.condition (gaussian.py:1753-1846) is a closer, forward-problem-free Kalman update than LinearGaussianInversion and is now cited on core.LinearKalmanFilter._update as a second route; (4) GaussianMeasure.log_density (gaussian.py:2046) is the scipy-free pointwise density, added to the two pdf rows; (5) examples/28_nonlinear_map.py:121-123 shows the gridded-posterior teaching pattern reconstructed by hand on top of LaplaceApproximation.log_posterior, added to ProbabilityGrid.bayes_update. Review A's chi_squared_from_residual no-op (problem.py:189-193, subtract then re-add measure.expectation) is verified and recorded as an observation.
